# Get token balances for a wallet

> Get the supported deposit token balances for a wallet `address` on a given `chain_type`.



## OpenAPI

````yaml POST /v1/addresses/balances
openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Unifold API
  description: >-
    The Unifold API provides programmatic access to treasury management and
    cross-chain transfer capabilities. Use it to create treasury accounts,
    manage users, and execute outbound transfers across supported blockchains.


    ## Authentication


    The Unifold API uses API keys to authenticate requests. Include your API key
    in the `Authorization` header using the Bearer scheme:


    ```

    Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...

    ```


    You must use your secret API key, which starts with `sk_` (e.g.,
    `sk_live_...` or `sk_test_...`). You can obtain your API key from the
    [Unifold Dashboard](https://dashboard.unifold.io). Keep your secret keys
    secure and never expose them in client-side code.


    All API requests must be made over HTTPS. Requests without authentication
    will fail with a `401 Unauthorized` error.
  version: '1.0'
  contact: {}
servers:
  - url: https://api.unifold.io
    description: Production server
security: []
tags:
  - name: Users
    description: User management endpoints
  - name: Payment Intents
    description: >-
      Payment Intents represent a fixed-amount crypto payment. Create one on
      your server, pass its `client_secret` to your frontend, and Unifold
      handles deposit address generation, cross-chain bridging, and settlement
      tracking.
  - name: Treasury
    description: Treasury account and outbound transfer endpoints
  - name: Onramps
    description: Fiat-to-crypto onramp session management
  - name: Webhooks
    description: Webhook endpoint management
  - name: Direct Executions
    description: Direct execution records for client users
  - name: Deposit Addresses
    description: >-
      Generate or fetch per-user deposit wallets across every supported source
      chain for a single destination (chain + token + recipient). Use this when
      you want to drive the deposit flow yourself instead of through a Payment
      Intent.
  - name: Addresses
    description: >-
      Wallet address utilities — query on-chain token balances for an address
      against the set of tokens Unifold supports as a deposit source.
  - name: Tokens
    description: >-
      Catalog endpoints for the tokens Unifold supports as a deposit source,
      including their per-chain availability and deposit constraints.
paths:
  /v1/addresses/balances:
    post:
      tags:
        - Addresses
      summary: Get token balances for a wallet
      description: >-
        Get the supported deposit token balances for a wallet `address` on a
        given `chain_type`.
      operationId: AddressesController_getBalancesBackend
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/GetBalancesDto'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Token balances retrieved successfully
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/BalancesResponse'
        '400':
          description: Invalid request parameters
        '401':
          description: Missing or invalid secret API key
        '500':
          description: Internal server error while fetching balances
      security:
        - bearer: []
components:
  schemas:
    GetBalancesDto:
      type: object
      properties:
        address:
          type: string
          description: Wallet address to query.
          example: '0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc9e7595f5Ad12'
        chain_type:
          type: string
          description: Chain family to query. `ethereum` covers all supported EVM chains.
          enum:
            - ethereum
            - solana
            - bitcoin
            - algorand
            - xrpl
          example: ethereum
      required:
        - address
        - chain_type
    BalancesResponse:
      type: object
      properties:
        address:
          type: string
          description: The wallet address queried
          example: '0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc9e7595f5Ad12'
        chain_type:
          type: string
          description: The chain family queried
          example: ethereum
        balances:
          type: array
          description: Token balances sorted by USD value, highest first.
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/AddressBalance'
      required:
        - address
        - chain_type
        - balances
    AddressBalance:
      type: object
      properties:
        amount:
          type: string
          description: Balance in the token's base units.
          example: '1000000000'
        amount_usd:
          type: string
          nullable: true
          description: USD value. `null` if no price is available.
          example: '1000.00'
        exchange_rate:
          type: string
          nullable: true
          description: >-
            USD price per whole unit of the token. `null` if no price is
            available.
          example: '1.00'
        is_eligible:
          type: boolean
          description: >-
            Whether the balance clears the token's minimum deposit threshold
            (with a 10% margin).
          example: true
        ineligibility_reason:
          type: string
          nullable: true
          description: Why the balance is ineligible. `null` when `is_eligible` is `true`.
          enum:
            - minimum_not_met
            - not_supported_deposit_from
          example: null
        token:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/AddressBalanceToken'
      required:
        - amount
        - is_eligible
        - token
    AddressBalanceToken:
      type: object
      description: Token and chain metadata for a balance entry
      properties:
        symbol:
          type: string
          description: Token symbol
          example: USDC
        name:
          type: string
          description: Full token name
          example: USD Coin
        icon_url:
          type: string
          description: Token icon URL (SVG)
          example: https://cdn.example.com/api/public/icons/tokens/svg/usdc.svg
        icon_urls:
          type: array
          description: Token icon URLs in multiple formats
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/AddressBalanceTokenIconUrl'
        token_address:
          type: string
          description: >-
            Token contract address, or `"native"` for the chain's native asset
            (ETH, SOL, BTC, XRP, ALGO).
          example: '0xa0b86991c6218b36c1d19d4a2e9eb0ce3606eb48'
        chain_id:
          type: string
          description: Chain ID where this token lives
          example: '1'
        chain_name:
          type: string
          description: Human-readable chain name
          example: Ethereum
        chain_type:
          type: string
          description: Chain family
          example: ethereum
        decimals:
          type: number
          description: Token decimals
          example: 6
        minimum_deposit_amount_usd:
          type: number
          description: Minimum deposit amount in USD.
          example: 3
        chain_icon_url:
          type: string
          description: Chain icon URL (SVG)
          example: https://cdn.example.com/api/public/icons/networks/svg/ethereum.svg
        chain_icon_urls:
          type: array
          description: Chain icon URLs in multiple formats
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/AddressBalanceTokenIconUrl'
    AddressBalanceTokenIconUrl:
      type: object
      properties:
        url:
          type: string
          example: https://cdn.example.com/api/public/icons/tokens/svg/usdc.svg
        format:
          type: string
          enum:
            - svg
            - png
          example: svg
  securitySchemes:
    bearer:
      type: http
      scheme: bearer
      bearerFormat: sk_api_key
      description: >-
        API key authentication using the Authorization header. Use your secret
        API key (starts with `sk_`): `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...`
      x-default: sk_api_key

````

# Create or get deposit addresses

> Create or get the deposit addresses for a specific user and destination (`chain_type`, `chain_id`, `token_address`, `recipient_address`). Can be used for both deposit and payment intent flows.



## OpenAPI

````yaml POST /v1/deposit_addresses
openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Unifold API
  description: >-
    The Unifold API provides programmatic access to treasury management and
    cross-chain transfer capabilities. Use it to create treasury accounts,
    manage users, and execute outbound transfers across supported blockchains.


    ## Authentication


    The Unifold API uses API keys to authenticate requests. Include your API key
    in the `Authorization` header using the Bearer scheme:


    ```

    Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...

    ```


    You must use your secret API key, which starts with `sk_` (e.g.,
    `sk_live_...` or `sk_test_...`). You can obtain your API key from the
    [Unifold Dashboard](https://dashboard.unifold.io). Keep your secret keys
    secure and never expose them in client-side code.


    All API requests must be made over HTTPS. Requests without authentication
    will fail with a `401 Unauthorized` error.
  version: '1.0'
  contact: {}
servers:
  - url: https://api.unifold.io
    description: Production server
security: []
tags:
  - name: Users
    description: User management endpoints
  - name: Payment Intents
    description: >-
      Payment Intents represent a fixed-amount crypto payment. Create one on
      your server, pass its `client_secret` to your frontend, and Unifold
      handles deposit address generation, cross-chain bridging, and settlement
      tracking.
  - name: Treasury
    description: Treasury account and outbound transfer endpoints
  - name: Onramps
    description: Fiat-to-crypto onramp session management
  - name: Webhooks
    description: Webhook endpoint management
  - name: Direct Executions
    description: Direct execution records for client users
  - name: Deposit Addresses
    description: >-
      Generate or fetch per-user deposit wallets across every supported source
      chain for a single destination (chain + token + recipient). Use this when
      you want to drive the deposit flow yourself instead of through a Payment
      Intent.
  - name: Addresses
    description: >-
      Wallet address utilities — query on-chain token balances for an address
      against the set of tokens Unifold supports as a deposit source.
  - name: Tokens
    description: >-
      Catalog endpoints for the tokens Unifold supports as a deposit source,
      including their per-chain availability and deposit constraints.
paths:
  /v1/deposit_addresses:
    post:
      tags:
        - Deposit Addresses
      summary: Create or get deposit addresses
      description: >-
        Create or get the deposit addresses for a specific user and destination
        (`chain_type`, `chain_id`, `token_address`, `recipient_address`). Can be
        used for both deposit and payment intent flows.
      operationId: DepositAddressesController_createDepositAddressesBackend
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/CreateDepositAddressDto'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Deposit addresses generated or retrieved successfully
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/DepositAddressesResponse'
        '400':
          description: >-
            Invalid request data (e.g., chain ID does not match chain type or
            project mode)
        '401':
          description: Missing or invalid secret API key
      security:
        - bearer: []
components:
  schemas:
    CreateDepositAddressDto:
      type: object
      properties:
        external_user_id:
          type: string
          description: External user ID. The user is created if it doesn't exist.
          example: user_123
        destination_chain_type:
          type: string
          description: Destination blockchain
          enum:
            - ethereum
            - solana
            - bitcoin
            - algorand
            - xrpl
            - cardano
            - n1
          example: ethereum
        destination_chain_id:
          type: string
          description: >-
            Destination chain ID. Must match `destination_chain_type`. See
            [Supported chains](/get-started/supported-chains) for valid values.
          example: '1'
        destination_token_address:
          type: string
          description: >-
            Destination token contract address. Use `"native"` for the chain's
            native asset.
          example: '0xa0b86991c6218b36c1d19d4a2e9eb0ce3606eb48'
        recipient_address:
          type: string
          description: Recipient address on the destination chain.
          example: '0xb5e4CB861F70356ce8b48D728D708ff04AE51848'
        action_type:
          type: string
          description: Flow these addresses are generated for.
          enum:
            - deposit
            - withdraw
          default: deposit
          example: deposit
        source_chain_type:
          type: string
          nullable: true
          description: >-
            Restricts address generation to a single source chain. Only honored
            when `action_type=withdraw`; ignored for `deposit`.
          enum:
            - ethereum
            - solana
            - bitcoin
            - algorand
            - xrpl
            - cardano
            - n1
          example: ethereum
        client_metadata:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: true
          description: Arbitrary metadata to attach to the addresses.
          example: {}
      required:
        - external_user_id
        - destination_chain_type
        - destination_chain_id
        - destination_token_address
        - recipient_address
    DepositAddressesResponse:
      type: object
      properties:
        data:
          type: array
          description: One deposit address per supported source chain.
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/DepositAddress'
      required:
        - data
    DepositAddress:
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          description: Unique wallet identifier
          example: wallet_2Qz9K5YX8r5C8jZ1bXZ8kQd7W5M
        chain_type:
          type: string
          description: Blockchain the deposit address lives on
          enum:
            - ethereum
            - solana
            - bitcoin
            - algorand
            - xrpl
          example: ethereum
        address_type:
          type: string
          nullable: true
          description: >-
            Address variant for chains with multiple formats (e.g., `segwit` for
            Bitcoin). `null` otherwise.
          example: null
        address:
          type: string
          description: Deposit address the payer sends funds to.
          example: '0xb314E99b06aA00CE32b13420C6115B9f2E765fCA'
        destination_chain_type:
          type: string
          description: Destination chain type for this address's recipient
          example: ethereum
        destination_chain_id:
          type: string
          description: Destination chain ID for this address's recipient
          example: '1'
        destination_token_address:
          type: string
          description: Destination token address for this address's recipient
          example: '0xa0b86991c6218b36c1d19d4a2e9eb0ce3606eb48'
        recipient_address:
          type: string
          description: Final recipient address on the destination chain
          example: '0xb5e4CB861F70356ce8b48D728D708ff04AE51848'
        is_primary:
          type: boolean
          description: Whether this is the primary wallet for the tuple.
          example: true
        is_transit_wallet:
          type: boolean
          description: Whether this is an intermediate transit wallet.
          example: false
        action_type:
          type: string
          description: Action this address was generated for
          enum:
            - deposit
            - withdraw
          example: deposit
      required:
        - id
        - chain_type
        - address
        - destination_chain_type
        - destination_chain_id
        - destination_token_address
        - recipient_address
        - is_primary
        - is_transit_wallet
        - action_type
  securitySchemes:
    bearer:
      type: http
      scheme: bearer
      bearerFormat: sk_api_key
      description: >-
        API key authentication using the Authorization header. Use your secret
        API key (starts with `sk_`): `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...`
      x-default: sk_api_key

````

# List direct executions

> Fetches direct execution records for a user identified by their external user ID. Supports cursor-based pagination and status filtering.

Use the `action_type` query parameter to filter results by `deposit` or `withdraw`. Each execution in the response includes an `action_type` field indicating whether it is a deposit or withdrawal.


## OpenAPI

````yaml GET /v1/direct_executions
openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Unifold API
  description: >-
    The Unifold API provides programmatic access to treasury management and
    cross-chain transfer capabilities. Use it to create treasury accounts,
    manage users, and execute outbound transfers across supported blockchains.


    ## Authentication


    The Unifold API uses API keys to authenticate requests. Include your API key
    in the `Authorization` header using the Bearer scheme:


    ```

    Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...

    ```


    You must use your secret API key, which starts with `sk_` (e.g.,
    `sk_live_...` or `sk_test_...`). You can obtain your API key from the
    [Unifold Dashboard](https://dashboard.unifold.io). Keep your secret keys
    secure and never expose them in client-side code.


    All API requests must be made over HTTPS. Requests without authentication
    will fail with a `401 Unauthorized` error.
  version: '1.0'
  contact: {}
servers:
  - url: https://api.unifold.io
    description: Production server
security: []
tags:
  - name: Users
    description: User management endpoints
  - name: Payment Intents
    description: >-
      Payment Intents represent a fixed-amount crypto payment. Create one on
      your server, pass its `client_secret` to your frontend, and Unifold
      handles deposit address generation, cross-chain bridging, and settlement
      tracking.
  - name: Treasury
    description: Treasury account and outbound transfer endpoints
  - name: Onramps
    description: Fiat-to-crypto onramp session management
  - name: Webhooks
    description: Webhook endpoint management
  - name: Direct Executions
    description: Direct execution records for client users
  - name: Deposit Addresses
    description: >-
      Generate or fetch per-user deposit wallets across every supported source
      chain for a single destination (chain + token + recipient). Use this when
      you want to drive the deposit flow yourself instead of through a Payment
      Intent.
  - name: Addresses
    description: >-
      Wallet address utilities — query on-chain token balances for an address
      against the set of tokens Unifold supports as a deposit source.
  - name: Tokens
    description: >-
      Catalog endpoints for the tokens Unifold supports as a deposit source,
      including their per-chain availability and deposit constraints.
paths:
  /v1/direct_executions:
    get:
      tags:
        - Direct Executions
      summary: List direct executions
      description: >-
        Fetches direct execution records for a user identified by their external
        user ID. Supports cursor-based pagination and status filtering.
      operationId: DirectExecutionsController_listDirectExecutions
      parameters:
        - name: external_user_id
          required: true
          in: query
          description: External user ID to query executions for
          example: test_user_123
          schema:
            type: string
        - name: action_type
          required: false
          in: query
          description: Filter by action type
          schema:
            type: string
            enum:
              - deposit
              - withdraw
        - name: status
          required: false
          in: query
          description: Filter by execution status
          schema:
            type: string
            enum:
              - delayed
              - pending
              - succeeded
              - failed
        - name: starting_after
          required: false
          in: query
          description: >-
            Execution ID cursor. Returns executions created after this execution
            (older). Cannot be used with ending_before.
          schema:
            type: string
        - name: ending_before
          required: false
          in: query
          description: >-
            Execution ID cursor. Returns executions created before this
            execution (newer). Cannot be used with starting_after.
          schema:
            type: string
        - name: limit
          required: false
          in: query
          description: Number of items to return per page
          schema:
            type: number
            minimum: 1
            maximum: 100
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Direct executions retrieved successfully
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/ListDirectExecutionsResponse'
              example:
                data:
                  - id: exec_2Qz9K5YX8r5C8jZ1bXZ8kQd7W5M
                    action_type: deposit
                    project_id: project_2Qz9K5YX8r5C8jZ1bXZ8kQd7W5M
                    user_id: user_2Qz9K5YX8r5C8jZ1bXZ8kQd7W5M
                    deposit_wallet_id: wallet_2Qz9K5YX8r5C8jZ1bXZ8kQd7W5M
                    transaction_hash: >-
                      5WreGSrR9Vbo1rZT5oCvctcUdXZG2ZArZB5BrSNC6yJ1r96HBqboBy7Bbo8NdYM6mZ8kSuD7SW7JGQaBkVjh5kh7
                    recipient_address: '0x606C49ca2Fa4982F07016265040F777eD3DA3160'
                    failure_reason: null
                    status: pending
                    source_chain_type: solana
                    source_chain_id: '792703809'
                    source_token_address: EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v
                    destination_chain_type: ethereum
                    destination_chain_id: '1'
                    destination_token_address: '0x2791bca1f2de4661ed88a30c99a7a9449aa84174'
                    source_amount_base_unit: '5000000'
                    source_amount_usd: '5.00'
                    destination_amount_base_unit: '4950000'
                    destination_amount_usd: '4.95'
                    destination_transaction_hashes: null
                    created_at: '2026-03-20T10:30:00.000Z'
                    updated_at: '2026-03-20T10:31:00.000Z'
                    explorer_url: >-
                      https://solscan.io/tx/5WreGSrR9Vbo1rZT5oCvctcUdXZG2ZArZB5BrSNC6yJ1r96HBqboBy7Bbo8NdYM6mZ8kSuD7SW7JGQaBkVjh5kh7
                    destination_explorer_url: null
                    source_token_metadata:
                      icon_url: https://cdn.example.com/public/icons/tokens/svg/usdc.svg
                      icon_urls:
                        - url: >-
                            https://cdn.example.com/public/icons/tokens/svg/usdc.svg
                          format: svg
                      decimals: 6
                    destination_token_metadata:
                      icon_url: https://cdn.example.com/public/icons/tokens/svg/usdc.svg
                      icon_urls:
                        - url: >-
                            https://cdn.example.com/public/icons/tokens/svg/usdc.svg
                          format: svg
                      decimals: 6
                    source_currency: usdc
                    destination_currency: usdc
                    estimated_processing_time: 60
                    deposit_wallet:
                      chain_type: solana
                      address_type: null
                      address: 9WzDXwBbmkg8ZTbNMqUxvQRAyrZzDsGYdLVL9zYtAWWM
                total_count: 1
                has_more: false
        '401':
          description: Missing or invalid secret API key
        '404':
          description: User not found
      security:
        - bearer: []
components:
  schemas:
    ListDirectExecutionsResponse:
      type: object
      properties:
        data:
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/DirectExecutionResponse'
        total_count:
          type: number
          description: Total number of executions matching the query (ignoring pagination)
          example: 42
        has_more:
          type: boolean
          description: Whether there are more results beyond the current page
          example: true
    DirectExecutionResponse:
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          description: Execution ID
          example: exec_2Qz9K5YX8r5C8jZ1bXZ8kQd7W5M
        action_type:
          type: string
          description: Type of execution action
          enum:
            - deposit
            - withdraw
          example: deposit
        project_id:
          type: string
          description: Project ID
          example: project_2Qz9K5YX8r5C8jZ1bXZ8kQd7W5M
        user_id:
          type: string
          nullable: true
          description: User ID
          example: user_2Qz9K5YX8r5C8jZ1bXZ8kQd7W5M
        deposit_wallet_id:
          type: string
          description: Deposit wallet ID
          example: wallet_2Qz9K5YX8r5C8jZ1bXZ8kQd7W5M
        transaction_hash:
          type: string
          nullable: true
          description: Source chain transaction hash
          example: >-
            5WreGSrR9Vbo1rZT5oCvctcUdXZG2ZArZB5BrSNC6yJ1r96HBqboBy7Bbo8NdYM6mZ8kSuD7SW7JGQaBkVjh5kh7
        recipient_address:
          type: string
          description: Recipient address on destination chain
          example: '0x606C49ca2Fa4982F07016265040F777eD3DA3160'
        failure_reason:
          type: string
          nullable: true
          description: Reason for execution failure, if applicable
          example: null
        status:
          type: string
          description: >-
            Current status of the execution. Previously failed executions are
            now returned as delayed.
          enum:
            - delayed
            - pending
            - succeeded
            - failed
          example: pending
        source_chain_type:
          type: string
          description: Source chain type
          example: solana
        source_chain_id:
          type: string
          description: Source chain ID
          example: '792703809'
        source_token_address:
          type: string
          description: Source token contract address
````

# Cancel a payment intent

> Cancels a `default` payment intent. Only possible when the status is `requires_payment`. A payment intent that is already `processing`, `succeeded`, or `canceled` cannot be canceled. **Locked-quote payment intents are not cancelable** — they auto-expire and use the [refund endpoint](/api-reference/payment-intents/refund) for late deposits.

<Warning>
  Cancellation only applies to **default** payment intents in `requires_payment` status. **Locked-quote** payment intents cannot be canceled — they auto-expire when their quote window closes and use the [refund](/api-reference/payment-intents/refund) flow for any late deposits.
</Warning>

A payment intent can only be canceled while its status is `requires_payment` — that is, before any deposit has been received.

Once a deposit arrives and the status moves to `processing`, the payment intent can no longer be canceled because funds are already being bridged to the destination. Payment intents that are already `succeeded`, `canceled`, `expired`, or in any refund state are also not cancelable.

<Note>
  **Default-mode** funds sent to a deposit address are **not refundable** through the API — once a transaction is submitted on-chain it cannot be reversed. **Locked-quote** intents support an explicit refund flow for late deposits via [Refund a payment intent](/api-reference/payment-intents/refund).
</Note>

# Create a payment intent

> Creates a new payment intent that generates deposit wallet addresses. Users can deposit any supported cryptocurrency to these addresses. Deposits are automatically bridged to the recipient on the destination chain. The payment intent is marked as "succeeded" when the destination amount reaches the target.

This endpoint creates a **default-mode** payment intent that accepts deposits on any supported source chain and bridges to the destination at settlement. For a rate-locked alternative with a single source token, see [Create a locked-quote payment intent](/api-reference/payment-intents/create-locked-quote-payment-intent).

<Warning>
  **Deposits are irreversible.** Once a user sends funds to a deposit address, the on-chain transaction cannot be reversed or refunded through the API. A payment intent can only be [canceled](/api-reference/payment-intents/cancel) while its status is `requires_payment` — before any deposit arrives. If you need refundable, rate-locked payments, use the [locked-quote flow](/api-reference/payment-intents/create-locked-quote-payment-intent) instead.
</Warning>

<Note>
  The request fields `destination_amount` and `destination_currency` are the canonical names. The legacy aliases `amount` and `currency` are still accepted for backwards compatibility — prefer the new names in new integrations.
</Note>

# Create a locked quote

> Creates a single-use locked quote that locks an exchange rate for a fixed window.

Creates a single-use locked quote that locks an exchange rate for a fixed window.

<Warning>
  Quotes are single-use and expire \~30 seconds after creation.
</Warning>

# Create a locked-quote payment intent

> Creates a payment intent backed by a previewed locked quote. The quote locks an exchange rate for a fixed window.

Commits a [locked quote](/api-reference/payment-intents/create-locked-quote) into a payment intent. The returned intent has `type: "locked_quote"` and tracks deposits on a single source chain. Once the locked `source_amount` is received, an atomic on-chain transaction settles the destination amount to `recipient_address`.

<Warning>
  The `quote_id` must come from a recent [Create a locked quote](/api-reference/payment-intents/create-locked-quote) call.
</Warning>

<Note>
  v1 only supports **Base USDC** as the destination. The source token is whatever was set on the locked quote.
</Note>


## OpenAPI

````yaml POST /v1/payment_intents/locked_quotes
openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Unifold API
  description: >-
    The Unifold API provides programmatic access to treasury management and
    cross-chain transfer capabilities. Use it to create treasury accounts,
    manage users, and execute outbound transfers across supported blockchains.


    ## Authentication


    The Unifold API uses API keys to authenticate requests. Include your API key
    in the `Authorization` header using the Bearer scheme:


    ```

    Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...

    ```


    You must use your secret API key, which starts with `sk_` (e.g.,
    `sk_live_...` or `sk_test_...`). You can obtain your API key from the
    [Unifold Dashboard](https://dashboard.unifold.io). Keep your secret keys
    secure and never expose them in client-side code.


    All API requests must be made over HTTPS. Requests without authentication
    will fail with a `401 Unauthorized` error.
````

> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.unifold.io/llms.txt

# List payment intents

> Returns payment intents for the project with cursor-based pagination, ordered by creation date descending. Optionally filter by user_id or external_user_id (mutually exclusive), and by status.

## Pagination

This endpoint uses **cursor-based pagination** with payment intent IDs (which are lexicographically sortable). Results are always ordered by creation date descending (newest first).

To paginate forward through results, pass the `id` of the **last item** in the current page as `starting_after`. To paginate backward, pass the `id` of the **first item** as `ending_before`. You cannot use both cursors in the same request.

The `has_more` field in the response indicates whether additional results exist beyond the current page.

<Warning>
  `starting_after` and `ending_before` are mutually exclusive. Providing both will result in a `400` error.
</Warning>

### Example: paginating through all payment intents

```bash theme={null}
# First page
curl https://api.unifold.io/v1/payment_intents?limit=10 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."

# Next page (use the last item's ID from the previous response)
curl https://api.unifold.io/v1/payment_intents?limit=10&starting_after=pi_2Qz8... \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

## Filtering

### By user

You can filter results by user using either `user_id` (Unifold's internal ID) or `external_user_id` (the ID you assigned when creating the user). These two filters are **mutually exclusive** — providing both returns a `400` error.

If the specified user does not exist in your project, the endpoint returns an empty list rather than an error.

```bash theme={null}
# Filter by internal user ID
curl https://api.unifold.io/v1/payment_intents?user_id=user_2Qz9K5YX... \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."

# Filter by your external user ID
curl https://api.unifold.io/v1/payment_intents?external_user_id=my-app-user-42 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

### By status

Use the `status` query parameter to return only payment intents in one or more statuses. Repeat the parameter to filter by multiple values.

| Status             | Applies to   | Description                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------ | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `requires_payment` | both         | Created but no deposit has been received yet.                                                                                        |
| `processing`       | both         | At least one deposit received; waiting for the destination amount to reach the target (or for the atomic payout, for locked quotes). |
| `succeeded`        | both         | Destination amount delivered to the recipient.                                                                                       |
| `canceled`         | both         | Canceled via the API before any deposit arrived.                                                                                     |
| `expired`          | locked-quote | Quote window elapsed before the locked source amount was deposited.                                                                  |
| `awaiting_refund`  | locked-quote | A deposit landed after expiration; merchant must call [refund](/api-reference/payment-intents/refund).                               |
| `refunding`        | locked-quote | Refund job is in progress (intermediate state).                                                                                      |
| `refunded`         | locked-quote | Source-chain refund tx confirmed.                                                                                                    |
| `refund_failed`    | locked-quote | Refund broadcast failed; can be retried with a corrected `refund_address`.                                                           |

```bash theme={null}
# Single status
curl https://api.unifold.io/v1/payment_intents?status=succeeded \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."

# Multiple statuses
curl "https://api.unifold.io/v1/payment_intents?status=requires_payment&status=processing" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

### By type

The `type` query parameter limits results to a single product mode. Defaults to returning both types.

```bash theme={null}
# Locked-quote payment intents only
curl https://api.unifold.io/v1/payment_intents?type=locked_quote \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

<Info>
  Filters can be combined — for example, you can filter by both `user_id` and `status` in the same request.
</Info>

````yaml GET /v1/payment_intents
            - algorand
            - xrpl
            - cardano
            - n1
          example: bitcoin
        source_chain_id:
          type: string
          nullable: true
          description: Source chain ID (locked-quote only)
          example: mainnet
        source_token_address:
          type: string
          nullable: true
          description: >-
            Source token contract address, or `"native"` for the chain's gas
            token. Locked-quote only.
          example: native
        source_token_decimals:
          type: number
          nullable: true
          description: Number of decimals for the source token (locked-quote only)
          example: 8
        transaction_hash:
          type: string
          nullable: true
          description: >-
            On-chain hash of the atomic payout from the payout pool to the
            recipient. Populated for `locked_quote` intents once `succeeded`.
          example: '0x9c84a0c4fbb14a0dac2f4ad7d83b9a2e5cf9e34c8a1d2c3b4a5f6e7d8c9b0a1f'
        settlement_tolerance_percent:
          type: number
          description: >-
            Acceptable underpayment tolerance as a percentage. Always `0` for
            `locked_quote` intents.
          example: 1
        stablecoin_parity:
          type: boolean
          description: >-
            Whether stablecoin deposits were credited 1:1 against
            `destination_amount` instead of using the swap output. Always
            `false` for `locked_quote` intents.
          example: false
        refund_address:
          type: string
          nullable: true
          description: >-
            Refund destination address provided by the merchant via [Refund a
            payment intent](/api-reference/payment-intents/refund). Locked-quote
            only.
          example: bc1q4vxn43l44h30nkluqfxd9eckf45vr2awz38lwa
        refund_amount:
          type: string
          nullable: true
          description: Refund amount in source-token base units, after network fees
          example: '124000'
        refund_amount_usd:
          type: string
          nullable: true
          description: USD value of the refund amount
          example: '49.60'
        refund_transaction_hash:
          type: string
          nullable: true
          description: On-chain hash of the refund transaction
          example: abc123def456...
        refunded_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          nullable: true
          description: When the refund was confirmed on-chain (ISO 8601)
          example: '2026-01-17T02:30:25.935Z'
        failure_reason:
          type: string
          nullable: true
          description: >-
            Human-readable reason for a failure (e.g. a refund broadcast error).
            `null` unless the intent is in a failure-related state.
          example: null
        cancellation_reason:
          type: string
          nullable: true
          description: Reason for cancellation
          example: null
        metadata:
          type: object
          nullable: true
          description: Arbitrary key-value metadata
          additionalProperties:
            type: string
          example:
            order_id: order_123
        description:
          type: string
          nullable: true
          description: Description of the payment intent
          example: Payment for order
        expires_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          nullable: true
          description: Expiration deadline (ISO 8601)
          example: '2026-12-31T23:59:59.000Z'
        expired_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          nullable: true
          description: >-
            Timestamp when the intent transitioned to `expired`. Locked-quote
            only.
          example: null
        canceled_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          nullable: true
          description: Timestamp when the payment intent was canceled
          example: null
        created_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          description: When the payment intent was created
          example: '2026-03-13T12:00:00.000Z'
        updated_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          description: When the payment intent was last updated
          example: '2026-03-13T12:00:00.000Z'
        amount:
          type: string
          deprecated: true
          description: Deprecated alias for `destination_amount`.
          example: '10000000'
        amount_usd:
          type: string
          deprecated: true
          description: Deprecated alias for `destination_amount_usd`.
          example: '10.00'
        amount_received:
          type: string
          deprecated: true
          description: Deprecated alias for `destination_amount_received`.
          example: '0'
        amount_received_usd:
          type: string
          deprecated: true
          description: Deprecated alias for `destination_amount_received_usd`.
          example: '0.00'
        currency:
          type: string
          deprecated: true
          description: Deprecated alias for `destination_currency`.
          example: usdc
      required:
        - id
        - type
        - status
        - client_secret
        - livemode
        - destination_amount
        - destination_amount_usd
        - destination_amount_received
        - destination_amount_received_usd
        - destination_currency
        - destination_network
        - destination_chain_type
        - destination_chain_id
        - destination_token_address
        - destination_token_decimals
        - recipient_address

        - stablecoin_parity
        - created_at
        - updated_at
        - amount
        - amount_usd
        - amount_received
        - amount_received_usd
        - currency
    PaymentIntentDepositAddressDto:
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          description: Unique identifier for the deposit wallet
          example: dw_2Qz9K5YX8r5C8jZ1bXZ8kQd7W5M
        chain_type:
          type: string
          description: Chain type for this deposit address
          enum:
            - ethereum
            - solana
            - bitcoin
            - algorand
            - xrpl
            - cardano
            - n1
          example: ethereum
        address_type:
          type: string
          nullable: true

          example: default

          type: string
````

# Get locked-quote limits

> Returns the minimum and maximum USD-equivalent destination amounts allowed when previewing a locked quote.

Returns the minimum and maximum USD-equivalent destination amounts allowed for a locked quote. Use these bounds to validate user input before calling [Create a locked quote](/api-reference/payment-intents/create-locked-quote).


## OpenAPI

````yaml GET /v1/payment_intents/locked_quotes/limits
openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Unifold API
  description: >-
    The Unifold API provides programmatic access to treasury management and
    cross-chain transfer capabilities. Use it to create treasury accounts,
    manage users, and execute outbound transfers across supported blockchains.


    ## Authentication


    The Unifold API uses API keys to authenticate requests. Include your API key
    in the `Authorization` header using the Bearer scheme:


    ```

    Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...

    ```


    You must use your secret API key, which starts with `sk_` (e.g.,
    `sk_live_...` or `sk_test_...`). You can obtain your API key from the
    [Unifold Dashboard](https://dashboard.unifold.io). Keep your secret keys
    secure and never expose them in client-side code.


    All API requests must be made over HTTPS. Requests without authentication
    will fail with a `401 Unauthorized` error.
  version: '1.0'
  contact: {}
servers:
  - url: https://api.unifold.io
    description: Production server
security: []
tags:
  - name: Users
    description: User management endpoints
  - name: Payment Intents
    description: >-
      Payment Intents represent a fixed-amount crypto payment. Create one on
      your server, pass its `client_secret` to your frontend, and Unifold
      handles deposit address generation, cross-chain bridging, and settlement
      tracking.
  - name: Treasury
    description: Treasury account and outbound transfer endpoints
  - name: Onramps
    description: Fiat-to-crypto onramp session management
  - name: Webhooks
    description: Webhook endpoint management
  - name: Direct Executions
    description: Direct execution records for client users
  - name: Deposit Addresses
    description: >-
      Generate or fetch per-user deposit wallets across every supported source
      chain for a single destination (chain + token + recipient). Use this when
      you want to drive the deposit flow yourself instead of through a Payment
      Intent.
  - name: Addresses
    description: >-
      Wallet address utilities — query on-chain token balances for an address
      against the set of tokens Unifold supports as a deposit source.
  - name: Tokens
    description: >-
      Catalog endpoints for the tokens Unifold supports as a deposit source,
      including their per-chain availability and deposit constraints.
````

# Refund a payment intent

> Initiates a refund for a `locked_quote` payment intent that received a deposit after its quote window expired.

Initiates a refund for a `locked_quote` payment intent that received a deposit after its quote window expired.

<Warning>
  Refunds only apply to **locked-quote** payment intents in `awaiting_refund` or `refund_failed` status. `default` payment intents and any other state return `400`.
</Warning>


## OpenAPI

````yaml POST /v1/payment_intents/{id}/refund
          example: null
        canceled_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          nullable: true
          description: Timestamp when the payment intent was canceled
          example: null
        created_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          description: When the payment intent was created
          example: '2026-03-13T12:00:00.000Z'
        updated_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          description: When the payment intent was last updated
          example: '2026-03-13T12:00:00.000Z'
        amount:
          type: string
          deprecated: true
          description: Deprecated alias for `destination_amount`.
          example: '10000000'
        amount_usd:
          type: string
          deprecated: true
          description: Deprecated alias for `destination_amount_usd`.
          example: '10.00'
        amount_received:
          type: string
          deprecated: true
          description: Deprecated alias for `destination_amount_received`.
          example: '0'
        amount_received_usd:
          type: string
          deprecated: true
          description: Deprecated alias for `destination_amount_received_usd`.
          example: '0.00'
        currency:
          type: string
          deprecated: true
          description: Deprecated alias for `destination_currency`.
          example: usdc
      required:
        - id
        - type
        - status
        - client_secret
        - livemode
        - destination_amount
        - destination_amount_usd
        - destination_amount_received
        - destination_amount_received_usd
        - destination_currency
        - destination_network
        - destination_chain_type
        - destination_chain_id
        - destination_token_address
        - destination_token_decimals
        - recipient_address
        - deposit_addresses
        - settlement_tolerance_percent
        - stablecoin_parity
        - created_at
        - updated_at
        - amount
        - amount_usd
        - amount_received
        - amount_received_usd
        - currency
    PaymentIntentDepositAddressDto:
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          description: Unique identifier for the deposit wallet
          example: dw_2Qz9K5YX8r5C8jZ1bXZ8kQd7W5M

            - ethereum
````

# Create an outbound transfer

> Creates a new outbound transfer from a treasury account. Funds are routed through a deposit address that auto-swaps to the destination. Requires an Idempotency-Key header to prevent duplicate transfers.

<Note>
  For Solana treasury sources, you must explicitly include
  `source.chain_id: "mainnet"` in the request body.
</Note>


## OpenAPI

````yaml POST /v1/treasury/outbound_transfers
openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Unifold API
  description: >-
    The Unifold API provides programmatic access to treasury management and
    cross-chain transfer capabilities. Use it to create treasury accounts,
    manage users, and execute outbound transfers across supported blockchains.


    ## Authentication


    The Unifold API uses API keys to authenticate requests. Include your API key
    in the `Authorization` header using the Bearer scheme:


    ```

    Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...

    ```


    You must use your secret API key, which starts with `sk_` (e.g.,
    `sk_live_...` or `sk_test_...`). You can obtain your API key from the
    [Unifold Dashboard](https://dashboard.unifold.io). Keep your secret keys
    secure and never expose them in client-side code.


    All API requests must be made over HTTPS. Requests without authentication
    will fail with a `401 Unauthorized` error.
  version: '1.0'
  contact: {}
servers:
  - url: https://api.unifold.io
    description: Production server
security: []
tags:
  - name: Users
    description: User management endpoints
  - name: Payment Intents
    description: >-
      Payment Intents represent a fixed-amount crypto payment. Create one on
      your server, pass its `client_secret` to your frontend, and Unifold
      handles deposit address generation, cross-chain bridging, and settlement
      tracking.
  - name: Treasury
    description: Treasury account and outbound transfer endpoints
  - name: Onramps
    description: Fiat-to-crypto onramp session management
  - name: Webhooks
    description: Webhook endpoint management
  - name: Direct Executions
    description: Direct execution records for client users
  - name: Deposit Addresses
    description: >-
      Generate or fetch per-user deposit wallets across every supported source
      chain for a single destination (chain + token + recipient). Use this when
      you want to drive the deposit flow yourself instead of through a Payment
      Intent.
  - name: Addresses
    description: >-
      Wallet address utilities — query on-chain token balances for an address
      against the set of tokens Unifold supports as a deposit source.
  - name: Tokens
    description: >-
      Catalog endpoints for the tokens Unifold supports as a deposit source,
      including their per-chain availability and deposit constraints.
paths:
  /v1/treasury/outbound_transfers:
    post:
      tags:
        - Treasury
      summary: Create an outbound transfer
      description: >-
        Creates a new outbound transfer from a treasury account. Funds are
        routed through a deposit address that auto-swaps to the destination.
        Requires an Idempotency-Key header to prevent duplicate transfers.
      operationId: OutboundTransfersController_createOutboundTransfer
      parameters:
        - name: idempotency-key
          required: true
          in: header
          description: Unique key to prevent duplicate transfers
          schema:
            type: string
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/CreateOutboundTransferDto'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Existing transfer returned (idempotent response)
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/OutboundTransferResponseDto'
        '201':
          description: Outbound transfer created successfully
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/OutboundTransferResponseDto'
        '400':
          description: Invalid request or missing Idempotency-Key header
        '404':
          description: Treasury account not found
      security:
        - bearer: []
components:
  schemas:
    CreateOutboundTransferDto:
      type: object
      properties:
        source:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/OutboundTransferSourceDto'
          description: Source of the transfer (treasury account)
        external_user_id:
          type: string
          description: External user ID to associate with this transfer
          example: new_user_123
        destination:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/OutboundTransferDestinationDto'
          description: Destination of the transfer
        amount:
          type: string
          description: Amount to send in base units (e.g., 4000000 for 4 USDC)
          example: '4000000'
      required:
        - source
        - external_user_id
        - destination
        - amount
    OutboundTransferResponseDto:
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          description: Unique identifier for the outbound transfer
          example: obt_38MUvgtKalr2mPtACLBdpx011JC
        project_id:
          type: string
          description: Project ID this transfer belongs to
          example: project_36CWZZpfLXajgfhYmnrlGLRhzNb
        user_id:
          type: string
          description: User ID associated with this transfer
          example: user_38MUvhtrMSCSyjA6yfcvttjr3CC
        user:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/OutboundTransferUserResponseDto'
          description: User details associated with this transfer
        deposit_wallet_address:
          type: string
          description: Deposit address (intermediate EOA)
          example: '0x6a755a72a46aba940f1460f0714d5a052f22d52c'
        status:
          type: string
          description: Current status of the transfer
          example: completed
          enum:
            - pending
            - processing
            - completed
            - failed
        source:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/OutboundTransferSourceResponseDto'
          description: Source details (treasury account and amount)
        destination:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/OutboundTransferDestinationResponseDto'
          description: Destination details (recipient address and chain)
        idempotency_key:
          type: string
          description: Idempotency key from request header
          example: test5
        failure_reason:
          type:
            - string
            - 'null'
          description: Error message when status is failed
          example: null
        created_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          description: When the transfer was created
          example: '2026-01-17T00:19:25.935Z'
        updated_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          description: When the transfer was last updated
          example: '2026-01-17T00:19:58.645Z'
        execution:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/OutboundTransferExecutionResponseDto'
          description: Execution details (present when transfer has been executed)
      required:
        - id
        - project_id
        - user_id
        - user
        - deposit_wallet_address
        - status
        - source
        - destination
        - idempotency_key
        - created_at
        - updated_at
    OutboundTransferSourceDto:
      type: object
      properties:
        treasury_account_id:
          type: string
          description: Treasury account ID to send from
          example: ta_380Q5HOf4oMuSacK7ZkPQ65Vc15
        currency:
          type: string
          description: Source currency (currently only USDC supported)
          example: usdc
        chain_id:
          type: string
          description: >-
            Source chain ID. Use `137` for Polygon, `8453` for Base, or
            `mainnet` for Solana. For Solana treasury sources, `mainnet` must be
            passed explicitly.
          enum:
            - '137'
            - '8453'
            - mainnet
          example: '137'
      required:
        - treasury_account_id
        - currency
        - chain_id
    OutboundTransferDestinationDto:
      type: object
      properties:
        recipient_address:
          type: string
          description: Final recipient address
          example: '0x606C49ca2Fa4982F07016265040F777eD3DA3160'
        chain_type:
          type: string
          description: Chain type (e.g., ethereum, solana)
          example: ethereum
        chain_id:
          type: string
          description: Chain ID
          example: '137'
        token_address:
          type: string
          description: Token contract address
          example: '0x2791bca1f2de4661ed88a30c99a7a9449aa84174'
      required:
        - recipient_address
        - chain_type
        - chain_id
        - token_address
    OutboundTransferUserResponseDto:
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          description: User ID
          example: user_38MUvhtrMSCSyjA6yfcvttjr3CC
        external_user_id:
          type: string
          description: External user ID
          example: new_user_123
        created_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          description: User creation timestamp
          example: '2026-01-17T00:19:25.375Z'
      required:
        - id
        - external_user_id
        - created_at
    OutboundTransferSourceResponseDto:
      type: object
      properties:
        treasury_account_id:
          type: string
          description: Treasury account ID funds were sent from
          example: ta_380Q5HOf4oMuSacK7ZkPQ65Vc15
        amount:
          type: string
          description: Amount sent in base units
          example: '4000000'
        transaction_hash:
          type:
            - string
            - 'null'
          description: >-
            Transaction hash of treasury to deposit address transfer (set after
            execution)
          example: '0x1baaa77f332144ae62826aa347199aa6ef5bfc1fd637411496d4aaa3400172c8'
      required:
        - treasury_account_id
        - amount
    OutboundTransferDestinationResponseDto:
      type: object
      properties:
        recipient_address:
          type: string
          description: Final recipient address
          example: '0x606C49ca2Fa4982F07016265040F777eD3DA3160'
        chain_type:
          type: string
          description: Destination chain type
          example: ethereum
        chain_id:
          type: string
          description: Destination chain ID
          example: '137'
        token_address:
          type: string
          description: Destination token address
          example: '0x2791bca1f2de4661ed88a30c99a7a9449aa84174'
      required:
        - recipient_address
        - chain_type
        - chain_id
        - token_address
    OutboundTransferExecutionResponseDto:
      type: object
      properties:
        execution_id:
          type: string

        status:
          type: string
          description: Execution status
          example: succeeded
          enum:
            - pending
            - processing
            - succeeded
            - failed
        transaction_hash:
          type:
            - string
            - 'null'
          description: Primary transaction hash
          example: '0x7ccf2c86a8e8fcd26c18533032a56dcd0e10b9d8da1507e9a5311bd2b2125c56'
        destination_transaction_hashes:
          type: array
          description: List of destination transaction hashes
          items:
            type: string
          example:
            - '0x7ccf2c86a8e8fcd26c18533032a56dcd0e10b9d8da1507e9a5311bd2b2125c56'
        created_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          description: Execution creation timestamp
          example: '2026-01-17T00:19:48.397Z'
        updated_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          description: Execution last update timestamp
          example: '2026-01-17T00:19:48.682Z'
      required:
        - execution_id
        - status
        - created_at
        - updated_at

      type: http
````

````yaml GET /v1/treasury/outbound_transfers/{id}
          type: string
          description: Execution status
          example: succeeded
          enum:
            - pending
            - processing
            - succeeded
            - failed
        transaction_hash:
          type:
            - string
            - 'null'
          description: Primary transaction hash
          example: '0x7ccf2c86a8e8fcd26c18533032a56dcd0e10b9d8da1507e9a5311bd2b2125c56'
        destination_transaction_hashes:
          type: array
          description: List of destination transaction hashes
          items:
            type: string
          example:
            - '0x7ccf2c86a8e8fcd26c18533032a56dcd0e10b9d8da1507e9a5311bd2b2125c56'
        created_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          description: Execution creation timestamp
          example: '2026-01-17T00:19:48.397Z'
        updated_at:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          description: Execution last update timestamp
          example: '2026-01-17T00:19:48.682Z'
      required:
        - execution_id
        - status
        - created_at
        - updated_at
  securitySchemes:
    bearer:
      type: http
      scheme: bearer
      bearerFormat: sk_api_key
      description: >-
        API key authentication using the Authorization header. Use your secret
        API key (starts with `sk_`): `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...`
      x-default: sk_api_key
````

# Deposit Modal

> Execute an arbitrary contract call on the destination chain. Unifold sweeps the full deposited balance into your proxy contract, which then processes the funds.

## Overview

Call Execution turns a Unifold deposit into an **on-chain action**, not just a transfer — Unifold delivers the funds, then runs the contract calls you provide (mint, stake, supply to a pool, top up a game balance, anything callable).

This flow is for **sweep-based deposits**, where the SDK deposit flow's **final amount is variable**. Since you can't know the exact delivered amount up front, your contract reads the allowance and live balance at execution time.

<Note>
  Call Execution is currently supported on **Web only** (the `@unifold/connect-react` SDK). Mobile SDK support is coming next.
</Note>

***

## Supported chains

Call Execution is available on the following destination chains:

| Chain                                                                                                                                                                                               | Chain Type | Chain ID |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | -------- |
| <img src="/_mintlify/image/unifold/images/chains/ethereum.svg" alt="Ethereum" style={{ width: '16px', height: '16px', display: 'inline', verticalAlign: 'middle', marginRight: '6px' }} /> Ethereum | `ethereum` | `1`      |
| <img src="/_mintlify/image/unifold/images/chains/arbitrum.svg" alt="Arbitrum" style={{ width: '16px', height: '16px', display: 'inline', verticalAlign: 'middle', marginRight: '6px' }} /> Arbitrum | `ethereum` | `42161`  |
| <img src="/_mintlify/image/unifold/images/chains/base.svg" alt="Base" style={{ width: '16px', height: '16px', display: 'inline', verticalAlign: 'middle', marginRight: '6px' }} /> Base             | `ethereum` | `8453`   |
| <img src="/_mintlify/image/unifold/images/chains/megaeth.svg" alt="MegaETH" style={{ width: '16px', height: '16px', display: 'inline', verticalAlign: 'middle', marginRight: '6px' }} /> MegaETH    | `ethereum` | `4326`   |

Users can still **deposit from any supported source chain and token** — the chains above are where the call gets *executed*.

### Want to support more chains?

Contact [support@unifold.io](mailto:support@unifold.io) and we'll work with you to enable Call Execution on additional chains.

***

## How it works

1. The user deposits any token from any supported chain through the SDK.
2. Unifold bridges and swaps to your **destination token** on the destination chain.
3. The delivered token lands at the **intent address**.
4. Unifold grants your contract an **approval** for the delivered amount, then runs your `contractCalls` **in the order you provided**.
5. Your contract reads the live allowance/balance and pulls it in (the "sweep"), then processes the deposit.

Because the delivered amount is variable, your contract calls can't hardcode it. Your contract must read the amount available at execution time.

***

## Contract requirements

The contract name and the function name don't matter — Unifold just calls whatever you point it at. What matters is the pattern inside the function:

1. Read the **allowance** `msg.sender` (the intent address) granted your contract.
2. Read the **balance** of `msg.sender` — this is the delivered amount you'll pull.
3. Make sure the **allowance covers the balance**, then `transferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount)`.
4. Do whatever you want with the funds now held by your contract.

Example:

```solidity theme={null}
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
pragma solidity ^0.8.25;

import {IERC20} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol";

contract DepositSweepReceiver {
    function execute(address token, address recipient) external {
        IERC20 erc20 = IERC20(token);

        uint256 allowance = erc20.allowance(msg.sender, address(this));
        uint256 amount = erc20.balanceOf(msg.sender);

        require(amount > 0, "no balance");
        require(allowance >= amount, "allowance too low");
        require(erc20.transferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount), "transfer failed");

        // Funds are now in this contract — do anything you want with `amount`.
        _executeDeposit(token, amount, recipient);
    }
}
```

<Note>
  Your calls run as a **batch transaction**, so expect every call to share the **same `msg.sender`**. The order of the contract calls matters. Make the **first call** your sweep function that reads the allowance and `transferFrom`s the balance (e.g. the `execute()` example shown above), so the balance is pulled into your contract before any later calls run.
</Note>

<Warning>
  We don't suggest hardcoding the deposit amount in the contract calls. The destination amount of the deposit is not deterministic due to slippage and fees. We suggest always pulling the live balance at execution time.
</Warning>

***

## Example

You attach an optional `contractCalls` param to the SDK deposit, typed as `EvmContractCall[]` and executed **in order** as a batch. Each entry is `{ to, data, value? }` — `value` is optional and defaults to `"0"`. The token approval to your contract is handled by Unifold before your calls run, so your first call just needs to sweep.

```typescript theme={null}
export interface EvmContractCall {
  to: `0x${string}`;
  data: `0x${string}`;
  value?: string; // optional, defaults to "0"
}
```

**Encode the contract call** for your contract's `execute` function:

```typescript theme={null}
import { encodeFunctionData } from "viem";

const executeData = encodeFunctionData({
  abi: [
    {
      name: "execute",
      type: "function",
      stateMutability: "nonpayable",
      inputs: [
        { name: "token", type: "address" },
        { name: "recipient", type: "address" },
      ],
      outputs: [],
    },
  ],
  functionName: "execute",
  args: [tokenAddress, userRecipientAddress],
});
```

**Pass the calls into the deposit:**

```tsx theme={null}
import { useUnifold } from '@unifold/connect-react';

function DepositButton() {
  const { beginDeposit } = useUnifold();

  const handleDeposit = async () => {
    const result = await beginDeposit({
      externalUserId: 'user_abc123',

      destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
      destinationChainId: '8453', // Base
      destinationTokenAddress: USDC_BASE,
      destinationTokenSymbol: 'USDC',

      recipientAddress: recipientAddress,
      contractCalls: [
        {
          to: <your contract>,
          data: executeData,
          value: '0',
        },
      ],
    });

    console.log('Execution complete:', result.executionId);
  };

  return <button onClick={handleDeposit}>Deposit</button>;
}
```

***

## Error handling

Call Execution is **fund-safe by design**.

* If **any call in the sequence reverts**, the delivered funds are **not lost** — they remain held at the **intent address** for that deposit.
* Unifold **continues to retry** the execution, so transient failures (e.g. a temporarily paused contract, a flaky dependency) can recover automatically.

***

# Functions

> Type reference for beginCheckout(), closeCheckout(), and related interfaces

## beginCheckout(config)

Launches the checkout modal with the specified configuration. Returns a Promise that resolves when the payment succeeds or rejects when the user cancels or an error occurs.

```typescript theme={null}
const result = await beginCheckout(config);
```

### CheckoutConfig

<ParamField path="clientSecret" type="string" required>
  The `client_secret` from a Payment Intent created on your server. This identifies the payment and authorizes the frontend to display it. Format: `pi_..._secret_...`
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onSuccess" type="(data: CheckoutResult) => void">
  Callback fired immediately when the payment succeeds. Useful for analytics, toasts, or updating local state. The Promise also resolves with the same data.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onError" type="(error: CheckoutError) => void">
  Callback fired immediately when an error occurs. The Promise also rejects with the same error.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onClose" type="() => void">
  Callback fired when the user dismisses the checkout dialog (X button, Escape key, or overlay click). Useful for re-enabling UI or tracking abandonment.
</ParamField>

### Returns

Returns a `Promise<CheckoutResult>` that:

* **Resolves** when the payment succeeds
* **Rejects** with a `CheckoutError` when an error occurs or the user cancels

***

## closeCheckout()

Programmatically closes the checkout modal.

```typescript theme={null}
closeCheckout();
```

Calling `closeCheckout()` will:

1. Fire the `onClose` callback (if provided)
2. Reject the Promise with code `CHECKOUT_CANCELLED`
3. Close the modal

***

## CheckoutResult

Returned when the payment succeeds (via Promise resolution and `onSuccess` callback).

```typescript theme={null}
interface CheckoutResult {
  paymentIntentId: string;
  status: string;
}
```

<ResponseField name="paymentIntentId" type="string">
  The ID of the Payment Intent that was fulfilled (e.g. `"pi_abc123"`).
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="status" type="string">
  The payment status. Possible values:

  * `"succeeded"` — Full payment confirmed on-chain
  * `"processing"` — Payment sent via browser wallet, awaiting on-chain confirmation
</ResponseField>

***

## CheckoutError

Returned when the checkout fails or is cancelled (via Promise rejection and `onError` callback).

```typescript theme={null}
interface CheckoutError {
  message: string;
  error?: unknown;
  code?: string;
}
```

<ResponseField name="message" type="string">
  Human-readable error description.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="error" type="unknown">
  The original underlying error, if available.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="code" type="string">
  Machine-readable error code for programmatic handling. See [Error Codes](/developer/checkout/overview#error-codes).
</ResponseField>

***

## PaymentIntent

The server-side Payment Intent object returned by the [Payment Intents API](/api-reference/payment-intents/create). The type is available as a re-export from the SDK packages.

```typescript theme={null}
interface PaymentIntent {
  id: string;
  user_id: string | null;
  amount: string;
  amount_usd: string;
  amount_received: string;
  amount_received_usd: string;
  currency: string;
  status: string;
  client_secret: string;
  destination_network: string | null;
  destination_chain_type: ChainType;
  destination_chain_id: string;
  destination_token_address: string;
  recipient_address: string;
  destination_token_decimals: number;
  deposit_addresses: PaymentIntentDepositAddress[];
  metadata: Record<string, string> | null;
  description: string | null;
  livemode: boolean;
  settlement_tolerance_percent: number;
  canceled_at: string | null;
  cancellation_reason: string | null;
  expires_at: string | null;
  created_at: string;
  updated_at: string;
}

interface PaymentIntentDepositAddress {
  id: string;
  chain_type: ChainType;
  address_type: string | null;
  address: string;
}
```

***

## Handling errors

```typescript theme={null}
function handleError(error: CheckoutError) {
  switch (error.code) {
    case 'CHECKOUT_CANCELLED':
      // User closed the modal — no action needed
      return;

    case 'CHECKOUT_SUPERSEDED':
      // A new checkout replaced the previous one
      break;

    default:
      showErrorMessage(error.message);
  }
}
```

***

## Usage patterns

### Promise pattern (async/await)

Best when your checkout handler needs to know the final outcome.

```typescript theme={null}
const handleCheckout = async () => {
  try {
    const result = await beginCheckout({ clientSecret });
    showConfirmation(result.paymentIntentId);
  } catch (error) {
    if (error.code === 'CHECKOUT_CANCELLED') return;
    showError(error.message);
  }
};
```

### Callback pattern

Best when you want to react to events as they happen without awaiting the Promise.

```typescript theme={null}
beginCheckout({
  clientSecret,
  onSuccess: (data) => {
    showConfirmation(data.paymentIntentId);
  },
  onError: (error) => {
    showError(error.message);
  },
  onClose: () => {
    reEnableCheckoutButton();
  },
});
```

### Hybrid pattern

Use both callbacks (for immediate side effects) and the Promise (for flow control).

```typescript theme={null}
try {
  const result = await beginCheckout({
    clientSecret,
    onSuccess: (data) => {
      analytics.track('checkout_success', { id: data.paymentIntentId });
    },
    onError: (error) => {
      analytics.track('checkout_error', { code: error.code });
    },
    onClose: () => {
      analytics.track('checkout_dismissed');
    },
  });

  navigateTo(`/order/confirmed?pi=${result.paymentIntentId}`);
} catch (error) {
  // Handle or ignore
}
```
