# Stripe

> Enable fiat-to-crypto on-ramps via Stripe Crypto Onramp

Configure Stripe Onramp to allow your users to purchase crypto with credit cards, debit cards, and Apple Pay directly within your application using Stripe's payment infrastructure and Stripe Link for fast checkout.

## Overview

Stripe is available as an onramp provider through two integration modes:

| Mode              | Experience                                                          | API Keys Required | Setup                                                                                                          |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | :---------------: | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Redirect flow** | Users are redirected to Stripe's hosted UI to complete the purchase |         No        | Available out of the box as a [built-in provider](/developer/integrations/onramps/overview#platform-providers) |
| **Embedded flow** | White-label, native in-app experience embedded directly in your app |        Yes        | Requires your own Stripe API credentials (configured below)                                                    |

<Info>
  The **redirect flow** works immediately with no configuration — Stripe is included as a built-in platform provider. This page covers the **embedded (headless) flow**, which gives you a fully branded in-app experience using the Stripe React Native SDK.
</Info>

<Note>
  **Platform support.** The embedded (headless) Stripe onramp is available on both **React Native / Expo** (native `@stripe/stripe-react-native` SDK) and **web** (`@unifold/connect-react`), where it is exposed as **Pay with Link** using the **`@stripe/crypto`** browser SDK. Both render the flow inline — no redirect. Select the **React (web)** tab in [Step 3](#step-3-integrate-in-your-app) below for the web peer dependencies and config.
</Note>

The embedded Stripe Onramp provides a native, in-app crypto purchasing experience with built-in KYC verification, Stripe Link for returning users, and support for Apple Pay. By configuring your own Stripe credentials, you get:

* **Bring your own Stripe account** — Use your own merchant pricing and payouts
* **Native mobile experience** — Full in-app flow via the Stripe React Native SDK (no redirects)
* **Stripe Link** — Returning users auto-fill their details for faster checkout
* **Apple Pay** — One-tap purchases on iOS devices

## Prerequisites

Before you begin, ensure you have:

* A Unifold account with Dashboard access
* A project created in your account
* A [Stripe](https://dashboard.stripe.com) account with Crypto Onramp enabled

<Note>
  Because Crypto Onramp is in **Private Preview**, two parts of the embedded (headless) setup are handled **by the Stripe team during onboarding** — they are not self-serve in the Stripe Dashboard:

  1. **Apple Pay domain whitelisting** — for the web (Pay with Link) flow, you send the Stripe team the domains that render the deposit modal and **they whitelist them**. See [Set up Apple Pay](#step-1-get-stripe-api-credentials).
  2. **Link OAuth credentials** — the Stripe team **provides you** with your Link OAuth client ID + secret (they aren't visible in your Dashboard). See [Get your Link OAuth credentials](#step-1-get-stripe-api-credentials).

  You then enter the OAuth credentials in the Unifold Dashboard in [Step 2](#step-2-configure-stripe-in-unifold).
</Note>

<Info>
  Stripe Crypto Onramp is currently in **Private Preview**. As a Stripe partner, **Unifold can fast-track your approval and unlock discounted processing fees**. Follow [Request Crypto Onramp access](#request-crypto-onramp-access) below, then [reach out to us](mailto:hello@unifold.io) and we'll help you get set up.
</Info>

## Request Crypto Onramp access

Because Crypto Onramp is in Private Preview, your Stripe account must be approved for the product before you can use the embedded (headless) flow. Unifold can fast-track this — complete the two steps below.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Submit your Stripe Crypto Onramp application">
    If you don't already have a Stripe account, [create one](https://dashboard.stripe.com/register). Then follow Stripe's guide to apply for Crypto Onramp:

    * [Submit your application](https://docs.stripe.com/crypto/onramp#submit-your-application) — Stripe's step-by-step instructions for requesting access to Crypto Onramp.
    * [Embedded onramp overview → Features](https://docs.stripe.com/crypto/onramp/embedded-overview#features) — details on the embedded (headless) experience Unifold integrates with, so you know what to expect.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Share your Stripe account ID with Unifold">
    So we can fast-track your KYB (Know Your Business) review and connect your account directly with the Stripe team, send us your **Stripe account ID** at [hello@unifold.io](mailto:hello@unifold.io).

    Your account ID is the merchant account identifier that starts with **`acct_`**. The easiest way to find it: log in to the [Stripe Dashboard](https://dashboard.stripe.com) and look at the URL — it appears in the path.

    ```text theme={null}
    https://dashboard.stripe.com/acct_1SqMxQPvQEGgglAj
                                  └──────┬──────────┘
                                    your account ID
    ```

    <Tip>
      You can also find it under **Settings → Business → Account details** in the Stripe Dashboard. It always begins with `acct_`.
    </Tip>

    Once we have your account ID, Unifold submits it to the Stripe team to fast-track KYB and connect you directly — no waiting in the general queue.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Step 1: Get Stripe API Credentials

You'll need four credentials from Stripe: your publishable key, secret key, and a Link OAuth client ID and secret.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Get your Stripe API keys">
    Log in to the [Stripe Dashboard](https://dashboard.stripe.com/apikeys) and navigate to **Developers → API keys**.

    Copy your **Publishable key** (`pk_live_...` or `pk_test_...`) and **Secret key** (`sk_live_...` or `sk_test_...`).

    <Warning>
      Use **test keys** (`pk_test_...` / `sk_test_...`) during development and switch to **live keys** for production. Never expose your secret key in client-side code.
    </Warning>
  </Step>

  <Step title="Get your Link OAuth credentials">
    Stripe Onramp uses [Stripe Link](https://stripe.com/link) for user authentication and returning-user flows. You need a **Link OAuth Client ID** and **Client Secret**.

    During Private Preview these credentials are **not self-serve in the Dashboard** — the **Stripe team provides them to you** as part of Crypto Onramp onboarding. If you don't have them yet, ask your Stripe contact (or [reach out to us](mailto:hello@unifold.io) and we'll coordinate with Stripe on your behalf).

    | Credential              | Description                       |
    | ----------------------- | --------------------------------- |
    | **OAuth Client ID**     | Your Link OAuth client identifier |
    | **OAuth Client Secret** | Your Link OAuth client secret     |
  </Step>

  <Step title="Set up Apple Pay (optional)">
    Apple Pay setup differs by platform, because the embedded (headless) flow runs on both **web** (Pay with Link) and **React Native / iOS**. Configure whichever platforms you ship.

    **Web (Pay with Link) — Stripe whitelists your domains**

    Because the web flow renders Apple Pay inline (no redirect to a Stripe-hosted page), **every domain** that shows the deposit modal must be whitelisted for Apple Pay. During Private Preview this is **not self-serve** — the **Stripe team manually whitelists the domains for you**:

    1. Make a list of every domain that renders Pay with Link (e.g. `app.yourcompany.com`) — including staging and local tunneling domains you test on
    2. Send the list to your Stripe contact (or to us at [hello@unifold.io](mailto:hello@unifold.io) and we'll relay it to Stripe)
    3. Stripe adds the domains and completes verification on their side

    <Warning>
      Apple Pay will silently **not appear** on the web until the Stripe team has whitelisted that exact domain. Submit **each** environment's domain (production, staging, preview) — wildcards are not supported, so add new domains before you launch on them.
    </Warning>

    **React Native / iOS — register a merchant ID**

    1. Navigate to **Settings → Payments → Apple Pay** in the Stripe Dashboard
    2. Register your Apple Merchant ID (e.g. `merchant.com.yourapp`)
    3. Complete Apple's domain verification process

    You'll enter this merchant ID in the Unifold Dashboard in the next step.

    <Info>
      Apple Pay is only available on Apple devices and Safari. If you don't configure it, the onramp flow still works with card payments and Stripe Link.
    </Info>
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Step 2: Configure Stripe in Unifold

<Steps>
  <Step title="Navigate to Integrations">
    From the Unifold Dashboard, click **Integrations** in the left sidebar, then select the **Onramps** tab.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Enable Stripe">
    Locate the Stripe integration and toggle it on. The configuration panel will expand automatically.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Enter API Credentials">
    Fill in your Stripe credentials:

    | Field                   | Required | Description                                                      |
    | ----------------------- | :------: | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
    | **Publishable Key**     |     ✅    | Your Stripe publishable key (`pk_live_...` or `pk_test_...`)     |
    | **Secret Key**          |     ✅    | Your Stripe secret key (`sk_live_...` or `sk_test_...`)          |
    | **OAuth Client ID**     |     ✅    | Your Link OAuth client identifier                                |
    | **OAuth Client Secret** |     ✅    | Your Link OAuth client secret                                    |
    | **Apple Merchant ID**   |     —    | Your Apple Pay merchant identifier (e.g. `merchant.com.yourapp`) |

    <Warning>
      The **Secret Key** and **OAuth Client Secret** are sensitive. They are encrypted at rest and masked in the Dashboard after saving. Unifold never exposes them in client-side code — they are only used for server-to-server communication.
    </Warning>
  </Step>

  <Step title="Save Changes">
    Click **Save changes** to apply your configuration. Unifold will store your credentials securely.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Step 3: Integrate in Your App

Integrate the Stripe Onramp with the Unifold SDK. The dashboard configuration in Steps 1–2 applies to both platforms — pick the tab that matches your app.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="React (web)" id="react-web">
    On the web, Stripe onramp is exposed as **Pay with Link** — the same headless flow as React Native. Card, Apple Pay / Google Pay, Stripe Link, and KYC all happen **inside the deposit modal, without leaving your page** (powered by Stripe Crypto Onramp) — there is **no redirect to a Stripe-hosted page**. You enable it on `UnifoldProvider`, and it appears as a **Pay with Link** option in the deposit menu opened by `beginDeposit`.

    <img src="/_mintlify/image/unifold/images/integrations/onramps/stripe-pay-with-link.png" alt="Pay with Link option in the web deposit modal" style={{ maxWidth: '420px', borderRadius: '18px', border: '1px solid #3a3a3a' }} />

    <Warning>
      **Stripe Crypto Onramp is required.** Your Stripe account must have the **Crypto Onramp** product enabled (it is in [Private Preview](https://docs.stripe.com/crypto/onramp/embedded-overview) — Unifold's Stripe partnership can fast-track approval and discounted fees; see [Prerequisites](#prerequisites)). The web flow reuses the credentials you saved in [Step 2](#step-2-configure-stripe-in-unifold); you never handle Stripe secret keys in the browser.
    </Warning>

    <Warning>
      **Apple Pay on the web requires domain whitelisting by Stripe.** For Apple Pay to appear in the deposit modal, every domain that renders Pay with Link must be whitelisted — during Private Preview the **Stripe team does this for you** once you send them your domains. See [Set up Apple Pay](#step-1-get-stripe-api-credentials). Card and Stripe Link still work without it.
    </Warning>

    ### Install peer dependencies

    Pay with Link loads Stripe's crypto onramp directly in the browser, so your web app must install **`@stripe/crypto`** alongside the other `@unifold/connect-react` peers:

    <CodeGroup>
      ```bash npm theme={null}
      npm install @unifold/connect-react @stripe/crypto@1.1.1 @solana/web3.js
      ```

      ```bash yarn theme={null}
      yarn add @unifold/connect-react @stripe/crypto@1.1.1 @solana/web3.js
      ```

      ```bash pnpm theme={null}
      pnpm add @unifold/connect-react @stripe/crypto@1.1.1 @solana/web3.js
      ```
    </CodeGroup>

    | Package           | Version   | Notes                                                               |
    | ----------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    | `@stripe/crypto`  | `1.1.1`   | Required for Pay with Link. Powers the headless Stripe onramp flow. |
    | `@solana/web3.js` | `^1.87.0` | Required peer used for Solana destinations                          |

    <Info>
      `@tanstack/react-query` is bundled by `@unifold/connect-react`. If your app already uses React Query, pass your own client via the `queryClient` prop on `UnifoldProvider` so Unifold shares your cache instead of creating a second client.
    </Info>

    Import the stylesheet once (e.g. in your app entry) so the deposit UI renders correctly:

    ```tsx theme={null}
    import '@unifold/connect-react/styles.css';
    ```

    ### Enable Pay with Link

    Set **`enablePayWithStripeLink: true`** on `UnifoldProvider`'s **`config`** to show **Pay with Link** in the deposit menu:

    ```tsx theme={null}
    import { UnifoldProvider } from '@unifold/connect-react';
    import '@unifold/connect-react/styles.css';

    <UnifoldProvider
      publishableKey="pk_test_your_key"
      config={{
        enablePayWithStripeLink: true, // shows "Pay with Link" in the deposit menu
      }}
    >
      {children}
    </UnifoldProvider>;
    ```

    | `config` field            | Type      | Default | Description                                                                  |
    | ------------------------- | --------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    | `enablePayWithStripeLink` | `boolean` | `false` | Show the **Pay with Link** headless Stripe onramp option in the deposit menu |

    ### Launch the flow

    Open the deposit menu with `beginDeposit`. Pass the signed-in user's email via **`user.email`** to pre-fill and auto-submit Stripe Link's email step:

    ```tsx theme={null}
    import { useUnifold } from '@unifold/connect-react';

    function BuyButton() {
      const { beginDeposit } = useUnifold();

      return (
        <button
          onClick={() =>
            beginDeposit({
              externalUserId: user.id,
              recipientAddress: user.walletAddress,
              destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
              destinationChainId: '8453',
              destinationTokenAddress: '0x…',
              destinationTokenSymbol: 'USDC',
              user: { email: user.email }, // pre-fills the Stripe Link email step
              onSuccess: (r) => console.log('Deposit complete', r.executionId),
              onError: (e) => console.error(e),
            })
          }
        >
          Buy Crypto
        </button>
      );
    }
    ```

    When the user taps **Pay with Link**, the whole flow (verification → amount → payment → confirmation) runs inside the deposit modal on your page — the same experience as the React Native tab, with no redirect.
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="React Native (mobile)">
    Once your Stripe credentials are saved in the Unifold Dashboard, Stripe Onramp is exposed as **Pay with Link** in the deposit menu. Enable it with **`config.enableStripeLink: true`** on `UnifoldProvider`, then open the flow with `beginDeposit` — there is no separate component to render.

    ```tsx theme={null}
    import { UnifoldProvider, useUnifold } from '@unifold/connect-react-native';

    // 1. Enable Pay with Link on the provider
    <UnifoldProvider
      publishableKey="pk_live_your_key"
      config={{ enableStripeLink: true }}
    >
      <RootNavigator />
    </UnifoldProvider>;

    // 2. Open the deposit menu — Pay with Link runs inline
    function BuyButton() {
      const { beginDeposit } = useUnifold();

      return (
        <Button
          title="Buy Crypto"
          onPress={() =>
            beginDeposit({
              externalUserId: user.id,
              recipientAddress: user.walletAddress,
              user: { email: user.email }, // pre-fills the Stripe Link email step
              onSuccess: (r) => console.log('Deposit complete', r.executionId),
            })
          }
        />
      );
    }
    ```

    When the user taps **Pay with Link**, the SDK automatically:

    1. Fetches the Stripe publishable key **and Apple Pay merchant identifier** from Unifold using your Unifold API key (both configured on your Unifold Dashboard — you don't pass them in code)
    2. Initializes the Stripe native SDK
    3. Renders the full onramp flow (verification → amount → payment → confirmation) inline in the deposit menu

    <Info>
      Your Unifold publishable key (`pk_live_...` or `pk_test_...`) identifies your project. The SDK fetches the Stripe publishable key from the Unifold API — you never hardcode Stripe keys in your app.
    </Info>

    For the full SDK reference, see the [Stripe Onramp SDK documentation](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/stripe-onramp/overview). Start with the [Integration checklist](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/integration-checklist) for required setup details. On React Native you must install **`@stripe/stripe-react-native`**, enable the **native Onramp** module (Expo `includeOnramp: true` + rebuild, or bare Podfile / Android settings), and use a **development build** — not Expo Go. If `configureSDK` fails with **StripeCryptoOnramp / Podfile**, see [React Native troubleshooting](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/stripe-onramp/troubleshooting).

    ### App Attest (iOS)

    Stripe Link Pay requires the **App Attest** entitlement on iOS. In your Expo `app.json`, add:

    ```json theme={null}
    "ios": {
      "entitlements": {
        "com.apple.developer.devicecheck.appattest-environment": "development"
      }
    }
    ```

    * **Simulator testing:** Set App Attest to `"development"`, enable **Test Mode** in the [Stripe Dashboard](https://dashboard.stripe.com/test/dashboard), and use Stripe **test keys** (`pk_test_...` / `sk_test_...`) in the Unifold Dashboard.
    * **Live / production:** Set App Attest to `"production"`, run the app on a **physical device** using TestFlight, and use Stripe **live keys** (`pk_live_...` / `sk_live_...`) in the Unifold Dashboard.

    To enable Apple Pay on iOS, provide these app attestation details to Stripe using your app-specific values:

    | Field                          | Value                   |
    | ------------------------------ | ----------------------- |
    | Stripe Live Account ID         | `acct_1ABCDefGhIJkLmNo` |
    | iOS App ID (App Store Connect) | `1234567890`            |
    | Android App ID (package)       | `co.yourcompany.app`    |
    | Bundle identifier              | `co.yourcompany.app`    |
    | iOS Team ID                    | `1A2BC3D4E5`            |

    For the full `app.json` configuration (including the Stripe plugin with `includeOnramp`, `merchantIdentifier`, and Apple Pay), see the [Stripe Onramp overview](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/stripe-onramp/overview#configure-appjson-expo).
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## How It All Connects

<Steps>
  <Step title="Dashboard">
    You configure your Stripe credentials in the Unifold Dashboard. These are stored securely on the server.
  </Step>

  <Step title="SDK">
    Your app uses the Unifold SDK with your Unifold publishable key. The SDK fetches the Stripe publishable key from the Unifold API automatically.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Stripe">
    Stripe handles the in-app payment flow — card collection, Apple Pay / Google Pay, Stripe Link, and KYC.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Unifold">
    Unifold coordinates wallet resolution, onramp session creation (using your Stripe secret key server-side), and crypto delivery to the user's wallet.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Test vs Live Mode

|                    | Test Mode                                 | Live Mode                                                       |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Unifold key**    | `pk_test_...`                             | `pk_live_...`                                                   |
| **Stripe keys**    | Test keys (`pk_test_...` / `sk_test_...`) | Live keys (`pk_live_...` / `sk_live_...`) — test keys also work |
| **Payments**       | Simulated (no real charges)               | Real charges                                                    |
| **KYC**            | Bypassed or simulated                     | Full verification required                                      |
| **Token delivery** | ❌ No tokens delivered                     | ✅ Delivered to the user's wallet                                |

<Note>
  Stripe **test keys** can be used in **both** test-mode and live-mode projects, but Stripe **live keys** work **only** in a live-mode project. Also note that in **test mode, Stripe does not deliver any tokens** — use live mode with live keys to complete real crypto delivery.
</Note>

<Tip>
  Start with test keys during development. When you're ready for production, update your Stripe credentials in the Dashboard to live keys and use your live Unifold publishable key in the app.
</Tip>

<Tip>
  **Already on a live-mode project (mainnet) to test end-to-end delivery?** You don't need a separate test-mode project — keep your live-mode project and simply use your **Stripe test key** during development, then swap in your **Stripe live key** once you go live.
</Tip>

<Warning>
  When switching between test and live mode, update **both** the Stripe Publishable Key **and** Secret Key in the Unifold Dashboard. Mixing test and live keys will cause API errors.
</Warning>

## Supported Features

| Feature                | Description                                                |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Credit/Debit Cards** | Visa, Mastercard, and other major networks via Stripe Link |
| **Apple Pay**          | One-tap purchase on iOS (requires Apple Merchant ID)       |
| **Stripe Link**        | Returning users auto-fill payment and identity details     |
| **KYC Verification**   | Built-in identity verification via Stripe Identity         |

## Troubleshooting

### "Failed to load Stripe config: 400"

The Unifold API rejected the request before reaching Stripe. Common causes:

* Your Unifold publishable key belongs to a **different project** or environment than expected (e.g. a key from Client A used against Client B's backend config)
* Stripe Onramp is not fully configured for this project — confirm all four credentials (publishable key, secret key, OAuth client ID, OAuth client secret) are saved in the Dashboard
* Mixing `pk_test_...` / `pk_live_...` keys with the wrong environment

**Debug tip:** Call the endpoint directly with `curl` to read the JSON error body (the SDK only shows the status code):

```bash theme={null}
curl -v https://api.unifold.io/v1/public/onramps/headless/stripe/config \
  -H "x-publishable-key: pk_live_YOUR_KEY"
```

### "Failed to load Stripe config: 401"

This means the Unifold API rejected the request. Common causes:

* Your Unifold publishable key doesn't match the environment (e.g. using a test key against production)
* Stripe credentials haven't been saved in the Dashboard yet
* The Stripe integration is disabled in the Dashboard

### "Stripe has not been initialized"

This is a client-side SDK issue. Ensure **`config.enableStripeLink: true`** is set on `UnifoldProvider` and that `@stripe/stripe-react-native` with the **native Onramp** module is installed and rebuilt — the SDK initializes Stripe automatically when the Pay with Link flow opens.

### Apple Pay Not Available

**Web (Pay with Link):**

* Confirm the **Stripe team has whitelisted the current domain** for Apple Pay — during Private Preview this is done by Stripe, not self-serve, and an un-whitelisted domain makes Apple Pay silently disappear
* Submit **each** environment separately (production, staging, preview); wildcards are not supported
* Apple Pay only renders in **Safari** on Apple devices

**React Native / iOS:**

* Verify you've entered the **Apple Merchant ID** in the Dashboard
* Confirm the merchant ID matches your Xcode capability configuration
* Apple Pay is only available on physical iOS devices (not simulators)

### KYC Rejected

Stripe's KYC verification may reject users based on their region or identity documents. The rejection is shown inline in the Pay with Link sheet, where the user can re-submit. See [Error Handling](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/stripe-onramp/error-handling) for guidance.

# Testnet Support

> Test your integration with Unifold using testnet mode

Unifold provides a testnet environment for you to test your integration before going live. This allows you to verify the end-to-end flow without using real funds.

<Warning>
  Testnet environments can be unstable due to limited DEX liquidity pools on test networks. While this may affect transaction reliability, it provides a valuable way to understand how the full end-to-end integration works.
</Warning>

## Supported Networks

Testnet mode currently supports **USDC** on the following networks for both source and destination token:

| Network      | Chain ID | Token | Address                                    |
| ------------ | -------- | ----- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Sepolia      | 11155111 | USDC  | 0x1c7d4b196cb0c7b01d743fbc6116a902379c7238 |
| Base Sepolia | 84532    | USDC  | 0x036cbd53842c5426634e7929541ec2318f3dcf7e |

<Warning>
  **Checkout** and **Payment Intents** are currently **mainnet only** and do not work in testnet mode. Attempting to create a payment intent with a test API key will fail. These features require live mode credentials (`pk_live_` / `sk_live_`).
</Warning>

## Step 1: Access Your Project Dashboard

Navigate to the [Unifold Dashboard](https://dashboard.unifold.io) and select your project.

<Frame>
  <img src="/_mintlify/image/unifold/images/integrations/testnet/dashboard-project.png" alt="Dashboard project overview" />
</Frame>

## Step 2: Enable Test Mode

Toggle to **Test Mode** using the switch in the dashboard header. When test mode is enabled, you'll see a visual indicator confirming you're in the test environment.

<Frame>
  <img src="/_mintlify/image/unifold/images/integrations/testnet/test-mode-toggle.png" alt="Test mode toggle" />
</Frame>

## Step 3: Get Your Test API Key

Once in test mode, navigate to the API Keys section. You'll see your test API key with the `pk_test_` prefix.

<Frame>
  <img src="/_mintlify/image/unifold/images/integrations/testnet/test-api-key.png" alt="Test API key" />
</Frame>

<Note>
  Test API keys always start with `pk_test_` while production keys start with `pk_live_`. Make sure you're using the correct key for each environment.
</Note>

## Step 4: Configure the SDK

Use your test API key when initializing the UnifoldProvider:

```tsx theme={null}
import { UnifoldProvider } from '@unifold/react';

function App() {
  return (
    <UnifoldProvider
      apiKey="pk_test_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"
      // ... other configuration
    >
      {/* Your app */}
    </UnifoldProvider>
  );
}
```

<Tip>
  We recommend storing your API keys in environment variables and switching between test and production keys based on your deployment environment.
</Tip>

```tsx theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  apiKey={process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_UNIFOLD_API_KEY}
  // ...
>
```

## What to Expect

In testnet mode:

* **No real funds** — All transactions use test tokens with no monetary value
* **Same user experience** — The UI and flow are identical to production
* **Webhook events** — Test events are sent to your configured webhook endpoints
* **Limited liquidity** — Transactions may occasionally fail due to DEX pool constraints

# Overview

> Connect third-party wallet providers to Unifold

Unifold integrates with third-party embedded wallet providers so your users can deposit using wallets managed by services like Privy, Dynamic, Turnkey, and others.

Instead of asking users to connect a browser extension or enter a wallet address manually, embedded wallet integrations let you programmatically resolve a user's wallet and wire it into Unifold's deposit flow.

## Why Embedded Wallets?

Traditional crypto wallets (MetaMask, Coinbase Wallet, etc.) require users to install extensions, manage seed phrases, and manually approve every transaction. Embedded wallets remove this friction:

* **Invisible to the user** — Wallets are created and managed behind the scenes by the wallet provider
* **No seed phrases** — Key management is handled by the provider's infrastructure
* **Programmatic access** — Your backend can resolve wallet addresses and initiate transactions without user interaction
* **Cross-platform** — Works on web, mobile, and server-side without browser extensions

## How It Works

1. **User authenticates** — Your user logs in through your app's existing auth flow (email, social, SSO, etc.)
2. **Wallet resolved** — The wallet provider creates or retrieves an embedded wallet for the user
3. **Address passed to Unifold** — Your app provides the wallet address to Unifold's SDK or API
4. **Funds flow** — Deposits land in the user's embedded wallet

<Frame caption="Embedded wallet providers handle key management while Unifold handles the payment and settlement infrastructure.">
  ```mermaid theme={null}
  sequenceDiagram
      participant User
      participant App
      participant Wallet Provider
      participant Unifold

      User->>App: Log in
      App->>Wallet Provider: Authenticate user
      Wallet Provider-->>App: Wallet address
      App->>Unifold: Initiate deposit (wallet address)
      Unifold-->>User: Funds delivered to embedded wallet
  ```
</Frame>

## Supported Providers

<CardGroup cols={1}>
  <Card href="/developer/integrations/wallets/privy">
    **Privy** — Embedded wallets with email, social, and custom auth. Server-side wallet creation and management via Privy's API.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

<Note>
  More wallet providers are coming soon. If you're using a provider not listed here, [contact us](mailto:support@unifold.io) and we can help you integrate.
</Note>

# Privy

> Integrate Privy embedded wallets with Unifold

Connect [Privy](https://www.privy.io/) embedded wallets to Unifold so your users can deposit without managing seed phrases or installing browser extensions.

## Overview

**[Privy](https://www.privy.io/)** provides embedded wallets that are created and managed on behalf of your users:

* **Seamless onboarding** — Users sign in with email, phone, social accounts, or custom auth and receive a wallet automatically
* **No wallet UX** — No extensions, no seed phrases, no manual address entry
* **Cross-chain support** — Wallets work across EVM chains and Solana

**[Unifold](https://unifold.io/)** handles the deposit infrastructure that gets funds into those wallets. Most apps run on a specific token on a specific chain (e.g. USDC on Base), but your users hold funds across many different tokens and chains. Unifold bridges that gap:

* **Multi-chain deposits** — Accept deposits from 10+ chains (Ethereum, Polygon, Base, Arbitrum, Solana, Bitcoin, and more)
* **Any-token support** — Users can send ETH, SOL, USDC, or any supported token — Unifold auto-converts to the exact token your app needs
* **Drop-in deposit modal** — Pre-built UI with deposit address, QR code, and real-time tracking
* **Fiat onramps** — Built-in card and bank transfer options via [integrated providers](/developer/integrations/onramps/overview)

Privy manages the wallet, Unifold powers the deposit flow.

## Prerequisites

Before you begin, ensure you have:

* A Unifold account with your **publishable key** (`pk_live_...` or `pk_test_...`) from the [Dashboard](https://dashboard.unifold.io)
* A [Privy](https://dashboard.privy.io/) account with an app configured

<Info>
  If you haven't set up Unifold yet, follow the [Quickstart](/get-started/quickstart) guide first.
</Info>

## Step 1: Get Privy Credentials

<Steps>
  <Step title="Create a Privy app">
    Log in to the [Privy Dashboard](https://dashboard.privy.io/) and create a new app (or use an existing one).

    Copy your **App ID** from the app settings page — this is used to initialize the Privy SDK on the client.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Configure login methods">
    Under **Login Methods** in the Privy Dashboard, enable the authentication methods you want to support (email, SMS, Google, Apple, etc.).

    Privy will automatically create an embedded wallet for each user upon their first login.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Step 2: Set Up Privy in Your App

Install the Privy SDK alongside the Unifold SDK.

<CodeGroup>
  ```bash npm theme={null}
  npm install @privy-io/react-auth @unifold/connect-react
  ```

  ```bash yarn theme={null}
  yarn add @privy-io/react-auth @unifold/connect-react
  ```

  ```bash pnpm theme={null}
  pnpm add @privy-io/react-auth @unifold/connect-react
  ```
</CodeGroup>

Wrap your app with both providers. The Privy provider handles authentication and wallet creation, while the Unifold provider handles deposits.

<Note>
  The `createOnLogin` option must be nested under the specific chain type you intend to use (e.g. `ethereum`, `solana`, or both). Choose whichever chain type matches your app's needs. See Privy's [automatic wallet creation docs](https://docs.privy.io/basics/react/advanced/automatic-wallet-creation) for full details.
</Note>

<CodeGroup>
  ```tsx Ethereum theme={null}
  import { PrivyProvider } from '@privy-io/react-auth';
  import { UnifoldProvider } from '@unifold/connect-react';
  import '@unifold/connect-react/styles.css';

  function App() {
    return (
      <PrivyProvider
        appId="YOUR_PRIVY_APP_ID"
        config={{
          embeddedWallets: {
            ethereum: {
              createOnLogin: 'users-without-wallets',
            },
          },
        }}
      >
        <UnifoldProvider publishableKey="YOUR_UNIFOLD_PUBLISHABLE_KEY">
          <YourApp />
        </UnifoldProvider>
      </PrivyProvider>
    );
  }
  ```

  ```tsx Solana theme={null}
  import { PrivyProvider } from '@privy-io/react-auth';
  import { UnifoldProvider } from '@unifold/connect-react';
  import '@unifold/connect-react/styles.css';

  function App() {
    return (
      <PrivyProvider
        appId="YOUR_PRIVY_APP_ID"
        config={{
          embeddedWallets: {
            solana: {
              createOnLogin: 'users-without-wallets',
            },
          },
        }}
      >
        <UnifoldProvider publishableKey="YOUR_UNIFOLD_PUBLISHABLE_KEY">
          <YourApp />
        </UnifoldProvider>
      </PrivyProvider>
    );
  }
  ```

  ```tsx Ethereum & Solana theme={null}
  import { PrivyProvider } from '@privy-io/react-auth';
  import { UnifoldProvider } from '@unifold/connect-react';
  import '@unifold/connect-react/styles.css';

  function App() {
    return (
      <PrivyProvider
        appId="YOUR_PRIVY_APP_ID"
        config={{
          embeddedWallets: {
            ethereum: {
              createOnLogin: 'users-without-wallets',
            },
            solana: {
              createOnLogin: 'users-without-wallets',
            },
          },
        }}
      >
        <UnifoldProvider publishableKey="YOUR_UNIFOLD_PUBLISHABLE_KEY">
          <YourApp />
        </UnifoldProvider>
      </PrivyProvider>
    );
  }
  ```
</CodeGroup>

## Step 3: Connect Privy Wallets to Unifold Deposits

Once a user authenticates through Privy, retrieve their embedded wallet address and use it as the deposit destination via Unifold's `beginDeposit()` flow.

### Client-side: Deposit to a Privy embedded wallet

```tsx theme={null}
import { usePrivy, useWallets } from '@privy-io/react-auth';
import { useUnifold } from '@unifold/connect-react';

function DepositButton() {
  const { authenticated, user } = usePrivy();
  const { wallets } = useWallets();
  const { beginDeposit } = useUnifold();

  const handleDeposit = async () => {
    const embeddedWallet = wallets.find(
      (wallet) => wallet.walletClientType === 'privy'
    );

    if (!embeddedWallet) return;

    try {
      const result = await beginDeposit({
        externalUserId: user?.id,
        recipientAddress: embeddedWallet.address,
        destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
        destinationChainId: '8453',
        destinationTokenAddress: '0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913',
        destinationTokenSymbol: 'USDC',
      });

      console.log('Deposit completed:', result.executionId);
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('Deposit failed:', error);
    }
  };

  if (!authenticated) return null;

  return <button onClick={handleDeposit}>Deposit</button>;
}
```

The `beginDeposit()` call opens the Unifold deposit modal, which shows the user a unique deposit address. The user can send any supported token from any chain — Unifold auto-swaps it to the destination token and delivers it to the Privy embedded wallet.

Since the deposit goes directly to the user's embedded wallet, there's no need for backend webhook handling or manual balance crediting — the funds arrive in the user's wallet automatically once the deposit completes.

<Tip>
  The deposit modal is fully customizable — colors, fonts, border radius, and individual component styles can all be themed to match your brand. Try the [live demo](https://demo.unifold.io/demo/customize) to preview options, or see the [customization docs](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/ui-customization/overview) for the full reference.
</Tip>

## Architecture

```mermaid theme={null}
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant App as Your App
    participant Privy as Privy SDK
    participant Unifold as Unifold SDK

    User->>App: Log in
    App->>Privy: Authenticate
    Privy-->>App: User + embedded wallet address

    User->>App: Click "Deposit"
    App->>Unifold: beginDeposit({ recipientAddress })
    Unifold-->>User: Deposit modal (address + QR code)
    User->>Unifold: Send any token from any chain
    Unifold->>Unifold: Auto-swap to destination token
    Unifold-->>User: Funds delivered to embedded wallet
```

## Test vs Live Mode

|                  | Test Mode                     | Live Mode                     |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| **Privy**        | Sandbox app with test users   | Production app                |
| **Unifold Keys** | `pk_test_...` / `sk_test_...` | `pk_live_...` / `sk_live_...` |
| **Wallets**      | Testnet wallets               | Mainnet wallets               |
| **Transactions** | Simulated                     | Real on-chain transactions    |

<Tip>
  Use Privy's sandbox environment and Unifold's test keys during development. Switch to production credentials when you're ready to go live.
</Tip>

## Troubleshooting

### User doesn't have an embedded wallet

If `wallets.find()` returns `undefined`, the user may not have created an embedded wallet yet. Ensure your Privy config includes `createOnLogin: 'users-without-wallets'` (or `'all-users'`) under the appropriate chain type (e.g. `embeddedWallets.ethereum.createOnLogin`) to auto-create wallets on first login. For existing users, you can trigger wallet creation with `createWallet()` from Privy's SDK.

### Wallet address is on the wrong chain

Privy embedded wallets are EVM-compatible by default. If your Unifold configuration targets a specific chain, ensure the wallet address is on the correct network. Use Privy's `switchChain` method to change chains before resolving the address.

# Geo restrictions

> Restrict access to users from specific countries and states/regions

## Overview

Geo restrictions are a project-wide access control. They apply across every Unifold flow — deposits, onramps, checkout, and withdrawals — not just a single feature. Use them to restrict access to users from specific countries or individual states/regions within a country, whether for compliance with local regulations or to limit your service to certain markets.

Geo restrictions consist of two parts:

1. **Dashboard Configuration** - Set which countries (and optionally states/regions) are restricted via the Unifold Dashboard
2. **Client-Side Hook** - Use the `useAllowedCountry` hook to check if a user is allowed before you open any flow

## Dashboard Configuration

### Restricting Countries

1. Navigate to your project in the [Unifold Dashboard](https://dashboard.unifold.io)
2. Go to **Country Restrictions**
3. Search and select the countries you want to block
4. Click **Save Changes**

<div style={{ maxWidth: '560px' }}>
  <Frame caption="Country Restrictions page — search and block countries from the list">
    <img src="/_mintlify/image/unifold/images/settings/country-restrictions.png" alt="Country Restrictions page showing a searchable list of countries with checkboxes to block them" />
  </Frame>
</div>

<Note>
  Changes take effect immediately. Users from blocked countries will be restricted on their next request.
</Note>

### Restricting States / Regions

For countries that support state-level configuration, a **Configure** button appears in the **States** column. Clicking it opens a modal where you can select specific states or regions to block within that country.

<div style={{ maxWidth: '480px' }}>
  <Frame caption="Configure States modal — select specific US states to block">
    <img src="/_mintlify/image/unifold/images/settings/configure-states-us.png" alt="Configure States modal for the United States showing a searchable list of US states with checkboxes to block them" />
  </Frame>
</div>

<Note>
  State/region-level blocking is available for certain countries. If a **Configure** button appears next to a country, it means granular state-level configuration is supported. Need state-level restrictions for a country that isn't listed? [Contact us](mailto:hello@unifold.io) to discuss your requirements.
</Note>

When state-level blocking is configured:

* If the country itself is blocked, all states are blocked regardless of individual state settings.
* If only specific states are blocked, users from those states are restricted while users from other states in the same country are allowed.

## Client-Side Usage

### useAllowedCountry Hook

The `useAllowedCountry` hook combines IP geolocation with your project's blocked countries configuration to determine if a user should be allowed access.

```tsx theme={null}
import { useAllowedCountry } from '@unifold/connect-react';

function MyComponent() {
  const { isAllowed, alpha2, country, isLoading, error } = useAllowedCountry();

  if (isLoading) {
    return <LoadingSpinner />;
  }

  if (error) {
    return <ErrorMessage error={error} />;
  }

  if (isAllowed === false) {
    return <GeoBlockedMessage country={country} />;
  }

  return <YourContent />;
}
```

# Allowed Domains

> Restrict client-side API key usage to specific origins

Allowed domains let you control which websites can use your publishable API keys. When configured, requests from unlisted origins are rejected, preventing unauthorized usage of your keys on other domains.

<Warning>
  Publishable keys are visible in client-side code. Without allowed domains configured, anyone who obtains your key can use it from any website.
</Warning>

## How it works

When you add domains to the allowed list, Unifold extracts the hostname from each origin and checks incoming requests against it. Subdomains are matched automatically, adding `https://example.com` also allows `https://app.example.com`, `https://staging.example.com`, etc.

If a request comes from an origin that doesn't match any entry in your allowed list, it is rejected with a `403` error.

| Allowed Domain        | Request Origin            | Result  |
| --------------------- | ------------------------- | ------- |
| `https://example.com` | `https://example.com`     | Allowed |
| `https://example.com` | `https://app.example.com` | Allowed |
| `https://example.com` | `https://other-site.com`  | Blocked |
| *(empty list)*        | `https://any-site.com`    | Allowed |

## Setup

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open project settings">
    Navigate to your project in the [Unifold Dashboard](https://dashboard.unifold.io) and click **Settings** in the sidebar.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Go to the Domains tab">
    Select the **Domains** tab at the top of the Settings page.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Add your domains">
    Enter your domain (e.g. `https://yourdomain.com`) in the input field and click **+ Add**. Repeat for each domain you want to allow.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Frame caption="Allowed Domains configuration in the Unifold Dashboard (Settings → Domains)">
  <img src="/_mintlify/image/unifold/images/settings/allowed-domains.png" alt="Allowed Domains settings page showing a configured domain and the add domain input" />
</Frame>

# Overview

> Real-time notifications for treasury, deposit, withdraw, and payment intent operations

Unifold sends webhook events when actions occur in your account. Subscribe to specific events to receive real-time notifications. Events are organised by domain — pick a category below for the lifecycle, payload structure, and JSON examples.

# Deposit Events

> Webhook events for the user-deposit lifecycle

Deposit events track the lifecycle of a user's deposit through the system. Each event uses a Stripe-style envelope with the event metadata at the top level and the execution data nested under `data.object`.

## Lifecycle

When a user sends a deposit, the execution moves through the following states:

```mermaid theme={null}
flowchart LR
    A[pending] --> B[delayed]
    A --> C[completed]
    B --> C[completed]
```

| State         | Webhook Event                        | When It Fires                                                                       |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **pending**   | `deposit.direct_execution.pending`   | Deposit received and processing has begun (swap/bridge in progress)                 |
| **delayed**   | `deposit.direct_execution.delayed`   | Processing is taking longer than expected (e.g., network congestion, bridge delays) |
| **completed** | `deposit.direct_execution.completed` | Deposit fully processed and USDC delivered to treasury                              |

<Note>
  The `received` state (initial on-chain detection before validation) does not fire a webhook event. The first webhook you receive is always `pending`, once Unifold has validated the incoming transaction.
</Note>

## Payload Structure

All deposit events share the same envelope and `data.object` structure. The `status` and `type` fields reflect the current lifecycle state.

### Envelope Fields

| Field         | Type    | Description                                                                   |
| ------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`          | string  | Unique event ID (e.g., `evt_...`)                                             |
| `object`      | string  | Always `"event"`                                                              |
| `type`        | string  | Event type (e.g., `deposit.direct_execution.pending`)                         |
| `created`     | integer | Unix timestamp when the event was created                                     |
| `livemode`    | boolean | `true` for live mode (production/mainnet), `false` for sandbox mode (testnet) |
| `data.object` | object  | The execution object at the time of the event                                 |

### `data.object` Fields

| Field                      | Type           | Description                                                                                    |
| -------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                       | string         | Execution ID (e.g., `exec_...`) — use as deduplication key                                     |
| `project_id`               | string         | ID of the project the execution belongs to (e.g., `proj_...`)                                  |
| `created_at`               | string         | ISO 8601 timestamp when the execution was created                                              |
| `updated_at`               | string         | ISO 8601 timestamp of the last status change                                                   |
| `user_id`                  | string         | Unifold's internal user ID                                                                     |
| `external_user_id`         | string         | Your platform's user ID (passed via `externalUserId` in the SDK)                               |
| `status`                   | string         | Current status: `pending`, `delayed`, or `completed`                                           |
| `amount`                   | string \| null | Final amount in base units (after conversion). `null` for `pending` and `delayed` events.      |
| `amount_usd`               | string \| null | Human-readable USD value. `null` for `pending` and `delayed` events.                           |
| `failure_reason`           | string \| null | Reason for failure, if applicable                                                              |
| `treasury_account_id`      | string \| null | Treasury account that received the deposit                                                     |
| `treasury_account_address` | string \| null | On-chain address of the treasury account                                                       |
| `recipient_address`        | string \| null | On-chain recipient address                                                                     |
| `details`                  | object \| null | Routing information — source/destination chain, token, and amounts. Present on deposit events. |

### `data.object.details` Fields

The `details` object contains routing information about the deposit — where it came from, where it's going, and the amounts before and after conversion.

| Field                       | Type           | Description                                                         |
| --------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `source_chain_type`         | string         | Source chain family (e.g., `ethereum`, `solana`, `bitcoin`)         |
| `source_chain_id`           | string         | Source chain identifier (e.g., `1`, `137`, `mainnet`)               |
| `source_token_address`      | string         | Contract address of the source token                                |
| `source_token_symbol`       | string \| null | Token the user deposited (e.g., `ETH`, `SOL`, `USDC`)               |
| `source_amount`             | string \| null | Original amount sent by the user (in base units, before conversion) |
| `source_amount_usd`         | string \| null | USD value of the source amount                                      |
| `destination_chain_type`    | string         | Destination chain family (e.g., `ethereum`)                         |
| `destination_chain_id`      | string         | Destination chain identifier (e.g., `137`)                          |
| `destination_token_address` | string         | Contract address of the destination token                           |
| `destination_token_symbol`  | string \| null | Destination token (e.g., `USDC`)                                    |
| `destination_amount`        | string \| null | Converted amount in base units on the destination chain             |
| `destination_amount_usd`    | string \| null | USD value of the destination amount                                 |

## `deposit.direct_execution.pending`

Fires when an incoming deposit has been received and processing (swap and/or bridge) is in progress.

Use this event to show users that their deposit has been received and is being processed.

```json theme={null}
{
  "id": "evt_2abc123def456ghi789jkl0mn",
  "object": "event",
  "type": "deposit.direct_execution.pending",
  "created": 1737072000,
  "livemode": true,
  "data": {
    "object": {
      "id": "exec_2abc123def456ghi789jkl0mn",
      "project_id": "proj_1abc234efg567hij890klm1no",
      "created_at": "2026-01-17T00:19:25.935Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-01-17T00:19:25.935Z",
      "user_id": "user_2abc123def456ghi789jkl0mn",
      "external_user_id": "external_user_123",
      "status": "pending",
      "amount": null,
      "amount_usd": null,
      "failure_reason": null,
      "treasury_account_id": null,
      "treasury_account_address": null,
      "recipient_address": "0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc9e7595f8E3c0",
      "details": {
        "source_chain_type": "ethereum",
        "source_chain_id": "1",
        "source_token_address": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000",
        "source_token_symbol": "ETH",
        "source_amount": "500000000000000000",
        "source_amount_usd": "1250.00",
        "destination_chain_type": "ethereum",
        "destination_chain_id": "137",
        "destination_token_address": "0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359",
        "destination_token_symbol": "USDC",
        "destination_amount": null,
        "destination_amount_usd": null
      }
    }
  }
}
```

<Info>
  The `amount`, `amount_usd`, `destination_amount`, and `destination_amount_usd` fields are `null` in `pending` events because the final converted amount is not yet known (swap has not completed).
</Info>

## `deposit.direct_execution.delayed`

Fires when deposit processing is taking longer than expected. Common causes include network congestion, high bridge wait times, or liquidity constraints.

Use this event to proactively notify users that their deposit is still being processed.

```json theme={null}
{
  "id": "evt_3bcd234efg567hij890klm1no",
  "object": "event",
  "type": "deposit.direct_execution.delayed",
  "created": 1737073800,
  "livemode": true,
  "data": {
    "object": {
      "id": "exec_2abc123def456ghi789jkl0mn",
      "project_id": "proj_1abc234efg567hij890klm1no",
      "created_at": "2026-01-17T00:19:25.935Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-01-17T00:49:25.935Z",
      "user_id": "user_2abc123def456ghi789jkl0mn",
      "external_user_id": "external_user_123",
      "status": "delayed",
      "amount": null,
      "amount_usd": null,
      "failure_reason": null,
      "treasury_account_id": null,
      "treasury_account_address": null,
      "recipient_address": "0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc9e7595f8E3c0",
      "details": {
        "source_chain_type": "ethereum",
        "source_chain_id": "1",
        "source_token_address": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000",
        "source_token_symbol": "ETH",
        "source_amount": "500000000000000000",
        "source_amount_usd": "1250.00",
        "destination_chain_type": "ethereum",
        "destination_chain_id": "137",
        "destination_token_address": "0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359",
        "destination_token_symbol": "USDC",
        "destination_amount": null,
        "destination_amount_usd": null
      }
    }
  }
}
```

<Tip>
  Not every deposit triggers a `delayed` event. It only fires if processing exceeds the expected time window. Most deposits go directly from `pending` to `completed`.
</Tip>

## `deposit.direct_execution.completed`

Fires when a deposit is fully processed — the USDC has been delivered to your treasury. This is the event you should use to credit user balances.

```json theme={null}

  "id": "evt_4cde345fgh678ijk901lmn2op",

  "type": "deposit.direct_execution.completed",
  "created": 1737075600,
  "livemode": true,
  "data": {
    "object": {
      "id": "exec_2abc123def456ghi789jkl0mn",

      "updated_at": "2026-01-17T01:19:25.935Z",
      "user_id": "user_2abc123def456ghi789jkl0mn",
      "external_user_id": "external_user_123",
      "status": "completed",
      "amount": "1000000",
      "amount_usd": "1.00",

      "treasury_account_address": "0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc9e7595f8E3c0",
      "recipient_address": "0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc9e7595f8E3c0",
      "details": {
        "source_chain_type": "ethereum",
        "source_chain_id": "1",
        "source_token_address": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000",

        "destination_token_symbol": "USDC",
        "destination_amount": "1000000",
        "destination_amount_usd": "1.00"
```

# Payment Intent Events

> Webhook events for default and locked-quote payment intents

Payment intent events fire when a [checkout payment](/developer/checkout/overview) changes status. Use these to confirm payments on your server, fulfill orders, or update your database.

The same `payment_intent.*` event types are emitted for both **default** (multi-source, bridged) and **locked-quote** (single-source, rate-locked, atomic payout) payment intents. The `data.object.type` field discriminates between the two — its value is either `"default"` or `"locked_quote"`. Source-side fields and refund fields are only populated for `locked_quote`.

## Default-mode lifecycle

```mermaid theme={null}
flowchart LR
    A[requires_payment] --> B[processing]
    B --> C[succeeded]
    A --> D[canceled]
```

| State        | Webhook                     | Notes                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------ | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `processing` | `payment_intent.processing` | Deposit detected; settlement bridging in progress. `destination_amount_received` may be less than `destination_amount` (partial payments). |
| `succeeded`  | `payment_intent.succeeded`  | Destination amount delivered (within `settlement_tolerance_percent`).                                                                      |

## Locked-quote lifecycle

```mermaid theme={null}
flowchart LR
    A[requires_payment] --> B[processing]
    B --> C[succeeded]
    A --> D[canceled]
    A --> E[expired]
    E --> F[awaiting_refund]
    F --> G[refunded]
    F --> H[refund_failed]
    H --> G
```

| State             | Webhook                          | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `processing`      | `payment_intent.processing`      | Source-side deposit detected. `source_amount_received` updates as deposits land.                                                                                                                                                         |
| `succeeded`       | `payment_intent.succeeded`       | Atomic payout from the payout pool to `recipient_address` confirmed. The destination-chain payout hash is **not** included in the webhook — fetch it from the payment intent's `transaction_hash` field via the REST API if you need it. |
| `expired`         | `payment_intent.expired`         | Quote window elapsed before any source-side deposit arrived. Terminal unless a late deposit arrives.                                                                                                                                     |
| `awaiting_refund` | `payment_intent.awaiting_refund` | A deposit landed after expiration; call [Refund a payment intent](/api-reference/payment-intents/refund) with the payer's source-chain address.                                                                                          |
| `refunded`        | `payment_intent.refunded`        | Source-chain refund tx confirmed; `refund_transaction_hash` and `refunded_at` are set.                                                                                                                                                   |
| `refund_failed`   | `payment_intent.refund_failed`   | Refund broadcast failed; `failure_reason` is set. Retry by calling refund with a corrected address — the next attempt fires `refunded` (or another `refund_failed`).                                                                     |

<Note>
  No webhook fires for the initial `requires_payment` state, the intermediate `refunding` state, or for `canceled` transitions.
</Note>

## Payload Structure

Payment intent webhooks use the same Stripe-style envelope as other events, with the payment intent object nested under `data.object`. Fields marked **LQ only** are populated (non-null) only when `type` is `"locked_quote"`; on `default` intents they are `null`.

### `data.object` Fields

| Field                             | Type           | Description                                                                                                                                   |
| --------------------------------- | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                              | string         | Payment intent ID (e.g., `pi_...`)                                                                                                            |
| `project_id`                      | string         | ID of the project the payment intent belongs to (e.g., `proj_...`)                                                                            |
| `type`                            | string         | `"default"` or `"locked_quote"`                                                                                                               |
| `status`                          | string         | Current status (see lifecycle tables above)                                                                                                   |
| `livemode`                        | boolean        | `true` for production, `false` for sandbox                                                                                                    |
| `destination_amount`              | string         | Target amount in destination token base units (e.g., `"10000000"` for 10 USDC)                                                                |
| `destination_amount_usd`          | string         | USD value of `destination_amount` at creation. Use this for order matching.                                                                   |
| `destination_amount_received`     | string         | Actual amount delivered to the recipient. For `locked_quote` this stays `"0"` until the atomic payout confirms.                               |
| `destination_amount_received_usd` | string         | USD value of `destination_amount_received`                                                                                                    |
| `destination_currency`            | string         | Destination currency code (e.g., `usdc`)                                                                                                      |
| `destination_network`             | string         | Destination network (e.g., `base`)                                                                                                            |
| `recipient_address`               | string         | Final recipient address                                                                                                                       |
| `source_currency`                 | string \| null | **LQ only.** Source token currency code                                                                                                       |
| `source_network`                  | string \| null | **LQ only.** Source network slug                                                                                                              |
| `source_amount`                   | string \| null | **LQ only.** Locked source amount in base units                                                                                               |
| `source_amount_usd`               | string \| null | **LQ only.** USD value of the locked source amount                                                                                            |
| `source_amount_received`          | string \| null | **LQ only.** Cumulative source-side deposits in base units                                                                                    |
| `source_amount_received_usd`      | string \| null | **LQ only.** USD value of `source_amount_received`                                                                                            |
| `intent_address`                  | string \| null | **LQ only.** Source-chain address the payer deposits to (locked quote uses a single intent address rather than per-chain `deposit_addresses`) |
| `refund_address`                  | string \| null | **LQ only.** Address you supplied via the refund endpoint                                                                                     |
| `refund_amount`                   | string \| null | **LQ only.** Refund amount net of network fees                                                                                                |
| `refund_amount_usd`               | string \| null | **LQ only.** USD value of the refund amount                                                                                                   |
| `refund_transaction_hash`         | string \| null | **LQ only.** Source-chain refund tx hash                                                                                                      |
| `refunded_at`                     | string \| null | **LQ only.** When the refund confirmed on-chain                                                                                               |
| `settlement_tolerance_percent`    | string \| null | Configured tolerance. `null` for `locked_quote` (always exact).                                                                               |
| `failure_reason`                  | string \| null | Reason for the most recent failure (e.g. refund error)                                                                                        |
| `expired_at`                      | string \| null | When the intent transitioned to `expired`                                                                                                     |
| `canceled_at`                     | string \| null | When the intent was canceled                                                                                                                  |
| `cancellation_reason`             | string \| null | Cancellation reason                                                                                                                           |
| `metadata`                        | object \| null | Your custom key-value metadata                                                                                                                |
| `description`                     | string \| null | Description you set when creating the intent                                                                                                  |
| `created_at`                      | string         | ISO 8601 creation timestamp                                                                                                                   |
| `updated_at`                      | string         | ISO 8601 last update timestamp                                                                                                                |

The legacy fields `amount`, `amount_usd`, `amount_received`, `amount_received_usd`, and `currency` are still emitted as deprecated aliases of their `destination_*` counterparts.

## `payment_intent.processing`

Fires when a deposit is detected against a payment intent and settlement is in progress.

For `default` intents, `destination_amount_received` may be less than `destination_amount` (partial payment). For `locked_quote`, the destination amount stays at `"0"` while source-side deposits accumulate (`source_amount_received` updates instead).

```json theme={null}
{
  "id": "evt_5abc123def456ghi789jkl0mn",
  "object": "event",
  "type": "payment_intent.processing",
  "created": 1737072000,
  "livemode": true,
  "data": {
    "object": {
      "type": "default",
      "id": "pi_5abc123def456ghi789jkl0mn",
      "project_id": "proj_1abc234efg567hij890klm1no",
      "status": "processing",
      "destination_amount": "10000000",
      "destination_amount_usd": "10.00",
      "destination_amount_received": "5000000",
      "destination_amount_received_usd": "5.00",
      "destination_currency": "usdc",
      "destination_network": "base",
      "recipient_address": "0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc9e7595f8E3c0",
      "settlement_tolerance_percent": "1",
      "source_amount_received": null,
      "source_amount_received_usd": null,
      "source_currency": null,
      "source_network": null,
      "source_amount": null,
      "source_amount_usd": null,
      "metadata": { "order_id": "order_123" },
      "description": "Payment for order #123",
      "livemode": true,
      "created_at": "2026-01-17T00:19:25.935Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-01-17T00:20:10.123Z"
    }
  }
}
```

<Info>
  Multiple deposits can accumulate toward the target on a `default` intent. Treat `processing` as informational — only fulfill orders on `succeeded`.
</Info>

## `payment_intent.succeeded`

Fires when the destination amount has been delivered to the recipient.

For `default`, `destination_amount_received` reaches `destination_amount` (within `settlement_tolerance_percent`). For `locked_quote`, the atomic payout from the payout pool to `recipient_address` has confirmed on-chain.

<Note>
  The destination-chain payout hash is **not** included in the webhook payload. Read it from the payment intent's `transaction_hash` field via [Retrieve a payment intent](/api-reference/payment-intents/get) when you need it.
</Note>

```json theme={null}
{
  "id": "evt_6def456ghi789jkl0mn1abc2",
  "object": "event",
  "type": "payment_intent.succeeded",
  "created": 1737072600,
  "livemode": true,
  "data": {
    "object": {
      "type": "default",
      "id": "pi_6def456ghi789jkl0mn1abc2",
      "project_id": "proj_1abc234efg567hij890klm1no",
      "status": "succeeded",
      "destination_amount": "10000000",
      "destination_amount_usd": "10.00",
      "destination_amount_received": "10000000",
      "destination_amount_received_usd": "10.00",
      "destination_currency": "usdc",
      "destination_network": "base",
      "recipient_address": "0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc9e7595f8E3c0",
      "settlement_tolerance_percent": "1",
      "metadata": { "order_id": "order_123" },
      "description": "Payment for order #123",
      "livemode": true,
      "created_at": "2026-01-17T00:19:25.935Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-01-17T00:25:30.456Z"
    }
  }
}
```

<Warning>
  Only fulfill orders on `payment_intent.succeeded`. The `processing` event is informational — the payment is not complete until `succeeded` fires.
</Warning>

<Note>
  **Use `destination_amount` / `destination_amount_usd` for order matching, not `destination_amount_received`.** Actual on-chain settlement may be slightly higher or lower than the target due to cross-chain slippage and DEX routing. For example, a 25.00 USD order may settle as 24.99 USD or 25.02 USD — both are considered fulfilled within the configured `settlement_tolerance_percent`. (This caveat does not apply to `locked_quote`, which always settles the exact amount.)
</Note>

## `payment_intent.expired`

Locked-quote only. Fires when the quote window elapses before any source-side deposit arrived. If a deposit lands later, the intent moves to `awaiting_refund` (next event). If no deposit ever arrives, `expired` is terminal.

```json theme={null}
{
  "id": "evt_7lqe111xyz",
  "object": "event",
  "type": "payment_intent.expired",
  "created": 1737073145,
  "livemode": true,
  "data": {
    "object": {
      "type": "locked_quote",
      "id": "pi_7lqe111xyz",
      "project_id": "proj_1abc234efg567hij890klm1no",
      "status": "expired",
      "destination_amount": "5000000",
      "destination_amount_usd": "5.00",
      "destination_amount_received": "0",
      "destination_amount_received_usd": "0.00",
      "destination_currency": "usdc",
      "destination_network": "base",
      "recipient_address": "0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc9e7595f8E3c0",
      "settlement_tolerance_percent": null,
      "source_currency": "btc",
      "source_network": "bitcoin",
      "source_amount": "260000",
      "source_amount_usd": "100.25",
      "source_amount_received": "0",
      "source_amount_received_usd": "0.00",
      "intent_address": "bc1q4vxn43l44h30nkluqfxd9eckf45vr2awz38lwa",

      "metadata": null,
      "description": null,
      "livemode": true,
      "created_at": "2026-01-17T02:14:25.935Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-01-17T02:19:25.935Z"
    }
  }
}
```

## `payment_intent.awaiting_refund`

Locked-quote only. Fires when a deposit arrives **after** the quote window expired. The merchant must initiate a refund — call [Refund a payment intent](/api-reference/payment-intents/refund) with the payer's source-chain address.


## `payment_intent.refund_failed`

Locked-quote only. Fires when a refund broadcast fails. `failure_reason` describes the error. You can retry by calling refund again with a corrected `refund_address` — the intent transitions back through `refunding` on the next attempt.

# Treasury Events

> Webhook events for outbound transfers from a treasury account

Treasury events fire when an [outbound transfer](/api-reference/treasury/outbound-transfers/create) from a treasury account changes terminal status. Use them to confirm payouts, update withdrawal records, or trigger retry/alert flows.

## `treasury.outbound_transfer.completed`

Fires when an outbound transfer from a treasury account successfully completes. Use this to confirm payouts and update withdrawal status.

```json theme={null}
{
  "id": "evt_3def456ghi789jkl0mn1abc2",
  "object": "event",
  "type": "treasury.outbound_transfer.completed",
  "created": 1737072000,
  "livemode": true,
  "data": {
    "object": {
      "id": "ot_3def456ghi789jkl0mn1abc2",
      "project_id": "proj_1abc234efg567hij890klm1no",
      "created_at": "2026-01-17T00:19:25.935Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-01-17T00:19:25.935Z",
      "user_id": "user_3def456ghi789jkl0mn1abc2",
      "external_user_id": "external_user_456",
      "status": "completed",
      "amount": "5000000",
      "amount_usd": "5.00",
      "failure_reason": null,
      "treasury_account_id": "ta_3def456ghi789jkl0mn1abc2",
      "treasury_account_address": "0x8ba1f109551bD432803012645Ac136ddd64DBA72",
      "recipient_address": "0x1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef12345678"
    }
  }
}
```

## `treasury.outbound_transfer.failed`

Fires when an outbound transfer fails. Use this to alert your team, trigger retry logic, or notify users of issues.

```json theme={null}
{
  "id": "evt_4ghi789jkl0mn1abc2def3",
  "object": "event",
  "type": "treasury.outbound_transfer.failed",
  "created": 1737072000,
  "livemode": true,
  "data": {
    "object": {
      "id": "ot_4ghi789jkl0mn1abc2def3",
      "project_id": "proj_1abc234efg567hij890klm1no",
      "created_at": "2026-01-17T00:19:25.935Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-01-17T00:19:25.935Z",
      "user_id": "user_4ghi789jkl0mn1abc2def3",
      "external_user_id": "external_user_789",
      "status": "failed",
      "amount": "10000000",
      "amount_usd": "10.00",
      "failure_reason": "Insufficient funds in treasury account",
      "treasury_account_id": "ta_4ghi789jkl0mn1abc2def3",
      "treasury_account_address": "0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7",
      "recipient_address": "0xabcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef12"
    }
  }
}
```
