
## Configuration

| Parameter                | Type           | Default | Description                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------ | -------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `enableCoinbaseApplePay` | `Bool?`        | `nil`   | Overrides the dashboard "Pay with Apple Pay" toggle. Resolves as `flag ?? dashboard ?? true`, still gated by provider availability |
| `user`                   | `UnifoldUser?` | `nil`   | Host user context; a trusted `email` skips the email-verification steps                                                            |
| `prefilledEmail`         | `String?`      | `nil`   | Pre-fills the email field (does not skip verification)                                                                             |

### Amounts

| Value       | Default             | Description                                                   |
| ----------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Minimum     | `$5`                | Minimum USD purchase (fallback if API limits are unavailable) |
| Maximum     | `$500`              | Maximum USD purchase (fallback)                               |
| Quick picks | `25, 100, 250, 500` | Suggested amounts on the numpad screen                        |

## Callbacks

### onDepositSuccess

Fires when the on-chain execution reaches **succeeded** status — i.e. the purchased crypto has been delivered to the destination address.

```swift theme={null}
onDepositSuccess: { data in
    // data.message      -> "Deposit completed successfully"
    // data.executionId  -> Unique execution ID (String?)
    // data.transaction  -> AutoSwapResponse with full execution details (Any?)
    refreshUserBalance()
}
```

### onEvent

Fires for deposit lifecycle events (e.g. an onramp session being created). Switch over `event.object` to narrow to the concrete payload.

### onDepositError

Fires for sheet-level errors. Verification and payment failures are handled inline in the UI with retry options.

### onDismiss

Fires when the user dismisses the deposit sheet.

## Flow States

| Screen                          | Description                                                                          |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Email Input**                 | Collect email + Coinbase legal agreements (skipped when a trusted email is provided) |
| **Phone Input / OTP**           | Collect and verify the phone number                                                  |
| **Amount**                      | Numpad + quick-pick amounts; payment session is created                              |
| **Apple Pay**                   | Native Apple Pay sheet inside a `WKWebView`                                          |
| **Checking Deposit**            | Polling the on-chain execution                                                       |
| **Success**                     | Execution succeeded                                                                  |
| **Guest Limit / Limit Upgrade** | DOB + SSN upgrade when guest-checkout caps are hit                                   |

## Webhooks

On-chain settlement is the source of truth for success. For reliable server-side confirmation, listen for deposit webhook events. See [Deposit Webhooks](/developer/webhooks/events/deposit).

# Connect Wallet

> Let users deposit from an external wallet app via a mobile deep link

Connect Wallet lets your users fund their account straight from an external wallet app (MetaMask, Phantom, Coinbase Wallet, and more). The SDK generates a mobile deep link, opens the wallet app so the user can send funds to their Unifold deposit address, then polls for the resulting on-chain deposit.

This mirrors the `ConnectWallet` flow in the React Native SDK.

## Prerequisites

* UnifoldSDK configured with a valid publishable key
* A destination chain and token configured
* The **Connect Wallet** option enabled — either on the dashboard for your project or via the `enableConnectWallet` flag (see [Enabling the Option](#enabling-the-option))

## How It Works

<Steps>
  <Step title="User picks a wallet">
    The deposit menu shows a **Connect Wallet** row ("Pay from your wallet app"). Tapping it lists the available wallet apps for your project.
  </Step>

  <Step title="User selects a network (multi-chain wallets)">
    For wallets that support multiple chains, the SDK shows a network picker so the user can choose which chain to deposit from.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Wallet app opens via deep link">
    The SDK requests a mobile deep link from the Unifold API and opens the selected wallet app, pre-filled to send funds to the user's Unifold deposit address.
  </Step>

  <Step title="SDK waits for the deposit">
    After returning to your app, the SDK polls for an incoming deposit on the deep-linked deposit wallet(s). A "checking for deposit" indicator appears after \~5 seconds.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Deposit is processed">
    Once a deposit is detected, the SDK tracks the on-chain execution (conversion and delivery to the destination chain) and shows a processing → summary state. `onDepositSuccess` fires when the execution succeeds.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Enabling the Option

The **Connect Wallet** row is resolved as:

```
enableConnectWallet (SDK flag) ?? dashboard "Connect Wallet" toggle ?? false
```

So it is **off by default** unless enabled on the dashboard or forced on with the SDK flag. Pass `enableConnectWallet: true` to show it regardless of the dashboard setting (for example, to test the flow before flipping the dashboard toggle).

<Note>
  The list of wallet apps offered comes from your project configuration. Configure which wallets are featured from the Unifold dashboard.
</Note>

## Integration

### Using the Deposit Sheet (SwiftUI)

```swift theme={null}

            recipientAddress: "0x...",
            destinationChainType: .ethereum,
            destinationChainId: "8453",
            destinationTokenAddress: "0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913",
            destinationTokenSymbol: "USDC",
            enableConnectWallet: true,
            onDepositSuccess: { data in
                print("Deposit complete: \(data.executionId ?? "")")
            }
        )
    }
}
```

### Using DepositConfiguration


## Configuration

| Parameter             | Type    | Default | Description                                                                               |
| --------------------- | ------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `enableConnectWallet` | `Bool?` | `nil`   | Overrides the dashboard "Connect Wallet" toggle. Resolves as `flag ?? dashboard ?? false` |

Destination and theming parameters behave the same as the rest of the deposit flow — see [Configuration](/get-started/sdk-reference/ios-swift/configuration).

## Flow States

| State                   | Description                                           |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| **Select Wallet**       | Pick from the available wallet apps                   |
| **Select Network**      | Choose a source chain (multi-chain wallets only)      |
| **Connecting**          | Generating the deep link and opening the wallet app   |
| **Waiting for Deposit** | Returned to your app; polling for an incoming deposit |
| **Deposit Processing**  | Deposit detected; on-chain execution in progress      |
| **Deposit Complete**    | Execution succeeded; summary shown                    |
| **Failed**              | Deep link or execution failed; user can retry         |

## Callbacks

### onDepositSuccess

Fires when the on-chain execution reaches **succeeded** status.

```swift theme={null}
onDepositSuccess: { data in
    // data.message      -> "Deposit completed successfully"
    // data.executionId  -> Unique execution ID (String?)
    // data.transaction  -> AutoSwapResponse with full execution details (Any?)
    refreshUserBalance()
}
```

### onDepositError

Fires for sheet-level errors (e.g. missing publishable key). Wallet-selection and deep-link failures are surfaced inline in the UI with retry options rather than through this callback.

### onDismiss

Fires when the user dismisses the deposit sheet.

## Webhooks

For reliable server-side confirmation — especially if the user doesn't return to your app before client polling stops — listen for deposit webhook events. See [Deposit Webhooks](/developer/webhooks/events/deposit).

# Deposit Menu Layout

> Switch the deposit menu between a stacked list and a tabbed "Use Crypto / Use Cash" layout

The deposit menu can be rendered in one of two layouts, controlled by the `depositMenuDisplay` option. Use it to present payment options either as a single vertical list (the default) or split into **Use Crypto** and **Use Cash** tabs.

## Layouts

The `DepositMenuDisplay` enum has two cases:

```swift theme={null}
public enum DepositMenuDisplay: String {
    case stacked  // Default — all options in one list
    case tabs     // Split into "Use Crypto" / "Use Cash" tabs
}
```

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Stacked (default)">
    All available options are shown in a single vertical list:

    * Transfer Crypto
    * Deposit with Card
    * Pay with Cash App *(if `enablePayWithCashApp`)*
    * Connect Exchange *(if `enableConnectExchange`)*
    * Deposit Tracker *(unless `hideDepositTracker`)*
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Tabs">
    Options are grouped under two tabs, so the user first chooses how they want to pay:

    * **Use Crypto** — Transfer Crypto, and Connect Exchange *(if `enableConnectExchange`)*
    * **Use Cash** — Deposit with Card, and Pay with Cash App *(if `enablePayWithCashApp`)*

    The **Deposit Tracker** appears below the tabs in both layouts (unless `hideDepositTracker` is set). The **Use Crypto** tab is selected by default.
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Usage

`depositMenuDisplay` defaults to `.stacked`. Pass `.tabs` to enable the tabbed layout.

### Using the Deposit Sheet (SwiftUI)

```swift theme={null}
import UnifoldSDK

struct WalletView: View {
    @State private var showDeposit = false

    var body: some View {
        Button("Deposit") {
            showDeposit = true
        }
        .depositSheet(
            isPresented: $showDeposit,
            externalUserId: "user_123",
            publishableKey: "pk_live_your_key",
            recipientAddress: "0x...",
            destinationChainType: .ethereum,
            destinationChainId: "8453",
            destinationTokenAddress: "0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913",
            destinationTokenSymbol: "USDC",
            enablePayWithCashApp: true,
            depositMenuDisplay: .tabs
        )
    }
}
```

### Using DepositConfiguration

```swift theme={null}
let config = DepositConfiguration(
    externalUserId: "user_123",
    publishableKey: "pk_live_your_key",
    recipientAddress: "0x...",
    destinationChainType: .ethereum,
    destinationChainId: "8453",
    destinationTokenAddress: "0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913",
    enablePayWithCashApp: true,
    depositMenuDisplay: .tabs
)

.depositSheet(
    isPresented: $showDeposit,
    configuration: config,
    callbacks: DepositCallbacks()
)
```

## Configuration

| Parameter            | Type                 | Default    | Description                                                                                       |
| -------------------- | -------------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `depositMenuDisplay` | `DepositMenuDisplay` | `.stacked` | `.stacked` shows all options in a list; `.tabs` splits them into "Use Crypto" and "Use Cash" tabs |

<Note>
  The tabbed layout only changes how the existing options are grouped — it does not add or remove any. Which options appear is still controlled by `enablePayWithCashApp`, `enableConnectExchange`, and `hideDepositTracker`. The sheet height adjusts automatically to fit the active tab.
</Note>

<Tip>
  The tabbed layout works best when you have payment options on both sides — for example, Transfer Crypto on the **Use Crypto** tab and Deposit with Card and/or Cash App on the **Use Cash** tab. If you only enable crypto options, the `.stacked` layout is usually a better fit.
</Tip>

# Geo-Fencing

> Restrict access to deposits based on user location

## Overview

Geo-fencing allows you to restrict access to deposit features based on the user's geographic location. The SDK automatically detects the user's country using IP geolocation and checks it against your project's blocked countries list configured in the Unifold dashboard.

<Note>
  Blocked countries are configured in the [Unifold Dashboard](https://dashboard.unifold.io) under Project Settings.
</Note>

## Using AllowedCountryChecker

The `AllowedCountryChecker` is the Swift equivalent of the `useAllowedCountry` React hook. It provides a reactive way to check if the current user is in an allowed country.

### Basic Usage

```swift theme={null}
import SwiftUI
import UnifoldSDK

struct MyView: View {
    @StateObject private var countryChecker = AllowedCountryChecker()
    
    var body: some View {
        Group {
            if countryChecker.result.isLoading {
                ProgressView()
            } else if countryChecker.result.isAllowed == false {
                GeoBlockedView(country: countryChecker.result.country)
            } else {
                // Your main content
                DepositContent()
            }
        }
        .task {
            await countryChecker.check()
        }
    }
}
```

### With Publishable Key

If you need to pass a specific publishable key:

```swift theme={null}
@StateObject private var countryChecker = AllowedCountryChecker(publishableKey: "pk_live_xxx")

// Or pass it when checking
.task {
    await countryChecker.check(publishableKey: "pk_live_xxx")
}
```

## AllowedCountryResult

The `result` property returns an `AllowedCountryResult` struct with the following properties:

| Property    | Type      | Description                                        |
| ----------- | --------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `isAllowed` | `Bool?`   | Whether the user is allowed. `nil` while loading.  |
| `alpha2`    | `String?` | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g., "us", "gb") |
| `country`   | `String?` | Full country name (e.g., "United States")          |
| `isLoading` | `Bool`    | Whether the check is in progress                   |
| `error`     | `Error?`  | Error if the API calls failed                      |

## Static Method

For one-off checks outside of SwiftUI views, use the static method:

```swift theme={null}
let result = await AllowedCountryChecker.checkAllowedCountry()

if result.isAllowed == true {
    // User is in an allowed country
    proceedWithDeposit()
} else if result.isAllowed == false {
    // User is geo-blocked
    showBlockedMessage(country: result.country)
} else {
    // Error occurred
    handleError(result.error)
}
```

## View Modifier

For a more declarative approach, use the view modifier:

```swift theme={null}
struct ContentView: View {
    @StateObject private var countryChecker = AllowedCountryChecker()
    
    var body: some View {
        DepositContent()
            .checkAllowedCountry(using: countryChecker) { country in
                // This is shown when user is blocked
                VStack {
                    Image(systemName: "location.slash")
                    Text("Not Available")
                    Text("Deposits are not available in \(country ?? "your region")")
                }
            }
    }
}
```

## Caching Behavior

The checker caches the IP address and project config to avoid unnecessary API calls:

* Use `check()` for normal checks (uses cache if available)
* Use `refresh()` to force a fresh check, clearing the cache
* Use `clearCache()` to manually clear cached data

```swift theme={null}
// Force refresh
await countryChecker.refresh()

// Clear cache without checking
countryChecker.clearCache()
```

## Built-in Integration

The `DepositView` component has geo-fencing built-in. It automatically checks the user's location and displays a "No Tokens Available" screen if they're in a blocked country.

```swift theme={null}
DepositView(
    configuration: DepositConfiguration(
        externalUserId: "user_123",
        publishableKey: "pk_live_xxx"
    )
)
// Geo-fencing is handled automatically
```

# Installation

> Add UnifoldSDK to your iOS project

UnifoldSDK can be installed using Swift Package Manager (SPM), the recommended dependency manager for Swift projects.

## Swift Package Manager

### Using Xcode

1. Open your project in Xcode
2. Go to **File > Add Package Dependencies...**
3. Enter the repository URL:
   ```
   https://github.com/unifold-io/unifold-ios.git
   ```
4. Select the appropriate version and click **Add Package**
5. Select `UnifoldSDK` and add it to your target

To find the latest SDK version, see the [GitHub Releases page](https://github.com/unifold-io/unifold-ios/releases).

### Using Package.swift

If you're using a `Package.swift` file, add UnifoldSDK to your dependencies:

```swift theme={null}
// swift-tools-version:5.9
import PackageDescription

let package = Package(
    name: "YourApp",
    platforms: [
        .iOS(.v16)
    ],
    dependencies: [
        .package(url: "https://github.com/unifold-io/unifold-ios.git", from: "X.Y.Z") // Replace with the latest version
    ],
    targets: [
        .target(
            name: "YourApp",
            dependencies: ["UnifoldSDK"]
        )
    ]
)
```

## XCFramework

For projects that require a pre-compiled binary, you can use the XCFramework distribution:

1. Download the latest `UnifoldSDK.xcframework` from the releases page
2. Drag the framework into your Xcode project
3. In your target's **General** tab, ensure the framework is listed under **Frameworks, Libraries, and Embedded Content**
4. Set the embed option to **Embed & Sign**

## Requirements

| Requirement | Minimum Version |
| ----------- | --------------- |
| iOS         | 16.0            |
| Xcode       | 15.0            |
| Swift       | 5.9             |

## Import the SDK

After installation, import UnifoldSDK in any file where you need to use it:

```swift theme={null}
import UnifoldSDK
```

<Note>
  UnifoldSDK automatically imports `SwiftUI` and `Foundation` through `@_exported import`,
  so you don't need to import them separately in files where you import UnifoldSDK.
</Note>

## Verify Installation

To verify the SDK is installed correctly, you can check the version or try creating a basic configuration:

```swift theme={null}
import SwiftUI
import UnifoldSDK

struct TestView: View {
    var body: some View {
        Text("UnifoldSDK installed!")
            .onAppear {
                // Configure the SDK (optional, can also be done via depositSheet)
                configure(
                    publishableKey: "pk_test_your_key"
                )
            }
    }
}
```

## Troubleshooting

### Package Not Found

If Xcode can't find the package:

* Ensure you have an internet connection
* Check that the repository URL is correct
* Try **File > Packages > Reset Package Caches**

### Minimum Deployment Target

If you see errors about deployment target:

* Ensure your project's iOS Deployment Target is set to 16.0 or higher
* Check both the project and target settings

### Module Not Found

If you see "No such module 'UnifoldSDK'":

* Clean the build folder (**Product > Clean Build Folder**)
* Close and reopen Xcode
* Verify the package is listed in your project's Package Dependencies

</Card>

# Overview

> Integrate crypto deposits and fiat onramp into your iOS app with UnifoldSDK for Swift.

UnifoldSDK is a Swift package that provides a seamless crypto deposit and fiat onramp experience for iOS applications. With just a few lines of code, you can enable your users to:

* **Transfer Crypto** - Deposit crypto from any supported chain with automatic bridging
* **Buy with Card** - Purchase crypto using credit/debit cards through trusted providers
* **Track Deposits** - View deposit history and transaction status

## Features

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Easy Integration" icon="plug">
    Add deposits to your app with a single view modifier
  </Card>

  <Card title="Multi-Chain Support" icon="link">
    Support for Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, Base, Solana, and more
  </Card>

  <Card title="Fiat Onramp" icon="credit-card">
    Built-in card payment support
  </Card>

  <Card title="Native UI" icon="mobile">
    Beautiful SwiftUI components that match iOS design guidelines
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

## How It Works

1. **User initiates deposit** - Your app presents the deposit sheet
2. **User chooses method** - Transfer crypto or buy with card
3. **User completes deposit** - Funds are automatically bridged to the destination chain
4. **Callback fired** - Your app receives confirmation of the deposit

## Requirements

* iOS 16.0+
* Xcode 15.0+
* Swift 5.9+

# Quickstart

> Get started with UnifoldSDK in 5 minutes

This guide will help you integrate UnifoldSDK into your iOS app in just a few minutes.

## Prerequisites

Before you begin, make sure you have:

* An Xcode project targeting iOS 16.0+
* A Unifold publishable key from [dashboard.unifold.io](https://dashboard.unifold.io)

## Step 1: Install the SDK

Add UnifoldSDK to your project using Swift Package Manager. To find the latest version, see the [GitHub Releases page](https://github.com/unifold-io/unifold-ios/releases).

1. In Xcode, navigate to **File > Add Package Dependencies...**
2. Enter the repository URL: `https://github.com/unifold-io/unifold-ios.git`
3. Select the appropriate version and click **Add Package**

For full installation options, see the [Installation guide](/get-started/sdk-reference/ios-swift/installation).

## Step 2: Import the SDK

```swift theme={null}
import SwiftUI
import UnifoldSDK
```

## Step 3: Add the Deposit Sheet

The simplest way to add deposits is using the `.depositSheet()` view modifier:

```swift theme={null}
import SwiftUI
import UnifoldSDK

struct ContentView: View {
    @State private var showDeposit = false
    
    var body: some View {
        VStack {
            Button("Deposit") {
                showDeposit = true
            }
        }
        .depositSheet(
            isPresented: $showDeposit,
            externalUserId: "your_user_id",
            publishableKey: "pk_live_your_key",
            recipientAddress: "0x...",
            destinationChainType: .ethereum,
            destinationChainId: "137",
            destinationTokenAddress: "0x2791bca1f2de4661ed88a30c99a7a9449aa84174",
            destinationTokenSymbol: "USDC"
        )
    }
}
```

## Step 4: Handle Callbacks (Optional)

Add callbacks to respond to deposit events:

```swift theme={null}
.depositSheet(
    isPresented: $showDeposit,
    externalUserId: "your_user_id",
    publishableKey: "pk_live_your_key",
    recipientAddress: "0x...",
    destinationChainType: .ethereum,
    destinationChainId: "137",
    destinationTokenAddress: "0x2791bca1f2de4661ed88a30c99a7a9449aa84174",
    destinationTokenSymbol: "USDC",
    onDepositSuccess: { data in
        print("Deposit successful: \(data.message)")
        // Update your UI, refresh balances, etc.
    },
    onDepositError: { error in
        print("Deposit failed: \(error.message)")
    },
    onDismiss: {
        print("User closed the deposit sheet")
    }
)
```

## Complete Example

Here's a complete example you can copy into your project:

```swift theme={null}
import SwiftUI
import UnifoldSDK

struct DepositView: View {
    @State private var showDeposit = false
    @State private var lastDeposit: String?
    
    // Replace with your actual values
    let userId = "user_123"
    let publishableKey = "pk_live_your_key"
    let walletAddress = "0x80589dF3471B01c821a815Aa65C0b29008125be8"
    
    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 20) {
            if let deposit = lastDeposit {
                Text("Last deposit: \(deposit)")
                    .foregroundColor(.green)
            }
            
            Button(action: { showDeposit = true }) {
                HStack {
                    Image(systemName: "plus.circle.fill")
                    Text("Deposit")
                }
                .font(.headline)
                .foregroundColor(.white)
                .padding()
                .background(Color.blue)
                .cornerRadius(12)
            }
        }
        .depositSheet(
            isPresented: $showDeposit,
            externalUserId: userId,
            publishableKey: publishableKey,
            modalTitle: "Add Funds",
            recipientAddress: walletAddress,
            destinationChainType: .ethereum,
            destinationChainId: "137",
            destinationTokenAddress: "0x2791bca1f2de4661ed88a30c99a7a9449aa84174",
            destinationTokenSymbol: "USDC",
            onDepositSuccess: { data in
                lastDeposit = data.executionId
            }
        )
    }
}
```

# UI Theming

Customize colors, component styles, and typography to match your brand in the Unifold iOS SDK.

The Unifold iOS SDK ships with a native dark and light theme out of the box. You can customize the look and feel at two levels: **general palette theming** for broad color changes, and **component styles** for granular control over individual UI elements.

All customization is passed through a single `UnifoldAppearance` struct on the `depositSheet` modifier or `beginDeposit` call.

```swift theme={null}
.depositSheet(
    isPresented: $showDeposit,
    // ...required params...
    appearance: UnifoldAppearance(
        accentColor: "#007AFF"
    )
)
```

***

## Customization Options

<CardGroup cols={3}>
  <Card title="General Theming" icon="palette" href="#approach-1--general-theming">
    Set a full color palette for dark and/or light mode. Controls backgrounds, text, borders, and brand colors across the entire SDK in one place.
  </Card>

  <Card title="Component Styles" icon="sliders" href="#approach-2--component-styles">
    Override individual styles on cards, containers, buttons, inputs, and more. Use this for precise, per-element control beyond palette-level changes.
  </Card>

  <Card title="Custom Fonts" icon="font" href="#custom-fonts">
    Use your own typography. Pass font family names and the SDK applies them to all text throughout the deposit flow.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

***

## UnifoldAppearance

The top-level customization struct accepted by `depositSheet` and `beginDeposit`.

| Property          | Type                                                                           | Description                                                                        |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `accentColor`     | `String?`                                                                      | Global accent/primary color override (hex). Applied in both dark and light mode.   |
| `backgroundColor` | `String?`                                                                      | Global sheet background color override (hex). Applied in both dark and light mode. |
| `dark`            | `UnifoldColorPalette?`                                                         | Full color palette for dark mode.                                                  |
| `light`           | `UnifoldColorPalette?`                                                         | Full color palette for light mode.                                                 |
| `components`      | `UnifoldComponentConfig?`                                                      | Per-component style overrides (cards, header, buttons, inputs, etc.).              |
| `fonts`           | [`UnifoldFonts?`](/get-started/sdk-reference/ios-swift/ui-customization/fonts) | Custom font family names. Your app must register these fonts in its bundle.        |

***

## Approach 1 — General Theming

General theming gives you broad, consistent control. You provide one or both color palettes (`dark`, `light`) and the SDK applies them throughout every screen in the flow.

### Accent Color

The quickest way to apply your brand. Sets the primary action color — buttons, selected borders, checkmarks, and interactive icons — in both modes.

```swift theme={null}
let appearance = UnifoldAppearance(
    accentColor: "#6366F1"
)
```

### Custom Palette

For full control, supply a `UnifoldColorPalette` for dark mode, light mode, or both. Any property you omit falls back to the SDK default.

```swift theme={null}
let appearance = UnifoldAppearance(
    dark: UnifoldColorPalette(
        background: "#0F0F0F",
        card: "#1A1A1A",
        muted: "#2A2A2A",
        foreground: "#FFFFFF",
        mutedForeground: "#A0A0A0",
        border: "#2E2E2E",
        accent: "#1A1A2E",
        primary: "#6366F1",
        success: "#22C55E"
    ),
    light: UnifoldColorPalette(
        background: "#FFFFFF",
        card: "#F5F5F5",
        muted: "#E8E8E8",
        foreground: "#111111",
        mutedForeground: "#6B7280",
        border: "#D1D5DB",
        accent: "#EEF2FF",
        primary: "#6366F1",
        success: "#16A34A"
    )
)
```

### Palette properties

All values are hex strings (e.g. `"#007AFF"`). Every property is optional in the `init` — unset properties inherit from the SDK defaults below.

| Property            | Description                                  | Dark Default | Light Default |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ------------- |
| `background`        | Sheet / modal background                     | `#1C1C1E`    | `#FFFFFF`     |
| `card`              | Card and section backgrounds                 | `#2C2C2E`    | `#F2F2F7`     |
| `muted`             | Skeleton / disabled backgrounds              | `#3A3A3C`    | `#E5E5EA`     |
| `foreground`        | Primary text                                 | `#FFFFFF`    | `#000000`     |
| `mutedForeground`   | Secondary / supporting text                  | `#8E8E93`    | `#8E8E93`     |
| `foregroundSubtle`  | Tertiary / least-prominent text              | `#636366`    | `#AEAEB2`     |
| `border`            | Borders and dividers                         | `#38383A`    | `#C6C6C8`     |
| `accent`            | Selected-state background highlight          | `#2C2C2E`    | `#F2F2F7`     |
| `primary`           | Primary action color — buttons, links, icons | `#007AFF`    | `#007AFF`     |
| `primaryForeground` | Text rendered on primary-colored surfaces    | `#FFFFFF`    | `#FFFFFF`     |
| `success`           | Success / positive indicator color           | `#34C759`    | `#34C759`     |

<Info>
  `primary` and `success` are the most commonly customized properties. `primary` controls the Continue button, selected provider border, and interactive icons. `success` controls the provider highlight text and the deposit completion badge.
</Info>

***

## Approach 2 — Component styles

Component styles let you override individual design decisions per UI element type. They are set via `UnifoldComponentConfig` on the `components` property of `UnifoldAppearance`.

```swift theme={null}
let appearance = UnifoldAppearance(
    components: UnifoldComponentConfig(
        card: UnifoldCardTokens(borderRadius: 16),
        container: UnifoldContainerTokens(buttonColor: "#6366F1"),
        input: UnifoldInputTokens(borderRadius: 12)
    )
)
```

Component styles take priority over palette-level colors when both are set.

***

### Header styles

Controls the sheet header bar — the title text and back/close button icons.

```swift theme={null}
UnifoldHeaderTokens(
    titleColor: "#FFFFFF",
    buttonColor: "#8E8E93"
)
```

| Property      | Type      | Default      | Description                      |
| ------------- | --------- | ------------ | -------------------------------- |
| `titleColor`  | `String?` | `foreground` | Sheet title text color           |
| `buttonColor` | `String?` | `foreground` | Back and close button icon color |

***

### Card styles

Controls all card and section backgrounds throughout the deposit flow — provider rows, asset selector rows, transaction detail rows, and the flow diagram card.

```swift theme={null}
UnifoldCardTokens(
    borderRadius: 16,
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: "#3A3A3C",
    backgroundColor: "#2C2C2E",
    titleColor: "#FFFFFF",
    subtitleColor: "#8E8E93"
)
```

| Property              | Type      | Default                  | Description                                                 |
| --------------------- | --------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `borderRadius`        | `CGFloat` | `12`                     | Corner radius for cards                                     |
| `borderWidth`         | `CGFloat` | `0`                      | Card border width                                           |
| `borderColor`         | `String?` | `border`                 | Card border color                                           |
| `backgroundColor`     | `String?` | `card`                   | Card background color                                       |
| `titleColor`          | `String?` | `foreground`             | Primary text inside cards (asset names, amounts, values)    |
| `subtitleColor`       | `String?` | `mutedForeground`        | Secondary text inside cards (dates, labels, descriptions)   |
| `iconColor`           | `String?` | `primary`                | Leading icon color                                          |
| `actionColor`         | `String?` | `mutedForeground`        | Right-side chevron / action icon color                      |
| `textRightColor`      | `String?` | `foreground`             | Right-aligned primary value text (e.g. USDC amount)         |
| `subtextRightColor`   | `String?` | `mutedForeground`        | Right-aligned secondary value text (e.g. fee)               |
| `labelColor`          | `String?` | `mutedForeground`        | Field label text above inputs and selectors                 |
| `labelRightColor`     | `String?` | `mutedForeground`        | Right-aligned label text (e.g. "Refreshing in 60s")         |
| `headerColor`         | `String?` | `mutedForeground`        | Sub-header label inside a card (e.g. "Auto-picked for you") |
| `descriptionColor`    | `String?` | `mutedForeground`        | Body / disclaimer text inside cards                         |
| `rowLeftLabel`        | `String?` | `mutedForeground`        | Left label in detail rows (e.g. "Deposit tx")               |
| `rowRightLabel`       | `String?` | `foreground`             | Right value in detail rows                                  |
| `actionIcon`          | `String?` | `mutedForeground`        | External link / action icon in detail rows                  |
| `iconBackgroundColor` | `String?` | `primary` at 15% opacity | Icon circle background color                                |

***

### Container styles

Controls the bottom sheet container itself and the deposit status screens (pending, completed).

```swift theme={null}
UnifoldContainerTokens(
    borderRadius: 24,
    titleColor: "#FFFFFF",
    subtitleColor: "#8E8E93",
    buttonColor: "#6366F1",
    buttonTitleColor: "#FFFFFF",
    iconBackgroundColor: "#22C55E"
)
```

| Property              | Type      | Default           | Description                                       |
| --------------------- | --------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `borderRadius`        | `CGFloat` | `20`              | Bottom sheet corner radius                        |
| `borderWidth`         | `CGFloat` | `0`               | Sheet border width                                |
| `borderColor`         | `String?` | `border`          | Sheet border color                                |
| `backgroundColor`     | `String?` | `background`      | Sheet background color                            |
| `titleColor`          | `String?` | `foreground`      | Status title text (e.g. "Processing deposit…")    |
| `subtitleColor`       | `String?` | `mutedForeground` | Status subtitle / supporting text                 |
| `actionTitle`         | `String?` | `mutedForeground` | Expandable toggle label (e.g. "See more details") |
| `actionColor`         | `String?` | `mutedForeground` | Expandable toggle chevron icon color              |
| `buttonColor`         | `String?` | `primary`         | Continue / primary action button background       |
| `buttonTitleColor`    | `String?` | `foreground`      | Continue / primary action button text             |
| `iconBackgroundColor` | `String?` | `success`         | Completion badge background color                 |
| `iconColor`           | `String?` | `foreground`      | Fallback asset icon color                         |

***

### Button styles

Controls the standalone primary buttons (distinct from the container's Continue button).

```swift theme={null}
UnifoldButtonTokens(
    borderRadius: 14,
    borderWidth: 0
)
```

| Property          | Type      | Default   | Description             |
| ----------------- | --------- | --------- | ----------------------- |
| `borderRadius`    | `CGFloat` | `12`      | Button corner radius    |
| `borderWidth`     | `CGFloat` | `0`       | Button border width     |
| `borderColor`     | `String?` | `border`  | Button border color     |
| `backgroundColor` | `String?` | `primary` | Button background color |

***

### Input styles

Controls text fields and currency/amount selectors.

```swift theme={null}
UnifoldInputTokens(
    borderRadius: 10,
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: "#3A3A3C"
)
```

| Property          | Type      | Default  | Description                  |
| ----------------- | --------- | -------- | ---------------------------- |
| `borderRadius`    | `CGFloat` | `8`      | Input field corner radius    |
| `borderWidth`     | `CGFloat` | `1`      | Input field border width     |
| `borderColor`     | `String?` | `border` | Input field border color     |
| `backgroundColor` | `String?` | `card`   | Input field background color |

***

### Search styles

Controls the search field in currency and asset picker sheets.

```swift theme={null}
UnifoldSearchTokens(
    backgroundColor: "#1C1C1E",
    inputColor: "#FFFFFF",
    placeholderColor: "#8E8E93"
)
```

| Property           | Type      | Default           | Description                             |
| ------------------ | --------- | ----------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `placeholderColor` | `String?` | `mutedForeground` | Search placeholder text and icon color  |
| `backgroundColor`  | `String?` | `card`            | Search field background color           |
| `inputColor`       | `String?` | `foreground`      | Search input text color and cursor tint |

***

### List styles

Controls section headers inside list picker sheets (e.g. "Popular currencies", "All currencies").

```swift theme={null}
UnifoldListTokens(
    titleSectionColor: "#8E8E93"
)
```

| Property            | Type      | Default           | Description                |
| ------------------- | --------- | ----------------- | -------------------------- |
| `titleSectionColor` | `String?` | `mutedForeground` | Section header label color |

***

## Complete Example

The example below combines both approaches — a custom palette for broad color changes and component styles for precise overrides.

```swift theme={null}
import UnifoldSDK

let appearance = UnifoldAppearance(
    // Approach 1 — General palette
    dark: UnifoldColorPalette(
        background: "#0F0F0F",
        card: "#1A1A1A",
        muted: "#252525",
        foreground: "#FFFFFF",
        mutedForeground: "#9CA3AF",
        border: "#2A2A2A",
        accent: "#1C1C35",
        primary: "#6366F1",
        success: "#22C55E"
    ),
    light: UnifoldColorPalette(
        background: "#FFFFFF",
        card: "#F9FAFB",
        muted: "#F3F4F6",
        foreground: "#111827",
        mutedForeground: "#6B7280",
        border: "#E5E7EB",
        accent: "#EEF2FF",
        primary: "#6366F1",
        success: "#16A34A"
    ),
    // Approach 2 — Component styles
    components: UnifoldComponentConfig(
        card: UnifoldCardTokens(
            borderRadius: 16,
            borderWidth: 1
        ),
        container: UnifoldContainerTokens(
            borderRadius: 28,
            buttonColor: "#6366F1",
            buttonTitleColor: "#FFFFFF",
            iconBackgroundColor: "#22C55E"
        ),
        input: UnifoldInputTokens(
            borderRadius: 12,
            borderWidth: 1
        ),
        header: UnifoldHeaderTokens(
            titleColor: "#FFFFFF",
            buttonColor: "#9CA3AF"
        ),
        search: UnifoldSearchTokens(
            backgroundColor: "#1A1A1A",
            inputColor: "#FFFFFF",
            placeholderColor: "#6B7280"
        )
    ),
    // Custom fonts (your app must register these in Info.plist)

        regular: "Inter-Regular",

// Pass to depositSheet
```

***

## Theme Mode

Control whether the SDK renders in dark mode, light mode, or follows the system setting.

```swift theme={null}
.depositSheet(
    // ...
    theme: .dark   // .dark | .light | .auto
)
```

| Value    | Behavior                                        |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `.dark`  | Always render in dark mode                      |
| `.light` | Always render in light mode                     |
| `.auto`  | Follow the device's system appearance (default) |

<Tip>
  When using `.auto`, supply both `dark` and `light` palettes in your `UnifoldAppearance` to ensure consistent branding in both modes.
</Tip>

***

## Custom Fonts

The SDK supports custom fonts through the `fonts` property on `UnifoldAppearance`. Your app registers the fonts in its bundle (`Info.plist` → `UIAppFonts`), and you pass the PostScript font names to the SDK. If a font name isn't found at render time, the SDK falls back to the system font.

```swift theme={null}
let appearance = UnifoldAppearance(
    fonts: UnifoldFonts(
        regular: "Inter-Regular",
        medium: "Inter-Medium",
        semibold: "Inter-SemiBold",
        bold: "Inter-Bold"
    )
)
```

| Property   | Weight | Used For                                          |
| ---------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `regular`  | 400    | Body text, descriptions, input text, placeholders |
| `medium`   | 500    | Labels, section headers, emphasized text          |
| `semibold` | 600    | Modal titles, card titles, buttons, asset names   |
| `bold`     | 700    | Strong emphasis (rarely used)                     |

All properties are optional. Unset weights fall back to the next lighter weight you provided, and ultimately to the system font.

  Step-by-step setup, partial overrides, troubleshooting, and popular font recommendations.
</Card>

# Fonts

Use custom fonts to match your app's typography in the Unifold iOS SDK.

The Unifold iOS SDK supports custom fonts so the deposit flow matches your app's typography. Pass font family names through `UnifoldFonts` on `UnifoldAppearance` — the SDK uses them for all text throughout the flow.

Your app is responsible for registering the fonts in its bundle. The SDK does **not** load font files — it only references fonts by name at render time, falling back to the system font (San Francisco) for any weight you don't provide.

## Quick Start

```swift theme={null}
.depositSheet(
    isPresented: $showDeposit,
    // ...required params...
    appearance: UnifoldAppearance(
        fonts: UnifoldFonts(
            regular: "Inter-Regular",
            medium: "Inter-Medium",
            semibold: "Inter-SemiBold",
            bold: "Inter-Bold"
        )
    )
)
```

***

## Step 1 — Add Font Files to Your App

1. Drag your `.ttf` or `.otf` files into your Xcode project (e.g. into a `Fonts/` group).
2. Make sure **"Add to targets"** is checked for your app target.
3. Verify the files appear in **Build Phases → Copy Bundle Resources**.

***

## Step 2 — Register Fonts in Info.plist

Add a `UIAppFonts` (or "Fonts provided by application") entry listing each font file name:

```xml theme={null}
<key>UIAppFonts</key>
<array>
    <string>Inter-Regular.ttf</string>
    <string>Inter-Medium.ttf</string>
    <string>Inter-SemiBold.ttf</string>
    <string>Inter-Bold.ttf</string>
</array>
```

<Info>
  The file names in `UIAppFonts` must match exactly, including the extension. The font **family name** you pass to `UnifoldFonts` may differ from the file name — use Font Book or `UIFont.familyNames` to find the correct PostScript name.
</Info>

***

## Step 3 — Pass Font Names to the SDK

```swift theme={null}
let appearance = UnifoldAppearance(
    fonts: UnifoldFonts(
        regular: "Inter-Regular",
        medium: "Inter-Medium",
        semibold: "Inter-SemiBold",
        bold: "Inter-Bold"
    )
)

.depositSheet(
    isPresented: $showDeposit,
    externalUserId: "user_123",
    publishableKey: "pk_live_...",
    appearance: appearance
)
```

***

## UnifoldFonts Reference

All properties are optional. Unset weights fall back to the next lighter weight you provided, and ultimately to the system font.

```swift theme={null}
public struct UnifoldFonts {
    public var regular: String?   // 400 weight
    public var medium: String?    // 500 weight
    public var semibold: String?  // 600 weight
    public var bold: String?      // 700 weight
}
```

| Property   | Weight | Fallback Chain                             | Used For                                          |
| ---------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `regular`  | 400    | System font                                | Body text, descriptions, input text, placeholders |
| `medium`   | 500    | `regular` → system                         | Labels, section headers, emphasized text          |
| `semibold` | 600    | `medium` → `regular` → system              | Modal titles, card titles, buttons, asset names   |
| `bold`     | 700    | `semibold` → `medium` → `regular` → system | Strong emphasis (rarely used)                     |

***

## Single Font for All Weights

If your font family uses a single file (e.g. a variable font), pass the same name for every weight:

```swift theme={null}
UnifoldFonts(
    regular: "MyFont",
    medium: "MyFont",
    semibold: "MyFont",
    bold: "MyFont"
)
```

Or provide only `regular` — the SDK falls back to it for all heavier weights:

```swift theme={null}
UnifoldFonts(regular: "MyFont")
```

***

## Partial Overrides

You don't need to provide all four weights. For example, to only customize semibold (used for titles and buttons) while keeping the system font everywhere else:

```swift theme={null}
UnifoldFonts(semibold: "Poppins-SemiBold")
```

***

## Combining with Color Theming

Fonts work alongside all other appearance customization:

```swift theme={null}
let appearance = UnifoldAppearance(
    accentColor: "#6366F1",
    dark: UnifoldColorPalette(
        background: "#0F0F0F",
        primary: "#6366F1"
    ),
    components: UnifoldComponentConfig(
        card: UnifoldCardTokens(borderRadius: 16)
    ),
    fonts: UnifoldFonts(
        regular: "Inter-Regular",
        medium: "Inter-Medium",
        semibold: "Inter-SemiBold",
        bold: "Inter-Bold"
    )
)
```

***

## Using with UIKit Presentation

Fonts are also supported when presenting via `beginDeposit`:

```swift theme={null}
beginDeposit(
    externalUserId: "user_123",
    publishableKey: "pk_live_...",
    appearance: UnifoldAppearance(
        fonts: UnifoldFonts(
            regular: "Inter-Regular",
            medium: "Inter-Medium",
            semibold: "Inter-SemiBold",
            bold: "Inter-Bold"
        )
    )
)
```

***

## Troubleshooting

### Fonts not appearing

1. **Check Info.plist** — Every font file must be listed in `UIAppFonts`.
2. **Check Build Phases** — Font files must be in **Copy Bundle Resources** for your app target.
3. **Verify the font name** — The name you pass to `UnifoldFonts` is the PostScript name, not the file name. Find it with:

```swift theme={null}
// Print all available font names at launch
for family in UIFont.familyNames.sorted() {
    for name in UIFont.fontNames(forFamilyName: family) {
        print(name)
    }
}
```

4. **Clean build** — After adding fonts, do a clean build (`Cmd+Shift+K`) and run again.

### System font is still showing

The SDK validates each font name at render time using `UIFont(name:size:)`. If the name doesn't resolve to a registered font, it falls back to the system font silently. Double-check the PostScript name as described above.

### Fonts look different from your app

Make sure you're using the same PostScript font names your app uses. Some font families have different names for the same visual weight (e.g. `Inter-Regular` vs `Inter_400Regular`).

***

## Popular Font Recommendations

| Font       | Style             | Notes                                      |
| ---------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Inter      | Modern, clean     | Excellent for UI; similar to San Francisco |
| Poppins    | Geometric, modern | Great for bold headings                    |
| Nunito     | Rounded, friendly | Good for consumer-facing apps              |
| Lato       | Professional      | Works well at all sizes                    |
| Montserrat | Bold, impactful   | Strong titles and CTAs                     |

# UIKit Integration

> Using UnifoldSDK in UIKit applications

While UnifoldSDK is built with SwiftUI, it provides convenient APIs for UIKit-based applications.

## Using beginDeposit

The `beginDeposit` function allows you to present the deposit flow from any UIViewController:

```swift theme={null}
import UIKit
import UnifoldSDK

class WalletViewController: UIViewController {
    
    @IBAction func depositButtonTapped(_ sender: UIButton) {
        beginDeposit(
            from: self,
            externalUserId: "user_123",
            publishableKey: "pk_live_your_key",
            modalTitle: "Add Funds",
            onDepositSuccess: { [weak self] data in
                self?.handleDepositSuccess(data)
            },
            onDepositError: { [weak self] error in
                self?.handleDepositError(error)
            },
            onDismiss: { [weak self] in
                self?.handleDismiss()
            }
        )
    }
    
    private func handleDepositSuccess(_ data: DepositSuccessData) {
        // Refresh balance, show success message, etc.
        print("Deposit successful: \(data.message)")
    }
    
    private func handleDepositError(_ error: DepositErrorData) {
        // Show error alert
        let alert = UIAlertController(
            title: "Deposit Failed",
            message: error.message,
            preferredStyle: .alert
        )
        alert.addAction(UIAlertAction(title: "OK", style: .default))
        present(alert, animated: true)
    }
    
    private func handleDismiss() {
        // Optional cleanup
    }
}
```

## Auto-detecting the Presenter

If you don't pass a view controller, the SDK will automatically find the top-most view controller:

```swift theme={null}
// Presenter is auto-detected
beginDeposit(
    externalUserId: "user_123",
    publishableKey: "pk_live_your_key"
)
```

This is useful when calling from non-view controller contexts like app delegates or coordinators.

## Using in a Coordinator

```swift theme={null}
import UIKit
import UnifoldSDK

class WalletCoordinator {
    weak var navigationController: UINavigationController?
    
    init(navigationController: UINavigationController) {
        self.navigationController = navigationController
    }
    
    func showDeposit() {
        beginDeposit(
            from: navigationController,
            externalUserId: UserManager.shared.userId,
            publishableKey: AppConfig.unifoldKey,
            onDepositSuccess: { [weak self] data in
                self?.handleSuccess(data)
            }
        )
    }
    
    private func handleSuccess(_ data: DepositSuccessData) {
        // Navigate to success screen or refresh balance
        NotificationCenter.default.post(
            name: .depositCompleted,
            object: nil,
            userInfo: ["executionId": data.executionId ?? ""]
        )
    }
}

extension Notification.Name {
    static let depositCompleted = Notification.Name("depositCompleted")
}
```

## Embedding SwiftUI Views

For more control, you can embed the deposit view using `UIHostingController`:

```swift theme={null}
import UIKit
import SwiftUI
import UnifoldSDK

class DepositContainerViewController: UIViewController {
    
    override func viewDidLoad() {
        super.viewDidLoad()
        
        let config = DepositConfiguration(
            externalUserId: "user_123",
            publishableKey: "pk_live_your_key",
            modalTitle: "Deposit",
            recipientAddress: "0x...",
            destinationChainType: .ethereum,
            destinationChainId: "137",
            destinationTokenAddress: "0x2791bca1f2de4661ed88a30c99a7a9449aa84174"
        )
        
        let callbacks = DepositCallbacks(
            onDepositSuccess: { data in
                print("Success: \(data.message)")
            },
            onDismiss: { [weak self] in
                self?.dismiss(animated: true)
            }
        )
        
        // Create SwiftUI view with wrapper
        let depositView = DepositViewWrapper(
            config: config,
            callbacks: callbacks
        )
        
        let hostingController = UIHostingController(rootView: depositView)
        
        // Add as child view controller
        addChild(hostingController)
        view.addSubview(hostingController.view)
        hostingController.view.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
        
        NSLayoutConstraint.activate([
            hostingController.view.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: view.topAnchor),
            hostingController.view.bottomAnchor.constraint(equalTo: view.bottomAnchor),
            hostingController.view.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: view.leadingAnchor),
            hostingController.view.trailingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: view.trailingAnchor)
        ])
        
        hostingController.didMove(toParent: self)
    }
}

// SwiftUI wrapper
struct DepositViewWrapper: View {
    let config: DepositConfiguration
    let callbacks: DepositCallbacks
    
    @State private var isPresented = true
    
    var body: some View {
        Color.clear
            .depositSheet(
                isPresented: $isPresented,
                configuration: config,
                callbacks: callbacks
            )
    }
}
```

## Presenting as Bottom Sheet

The `beginDeposit` function automatically configures the sheet presentation:

* Uses medium and large detents
* Hidden drag indicator
* 20pt corner radius

If you need custom sheet configuration:

```swift theme={null}
func presentDepositSheet() {
    let depositView = /* Create your SwiftUI view */
    let hostingController = UIHostingController(rootView: depositView)
    
    if let sheet = hostingController.sheetPresentationController {
        sheet.detents = [.medium(), .large()]
        sheet.prefersGrabberVisible = false
        sheet.preferredCornerRadius = 20
        sheet.prefersScrollingExpandsWhenScrolledToEdge = false
    }
    
    present(hostingController, animated: true)
}
```

## Objective-C Compatibility

For Objective-C projects, create a Swift wrapper:

```swift theme={null}
// DepositBridge.swift
import Foundation
import UnifoldSDK

@objc public class UnifoldBridge: NSObject {
    
    @objc public static func showDeposit(
        from viewController: UIViewController,
        userId: String,
        publishableKey: String,
        onSuccess: @escaping (String) -> Void,
        onError: @escaping (String) -> Void
    ) {
        beginDeposit(
            from: viewController,
            externalUserId: userId,
            publishableKey: publishableKey,
            onDepositSuccess: { data in
                onSuccess(data.message)
            },
            onDepositError: { error in
                onError(error.message)
            }
        )
    }
}
```

Then call from Objective-C:

```objc theme={null}
// MyViewController.m
#import "YourProject-Swift.h"

- (IBAction)depositTapped:(id)sender {
    [UnifoldBridge showDepositFrom:self
                           userId:@"user_123"
                   publishableKey:@"pk_live_your_key"
                        onSuccess:^(NSString *message) {
        NSLog(@"Success: %@", message);
    }
                          onError:^(NSString *error) {
        NSLog(@"Error: %@", error);
    }];
}
```

## Thread Safety

All UI operations are performed on the main thread. The `beginDeposit` function is marked with `@MainActor`, so it must be called from the main thread:

```swift theme={null}
// Correct - on main thread
DispatchQueue.main.async {
    beginDeposit(...)
}

// Or use Task with MainActor
Task { @MainActor in
    beginDeposit(...)
}
```

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.unifold.io/llms.txt

# Overview

The Withdraw flow enables users to send crypto from your platform back to an external wallet address. Users select a destination token, enter an amount and recipient address, confirm in a sheet, and Unifold handles routing, tracking, and confirmation callbacks.

## How it works

1. Your app calls `.withdrawSheet()` (SwiftUI) or `beginWithdraw()` (UIKit) with the source token, the user's sender address, and a `withdraw` closure
2. Unifold opens a bottom sheet where the user selects a destination token, enters an amount, and provides a recipient address
3. When the user confirms, Unifold calls your `withdraw` closure with the full transaction details (`WithdrawTransactionInfo`)
4. Your app signs and broadcasts the transaction using your own wallet infrastructure
5. Unifold tracks the withdrawal and fires `onSuccess` or `onError` when it resolves

<Note>
  The iOS Swift SDK is **wallet-agnostic**. `senderAddress` is a plain string used only to fetch the user's balance — the SDK has no knowledge of or dependency on any wallet library. You own the signing and broadcasting logic entirely inside the `withdraw` closure.
</Note>

## Prerequisites

Add UnifoldSDK to your project using Swift Package Manager. Requires iOS 16.0+. To find the latest version, see the [GitHub Releases page](https://github.com/unifold-io/unifold-ios/releases).

1. In Xcode, navigate to **File > Add Package Dependencies...**
2. Enter the repository URL: `https://github.com/unifold-io/unifold-ios.git`
3. Select the appropriate version and click **Add Package**

For full installation options, see the [Installation guide](/get-started/sdk-reference/ios-swift/installation).

## Quick start

### SwiftUI — `.withdrawSheet()`

Use the `.withdrawSheet()` view modifier to present the withdraw flow as a bottom sheet:

```swift theme={null}
import SwiftUI
import UnifoldSDK

struct WalletView: View {
    @State private var showWithdraw = false

    // Replace with your actual values
    let userId = "user_123"
    let publishableKey = "pk_live_your_key"
    let walletAddress = "0x80589dF3471B01c821a815Aa65C0b29008125be8"

    var body: some View {
        Button("Withdraw") {
            showWithdraw = true
        }
        .withdrawSheet(
            isPresented: $showWithdraw,
            externalUserId: userId,
            publishableKey: publishableKey,
            senderAddress: walletAddress,

            // Source token — what the user is sending from
            sourceChainType: .ethereum,
            sourceChainId: "8453",        // Base
            sourceTokenAddress: "0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913",
            sourceTokenSymbol: "USDC",

            // Your app signs and broadcasts the transaction
            withdraw: { txInfo in
                // See Withdraw Functions for a ready-to-use Privy implementation
                try await myWallet.signAndBroadcast(txInfo)
            },

            onSuccess: { data in print("Withdrawal complete: \(data.message)") },
            onError: { err in print("Withdrawal failed: \(err.message)") },
            onClose: { print("Sheet dismissed") }
        )
    }
}
```

### SwiftUI — full configuration object

For reusable or complex setups, build a `WithdrawConfiguration` and `WithdrawCallbacks` separately:

```swift theme={null}
let config = WithdrawConfiguration(
    externalUserId: userId,
    publishableKey: publishableKey,
    senderAddress: walletAddress,
    sourceChainType: .ethereum,
    sourceChainId: "8453",
    sourceTokenAddress: "0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913",
    sourceTokenSymbol: "USDC",
    withdraw: { txInfo in
        try await myWallet.signAndBroadcast(txInfo)
    }
)

let callbacks = WithdrawCallbacks(
    onSuccess: { data in handleSuccess(data) },
    onError: { err in handleError(err) },
    onClose: { handleDismiss() }
)

// Apply to any view
someView.withdrawSheet(
    isPresented: $showWithdraw,
    configuration: config,
    callbacks: callbacks
)
```

### UIKit — `beginWithdraw()`

For UIKit apps, call `beginWithdraw()` directly. It presents the sheet from the top-most view controller by default:

```swift theme={null}
import UnifoldSDK

@MainActor
func showWithdrawSheet() {
    beginWithdraw(
        externalUserId: "user_123",
        publishableKey: "pk_live_your_key",
        senderAddress: walletAddress,
        sourceChainType: .ethereum,
        sourceChainId: "8453",
        sourceTokenAddress: "0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913",
        sourceTokenSymbol: "USDC",

        withdraw: { txInfo in
            try await myWallet.signAndBroadcast(txInfo)
        },

        onSuccess: { data in print("Withdrawal complete: \(data.message)") },
        onError: { err in print("Withdrawal failed: \(err.message)") },
        onClose: { print("Sheet dismissed") }
    )
}
```

Pass a `from: viewController` parameter to control which view controller presents the sheet.

***

## WithdrawConfiguration

<ParamField path="externalUserId" type="String" required>
  Your platform's unique user identifier.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="publishableKey" type="String" required>
  Your Unifold publishable key from [dashboard.unifold.io](https://dashboard.unifold.io).
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="senderAddress" type="String" required>
  The user's wallet address. Used only to fetch balance for display — wallet-agnostic, pass any address string.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="sourceChainType" type="ChainType" required>
  Source token chain type. Accepted values: `.ethereum`, `.solana`, `.bitcoin`.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="sourceChainId" type="String" required>
  Source token chain ID (e.g. `"8453"` for Base, `"1"` for Ethereum mainnet). See [Supported Chains](/get-started/supported-chains).
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="sourceTokenAddress" type="String" required>
  Contract address of the token the user is sending. Use `"native"` for the chain's native currency (ETH, MATIC, etc.).
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="sourceTokenSymbol" type="String?">
  Token symbol for display (e.g. `"USDC"`). Inferred from the API if omitted.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="recipientAddress" type="String?">
  Pre-fills the recipient address field in the sheet.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="modalTitle" type="String">
  Custom title for the sheet. Defaults to `"Withdraw Crypto"`.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="theme" type="UnifoldTheme">
  Color scheme to use. Accepted values: `.dark` (default), `.light`, `.auto` (follows system).
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="appearance" type="UnifoldAppearance?">
  Fine-grained appearance customization (accent color, color palette, component tokens). See [Theming](/get-started/sdk-reference/ios-swift/theming).
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="withdraw" type="(WithdrawTransactionInfo) async throws -> Void" required>
  Called when the user confirms the withdrawal. Your app must sign and broadcast the transaction — Unifold never holds a private key. Throw an error to surface a message in the sheet. See [Withdraw Functions](/get-started/sdk-reference/ios-swift/withdraw/withdraw-functions) for implementations.
</ParamField>

***

## WithdrawCallbacks

All three callbacks are optional. Pass them as inline parameters on `.withdrawSheet()` / `beginWithdraw()`, or group them in a `WithdrawCallbacks` struct when using the configuration object form.

<ParamField path="onSuccess" type="((WithdrawSuccessData) -> Void)?">
  Fired when the withdrawal execution reaches a succeeded state.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onError" type="((WithdrawErrorData) -> Void)?">
  Fired when an error occurs during the withdrawal.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onClose" type="(() -> Void)?">
  Fired when the user dismisses the withdraw sheet.
</ParamField>

***

## WithdrawTransactionInfo

The object passed to your `withdraw` closure.

```swift theme={null}
public struct WithdrawTransactionInfo: Sendable {
    public let senderAddress: String
    public let sourceChainType: String
    public let sourceChainId: String
    public let sourceTokenAddress: String
    public let sourceTokenSymbol: String
    public let destinationChainType: String
    public let destinationChainId: String
    public let destinationTokenAddress: String
    public let destinationTokenSymbol: String
    public let amount: String           // human-readable, e.g. "1.50"
    public let amountBaseUnit: String   // exact, e.g. "1500000" for 1.5 USDC (6 decimals)
    public let withdrawIntentAddress: String
    public let recipientAddress: String
    public let submittedAt: Date?       // when the user confirmed the withdrawal
}
```

| Field                   | Description                                                                                                           |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `senderAddress`         | The user's wallet address — use as the `from` field when constructing the transaction.                                |
| `withdrawIntentAddress` | **The address your app must transfer funds to.** This is Unifold's intent address — not the user's final destination. |
| `amountBaseUnit`        | Use this for the transaction — it is exact. `amount` is for display only.                                             |
| `recipientAddress`      | The user's final destination. For display/logging only — do not send funds here directly.                             |
| `submittedAt`           | When the user confirmed the withdrawal. Shown in the confirming and details screens.                                  |
