# Pay with Apple Pay

> Instant USD deposits via a headless Coinbase Apple Pay onramp.

**Pay with Apple Pay** lets your users buy crypto instantly with Apple Pay, powered by a **headless Coinbase onramp**. The SDK runs the entire flow in-app — contact verification, amount entry, the Apple Pay sheet, and on-chain settlement — without sending the user to an external browser.

Unlike Stripe Onramp, this flow has **no standalone component**: you enable it inside the built-in **deposit menu** (`beginDeposit`) via a single `UnifoldProvider` config flag. It is **iOS only**.

## Prerequisites

<Steps>
  <Step title="Coinbase onramp in the Unifold Dashboard">
    Enable the **Pay with Apple Pay** onramp for your project and connect Coinbase. See the [Coinbase integration guide](/developer/integrations/coinbase). Availability is also geo-gated per region (see [Availability & gating](#availability--gating)).
  </Step>

  <Step title="Install peer dependencies in your app">
    The flow renders the Apple Pay sheet inside a `WebView`, so **`react-native-webview`** must be installed in your app alongside the other peers listed in [Installation](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/installation) (gesture handler, SVG, Async Storage). No `@stripe/stripe-react-native` or native Onramp module is required for this flow.
  </Step>

  <Step title="iOS build">
    Apple Pay is presented natively inside a `WebView` — no extra Apple Pay entitlement or `merchantIdentifier` is required in your `app.json` for this flow. Run on a **physical iOS device** with a card in Wallet to test (the Apple Pay sheet is unavailable in the Simulator).
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Note>
  This option is **iOS only** — `Platform.OS === 'ios'`. It never appears on Android.
</Note>

## How it works

<Steps>
  <Step title="User enters email">
    The user provides an email (or it's prefilled and trusted — see [Skipping the email step](#skipping-the-email-step)). Coinbase legal agreements are shown.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Phone verification">
    The user enters a phone number and verifies it with a one-time code. Phone verification is always required (Coinbase's 60-day freshness rule).
  </Step>

  <Step title="User enters amount">
    An amount screen with a numpad and quick-pick amounts ($25, $100, $250, $500) is shown. A payment session is created for the entered amount.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Apple Pay">
    The native Apple Pay sheet is presented (inside an embedded `WebView`). The user authorizes the purchase with Face ID / Touch ID.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Deposit is settled on-chain">
    The SDK polls the on-chain execution — this is the source of truth for success, not Coinbase's payment messages. `onSuccess` fires once the crypto is delivered to the destination address.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Note>
  If a guest-checkout limit is reached, the flow offers an in-app limit-upgrade step (date of birth + last 4 of SSN) before continuing.
</Note>

## Availability & gating

The **Pay with Apple Pay** row appears only when **all** of these are true:

1. The platform is iOS (`Platform.OS === 'ios'`).
2. The option is enabled: `config.enableCoinbaseApplePay (SDK flag) ?? dashboard "Pay with Apple Pay" toggle ?? false`. Like Cash App and Connect Wallet, it's **opt-in** — enable it on the dashboard or via the SDK flag.
3. The geo-gated providers check returns an enabled provider for the user's region.

Because availability depends on a live providers check, the row may not appear even when the toggle is on (for example, in an unsupported region, or on Android).

## Enable it in the deposit menu

Set **`enableCoinbaseApplePay: true`** on `UnifoldProvider` **`config`** (not on `beginDeposit`):

```tsx app/_layout.tsx theme={null}
import { UnifoldProvider } from '@unifold/connect-react-native';

export default function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <UnifoldProvider
      publishableKey="pk_live_your_key"
      config={{ enableCoinbaseApplePay: true }}
    >
      <App />
    </UnifoldProvider>
  );
}
```

Then open the deposit menu from anywhere with the `useUnifold` hook:

```tsx DepositButton.tsx theme={null}
import { useUnifold } from '@unifold/connect-react-native';

export function DepositButton() {
  const { beginDeposit } = useUnifold();

  return (
    <Button
      title="Deposit"
      onPress={() =>
        beginDeposit({
          externalUserId: 'user_123',
          recipientAddress: '0x…',
          destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
          destinationChainId: '8453',
          destinationTokenAddress: '0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913',
          destinationTokenSymbol: 'USDC',
          onSuccess: (result) => console.log('Deposit complete', result.executionId),
        })
      }
    />
  );
}
```

### Open Apple Pay directly

To skip the deposit menu and land straight on the Apple Pay flow, pass **`initialScreen: 'apple_pay'`** on `beginDeposit`:

```tsx theme={null}
await beginDeposit({
  externalUserId: 'user_123',
  recipientAddress: '0x…',
  destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
  destinationChainId: '8453',
  destinationTokenAddress: '0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913',
  destinationTokenSymbol: 'USDC',
  initialScreen: 'apple_pay',
});
```

Closing a direct-entry Apple Pay screen dismisses the entire deposit flow. If Apple Pay isn't available (Android or gated off), the flow falls back to the main deposit menu. See [Initial Screen](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/initial-screen).

## Skipping the email step

Pass a **host-trusted email** via the **`user`** object on `beginDeposit` to skip the email-entry and email-OTP steps. The user then only needs to verify their phone.

```tsx theme={null}
await beginDeposit({
  externalUserId: 'user_123',
  recipientAddress: '0x…',
  destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
  destinationChainId: '8453',
  destinationTokenAddress: '0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913',
  destinationTokenSymbol: 'USDC',
  user: { email: 'jane@example.com' },
});
```

| Field        | Type      | Effect                                                                                                  |
| ------------ | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `user.email` | `string?` | When set and valid, the email-entry and email-OTP steps are **skipped**. Phone verification still runs. |

<Note>
  `user` is set on each **`beginDeposit`** call, not on `UnifoldProvider`. The same object also powers **Pay with Link** (Stripe) prefill — see [useUnifold](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/use-unifold) for the full `UnifoldUser` shape.
</Note>

## Configuration

| Parameter                            | Where                            | Type                  | Default                 | Description                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- | --------------------- | ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `enableCoinbaseApplePay`             | `UnifoldProvider` `config`       | `boolean?`            | dashboard, else `false` | Overrides the dashboard "Pay with Apple Pay" toggle. Resolves as `flag ?? dashboard ?? false` (opt-in), still gated by iOS and provider availability. |
| `user`                               | `beginDeposit` (`DepositConfig`) | `UnifoldUser?`        | —                       | Host user context; a trusted `user.email` skips the email-verification steps.                                                                         |
| `initialScreen`                      | `beginDeposit` (`DepositConfig`) | `'apple_pay'`         | `'main'`                | Open the Apple Pay flow directly instead of the deposit menu.                                                                                         |
| `sheetBorderRadius.coinbaseApplePay` | `UnifoldProvider` `config`       | `BorderRadiusConfig?` | —                       | Per-sheet top corner radius for the Apple Pay sheet. See [Border Radius](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/ui-customization/border-radius).     |

### Amounts

| Value       | Default             | Description                                                    |
| ----------- | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Minimum     | `$5`                | Minimum USD purchase (fallback if API limits are unavailable). |
| Maximum     | `$500`              | Maximum USD purchase (fallback).                               |
| Quick picks | `25, 100, 250, 500` | Suggested amounts on the numpad screen.                        |

## Handling results

Results are delivered through the standard deposit callbacks on `DepositConfig` (and the `Promise` returned by `beginDeposit`). See [Handling results](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/handling-results).

<ParamField path="onSuccess" type="(data: DepositResult) => void">
  Fires when the on-chain execution reaches **succeeded** status — the purchased crypto has been delivered to the destination address. `data.executionId` is the unique execution ID and `data.transaction` carries the full execution details.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onError" type="(error: DepositError) => void">
  Fires for sheet-level errors. Verification and payment failures are handled inline in the UI with retry options, so most transient issues never reach this callback.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onDismiss" type="() => void">
  Fires when the user dismisses the deposit flow.
</ParamField>

```tsx theme={null}
await beginDeposit({
  externalUserId: 'user_123',
  recipientAddress: '0x…',
  destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
  destinationChainId: '8453',
  destinationTokenAddress: '0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913',
  destinationTokenSymbol: 'USDC',
  onSuccess: (data) => {
    // data.message      -> "Deposit completed successfully"
    // data.executionId  -> unique execution ID
    // data.transaction  -> full execution details
    refreshBalance();
  },
  onDismiss: () => console.log('user closed the deposit flow'),
});
```

## Customize the sheet

Round the Apple Pay sheet's top corners with `sheetBorderRadius.coinbaseApplePay`:

```tsx theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey="pk_live_your_key"
  config={{
    enableCoinbaseApplePay: true,
    sheetBorderRadius: {
      coinbaseApplePay: { borderTopLeftRadius: 24, borderTopRightRadius: 24 },
    },
  }}
>
  <App />
</UnifoldProvider>
```

See [Border Radius](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/ui-customization/border-radius) for the full resolution order.

## Flow states

| Screen                          | Description                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Email Input**                 | Collect email + Coinbase legal agreements (skipped when a trusted `user.email` is provided). |
| **Phone Input / OTP**           | Collect and verify the phone number.                                                         |
| **Amount**                      | Numpad + quick-pick amounts; the payment session is created.                                 |
| **Apple Pay**                   | Native Apple Pay sheet inside a `WebView`.                                                   |
| **Checking Deposit**            | Polling the on-chain execution.                                                              |
| **Success**                     | Execution succeeded; the deposit detail screen is shown.                                     |
| **Guest Limit / Limit Upgrade** | DOB + SSN (last 4) upgrade when guest-checkout caps are hit.                                 |

## Webhooks

On-chain settlement is the source of truth for success. For reliable server-side confirmation, listen for deposit webhook events rather than relying solely on the client callback. See [Deposit Webhooks](/developer/webhooks/events/deposit).

# Geo-Fencing

> Restrict access to deposit features based on user location

# Geo-Fencing with useAllowedCountry

The `useAllowedCountry` hook allows you to check if a user is accessing your app from a permitted location. This is useful for compliance with regional regulations or to restrict access to certain features based on geography.

## How It Works

The hook combines two API calls:

1. **IP Geolocation** - Determines the user's country based on their IP address
2. **Project Configuration** - Fetches your project's list of blocked countries

If the user's country appears in the blocked list, `isAllowed` returns `false`.

## Installation

The hook is included in the `@unifold/connect-react-native` package:

```bash theme={null}
npm install @unifold/connect-react-native
```

## Basic Usage

```tsx theme={null}
import { useAllowedCountry } from "@unifold/connect-react-native";

function DepositScreen() {
  const { isAllowed, isLoading, country, error } = useAllowedCountry("pk_live_your_key");

  if (isLoading) {
    return <ActivityIndicator />;
  }

  if (error) {
    return <Text>Unable to verify location</Text>;
  }

  if (!isAllowed) {
    return (
      <View>
        <Text>Service Unavailable</Text>
        <Text>This feature is not available in {country}.</Text>
      </View>
    );
  }

  return <YourDepositComponent />;
}
```

## API Reference

### Parameters

| Parameter        | Type      | Required | Description                                |
| ---------------- | --------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `publishableKey` | `string`  | Yes      | Your Unifold publishable key               |
| `enabled`        | `boolean` | No       | Whether to run the check (default: `true`) |

### Return Value

The hook returns an `AllowedCountryResult` object:

```typescript theme={null}
interface AllowedCountryResult {
  /** Whether the user is in an allowed country. null while loading. */
  isAllowed: boolean | null;
  
  /** ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code in lowercase (e.g., "us", "pt") */
  alpha2: string | null;
  
  /** Full country name (e.g., "United States", "Portugal") */
  country: string | null;
  
  /** Whether the hook is still loading data */
  isLoading: boolean;
  
  /** Error if either API call failed */
  error: Error | null;
}
```

## Advanced Usage

### Conditional Check

You can disable the geo-check until needed:

```tsx theme={null}
const [shouldCheck, setShouldCheck] = useState(false);
const { isAllowed, isLoading } = useAllowedCountry(publishableKey, shouldCheck);

// Trigger check when user attempts to access restricted feature
const handleDepositPress = () => {
  setShouldCheck(true);
};
```

### With UnifoldProvider

The `DepositModal` component automatically performs geo-fencing. If you're using `beginDeposit()` from the `useUnifold` hook, geo-restriction is handled for you:

```tsx theme={null}
import { UnifoldProvider, useUnifold } from "@unifold/connect-react-native";

function App() {
  return (
    <UnifoldProvider publishableKey="pk_live_your_key">
      <DepositButton />
    </UnifoldProvider>
  );
}

function DepositButton() {
  const { beginDeposit } = useUnifold();
  
  // Geo-fencing is automatically applied when the modal opens
  return (
    <Button onPress={() => beginDeposit({ externalUserId: "user_123" })}>
      Deposit
    </Button>
  );
}
```

### Custom Blocked Message

Display a custom message based on the user's location:

```tsx theme={null}
function GeoBlockedView() {
  const { country, alpha2 } = useAllowedCountry(publishableKey);
  
  return (
    <View style={styles.container}>
      <MapPinOffIcon size={48} color="#666" />
      <Text style={styles.title}>Service Unavailable</Text>
      <Text style={styles.description}>
        Unfortunately, our deposit services are not available in {country}.
        Please contact support if you believe this is an error.
      </Text>
    </View>
  );
}
```

## Configuring Blocked Countries

Blocked countries are configured in the [Unifold Dashboard](https://dashboard.unifold.io) under **Country Restrictions**.

To manage your geo-fencing rules:

1. Navigate to [dashboard.unifold.io](https://dashboard.unifold.io)
2. Go to **Country Restrictions** in the sidebar
3. Add or remove countries from your blocked list
4. Changes take effect immediately for all users

<Note>
  The geo-check is based on IP address geolocation, which may not be 100% accurate for users on VPNs or proxy services.
</Note>

## Best Practices

1. **Show loading state** - Always display a loading indicator while `isLoading` is true
2. **Handle errors gracefully** - If the geo-check fails, decide whether to block or allow access
3. **Provide clear messaging** - Tell users why they're blocked and how to get help
4. **Cache results** - The hook caches results for the session to avoid repeated API calls

# Initial Screen

> Open the deposit flow directly on Transfer Crypto, Buy with Card, or Deposit Tracker instead of the main menu.

## Overview

By default, `beginDeposit()` opens the **deposit menu** — a list of options (Transfer Crypto, Buy with Card, Deposit Tracker, and optional Stripe Link Pay). For embedded flows where the path is already decided, you can skip that menu entirely and open a **specific screen** using `initialScreen`.

## `initialScreen` on `beginDeposit`

Pass `initialScreen` to any `beginDeposit()` call:

```ts theme={null}
type DepositInitialScreen =
  | 'main'
  | 'transfer'
  | 'card'
  | 'tracker'
  | 'cashapp'
  | 'wallet'
  | 'apple_pay'
  | 'stripe_link';
```

| Value                | Opens                                                                                     | Falls back to `'main'` when                              |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `'main'` *(default)* | Deposit menu                                                                              | —                                                        |
| `'transfer'`         | Transfer Crypto form                                                                      | `enableTransferCrypto` disabled                          |
| `'card'`             | Buy with Card form                                                                        | `enableFiatOnramp` disabled                              |
| `'tracker'`          | Deposit Tracker                                                                           | `hideDepositTracker` is `true`                           |
| `'cashapp'`          | Pay with Cash App                                                                         | `enableCashApp` disabled                                 |
| `'wallet'`           | Connect Wallet                                                                            | `enableConnectWallet` disabled                           |
| `'apple_pay'`        | [Pay with Apple Pay](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/coinbase-apple-pay) | Android, gated off, or `enableCoinbaseApplePay` disabled |
| `'stripe_link'`      | [Pay with Link](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/stripe-onramp/overview)  | `enableStripeLink` disabled                              |

When a sub-screen is the entry point, there is **no "back to menu"** — closing the sheet dismisses the entire deposit flow. This is intentional: the menu was never shown, so there is nothing to go back to.

<Note>
  If `hideDepositTracker: true` is set on the provider and you pass `initialScreen: 'tracker'`, the tracker is suppressed and the flow falls back to `'main'`. The same fallback applies to any screen whose feature is disabled — e.g. `'apple_pay'` on Android or `'stripe_link'` without `config.enableStripeLink`.
</Note>

## Usage

```tsx theme={null}
import { useUnifold, type DepositInitialScreen } from '@unifold/connect-react-native';

const { beginDeposit } = useUnifold();

// Open Transfer Crypto immediately
await beginDeposit({
  externalUserId: 'user_123',
  destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
  destinationChainId: '137',
  destinationTokenAddress: '0x2791bca1f2de4661ed88a30c99a7a9449aa84174',
  destinationTokenSymbol: 'USDC',
  recipientAddress: '0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc9e7595f0bEb2',
  initialScreen: 'transfer',
});
```

## Examples

### Transfer Crypto only

Useful when users have already selected a token or you want to remove the choice layer.

```tsx theme={null}
await beginDeposit({
  externalUserId: user.id,
  destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
  destinationChainId: '8453',
  destinationTokenAddress: '0x833589fcd6edb6e08f4c7c32d4f71b54bda02913',
  destinationTokenSymbol: 'USDC',
  recipientAddress: user.walletAddress,
  initialScreen: 'transfer',
});
```

### Buy with Card only

```tsx theme={null}
await beginDeposit({
  externalUserId: user.id,
  destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
  destinationChainId: '137',
  destinationTokenAddress: '0x2791bca1f2de4661ed88a30c99a7a9449aa84174',
  destinationTokenSymbol: 'USDC',
  recipientAddress: user.walletAddress,
  initialScreen: 'card',
});
```

### Deposit Tracker

Open directly to the user's deposit history — no active deposit required.

```tsx theme={null}
await beginDeposit({
  externalUserId: user.id,
  initialScreen: 'tracker',
});
```

### Dynamic initial screen

```tsx theme={null}
type DepositPath = 'transfer' | 'card';

function openDeposit(path: DepositPath) {
  beginDeposit({
    externalUserId: user.id,
    destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
    destinationChainId: '137',
    destinationTokenAddress: '0x2791bca1f2de4661ed88a30c99a7a9449aa84174',
    destinationTokenSymbol: 'USDC',
    recipientAddress: user.walletAddress,
    initialScreen: path,
  });
}

// In your UI
<Button onPress={() => openDeposit('transfer')} title="Pay with crypto" />
<Button onPress={() => openDeposit('card')} title="Pay with card" />
```

## Geo-fencing

Country restrictions apply to `'transfer'` and `'card'` initial screens exactly as they do when those screens are reached through the main menu. If a user's country is blocked, the sheet opens but shows a "No Tokens Available" message instead of the form.

The `'tracker'` screen is always accessible regardless of country restrictions — deposit history is not geo-gated.

See [Geo-Fencing](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/geo-fencing) for configuration details.

## Comparison with the web SDK

The React Native `initialScreen` behaviour matches the [web standalone entry screens](/developer/deposit/entry-screens) with one difference: React Native does **not** have a `defaultInitialScreen` on the provider. If you want a consistent entry point across all calls, pass `initialScreen` explicitly on each `beginDeposit()`.

# Configuration

> Configure Pay with Link (Stripe) with the enableStripeLink flag and beginDeposit.

Pay with Link is enabled entirely through configuration — there is no standalone component to render. Turn it on with **`config.enableStripeLink`** on `UnifoldProvider`, then open the flow with **`beginDeposit`**. The SDK fetches your Stripe keys from Unifold, initializes the native SDK, and runs the full onramp inside the deposit menu.

## Provider config

Set these on **`UnifoldProvider`**'s **`config`**.

<ParamField path="config.enableStripeLink" type="boolean" default="false">
  When `true`, shows the **Pay with Link** (Stripe) option in the deposit menu opened via `beginDeposit`. Requires **`@stripe/stripe-react-native`** installed in your app and the **native Onramp** module enabled (Expo `includeOnramp: true` or the bare equivalent — see [Overview](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/stripe-onramp/overview)). Stripe onramp is bundled with the main package; no separate `import '@unifold/connect-react-native/stripe'` is required.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="config.stripeLink" type="object">
  Pay with Link tuning options. Only applies when `enableStripeLink` is `true`.

  <Expandable title="stripeLink properties">
    <ParamField path="paymentSelectorPosition" type="'header' | 'inline'" default="'header'">
      Where to render the payment method selector: above the amount (`'header'`) or below it (`'inline'`).
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="skipSuccessConfirmation" type="boolean" default="false">
      Skip the success confirmation screen and complete immediately.
    </ParamField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>

```tsx theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey="pk_live_your_key"
  config={{
    enableStripeLink: true,
    stripeLink: {
      paymentSelectorPosition: 'inline',
      skipSuccessConfirmation: false,
    },
  }}
>
  <RootNavigator />
</UnifoldProvider>
```

<Note>
  There is **no** `merchantIdentifier` config or prop. The Apple Pay merchant identifier is read automatically at runtime from your **Unifold dashboard** (via the Stripe config endpoint). You only need to keep the `merchantIdentifier` in your `app.json` Stripe plugin (native entitlement) in sync with the dashboard value. If the dashboard has no merchant id, Apple Pay is disabled and hidden in the flow; card/bank still works. See [Apple Pay `merchantIdentifier`](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/integration-checklist#apple-pay-merchantidentifier).
</Note>

## `beginDeposit` fields

Pass these on the **`DepositConfig`** you give to **`beginDeposit`** — they drive the destination and pre-fill the Stripe Link steps for the current session.

<ParamField path="externalUserId" type="string" required>
  Your unique identifier for the user. Used to resolve their deposit wallet address via the Unifold API.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="recipientAddress" type="string">
  The wallet address that receives the funds. If not set, it is resolved from `externalUserId` via the Unifold API.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="destinationChainType" type="'ethereum' | 'solana' | 'bitcoin'">
  The blockchain type for the destination.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="destinationChainId" type="string">
  The chain ID for the destination (e.g. `'8453'` for Base, `'1'` for Ethereum mainnet, `'137'` for Polygon). See [Supported Chains](/get-started/supported-chains).
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="destinationTokenAddress" type="string">
  The token contract address on the destination chain. If not provided, the default token for the chain is used.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="user" type="{ email?: string; phone?: string }">
  Host-app-supplied identity used to pre-fill the Stripe Link steps.

  * `user.email` — pre-fills the email step.
  * `user.phone` — pre-fills the phone step (E.164 recommended, e.g. `+12125551234`). When combined with `email`, Stripe may skip both verify steps.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onSuccess" type="(data: DepositResult) => void">
  Called when the deposit completes successfully.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onError" type="(error: DepositError) => void">
  Called when an error occurs during the flow. See [Error Handling](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/stripe-onramp/error-handling).
</ParamField>

```tsx theme={null}
const { beginDeposit } = useUnifold();

await beginDeposit({
  externalUserId: user.id,
  recipientAddress: user.walletAddress,
  destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
  destinationChainId: '8453',
  destinationTokenAddress: '0x…',
  user: { email: user.email, phone: user.phone },
  onSuccess: (data) => console.log('Deposit complete', data.executionId),
  onError: (err) => console.error(err.code, err.message),
});
```

See [useUnifold](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/use-unifold) for the complete `DepositConfig` reference (source-token pre-selection, `initialScreen`, confirmation modes, and more).

## Result types

The deposit-menu flow reports outcomes through `beginDeposit`'s callbacks and returned promise.

### DepositResult

Returned in `onSuccess` and resolved by the promise when a purchase completes.

```tsx theme={null}
interface DepositResult {
  message: string;
  transaction?: unknown;
  executionId?: string;
}
```

### DepositError

Passed to `onError` (and rejected by the promise) when the flow fails or the user closes it.

```tsx theme={null}
interface DepositError {
  message: string;
  error?: unknown;
  code?: string; // e.g. 'DEPOSIT_CANCELLED' when the user closes the modal
}
```

See [Types](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/types) for the full type reference.

# Error Handling

> How errors surface in the Pay with Link (Stripe) deposit flow.

Pay with Link runs inside the deposit menu, so it uses the same error surface as every other deposit method: the **`onError`** callback on `beginDeposit` (and the rejected promise).

<Info>
  You don't need to render Stripe error messages yourself — the **Pay with Link sheet displays errors inline** at each step (invalid email, KYC rejection, declined card, etc.) and lets the user retry within the flow. The `onError` callback is primarily for **logging, analytics, and deciding whether to exit the flow**.
</Info>

## Basic error handling

```tsx theme={null}
const { beginDeposit } = useUnifold();

await beginDeposit({
  externalUserId: user.id,
  user: { email: user.email },
  onError: (err) => {
    if (err.code !== 'DEPOSIT_CANCELLED') {
      console.error(`[${err.code}] ${err.message}`);
    }
  },
});
```

You can also handle rejection with `try/catch`, since `beginDeposit` returns a promise:

```tsx theme={null}
try {
  await beginDeposit({ externalUserId: user.id, user: { email: user.email } });
} catch (err) {
  if (err.code === 'DEPOSIT_CANCELLED') return; // user closed the sheet
  showErrorToast(err.message);
}
```

## DepositError

`onError` receives a `DepositError`:

```tsx theme={null}
interface DepositError {
  message: string;   // Human-readable message
  error?: unknown;    // Original error object, when available
  code?: string;      // Deposit-level error code (see below)
}
```

| Code                 | Description                                                   | Suggested action              |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| `DEPOSIT_CANCELLED`  | User closed the sheet without completing                      | Treat as normal — no error UI |
| `DEPOSIT_SUPERSEDED` | A new `beginDeposit` started while a previous one was pending | Ignore the superseded result  |
| `NETWORK_ERROR`      | A network request failed                                      | Prompt the user to retry      |
| `INVALID_CONFIG`     | Invalid configuration passed to `beginDeposit`                | Fix the deposit config        |

## Errors handled inline by the sheet

These happen **inside** the Pay with Link flow and are shown to the user in the sheet, where they can retry — they do not require host-side handling:

| Scenario                         |   Recoverable in the sheet?   |
| -------------------------------- | :---------------------------: |
| Invalid email / amount           |     ✅ — inline validation     |
| Stripe Link authorization denied |       ✅ — user can retry      |
| KYC / identity document rejected |     ✅ — user can re-submit    |
| Card declined or payment failed  | ✅ — user can try another card |

## Configuration errors

If the native Onramp module is missing, the flow fails to initialize with a `StripeCryptoOnramp is not available` error in the console (and the option may not open). This is a build/setup problem, not a runtime user error — enable the native Onramp module and rebuild. See [Troubleshooting](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/stripe-onramp/troubleshooting).

If the Unifold API rejects the Stripe config request (e.g. `Failed to load Stripe config: 400`), verify your Stripe integration in the [Unifold Dashboard](/developer/integrations/stripe). See [Troubleshooting](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/stripe-onramp/troubleshooting#failed-to-load-stripe-config-400).

## Error handling with analytics

```tsx theme={null}
await beginDeposit({
  externalUserId: user.id,
  user: { email: user.email },
  onError: (err) => {
    // Cancellation is expected — don't treat it as an error
    if (err.code === 'DEPOSIT_CANCELLED') return;

    analytics.track('deposit_error', {
      code: err.code,
      message: err.message,
    });

    Alert.alert('Something went wrong', err.message);
  },
});
```

# Examples

> Code examples for integrating Pay with Link (Stripe) via the deposit menu.

Pay with Link runs inside the built-in deposit menu. Enable it once on `UnifoldProvider` with **`config.enableStripeLink: true`**, then open the flow with **`beginDeposit`**.

<Info>
  Install **`@stripe/stripe-react-native`**, enable the **native Onramp** module, and use a **development build** (not Expo Go). See [Overview](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/stripe-onramp/overview) and [Troubleshooting](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/stripe-onramp/troubleshooting).
</Info>

## Enable Pay with Link

Turn on the menu row on the provider (Stripe is registered when you import `@unifold/connect-react-native`):

```tsx theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey="pk_live_…"
  config={{ enableStripeLink: true }}
>
  …
</UnifoldProvider>
```

## Minimal

The simplest integration — just a user ID. Tapping **Pay with Link** in the menu runs the full flow.

```tsx theme={null}
import { useUnifold } from '@unifold/connect-react-native';

function DepositButton() {
  const { beginDeposit } = useUnifold();

  return (
    <Button
      title="Add Funds"
      onPress={() => beginDeposit({ externalUserId: 'user_123' })}
    />
  );
}
```

## Pre-fill Email

Skip the email screen by passing the user's email from your app. This is the recommended pattern — your app already knows the user's email.

```tsx theme={null}
await beginDeposit({
  externalUserId: user.id,
  user: { email: user.email },
});
```

## Pre-fill Email + Phone

Skip both email and phone screens. The flow goes straight to Stripe Link authorization.

```tsx theme={null}
await beginDeposit({
  externalUserId: user.id,
  user: { email: user.email, phone: user.phone },
});
```

## Specific Chain and Token

Target a specific chain and token for the purchase via the destination fields.

```tsx theme={null}
await beginDeposit({
  externalUserId: user.id,
  recipientAddress: user.walletAddress,
  destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
  destinationChainId: '8453',
  destinationTokenAddress: '0x833589fcd6edb6e08f4c7c32d4f71b54bda02913',
  user: { email: user.email },
});
```

## Payment selector inline

Render the Stripe payment method selector below the amount instead of in the header via `config.stripeLink`.

```tsx theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey="pk_live_…"
  config={{
    enableStripeLink: true,
    stripeLink: { paymentSelectorPosition: 'inline' },
  }}
>
  …
</UnifoldProvider>
```

## Open Pay with Link directly

Skip the deposit menu and land straight on the Pay with Link flow with `initialScreen: 'stripe_link'` (requires `config.enableStripeLink: true`; falls back to `'main'` when disabled).

```tsx theme={null}
await beginDeposit({
  externalUserId: user.id,
  recipientAddress: user.walletAddress,
  destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
  destinationChainId: '8453',
  destinationTokenAddress: '0x…',
  user: { email: user.email },
  initialScreen: 'stripe_link',

```

## With Callbacks

Track completion and errors through the deposit callbacks.

```tsx theme={null}
await beginDeposit({
  externalUserId: user.id,
  recipientAddress: user.walletAddress,
  destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
  destinationChainId: '8453',
  destinationTokenAddress: '0x833589fcd6edb6e08f4c7c32d4f71b54bda02913',
  user: { email: user.email },
  onSuccess: (data) => {
    console.log('Deposit complete', data.executionId);
    showSuccessToast('Purchase complete!');
  },
  onError: (err) => {
    if (err.code !== 'DEPOSIT_CANCELLED') {
      console.error(`[${err.code}] ${err.message}`);
      analytics.track('deposit_error', { code: err.code });
    }
  },
});
```

## Complete Screen (Expo Router)

A full screen component using Expo Router.

```tsx app/buy.tsx theme={null}
import React from 'react';
import { Button, View } from 'react-native';

export default function BuyScreen() {

  const handleBuy = () =>
    beginDeposit({
      externalUserId: currentUser.id,
      destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
      destinationChainId: '8453',
      user: { email: currentUser.email },
      onSuccess: (data) => {
        Alert.alert('Purchase Complete', `Execution ${data.executionId}`);
      },
    });

  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, justifyContent: 'center', padding: 20 }}>
      <Button title="Buy Crypto" onPress={handleBuy} />
    </View>
  );
}
```

## Complete Screen (React Navigation)

A full screen component using React Navigation.

```tsx screens/BuyScreen.tsx theme={null}
import React from 'react';
import { Alert, Button, View } from 'react-native';
import { useUnifold } from '@unifold/connect-react-native';

export default function BuyScreen() {

```

# Overview

> Let users buy crypto with credit/debit cards and Apple Pay via Stripe.

The Stripe Onramp integration lets your users purchase crypto directly within your app using Stripe's payment infrastructure — credit/debit cards, Apple Pay, and Stripe Link.

Unifold handles the flow wiring: Stripe configuration, KYC verification, wallet resolution, and payment processing. You enable it with a single flag — **`config.enableStripeLink`** on `UnifoldProvider` — which adds a **Pay with Link** option to the built-in **deposit menu** (`beginDeposit`).

## Prerequisites

<Steps>
  <Step title="Stripe integration in Unifold Dashboard">
    Navigate to **Integrations → Onramps** in your [Unifold Dashboard](https://dashboard.unifold.io) and connect your Stripe account. This stores your Stripe publishable key, secret key, Link OAuth credentials, and optionally your Apple Merchant ID in Unifold. See the [Stripe Dashboard setup guide](/developer/integrations/stripe) for step-by-step instructions.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Install peer dependencies in your app">
    Install **`@stripe/stripe-react-native`** and the other peers listed in [Installation](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/installation) (gesture handler, SVG, Webview, Async Storage). The SDK expects these in **your** `package.json` so Metro resolves a single native copy.

    <CodeGroup>
      ```bash npm theme={null}
      npm install @stripe/stripe-react-native
      ```

      ```bash yarn theme={null}
      yarn add @stripe/stripe-react-native
      ```

      ```bash pnpm theme={null}
      pnpm add @stripe/stripe-react-native
      ```

      ```bash expo theme={null}
      npx expo install @stripe/stripe-react-native
      ```
    </CodeGroup>

    Use a version compatible with your Expo / React Native stack (the SDK typically requires **≥ 0.62.0**).
  </Step>

  <Step title="Configure app.json (Expo)">
    Your `app.json` (or `app.config.js`) needs both the **iOS entitlements** and the **Stripe config plugin**. Here is a minimal example with the required fields:

    ```json theme={null}
    {
      "expo": {
        "ios": {
          "supportsTablet": true,
          "bundleIdentifier": "com.yourcompany.yourapp",
          "entitlements": {
            "com.apple.developer.devicecheck.appattest-environment": "development"
          }
        },
        "plugins": [
          [
            "@stripe/stripe-react-native",
            {
              "merchantIdentifier": "merchant.com.yourapp",
              "enableGooglePay": false,
              "enableApplePay": true,
              "includeOnramp": true
            }
          ]
        ]
      }
    }
    ```

    <Info>
      **App Attest** (`com.apple.developer.devicecheck.appattest-environment`) is **required** for Stripe Link Pay on iOS. Set the value to `"development"` for Simulator and test builds, or `"production"` for TestFlight and App Store builds.
    </Info>

    After changing plugins or entitlements, **regenerate native projects** and use a **development build** (not Expo Go):

    ```bash theme={null}
    npx expo prebuild --clean
    npx expo run:ios
    ```

    **Bare React Native:** add the **`stripe-react-native/Onramp`** CocoaPods subspec and run `pod install`, per [Stripe's mobile SDK configuration](https://docs.stripe.com/crypto/onramp/embedded-components-integration-guide). On Android, set **`StripeSdk_includeOnramp=true`** in `gradle.properties` when using bare workflow, if your Stripe RN version requires it. For App Attest, add the `com.apple.developer.devicecheck.appattest-environment` entitlement in your Xcode project capabilities.

    <Warning>
      Changing `includeOnramp`, entitlements, or Podfile does **not** fix an already-installed binary. You must **rebuild** the iOS/Android app after enabling Onramp.
    </Warning>
  </Step>

  <Step title="iOS: Apple Pay (optional)">
    If you want Apple Pay in the flow, add the Apple Pay capability and register a merchant identifier (e.g. `merchant.com.yourapp`) in [Apple Developer](https://developer.apple.com), and set the same **`merchantIdentifier`** in the Expo plugin / native config (this is the native entitlement, still required). The merchant id used at **runtime** is read automatically from your **Unifold dashboard** (via the Stripe config endpoint) — you do **not** pass it to the SDK. Set it on the dashboard and keep it in sync with the `app.json` plugin value. See [Integration checklist](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/integration-checklist#apple-pay-merchantidentifier).
  </Step>
</Steps>

***

## Test mode vs live mode

Stripe Link Pay behavior depends on the **App Attest environment** and the **Stripe key mode** configured in the Unifold Dashboard.

| Scenario              | App Attest entitlement | Stripe keys in Unifold Dashboard          | Device                                    |
| --------------------- | ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| **Simulator testing** | `"development"`        | Test mode (`pk_test_...` / `sk_test_...`) | iOS Simulator                             |
| **Live / production** | `"production"`         | Live mode (`pk_live_...` / `sk_live_...`) | Physical device (TestFlight or App Store) |

<Warning>
  When switching between test and live mode, you must update **both** the Stripe Publishable Key and Secret Key in the [Unifold Dashboard](/developer/integrations/stripe) to match. Test keys begin with `pk_test_` / `sk_test_`, live keys begin with `pk_live_` / `sk_live_`. You also need to enable **Test Mode** in the [Stripe Dashboard](https://dashboard.stripe.com/test/dashboard) for simulator testing.
</Warning>

***

## Enable Pay with Link

Stripe Onramp is exposed through the built-in **deposit menu**. There is no separate component to render — turn it on with one config flag and open the deposit flow with `beginDeposit`.

1. Set **`enableStripeLink: true`** on `UnifoldProvider` **`config`** (not on `beginDeposit`). Stripe onramp is bundled with the main package and registered when your app imports `@unifold/connect-react-native`; no extra side-effect import is required.

2. Ensure **`@stripe/stripe-react-native`** is installed and **native Onramp** is enabled (see the prerequisites above).

```tsx App.tsx theme={null}
import { UnifoldProvider } from '@unifold/connect-react-native';

export default function App() {
  return (
    <UnifoldProvider
      publishableKey="pk_live_your_key"
      config={{ enableStripeLink: true }}
    >
      <RootNavigator />
    </UnifoldProvider>
  );
}
```

The Apple Pay merchant id is read automatically from your Unifold dashboard — there's nothing to set in code. See [Apple Pay `merchantIdentifier`](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/integration-checklist#apple-pay-merchantidentifier).

When the user opens the deposit modal and taps **Pay with Link**, the SDK runs the full Stripe onramp flow (verification → amount → payment → confirmation) inline, using the `publishableKey` and the destination fields from the active `beginDeposit` session.

### Open the deposit flow

Call `beginDeposit` from `useUnifold`. Optionally pre-fill the Stripe Link email/phone steps with a **`user`** object on **`DepositConfig`** (passed to **`beginDeposit`**, not the provider):

| Field         | Effect on Pay with Link                                                                                            |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `user.email?` | Pre-fills the email step                                                                                           |
| `user.phone?` | Pre-fills the phone step (E.164 recommended, e.g. `+12125551234`); with `email`, Stripe may skip both verify steps |

```tsx theme={null}
const { beginDeposit } = useUnifold();

await beginDeposit({
  externalUserId: user.id,
  recipientAddress: user.walletAddress,
  destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
  destinationChainId: '8453',
  destinationTokenAddress: '0x…',
  user: { email: user.email, phone: user.phone },
});
```

### Tuning options

Fine-tune the Pay with Link sheet with **`config.stripeLink`** (only applies when `enableStripeLink` is `true`):

| Option                    | Type                   | Default    | Description                                                                                         |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `paymentSelectorPosition` | `'header' \| 'inline'` | `'header'` | Where to render the payment method selector: above the amount (`'header'`) or below it (`'inline'`) |
| `skipSuccessConfirmation` | `boolean`              | `false`    | Skip the success confirmation screen and complete immediately                                       |

See [Configuration](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/stripe-onramp/configuration) for the full reference, and [Types](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/types) / [useUnifold](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/use-unifold) for the `DepositConfig` shape.

### Open Pay with Link directly

To skip the deposit menu and land straight on Pay with Link, pass **`initialScreen: 'stripe_link'`** on `beginDeposit` (requires `config.enableStripeLink: true`; falls back to `'main'` when disabled):

```tsx theme={null}
await beginDeposit({
  externalUserId: user.id,
  recipientAddress: user.walletAddress,
  destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
  destinationChainId: '8453',
  destinationTokenAddress: '0x…',
  user: { email: user.email, phone: user.phone },
  initialScreen: 'stripe_link',
});
```

See [Initial Screen](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/initial-screen) for how direct-entry screens behave.

***

| Method            | Support                       |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------- |
| Credit/Debit Card | ✅                             |
| Apple Pay         | ✅ (iOS, requires merchant ID) |
| Stripe Link       | ✅                             |

# Troubleshooting

> Fix common Stripe Onramp and Pay with Link issues on React Native.

## `StripeCryptoOnramp is not available` / Podfile Onramp subspec

**Symptom:** Console shows something like:

`configureSDK error: StripeCryptoOnramp is not available. To enable, add the 'stripe-react-native/Onramp' subspec to your Podfile`

**Cause:** The JavaScript SDK is calling the onramp API, but the **native Onramp module** was not compiled into your iOS app. Stripe ships Onramp as an **optional** native add-on (smaller default install).

**Fix (Expo):**

1. In `app.json` / `app.config.js`, configure both the **iOS entitlements** and the **Stripe config plugin**:

```json theme={null}
{
  "expo": {
    "ios": {
      "supportsTablet": true,
      "bundleIdentifier": "com.yourcompany.yourapp",
      "entitlements": {
        "com.apple.developer.devicecheck.appattest-environment": "development"
      }
    },
    "plugins": [
      [
        "@stripe/stripe-react-native",
        {
          "merchantIdentifier": "merchant.com.yourapp",
          "enableGooglePay": false,
          "enableApplePay": true,
          "includeOnramp": true
        }
      ]
    ]
  }
}
```

<Info>
  The **App Attest** entitlement is **required** for Stripe Link Pay. Use `"development"` for Simulator / test builds and `"production"` for TestFlight / App Store. See [Test mode vs live mode](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/stripe-onramp/overview#test-mode-vs-live-mode).
</Info>

2. **Regenerate native projects** after changing this (existing `ios/` may have been built without Onramp):

```bash theme={null}
npx expo prebuild --clean
npx expo run:ios
```

3. Use a **development build** (or release build). **Expo Go** does not include your app's custom native modules, so Onramp will not work there.

**Fix (bare React Native):** In `ios/Podfile`, include the Onramp subspec per [Stripe's Embedded Components guide](https://docs.stripe.com/crypto/onramp/embedded-components-integration-guide), then:

```bash theme={null}
cd ios && pod install && cd ..
```

Rebuild the app from Xcode or `npx react-native run-ios`. For App Attest, add the `com.apple.developer.devicecheck.appattest-environment` entitlement in your Xcode project capabilities.

**Android (bare):** Set `StripeSdk_includeOnramp=true` in `android/gradle.properties` if required by your Stripe RN version; then clean rebuild. Expo's config plugin may set this when `includeOnramp` is true—confirm in generated Gradle files after prebuild.

***

## Metro: `Unable to resolve module @stripe/stripe-react-native`

**Cause:** `@stripe/stripe-react-native` is a **peer** of `@unifold/connect-react-native`. It must be installed in **your app's** `package.json`.

**Fix:**

```bash theme={null}
npx expo install @stripe/stripe-react-native
# or: npm install @stripe/stripe-react-native
```

Use a version that satisfies the SDK peer range (typically `>=0.62.0`). Restart Metro with cache clear if needed: `npx expo start --clear`.

***

## "Pay with Link" never appears in the deposit menu

**Checklist:**

1. **`enableStripeLink: true`** on `UnifoldProvider` `config`.
2. Your app **imports the main package** somewhere before opening the deposit flow (e.g. `import { UnifoldProvider } from '@unifold/connect-react-native'`). That import registers the Stripe onramp — there is **no** separate `@unifold/connect-react-native/stripe` import anymore.
3. **`@stripe/stripe-react-native`** installed (see above).
4. **Geo:** If the SDK treats the user's region as blocked for tokens, the main deposit options (including Stripe) are not shown—only the blocked state.

***

## `beginDeposit` Stripe prefill not applied

**Stripe Link Pay prefill** uses the optional **`user`** object on **`beginDeposit`**, not on `UnifoldProvider`:

* `user.email` → pre-fills the Stripe Link email step
* `user.phone` → pre-fills the Stripe Link phone step

Pass `user: { email, phone }` on each `beginDeposit({ ... })` call for the session where you want prefill. Both fields are optional.

***

## Apple Pay not showing / `merchantIdentifier`

The Apple Pay merchant identifier is **not** something you pass to the SDK anymore — there is no `merchantIdentifier` prop and no `config.stripeMerchantIdentifier`. It is resolved from two independent places:

* **Native entitlement (build time):** the `merchantIdentifier` in your Stripe Expo plugin (`app.json`) or Xcode capabilities on bare RN. Required for Apple Pay to work at the OS level.
* **Runtime value (automatic):** read from your **Unifold dashboard** via the Stripe config endpoint when the Pay with Link flow initializes.

**If Apple Pay is missing:**

1. Confirm the Apple Pay **merchant identifier is set for your project on the Unifold dashboard**. If it's empty, Apple Pay is silently hidden (card/bank still works).
2. Confirm the **same id** is set in your `app.json` Stripe plugin and that you **rebuilt** the native app after adding it.
3. Test Apple Pay on a **physical device** — the Simulator can behave differently.

See [Apple Pay `merchantIdentifier`](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/integration-checklist#apple-pay-merchantidentifier).

***

## `Failed to load Stripe config: 400`

**Symptom:** `[StripeOnramp] Init failed: [Error: Failed to load Stripe config: 400]`

**Cause:** The SDK calls `GET /v1/public/onramps/headless/stripe/config` with your **Unifold publishable key** in the `x-publishable-key` header. A **400** response means the Unifold API rejected the request before Stripe is even initialized.

**Common causes:**

* **Wrong publishable key for the environment.** If your key belongs to one Unifold project but the API host points to another environment (or vice versa), the server returns 400. Double-check that your `pk_live_...` / `pk_test_...` key matches the Unifold project where Stripe Onramp is configured.
* **Stripe not configured for this project.** The Unifold project linked to that key may not have Stripe Onramp enabled or fully set up in the [Dashboard](/developer/integrations/stripe). Confirm all four Stripe credentials (publishable key, secret key, OAuth client ID, OAuth client secret) are saved.
* **Mixing test and live keys.** Using a `pk_test_...` Unifold key against a project that only has live Stripe credentials configured (or vice versa) can produce a 400.

**Debug tip:** Reproduce the request with `curl` or a proxy to read the JSON error body — the SDK only shows the HTTP status code, but the response body usually explains the exact validation failure:

```bash theme={null}
curl -v https://api.unifold.io/v1/public/onramps/headless/stripe/config \
  -H "x-publishable-key: pk_live_YOUR_KEY"
```

***

## Still stuck

* Confirm [Stripe is configured in the Unifold Dashboard](/developer/integrations/stripe) (Onramps / Stripe).
* Confirm you rebuilt the **native** app after any `app.json` plugin, entitlement, or Podfile change (JS-only refresh is not enough for native errors).
* Confirm the **App Attest environment** in your entitlements matches your mode — `"development"` for Simulator with test keys, `"production"` for physical devices with live keys.

# Handling Results

> Learn how to handle deposit success, errors, and cancellation

The Unifold SDK provides multiple ways to handle the outcome of a deposit flow.

## Two Ways to Handle Results

### 1. Callbacks (Recommended)

Callbacks fire immediately when events occur, even before the modal closes:

```tsx theme={null}
await beginDeposit({
  externalUserId: 'user_123',
  onSuccess: (data) => {
    // ✅ Fires immediately when deposit succeeds
    console.log('Deposit succeeded!', data.executionId);
    refreshBalance();
  },
  onError: (error) => {
    // ✅ Fires immediately when error occurs
    console.error('Deposit failed:', error.message);
    logToAnalytics('deposit_error', error);
  },
});
```

### 2. Promise

The promise resolves/rejects when the modal closes:

```tsx theme={null}
try {
  const result = await beginDeposit({
    externalUserId: 'user_123',
  });
  // ✅ Resolves after modal closes with success
  console.log('Completed:', result.message);
} catch (error) {
  // ❌ Rejects when modal closes without success
  console.log('Failed or cancelled:', error.message);
}
```

## Handling Success

When a deposit completes successfully:

```tsx theme={null}
const handleDeposit = async () => {
  try {
    const result = await beginDeposit({
      externalUserId: 'user_123',
      onSuccess: (data) => {
        // Immediate callback - good for real-time updates
        showSuccessToast('Deposit received!');
        
        // Track the execution
        if (data.executionId) {
          trackDeposit(data.executionId);
        }
      },
    });
    
    // Promise resolved - good for post-flow actions
    navigateToPortfolio();
    
  } catch (error) {
    // Handle errors/cancellation
  }
};
```

### DepositResult Properties

```tsx theme={null}
interface DepositResult {
  message: string;        // "Deposit completed successfully"
  executionId?: string;   // "exec_abc123" - use to track status
  transaction?: unknown;  // Transaction details if available
}
```

## Handling Errors

Errors can occur during the deposit flow:

```tsx theme={null}
await beginDeposit({
  externalUserId: 'user_123',
  onError: (error) => {
    // Log to your error tracking service
    Sentry.captureException(error);
    
    // Show user-friendly message
    showErrorToast(error.message);
    
    // Handle specific error codes
    if (error.code === 'NETWORK_ERROR') {
      showRetryButton();
    }
  },
});
```

### DepositError Properties

```tsx theme={null}
interface DepositError {
  message: string;   // Human-readable message
  code?: string;     // Error code for programmatic handling
  error?: unknown;   // Original error object
}
```

## Handling Cancellation

When the user closes the modal without completing:

```tsx theme={null}
try {
  await beginDeposit({ externalUserId: 'user_123' });
} catch (error) {
  if (error.code === 'DEPOSIT_CANCELLED') {
    // ✅ User simply closed the modal - this is normal!
    // Don't show an error, just log it
    analytics.track('deposit_modal_closed');
    return;
  }
  
  // ❌ Actual error - show message
  showErrorToast(error.message);
}
```

<Warning>
  Don't treat `DEPOSIT_CANCELLED` as an error! It's expected behavior when users close the modal. Only show error messages for actual failures.
</Warning>

## Complete Example

Here's a production-ready implementation:

```tsx theme={null}
import { useUnifold } from '@unifold/connect-react-native';
import { Alert } from 'react-native';

function useDeposit() {
  const { beginDeposit } = useUnifold();
  const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(false);

  const deposit = async (userId: string) => {
    setIsLoading(true);
    
    try {
      const result = await beginDeposit({
        externalUserId: userId,
        
        onSuccess: (data) => {
          // Immediate feedback
          hapticFeedback('success');
          
          // Refresh data
          queryClient.invalidateQueries(['balance', userId]);
          
          // Analytics
          analytics.track('deposit_success', {
            executionId: data.executionId,
          });
        },
        
        onError: (error) => {
          // Error tracking
          Sentry.captureException(error, {
            extra: { userId, code: error.code },
          });
          
          // Analytics
          analytics.track('deposit_error', {
            code: error.code,
            message: error.message,
          });
        },
      });
      
      // Show success message after modal closes
      Alert.alert(
        'Deposit Complete',
        result.message,
        [{ text: 'View Portfolio', onPress: goToPortfolio }]
      );
      
    } catch (error) {
      if (error.code === 'DEPOSIT_CANCELLED') {
        // User cancelled - track but don't show error
        analytics.track('deposit_cancelled');
        return;
      }
      
      // Show error alert
      Alert.alert('Deposit Failed', error.message);
      
    } finally {
      setIsLoading(false);
    }
  };

  return { deposit, isLoading };
}
```

# Installation

> Install the Unifold React Native SDK

## Prerequisites

Before installing, ensure you have:

* React Native >= 0.72.0 or Expo >= 49.0.0
* Node.js >= 18.0.0

## Install the package and peers

Native-linked libraries are **peer dependencies** of `@unifold/connect-react-native`. Install them in **your** app so versions match Expo / React Native and you avoid duplicate native modules (no `overrides` workarounds for `react-native-svg` / `react-native-webview`).

<CodeGroup>
  ```bash npm theme={null}
  npm install @unifold/connect-react-native \
    @react-native-async-storage/async-storage \
    @stripe/stripe-react-native \
    react-native-gesture-handler \
    react-native-svg \
    react-native-webview
  ```

  ```bash yarn theme={null}
  yarn add @unifold/connect-react-native \
    @react-native-async-storage/async-storage \
    @stripe/stripe-react-native \
    react-native-gesture-handler \
    react-native-svg \
    react-native-webview
  ```

  ```bash pnpm theme={null}
  pnpm add @unifold/connect-react-native \
    @react-native-async-storage/async-storage \
    @stripe/stripe-react-native \
    react-native-gesture-handler \
    react-native-svg \
    react-native-webview
  ```

  ```bash expo theme={null}
  npx expo install @unifold/connect-react-native \
    @react-native-async-storage/async-storage \
    @stripe/stripe-react-native \
    react-native-gesture-handler \
    react-native-svg \
    react-native-webview
  ```
</CodeGroup>

`expo` is an optional peer (Expo projects include it automatically). See [Integration checklist](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/integration-checklist) for staging API, Stripe, and Expo Go vs development builds.

## iOS setup (bare React Native only)

If you're using bare React Native (not Expo managed workflow), install the native dependencies:

```bash theme={null}
cd ios && pod install
```

## Expo and Stripe native code

If you use [Stripe Link Pay](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/stripe-onramp/overview) (`config.enableStripeLink`), install **`@stripe/stripe-react-native`** and add the [Stripe config plugin](https://docs.expo.dev/guides/using-stripe/) to `app.json` with **`includeOnramp: true`** (and Apple Pay options such as **`merchantIdentifier`** if needed). Then regenerate native projects and rebuild:

```bash theme={null}
npx expo prebuild
npx expo run:ios
# or
npx expo run:android
```

See [Stripe troubleshooting](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/stripe-onramp/troubleshooting) for Onramp native module errors.

<Note>
  **Expo Go** cannot load your app’s custom native modules (including Stripe Crypto Onramp). Use a **development build** (`npx expo run:ios` / `run:android` or EAS) for deposits and Stripe flows. You can still use **`expo start`** for JavaScript; the installed app binary is custom, not Expo Go.
</Note>

## Verify installation

Create a simple test to verify the installation:

```tsx theme={null}
import { UnifoldProvider } from '@unifold/connect-react-native';

export default function App() {
  return (
    <UnifoldProvider publishableKey="pk_test_your_key">
      <Text>Unifold SDK installed!</Text>
    </UnifoldProvider>
  );
}
```

If the app runs without errors, the installation is complete.

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Metro bundler errors">
    Clear the Metro cache and restart:

    ```bash theme={null}
    npx expo start --clear
    # or for bare RN
    npx react-native start --reset-cache
    ```
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="iOS pod install fails">
    Try cleaning and reinstalling pods:

    ```bash theme={null}
    cd ios
    rm -rf Pods Podfile.lock
    pod install
    ```
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Android build fails">
    Clean the Android build:

    ```bash theme={null}
    cd android
    ./gradlew clean
    cd ..
    npx react-native run-android
    ```
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Stripe: Metro cannot resolve @stripe/stripe-react-native">
    Add the peer to your app, e.g. `npx expo install @stripe/stripe-react-native`, and restart Metro with `--clear` if needed.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Stripe: StripeCryptoOnramp / Onramp subspec errors at runtime">
    Enable the native Onramp module (Expo plugin `includeOnramp: true`, or bare Podfile / Android Gradle per Stripe), then **clean prebuild and rebuild** the native app. See [Stripe Onramp troubleshooting](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/stripe-onramp/troubleshooting).
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

# Integration checklist

> Peer dependencies, Expo vs development builds, Stripe, and other details when wiring @unifold/connect-react-native.

Use this page together with [Installation](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/installation) and [Stripe Onramp overview](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/stripe-onramp/overview).

## Peer dependencies

Install **all** native-linked peers in **your** app so Metro and CocoaPods / Gradle resolve **one** copy each. The SDK lists them as peers (not nested dependencies) to avoid duplicate `react-native-svg`, `react-native-webview`, etc.

**Expo (recommended):**

```bash theme={null}
npx expo install @unifold/connect-react-native \
  @react-native-async-storage/async-storage \
  @stripe/stripe-react-native \
  react-native-gesture-handler \
  react-native-svg \
  react-native-webview
```

`expo` is an optional peer (Expo projects include it automatically).

## `react-native-gesture-handler`

On **bare React Native**, import gesture handler at the **entry file** first (see [React Navigation](https://reactnavigation.org/docs/getting-started/#installing-dependencies-into-a-bare-react-native-project)). **Expo Router** projects usually already satisfy this.

## `UnifoldProvider` placement

Wrap **near the root** so `useUnifold()`, theming, and the deposit modal behave predictably.

## Stripe Link Pay

* Set **`config.enableStripeLink: true`** on `UnifoldProvider`. You do **not** need a separate `import '@unifold/connect-react-native/stripe'` — Stripe onramp is registered when you import the main package.
* Install **`@stripe/stripe-react-native`**, enable the **native Onramp** module (`includeOnramp: true` in the Expo Stripe plugin, or bare Podfile / Gradle per Stripe), then **rebuild** the native app after any plugin change.
* **Expo Go** does not include your custom native modules. Use a **development build** (`npx expo prebuild` then `npx expo run:ios` / `run:android`, or EAS). You can still use **`expo start`** for JS; the installed binary is your app, not Expo Go.

### App Attest (required for Stripe Link Pay)

Stripe Link Pay requires the **App Attest** entitlement on iOS. Add it to the `ios.entitlements` section of your `app.json`:

```json theme={null}
"ios": {
  "supportsTablet": true,
  "bundleIdentifier": "com.yourcompany.yourapp",
  "entitlements": {
    "com.apple.developer.devicecheck.appattest-environment": "development"
  }
}
```

The full Stripe plugin configuration should look like:

```json theme={null}
"plugins": [
  [
    "@stripe/stripe-react-native",
    {
      "merchantIdentifier": "merchant.com.yourapp",
      "enableGooglePay": false,
      "enableApplePay": true,
      "includeOnramp": true
    }
  ]
]
```

| Environment             | App Attest value | Stripe keys in Unifold Dashboard          | Device                         |
| ----------------------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| **Simulator / testing** | `"development"`  | Test mode (`pk_test_...` / `sk_test_...`) | iOS Simulator                  |
| **Production**          | `"production"`   | Live mode (`pk_live_...` / `sk_live_...`) | Physical device via TestFlight |

* **Simulator (test mode):** Set the entitlement to `"development"` and enable **Test Mode** in the [Stripe Dashboard](https://dashboard.stripe.com/test/dashboard). In the [Unifold Dashboard](/developer/integrations/stripe), switch the Stripe Publishable Key and Secret Key to use Stripe **test** keys (`pk_test_...` / `sk_test_...`).
* **Physical device (live mode):** Set the entitlement to `"production"` and run the app on a physical device using **TestFlight**. In the Unifold Dashboard, switch the Stripe Publishable Key and Secret Key to use Stripe **live** keys (`pk_live_...` / `sk_live_...`).

<Warning>
  When switching between test and live mode, update **both** the Stripe Publishable Key **and** Secret Key in the Unifold Dashboard to match. Mixing test and live keys will cause `Failed to load Stripe config` errors.
</Warning>

### Expo Go vs development build vs prebuild

* **Expo Go** cannot run Stripe Crypto Onramp — that is an Expo Go limitation, not "Expo" in general.
* A **development build** is your app with the Stripe plugin compiled in. **`npx expo prebuild`** generates `ios/` / `android/`; **`npx expo run:ios`** builds and installs it. JS workflow stays the same with **`expo start`**.
* **Simulator:** A dev build usually runs on the **iOS Simulator** for most flows. **Apple Pay** can still behave differently than on device — test on a **physical device** when debugging wallet / merchant issues.
* **Signing:** Debug simulator builds often work with **Xcode automatic signing**. **Apple Pay** still needs a **merchant identifier** registered in [Apple Developer](https://developer.apple.com) and matching `app.json` / Stripe.

### Apple Pay `merchantIdentifier`

* **Native entitlement (still required):** Configure `merchantIdentifier` in the **Stripe Expo plugin** in `app.json` (or Xcode capabilities on bare RN). This is what registers the merchant id into the native build's entitlements at compile time.
* **Runtime value (automatic):** The merchant id used at runtime is read **only** from your **Unifold dashboard** via the Stripe config endpoint — you do **not** pass it to the SDK. There is no `config.stripeMerchantIdentifier`. Set the Apple Pay merchant identifier for your project on the dashboard, and make sure it **matches** the id in your `app.json` plugin.
* If the dashboard has no merchant id set, Apple Pay is simply hidden in the deposit flow; card/bank still works.

## Theme

`UnifoldProvider` wraps children in the SDK **`ThemeProvider`**. Components that use **`useTheme`** from the Unifold UI path under the provider use Unifold design tokens. If you use another theme system, decide **nesting order** deliberately.

## React Query

The Connect SDK **does not** wrap your app in `@tanstack/react-query`'s `QueryClientProvider`. Your app's **`useQuery`** / **`QueryClientProvider`** setup is unchanged.

## Single JS bundle

`@unifold/connect-react-native` ships one prebuilt entry. Importing the package runs Stripe onramp **registration** once. **`enableStripeLink: false`** only hides the deposit-menu row; the Stripe-related JS is still part of the package graph.

## After upgrading

When you bump the SDK or Stripe / native peers, **rebuild the native app** (not only reload JS) when you see native-module or entitlement errors.

# Overview

> Integrate crypto deposits and fiat onramp into your React Native or Expo app.

The `@unifold/connect-react-native` SDK provides a seamless way to integrate crypto deposits and fiat onramp into your React Native or Expo application.

## Features

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Crypto Deposits" icon="wallet">
    Accept crypto deposits from any wallet via QR code or address copy
  </Card>

  <Card title="Fiat Onramp" icon="credit-card">
    Buy with card (MoonPay-style providers) from the deposit menu
  </Card>

  <Card title="Stripe Link Pay" icon="link">
    Stripe Crypto Onramp in the deposit menu — enable with the `enableStripeLink` flag; requires native setup and an Expo **development build** (not Expo Go). See [Stripe Onramp](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/stripe-onramp/overview).
  </Card>

  <Card title="Multi-Chain Support" icon="link">
    Support for Ethereum, Polygon, Solana, Bitcoin, and more
  </Card>

  <Card title="Customizable UI" icon="palette">
    Light and dark mode with customizable theming
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

## How It Works

1. **Wrap your app** with `UnifoldProvider` using your publishable key
2. **Call `beginDeposit()`** to open the deposit modal
3. **Handle the result** via callbacks or the returned promise

```tsx theme={null}
import { UnifoldProvider, useUnifold } from '@unifold/connect-react-native';

// 1. Wrap your app
<UnifoldProvider publishableKey="pk_live_...">
  <App />
</UnifoldProvider>

// 2. Launch deposit flow
const { beginDeposit } = useUnifold();
await beginDeposit({ externalUserId: 'user_123' });
```

| Expo Go                 | ⚠️ Fine for trying the deposit UI; **Stripe Onramp** needs a **development build** (Expo Go does not include your native modules) |

# Quickstart

> Get up and running with Unifold in 5 minutes.

This guide will help you integrate Unifold deposits into your React Native app in just a few minutes.

## Step 1: Get Your Publishable Key

<Steps>
  <Step title="Sign up for Unifold">
    Create an account at [dashboard.unifold.io](https://dashboard.unifold.io)
  </Step>

  <Step title="Get your API keys">
    Create a project then navigate to API Keys in your dashboard
  </Step>

  <Step title="Copy your publishable key">
    Use `pk_test_...` for development, `pk_live_...` for production
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Step 2: Set Up the Provider

Wrap your app's root component with `UnifoldProvider`:

```tsx App.tsx theme={null}
import { UnifoldProvider } from '@unifold/connect-react-native';

export default function App() {
  return (
    <UnifoldProvider 
      publishableKey="pk_live_your_key"
      config={{
        appearance: 'dark', // or 'light' or 'auto'
      }}
    >
      <RootNavigator />
    </UnifoldProvider>
  );
}
```

<Info>
  For Expo Router, add the provider in `app/_layout.tsx`.
</Info>

## Step 3: Create a Deposit Button

Use the `useUnifold` hook to trigger the deposit flow:

```tsx DepositScreen.tsx theme={null}
import { useUnifold } from '@unifold/connect-react-native';
import { View, Button, Alert } from 'react-native';

export default function DepositScreen() {
  const { beginDeposit } = useUnifold();

  const handleDeposit = async () => {
    try {
      const result = await beginDeposit({
        // Required: Your user's unique identifier
        externalUserId: 'user_123',
        
        // Optional: Pre-configure the destination
        destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
        destinationChainId: '137', // Polygon
        destinationTokenAddress: '0x3c499c542cef5e3811e1192ce70d8cc03d5c3359',
        destinationTokenSymbol: 'USDC',
        recipientAddress: '0x...user_wallet',
        
        // Optional: Callbacks
        onSuccess: (data) => {
          console.log('Deposit successful!', data);
        },
        onError: (error) => {
          console.error('Deposit failed:', error);
        },
      });
      
      Alert.alert('Success', `Deposit completed: ${result.message}`);
    } catch (error) {
      // User closed the modal
      console.log('Deposit cancelled');
    }
  };

  return (
    <View style={{ flex: 1, justifyContent: 'center', padding: 20 }}>
      <Button title="Deposit Crypto" onPress={handleDeposit} />
    </View>
  );
}
```

## Step 4: Test the Integration

Run your app and tap the deposit button.

Users can:

* **Transfer Crypto**: Send from any wallet via QR code or address
* **Buy with Card**: Purchase crypto with credit/debit card
* **Pay with Link** (optional): Set `UnifoldProvider` `config.enableStripeLink: true`, install and configure [`@stripe/stripe-react-native`](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/stripe-onramp/overview) (native Onramp, development build on Expo — not Expo Go). No separate Stripe entry import is required. See [Integration checklist](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/integration-checklist).

## Complete Example

Here's a complete minimal example:

```tsx App.tsx theme={null}
import React from 'react';
import { View, Button, StyleSheet } from 'react-native';
import { UnifoldProvider, useUnifold } from '@unifold/connect-react-native';

function DepositButton() {
  const { beginDeposit } = useUnifold();

  return (
    <Button
      title="Deposit"
      onPress={() => beginDeposit({ externalUserId: 'user_123' })}
    />
  );
}

export default function App() {
  return (
    <UnifoldProvider publishableKey="pk_live_your_key">
      <View style={styles.container}>
        <DepositButton />
      </View>
    </UnifoldProvider>
  );
}

const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  container: {
    flex: 1,
    justifyContent: 'center',
    alignItems: 'center',
  },
});
```
