# Types

> TypeScript type definitions for the Unifold SDK

## Type Definitions

### DepositConfig

Configuration passed to `beginDeposit()`.

```tsx theme={null}
type DepositChainType = 'ethereum' | 'solana' | 'bitcoin';

interface DepositConfig {
  // Required
  externalUserId: string;

  // Optional — destination configuration
  destinationChainType?: DepositChainType;
  destinationChainId?: string;
  destinationTokenAddress?: string;
  destinationTokenSymbol?: string;
  recipientAddress?: string;

  // Optional — pre-select source token/network (Transfer Crypto)
  defaultChainType?: DepositChainType;
  defaultChainId?: string;
  defaultTokenAddress?: string;

  // Optional — display and behavior
  showBalance?: boolean;
  depositConfirmationMode?: 'auto_ui' | 'auto_silent' | 'manual';
  initialScreen?: 'main' | 'transfer' | 'card' | 'tracker' | 'cashapp' | 'wallet' | 'apple_pay' | 'stripe_link';

  // Optional — user identity used to pre-fill supported flows
  // (Pay with Apple Pay: a trusted user.email skips the email steps;
  //  Stripe Link Pay: user.email/user.phone pre-fill)
  user?: UnifoldUser;

  // Optional — callbacks
  onSuccess?: (data: DepositResult) => void;
  onError?: (error: DepositError) => void;
}
```

### UnifoldUser

Host-app-supplied user identity used to pre-fill supported flows. It's an object so more fields can be added later without new top-level `beginDeposit` params. Consumed by **Pay with Apple Pay** (Coinbase) and **Pay with Link** (Stripe).

```tsx theme={null}
interface UnifoldUser {
  /**
   * Host-trusted email. For Pay with Apple Pay, a valid value skips the
   * email-entry and email-OTP steps (phone verification still runs). For
   * Pay with Link (Stripe), it pre-fills the email step.
   */
  email?: string;
  /** Pre-fills the user's phone (Pay with Link); with `email`, Stripe may skip verify steps. */
  phone?: string;
}
```

### DepositResult

Returned when a deposit completes successfully.

```tsx theme={null}
interface DepositResult {
  message: string;
  transaction?: unknown;
  executionId?: string;
}
```

### DepositError

Returned when a deposit fails or is cancelled.

```tsx theme={null}
interface DepositError {
  message: string;
  error?: unknown;
  code?: string;
}
```

#### Error Codes

| Code                 | Description                                                                     |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DEPOSIT_CANCELLED`  | User closed the modal without completing                                        |
| `DEPOSIT_SUPERSEDED` | A new `beginDeposit` started while a previous deposit promise was still pending |
| `NETWORK_ERROR`      | Network request failed                                                          |
| `INVALID_CONFIG`     | Invalid configuration provided                                                  |

### ThemeMode

Theme appearance options.

```tsx theme={null}
type ThemeMode = 'light' | 'dark';
```

<Note>
  Use `'auto'` in `config.appearance` to follow system preference. The `ThemeMode` type itself only includes `'light'` and `'dark'`.
</Note>

### UnifoldProviderProps

Props for the `UnifoldProvider` component.

```tsx theme={null}
interface UnifoldProviderProps {
  children: ReactNode;
  publishableKey: string;
  config?: {
    modalTitle?: string;
    hideDepositTracker?: boolean;
    appearance?: ThemeMode | 'auto';
    transferInputVariant?: 'single_input' | 'double_input' | 'compact';
    /** Deposit menu layout: 'stacked' (list) or 'tabs' ('Use Crypto' / 'Use Cash') */
    depositMenuDisplay?: 'stacked' | 'tabs';
    accentColor?: string;
    theme?: ThemeConfig;
    fontFamily?: string;
    fonts?: FontConfig;
    components?: ComponentConfig;
    sheetBorderRadius?: SheetBorderRadius;
    /** Show "Pay with Link" (Stripe) on the deposit menu; requires `@stripe/stripe-react-native` + native Onramp */
    enableStripeLink?: boolean;
    /** Stripe Link Pay tuning options (only applies when `enableStripeLink` is true) */
    stripeLink?: {
      /** Where to render the payment method selector: 'header' (above amount) or 'inline' (below). Default: 'header' */
      paymentSelectorPosition?: 'header' | 'inline';
      /** Skip the success confirmation screen and complete immediately. Default: false */
      skipSuccessConfirmation?: boolean;
    };
  };
}
```

<Note>
  There's no `stripeMerchantIdentifier` config. The Apple Pay merchant identifier is read automatically from your Unifold dashboard (via the Stripe config endpoint) at runtime — you don't pass it to the SDK. See the [Integration checklist](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/integration-checklist#apple-pay-merchantidentifier).
</Note>

## Usage Examples

### Typed Deposit Handler

```tsx theme={null}
import type { DepositConfig, DepositResult, DepositError } from '@unifold/connect-react-native';

const depositConfig: DepositConfig = {
  externalUserId: 'user_123',
  destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
  destinationChainId: '137',
  destinationTokenAddress: '0x3c499c542cef5e3811e1192ce70d8cc03d5c3359',
  destinationTokenSymbol: 'USDC',
  recipientAddress: '0x...',
  onSuccess: (result: DepositResult) => {
    console.log('Success:', result.message);
  },
  onError: (error: DepositError) => {
    console.error('Error:', error.code, error.message);
  },
};

await beginDeposit(depositConfig);
```

### Stripe Link Pay prefill (deposit menu)

When `enableStripeLink` is enabled on the provider, pass optional prefill via the **`user`** object on **`beginDeposit`**:

```tsx theme={null}
await beginDeposit({
  externalUserId: user.id,
  recipientAddress: user.walletAddress,
  destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
  destinationChainId: '8453',
  destinationTokenAddress: '0x…',
  user: { email: user.email, phone: user.phone },
});
```

### Typed Provider Config

```tsx theme={null}
import type { UnifoldProviderProps } from '@unifold/connect-react-native';

const providerConfig: UnifoldProviderProps['config'] = {
  appearance: 'dark',
  modalTitle: 'Add Funds',
  hideDepositTracker: false,
};

<UnifoldProvider publishableKey="pk_live_..." config={providerConfig}>
  <App />
</UnifoldProvider>
```

### Type Guards

```tsx theme={null}
function isDepositCancelled(error: DepositError): boolean {
  return error.code === 'DEPOSIT_CANCELLED';
}

try {
  await beginDeposit({ externalUserId: 'user_123' });
} catch (error) {
  const depositError = error as DepositError;
  if (isDepositCancelled(depositError)) {
    // Handle cancellation
  }
}
```

# Border Radius

> Customize the corner radius of every screen in the Unifold React Native SDK.

## Overview

Every screen in the Unifold deposit flow is rendered with rounded top corners. By default, each screen uses a border radius of **24** on both the top-left and top-right corners.

The `sheetBorderRadius` config lets you:

1. Set **global defaults** that apply to every sheet at once.
2. **Override individual sheets** when you need one sheet to look different from the rest.

Per-sheet values always take priority over global values, and global values take priority over the built-in default of `24`.

```
per-sheet override  →  global default  →  24 (built-in)
```

## Quick Start

Pass `sheetBorderRadius` to your `UnifoldProvider` config:

```tsx theme={null}
import { UnifoldProvider } from "@unifold/connect-react-native";

<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey="pk_live_..."
  config={{
    sheetBorderRadius: {
      globalBorderTopLeftRadius: 16,
      globalBorderTopRightRadius: 16,
    },
  }}
>
  <App />
</UnifoldProvider>
```

This sets every bottom sheet in the deposit flow to use a `16px` corner radius.

## Sharp Corners (No Rounding)

To remove all rounding and make every sheet flush with the screen edges:

```tsx theme={null}
config={{
  sheetBorderRadius: {
    globalBorderTopLeftRadius: 0,
    globalBorderTopRightRadius: 0,
  },
}}
```

## Per-Sheet Overrides

You can override the radius for any specific sheet while keeping the global default for the rest:

```tsx theme={null}
config={{
  sheetBorderRadius: {
    // All sheets default to sharp corners
    globalBorderTopLeftRadius: 0,
    globalBorderTopRightRadius: 0,

    // But the main modal gets rounded corners
    main: {
      borderTopLeftRadius: 24,
      borderTopRightRadius: 24,
    },

    // And the currency picker gets a subtle rounding
    currencyModal: {
      borderTopLeftRadius: 12,
      borderTopRightRadius: 12,
    },
  },
}}
```

## Asymmetric Corners

You can set different radii for the left and right corners:

```tsx theme={null}
config={{
  sheetBorderRadius: {
    globalBorderTopLeftRadius: 24,
    globalBorderTopRightRadius: 0,
  },
}}
```

This also works at the per-sheet level. You can override just one side and let the other fall back to the global:

```tsx theme={null}
config={{
  sheetBorderRadius: {
    globalBorderTopLeftRadius: 24,
    globalBorderTopRightRadius: 24,
    main: {
      borderTopLeftRadius: 0,
      // borderTopRightRadius falls back to global (24)
    },
  },
}}
```

## Available Sheets

The deposit flow is composed of multiple bottom sheets. Each one can be individually targeted by its key.

<ParamField path="globalBorderTopLeftRadius" type="number" default="24">
  Default top-left corner radius applied to all sheets.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="globalBorderTopRightRadius" type="number" default="24">
  Default top-right corner radius applied to all sheets.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="main" type="BorderRadiusConfig">
  The primary deposit modal — the first sheet the user sees when the deposit flow opens.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="transferCrypto" type="BorderRadiusConfig">
  The transfer crypto wrapper sheet, shown when the user selects cross-chain transfer.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="buyWithCard" type="BorderRadiusConfig">
  The buy-with-card wrapper sheet, shown when the user selects fiat onramp.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="depositsTracker" type="BorderRadiusConfig">
  The deposits tracker modal that shows the user's pending and completed deposits.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="tokenSelector" type="BorderRadiusConfig">
  The token selector sheet inside the transfer crypto flow.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="chainSelector" type="BorderRadiusConfig">
  The chain/network selector sheet inside the transfer crypto flow. Used when `transferInputVariant` is `"double_input"` or `"compact"`.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="currencyModal" type="BorderRadiusConfig">
  The fiat currency selector inside the buy-with-card flow.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="providerModal" type="BorderRadiusConfig">
  The payment provider selector inside the buy-with-card flow.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="depositStatus" type="BorderRadiusConfig">
  The deposit status sheet shown while a deposit is being processed.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="infoSheet" type="BorderRadiusConfig">
  The informational sheet for price impact, slippage, and fee details.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="stripeLink" type="BorderRadiusConfig">
  The Pay with Link (Stripe) sheet, shown when the user selects Stripe Link Pay from the deposit menu (requires `config.enableStripeLink`).
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="cashApp" type="BorderRadiusConfig">
  The Cash App sheet, shown when the user selects the Cash App deposit option.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="coinbaseApplePay" type="BorderRadiusConfig">
  The Pay with Apple Pay sheet, shown when the user selects the Coinbase Apple Pay deposit option (requires `config.enableCoinbaseApplePay`; iOS only).
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="connectWallet" type="BorderRadiusConfig">
  The Connect Wallet sheet, shown when the user selects the connect-wallet deposit option.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="webView" type="BorderRadiusConfig">
  The WebView sheet used for third-party payment provider checkout inside buy-with-card.
</ParamField>

## TypeScript

### `BorderRadiusConfig`

```tsx theme={null}
interface BorderRadiusConfig {
  borderTopLeftRadius?: number;
  borderTopRightRadius?: number;
}
```

### Full config type

```tsx theme={null}
interface SheetBorderRadius {
  globalBorderTopLeftRadius?: number;
  globalBorderTopRightRadius?: number;
  main?: BorderRadiusConfig;
  transferCrypto?: BorderRadiusConfig;
  buyWithCard?: BorderRadiusConfig;
  depositsTracker?: BorderRadiusConfig;
  tokenSelector?: BorderRadiusConfig;
  chainSelector?: BorderRadiusConfig;
  currencyModal?: BorderRadiusConfig;
  providerModal?: BorderRadiusConfig;
  depositStatus?: BorderRadiusConfig;
  infoSheet?: BorderRadiusConfig;
  stripeLink?: BorderRadiusConfig;
  cashApp?: BorderRadiusConfig;
  coinbaseApplePay?: BorderRadiusConfig;
  connectWallet?: BorderRadiusConfig;
  webView?: BorderRadiusConfig;
}
```

Import the type directly from the SDK:

```tsx theme={null}
import type { BorderRadiusConfig } from "@unifold/connect-react-native";
```

## Resolution Order

When rendering a specific sheet, the SDK resolves each corner radius in this order:

| Priority    | Source             | Example                            |
| ----------- | ------------------ | ---------------------------------- |
| 1 (highest) | Per-sheet override | `main: { borderTopLeftRadius: 0 }` |
| 2           | Global default     | `globalBorderTopLeftRadius: 16`    |
| 3 (lowest)  | Built-in default   | `24`                               |

If `main.borderTopLeftRadius` is set, that value is used. Otherwise it falls back to `globalBorderTopLeftRadius`. If that is also unset, the built-in default of `24` is used.

## Full Example

```tsx theme={null}
import { UnifoldProvider } from "@unifold/connect-react-native";

export default function App() {
  return (
    <UnifoldProvider
      publishableKey="pk_live_..."
      config={{
        appearance: "dark",
        accentColor: "#8B5CF6",

        sheetBorderRadius: {
          // Global: all sheets use 16px corners
          globalBorderTopLeftRadius: 16,
          globalBorderTopRightRadius: 16,

          // Main modal: no rounding (flush with screen)
          main: {
            borderTopLeftRadius: 0,
            borderTopRightRadius: 0,
          },

          // Token selector: extra round
          tokenSelector: {
            borderTopLeftRadius: 32,
            borderTopRightRadius: 32,
          },

          // Deposit status: asymmetric
          depositStatus: {
            borderTopLeftRadius: 24,
            borderTopRightRadius: 0,
          },
        },
      }}
    >
      <App />
    </UnifoldProvider>
  );
}
```

# Card back shadow

Add a customizable "back shadow" behind cards per surface—deposit menu, deposit address, quote provider, or tracker rows.

The SDK supports an optional **back shadow** for cards: a separate view rendered *behind* each card with an offset, so it looks like a drop shadow. Back shadow is **only configurable per surface**—there is no global setting. You enable it per surface (e.g. only on the deposit menu, or only on tracker rows).

## How it works

* A **second view** is drawn behind the card with the same border radius.
* You set its **color** and **offset** (e.g. 4px down/right) via that surface’s card tokens.
* **Vertical spacing** between stacked cards can be increased when the shadow is on (`backShadowSpacing`), so shadows don’t overlap.

No native shadow APIs are used; it’s a simple offset rectangle, so it behaves consistently across platforms.

## Config shape

Back shadow is configured **only** on per-surface card overrides. There is no global `components.card` back shadow.

* `depositMenu.card` — Add Funds menu options (Transfer Crypto, Deposit with Card, Deposit Tracker)
* `transferCrypto.depositAddress.card` — Transfer Crypto deposit address box
* `depositCard.quoteProvider.card` — Deposit with Card provider card and quote rows
* `depositTracker.executionRow.card` — Deposit Tracker execution rows

Example: back shadow on the deposit menu only:

```tsx theme={null}
import { UnifoldProvider } from "@unifold/connect-react-native";

<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey="your_key"
  config={{
    components: {
      depositMenu: {
        card: {
          backShadowColor: "#000000",
          backShadowOffset: { top: 4, left: 4, right: -4, bottom: -4 },
          backShadowSpacing: 12,
        },
      },
    },
  }}
>
  {children}
</UnifoldProvider>
```

Example: back shadow on multiple surfaces:

```tsx theme={null}
config={{
  components: {
    depositMenu: {
      card: {
        backShadowColor: "rgba(0,0,0,0.15)",
        backShadowSpacing: 8,
      },
    },
    depositTracker: {
      executionRow: {
        card: {
          backShadowColor: "rgba(0,0,0,0.1)",
          backShadowSpacing: 6,
        },
      },
    },
  },
}}
```

## Tokens

| Token               | Type                           | Default                                      | Description                                                                                         |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `backShadowColor`   | `string`                       | `"transparent"`                              | Color of the view behind the card. Use `"transparent"` to disable the back shadow.                  |
| `backShadowOffset`  | `{ top, left, right, bottom }` | `{ top: 4, left: 4, right: -4, bottom: -4 }` | Inset (in pixels) of the back view. Negative `right`/`bottom` make the shadow extend past the card. |
| `backShadowSpacing` | `number`                       | `8`                                          | Extra vertical space below the card when the back shadow is on.                                     |

Defaults apply when a surface does not set these; surfaces that don’t override have no back shadow (`backShadowColor` stays `"transparent"`).

## Where each surface is used

| Config path                          | UI                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `depositMenu.card`                   | Add Funds menu: Transfer Crypto, Deposit with Card, Deposit Tracker buttons |
| `transferCrypto.depositAddress.card` | Transfer Crypto: deposit address box with copy                              |
| `depositCard.quoteProvider.card`     | Deposit with Card: main provider card and quote list rows                   |
| `depositTracker.executionRow.card`   | Deposit Tracker: each execution row                                         |

## Disabling the back shadow

For a surface that currently has a back shadow, set `backShadowColor` to `"transparent"` for that surface’s card. If you don’t set any back shadow tokens for a surface, it has no back shadow by default.

## Light / dark

You can set different back shadow settings per theme using `components.light` and `components.dark`:

```tsx theme={null}
components: {
  light: {
    depositMenu: {
      card: {
        backShadowColor: "rgba(0,0,0,0.08)",
        backShadowSpacing: 8,
      },
    },
  },
  dark: {
    depositMenu: {
      card: {
        backShadowColor: "rgba(0,0,0,0.3)",
        backShadowSpacing: 10,
      },
    },
  },
}
```

## Example: subtle shadow on menu and tracker

```tsx theme={null}
components: {
  depositMenu: {
    card: {
      backShadowColor: "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.12)",
      backShadowOffset: { top: 2, left: 2, right: -2, bottom: -2 },
      backShadowSpacing: 8,
    },
  },
  depositTracker: {
    executionRow: {
      card: {
        backShadowColor: "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.08)",
        backShadowSpacing: 6,
      },
    },
  },
}
```

The deposit address box and quote provider cards have no back shadow unless you add overrides for `transferCrypto.depositAddress.card` or `depositCard.quoteProvider.card`.

# Card borders

Customize border radius, width, and color for cards, buttons, inputs, and other components in the React Native SDK

The SDK lets you control **border radius**, **border width**, and **border color** for cards and other UI components via the `components` config. You can set a **global** `card` (applies to all card surfaces) or override **per surface** so each area has its own look.

## Config shape

* **Global** `components.card` — default for every card surface. Use it when you want one style everywhere.
* **Per-surface** overrides — merge on top of the global card so you can style each area independently:
  * `depositMenu.card` — Add Funds menu options (Transfer Crypto, Deposit with Card, Deposit Tracker)
  * `transferCrypto.depositAddress.card` — Transfer Crypto deposit address box (with copy)
  * `depositCard.quoteProvider.card` — Deposit with Card main provider card and quote list rows
  * `depositTracker.executionRow.card` — Deposit Tracker execution rows

Example: global card plus a per-surface override for the deposit menu only:

```tsx theme={null}
import { UnifoldProvider } from "@unifold/connect-react-native";

<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey="your_key"
  config={{
    components: {
      card: {
        borderRadius: 12,
        borderWidth: 1,
        borderColor: "#E2E8F0",
      },
      depositMenu: {
        card: {
          borderRadius: 16,
          borderWidth: 2,
        },
      },
      button: {
        borderRadius: 8,
        borderWidth: 0,
        borderColor: "#E2E8F0",
      },
      input: {
        borderRadius: 8,
        borderWidth: 1,
        borderColor: "#E2E8F0",
      },
    },
  }}
>
  {children}
</UnifoldProvider>
```

## Card tokens

| Token                       | Type     | Default            | Description                                    |
| --------------------------- | -------- | ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `borderRadius`              | `number` | `12`               | Corner radius for cards and card-like rows.    |
| `borderWidth`               | `number` | `0`                | Border width in pixels. Use `0` for no border. |
| `borderColor`               | `string` | Theme border color | Border color (hex or theme token).             |
| `iconContainerBorderRadius` | `number` | `12`               | Radius for small icon circles inside cards.    |

## Where each surface is used

| Config path                          | UI                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `depositMenu.card`                   | Add Funds menu: Transfer Crypto, Deposit with Card, Deposit Tracker buttons                                                               |
| `transferCrypto.depositAddress.card` | Transfer Crypto: deposit address box with copy button                                                                                     |
| `depositCard.quoteProvider.card`     | Deposit with Card: main provider card and each quote row in the provider list                                                             |
| `depositTracker.executionRow.card`   | Deposit Tracker: each execution row                                                                                                       |
| `card` (global)                      | Default for all of the above; also used by the QR code wrapper (with a 1px border when global `borderWidth` is 0 so the frame is visible) |

## Button tokens

| Token          | Type     | Default            | Description                |
| -------------- | -------- | ------------------ | -------------------------- |
| `borderRadius` | `number` | `12`               | Corner radius for buttons. |
| `borderWidth`  | `number` | `0`                | Button border width.       |
| `borderColor`  | `string` | Theme border color | Button outline color.      |

## Input tokens

| Token          | Type     | Default            | Description                |
| -------------- | -------- | ------------------ | -------------------------- |
| `borderRadius` | `number` | `8`                | Input field corner radius. |
| `borderWidth`  | `number` | `1`                | Input border width.        |
| `borderColor`  | `string` | Theme border color | Input border color.        |

## Other components

* **Search**: `search.borderRadius` (default `8`) — search container.
* **List**: `list.rowBorderRadius` (default `12`) — list row corners.
* **Badge**: `badge.borderRadius` (default `8`) — badges and tags.
* **Sheet**: `sheet.shadowColor`, `sheet.shadowOffset`, `sheet.shadowOpacity`, `sheet.shadowRadius`, `sheet.elevation` — modal sheet shadow (no border tokens).

## Light / dark overrides

You can set different borders per theme:

```tsx theme={null}
config={{
  components: {
    light: {
      card: { borderRadius: 12, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: "#E2E8F0" },
    },
    dark: {
      card: { borderRadius: 8, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: "#38383A" },
    },
  },
}}
```

## Sharp / no-radius preset

For a “sharp” look with no rounding and visible borders:

```tsx theme={null}
components: {
  card: {
    borderRadius: 0,
    borderWidth: 2,
    borderColor: "#000000",
  },
  button: {
    borderRadius: 0,
    borderWidth: 2,
    borderColor: "#000000",
  },
}
```

All card surfaces inherit the global `card` unless you override a specific surface (e.g. `depositMenu.card`, `transferCrypto.depositAddress.card`).

# Font Customization

> Use custom fonts to match your app's typography.

The Unifold SDK supports custom fonts to match your app's typography. Your app must load fonts before rendering the SDK - the SDK does not load fonts automatically.

## Quick Start

```tsx theme={null}
import { UnifoldProvider } from "@unifold/connect-react-native";

<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey="pk_test_..."
  config={{
    fonts: {
      regular: "Inter-Regular",
      medium: "Inter-Medium",
      semibold: "Inter-SemiBold",
      bold: "Inter-Bold",
    },
  }}
>
  <YourApp />
</UnifoldProvider>
```

***

## Loading Fonts in Expo

Expo provides the easiest way to load custom fonts using `expo-font`.

### Step 1: Install expo-font

```bash theme={null}
npx expo install expo-font
```

### Step 2: Add Font Files

Place your font files in your project (e.g., `assets/fonts/`):

```
assets/
  fonts/
    Inter-Regular.ttf
    Inter-Medium.ttf
    Inter-SemiBold.ttf
    Inter-Bold.ttf
```

### Step 3: Load Fonts Before Rendering

```tsx theme={null}
import { useFonts } from "expo-font";
import { UnifoldProvider } from "@unifold/connect-react-native";
import * as SplashScreen from "expo-splash-screen";
import { useEffect } from "react";

// Prevent splash screen from hiding until fonts are loaded
SplashScreen.preventAutoHideAsync();

export default function App() {
  const [fontsLoaded, fontError] = useFonts({
    "Inter-Regular": require("./assets/fonts/Inter-Regular.ttf"),
    "Inter-Medium": require("./assets/fonts/Inter-Medium.ttf"),
    "Inter-SemiBold": require("./assets/fonts/Inter-SemiBold.ttf"),
    "Inter-Bold": require("./assets/fonts/Inter-Bold.ttf"),
  });

  useEffect(() => {
    if (fontsLoaded || fontError) {
      SplashScreen.hideAsync();
    }
  }, [fontsLoaded, fontError]);

  if (!fontsLoaded && !fontError) {
    return null;
  }

  return (
    <UnifoldProvider
      publishableKey="pk_test_..."
      config={{
        fonts: {
          regular: "Inter-Regular",
          medium: "Inter-Medium",
          semibold: "Inter-SemiBold",
          bold: "Inter-Bold",
        },
      }}
    >
      <YourApp />
    </UnifoldProvider>
  );
}
```

***

## Using Google Fonts with Expo

Expo provides pre-packaged Google Fonts that are easy to use.

### Step 1: Install the Font Package

```bash theme={null}
npx expo install @expo-google-fonts/inter expo-font
```

Other popular fonts:

```bash theme={null}
# Roboto
npx expo install @expo-google-fonts/roboto

# Open Sans
npx expo install @expo-google-fonts/open-sans

# Poppins
npx expo install @expo-google-fonts/poppins

# SF Pro (system font alternative)
npx expo install @expo-google-fonts/source-sans-pro
```

### Step 2: Load and Use

```tsx theme={null}
import {
  useFonts,
  Inter_400Regular,
  Inter_500Medium,
  Inter_600SemiBold,
  Inter_700Bold,
} from "@expo-google-fonts/inter";
import { UnifoldProvider } from "@unifold/connect-react-native";

export default function App() {
  const [fontsLoaded] = useFonts({
    Inter_400Regular,
    Inter_500Medium,
    Inter_600SemiBold,
    Inter_700Bold,
  });

  if (!fontsLoaded) return null;

  return (
    <UnifoldProvider
      publishableKey="pk_test_..."
      config={{
        fonts: {
          regular: "Inter_400Regular",
          medium: "Inter_500Medium",
          semibold: "Inter_600SemiBold",
          bold: "Inter_700Bold",
        },
      }}
    >
      <YourApp />
    </UnifoldProvider>
  );
}
```

***

## Loading Fonts in Bare React Native

For bare React Native projects (without Expo), you have two options.

### Option 1: Using expo-font (Recommended)

`expo-font` works in bare React Native projects without requiring the full Expo SDK.

```bash theme={null}
npm install expo-font
```

Then follow the same approach as the Expo examples above.

### Option 2: Native Font Linking

Link fonts directly in your native iOS and Android projects.

#### iOS Setup

1. Create a `Resources` folder in your iOS project if it doesn't exist

2. Add font files to `ios/YourApp/Resources/`

3. Add fonts to `Info.plist`:

```xml theme={null}
<key>UIAppFonts</key>
<array>
  <string>Inter-Regular.ttf</string>
  <string>Inter-Medium.ttf</string>
  <string>Inter-SemiBold.ttf</string>
  <string>Inter-Bold.ttf</string>
</array>
```

4. In Xcode, ensure fonts are included in "Copy Bundle Resources" build phase

#### Android Setup

1. Create the fonts directory:

```
android/app/src/main/assets/fonts/
```

2. Add your font files to this directory:

```
android/app/src/main/assets/fonts/
  Inter-Regular.ttf
  Inter-Medium.ttf
  Inter-SemiBold.ttf
  Inter-Bold.ttf
```

#### Usage

After native linking, use the font family name (without the file extension):

```tsx theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey="pk_test_..."
  config={{
    fonts: {
      regular: "Inter-Regular",
      medium: "Inter-Medium",
      semibold: "Inter-SemiBold",
      bold: "Inter-Bold",
    },
  }}
>
  <YourApp />
</UnifoldProvider>
```

***

## SDK Font Configuration Options

### Single Font Family

Apply one font family to all text weights. Useful for variable fonts or when you want consistent typography:

```tsx theme={null}
config={{
  fontFamily: "Inter"
}}
```

### Granular Font Weights

Specify different font files for each weight:

```tsx theme={null}
config={{
  fonts: {
    regular: "Inter-Regular",    // 400 weight - body text, descriptions
    medium: "Inter-Medium",      // 500 weight - labels, emphasized text
    semibold: "Inter-SemiBold",  // 600 weight - headings, buttons, titles
    bold: "Inter-Bold"           // 700 weight - strong emphasis (rarely used)
  }
}}
```

### Combining Both

If you provide both `fontFamily` and `fonts`, the granular `fonts` config takes precedence, with `fontFamily` as fallback for any missing weights:

```tsx theme={null}
config={{
  fontFamily: "Inter",  // Fallback for any missing weights
  fonts: {
    semibold: "Inter-SemiBold",  // Only override semibold
  }
}}
```

***

## Font Weight Usage in SDK

The SDK uses different font weights for different UI elements:

| Weight         | Config Key | Used For                                          |
| -------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Regular (400)  | `regular`  | Body text, descriptions, input text, placeholders |
| Medium (500)   | `medium`   | Labels, section headers, slightly emphasized text |
| SemiBold (600) | `semibold` | Modal titles, card titles, buttons, token names   |
| Bold (700)     | `bold`     | Strong emphasis (rarely used in the SDK)          |

***

## Troubleshooting

### Fonts Not Showing

1. **Ensure fonts are loaded before rendering the SDK**
   ```tsx theme={null}
   if (!fontsLoaded) return null; // or a loading screen
   ```

2. **Check font file names match exactly** - Font names are case-sensitive

3. **Verify font files are valid** - Try opening them in a font viewer

4. **Rebuild your app** - Native font changes require a full rebuild:
   ```bash theme={null}
   # Expo
   npx expo start -c

   # Bare React Native
   cd ios && pod install && cd ..
   npx react-native run-ios
   ```

### Fonts Look Different on iOS vs Android

iOS and Android may render the same font slightly differently. This is normal system behavior. If you need pixel-perfect consistency, consider using a font that renders similarly on both platforms.

### Using System Fonts

To use the system font (San Francisco on iOS, Roboto on Android), simply don't provide any font configuration:

```tsx theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider publishableKey="pk_test_...">
  {/* Uses system fonts by default */}
</UnifoldProvider>
```

***

## Popular Font Recommendations

| Font       | Style              | Google Fonts Package            |
| ---------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------- |
| Inter      | Modern, clean      | `@expo-google-fonts/inter`      |
| Roboto     | Android default    | `@expo-google-fonts/roboto`     |
| Open Sans  | Friendly, readable | `@expo-google-fonts/open-sans`  |
| Poppins    | Geometric, modern  | `@expo-google-fonts/poppins`    |
| Nunito     | Rounded, friendly  | `@expo-google-fonts/nunito`     |
| Lato       | Professional       | `@expo-google-fonts/lato`       |
| Montserrat | Bold, impactful    | `@expo-google-fonts/montserrat` |

***

## TypeScript Support

```tsx theme={null}
import type { FontConfig } from "@unifold/connect-react-native";

const myFonts: FontConfig = {
  regular: "Inter-Regular",
  medium: "Inter-Medium",
  semibold: "Inter-SemiBold",
  bold: "Inter-Bold",
};
```

# Theme Reference

> Complete reference for all theme tokens and their inheritance.

Component tokens inherit from base color tokens. Here's the inheritance chain:

```
Base Colors (theme.dark / theme.light)
│
├── foreground
│   ├── header.titleColor
│   ├── header.buttonColor
│   ├── card.titleColor
│   ├── card.textRightColor
│   ├── card.rowRightLabel
│   ├── container.titleColor
│   ├── container.iconColor
│   ├── input.textColor
│   ├── search.inputColor
│   └── button.secondaryText
│
├── foregroundMuted
│   ├── card.subtitleColor
│   ├── card.labelColor
│   ├── card.headerColor
│   ├── card.labelRightColor
│   ├── card.subtextRightColor
│   ├── card.rowLeftLabel
│   ├── card.actionColor
│   ├── card.actionIcon
│   ├── card.descriptionColor
│   ├── container.subtitleColor
│   ├── container.actionColor
│   ├── container.actionTitle
│   ├── input.placeholderColor
│   ├── search.placeholderColor
│   └── list.titleSectionColor
│
├── card
│   ├── card.backgroundColor
│   ├── input.backgroundColor
│   ├── search.backgroundColor
│   └── button.secondaryBackground
│
├── primary
│   ├── card.iconColor
│   ├── card.iconBackgroundColor (+ 26% opacity)
│   ├── container.buttonColor
│   └── button.primaryBackground
│
├── primaryForeground
│   ├── container.buttonTitleColor
│   └── button.primaryText
│
├── warning
│   └── card.labelHighlightRightColor
│
├── success
│   └── container.iconBackgroundColor
│
└── border
    └── input.borderColor
```

***

## Quick Override Examples

### Dark Purple Theme

```tsx theme={null}
config={{
  appearance: "dark",
  theme: {
    dark: {
      primary: "#8B5CF6",
      background: "#0F0F10",
      card: "#1A1A1D"
    }
  },
  components: {
    card: {
      iconBackgroundColor: "rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.15)"
    }
  }
}}
```

### Light Minimal Theme

```tsx theme={null}
config={{
  appearance: "light",
  theme: {
    light: {
      primary: "#000000",
      card: "#FAFAFA",
      foregroundMuted: "#737373"
    }
  }
}}
```

### Custom Status Colors

```tsx theme={null}
config={{
  components: {
    container: {
      iconBackgroundColor: "#10B981", // Custom success green
      iconColor: "#FFFFFF"
    },
    card: {
      labelHighlightRightColor: "#EAB308" // Custom warning yellow
    }
  }
}}
```

### Auto Mode with Light/Dark Component Tokens

```tsx theme={null}
config={{
  appearance: "auto", // Follow system preference
  components: {
    // Light mode cards
    light: {
      card: {
        backgroundColor: "#FFFFFF",
        titleColor: "#0F172A",
        subtitleColor: "#64748B"
      },
      header: {
        titleColor: "#0F172A"
      }
    },
    // Dark mode cards
    dark: {
      card: {
        backgroundColor: "#1E1E1E",
        titleColor: "#FAFAFA",
        subtitleColor: "#A1A1AA"
      },
      header: {
        titleColor: "#FAFAFA"
      }
    }
  }
}}
```

# Theming

> Customize the appearance of deposit UI components to match your app's design.

The Unifold React Native SDK provides a comprehensive theming system that allows you to customize the appearance of all deposit UI components to match your app's design.

## Overview

The SDK supports three levels of customization:

1. **General Theme** - Quick setup with appearance mode and accent color
2. **Base Color Tokens** - Full control over the color palette
3. **Component Tokens** - Granular control over individual UI elements

## Quick Start

```tsx theme={null}
import { UnifoldProvider } from "@unifold/connect-react-native";

function App() {
  return (
    <UnifoldProvider
      publishableKey="pk_test_..."
      config={{
        appearance: "dark",
        accentColor: "#8B5CF6", // Purple accent
      }}
    >
      <YourApp />
    </UnifoldProvider>
  );
}
```

***

## General Theme Configuration

### Appearance Mode

Control the overall theme appearance:

```tsx theme={null}
config={{
  appearance: "dark" | "light" | "auto"
}}
```

| Value     | Description              |
| --------- | ------------------------ |
| `"dark"`  | Dark mode (default)      |
| `"light"` | Light mode               |
| `"auto"`  | Follow system preference |

### Accent Color

Set a primary brand color that applies to buttons, links, and interactive elements:

```tsx theme={null}
config={{
  accentColor: "#8B5CF6" // Your brand color
}}
```

This overrides the `primary` color in both light and dark modes.

***

## Base Color Tokens

For full control over the color palette, use the `theme` configuration:

```tsx theme={null}
config={{
  theme: {
    light: {
      background: "#FFFFFF",
      card: "#F8FAFC",
      foreground: "#0F172A",
      primary: "#3B82F6",
      // ... other tokens
    },
    dark: {
      background: "#2D2C2F",
      card: "#3A393C",
      foreground: "#F8FAFC",
      primary: "#3B82F6",
      // ... other tokens
    }
  }
}}
```

### Available Base Color Tokens

| Token               | Description              | Light Default     | Dark Default           |
| ------------------- | ------------------------ | ----------------- | ---------------------- |
| `background`        | Modal/sheet background   | `#FFFFFF`         | `#2D2C2F`              |
| `card`              | Card backgrounds         | `#F8FAFC`         | `#3A393C`              |
| `cardHover`         | Card hover/pressed state | `#F1F5F9`         | `#48474A`              |
| `foreground`        | Primary text color       | `#0F172A`         | `#F8FAFC`              |
| `foregroundMuted`   | Secondary text color     | `#64748B`         | `#94A3B8`              |
| `foregroundSubtle`  | Tertiary text color      | `#94A3B8`         | `#64748B`              |
| `border`            | Primary border color     | `#E2E8F0`         | `#38383A`              |
| `borderSecondary`   | Secondary border color   | `#CBD5E1`         | `#48484A`              |
| `primary`           | Brand/accent color       | `#3B82F6`         | `#3B82F6`              |
| `primaryForeground` | Text on primary color    | `#FFFFFF`         | `#FFFFFF`              |
| `success`           | Success state color      | `#22C55E`         | `#22C55E`              |
| `successBackground` | Success background       | `#DCFCE7`         | `rgba(34,197,94,0.1)`  |
| `warning`           | Warning state color      | `#F59E0B`         | `#F59E0B`              |
| `warningBackground` | Warning background       | `#FEF3C7`         | `rgba(245,158,11,0.1)` |
| `error`             | Error state color        | `#EF4444`         | `#EF4444`              |
| `errorBackground`   | Error background         | `#FEE2E2`         | `rgba(239,68,68,0.1)`  |
| `overlay`           | Modal overlay            | `rgba(0,0,0,0.5)` | `rgba(0,0,0,0.7)`      |

***

## Font Customization

The SDK supports custom fonts to match your app's typography.

```tsx theme={null}
config={{
  fonts: {
    regular: "Inter-Regular",
    medium: "Inter-Medium",
    semibold: "Inter-SemiBold",
    bold: "Inter-Bold",
  }
}}
```

Or use a single font family for all weights:

```tsx theme={null}
config={{
  fontFamily: "Inter"
}}
```

> **Important:** Your app must load fonts before rendering the SDK. The SDK does not load fonts automatically.

For complete instructions on loading fonts in Expo, bare React Native, and using Google Fonts, see the **[Font Customization Guide](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/ui-customization/fonts)**.

***

## Component Tokens (Granular Customization)

For pixel-perfect control, override specific component tokens:

```tsx theme={null}
config={{
  components: {
    header: {
      titleColor: "#FFFFFF",
      buttonColor: "#FFFFFF"
    },
    card: {
      backgroundColor: "#1F1F23",
      titleColor: "#FFFFFF",
      subtitleColor: "#9CA3AF"
    },
    // ... other components
  }
}}
```

### Light/Dark Mode Support

Component tokens support separate light and dark mode configurations:

```tsx theme={null}
config={{
  components: {
    // Flat overrides apply to BOTH modes
    header: {
      titleColor: "#FFFFFF"
    },
    
    // Mode-specific overrides (takes priority over flat)
    light: {
      card: {
        backgroundColor: "#F5F5F5",
        titleColor: "#1A1A1A"
      }
    },
    dark: {
      card: {
        backgroundColor: "#1F1F23",
        titleColor: "#FFFFFF"
      }
    }
  }
}}
```

**Override Priority (highest wins):**

1. Mode-specific overrides (`components.light.*` or `components.dark.*`)
2. Flat overrides (`components.header.*`, `components.card.*`, etc.)
3. Base color defaults (inherited from `theme.light` or `theme.dark`)

### Header Tokens

Controls the modal header appearance.

| Token         | Description             | Default Base Token |
| ------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------ |
| `titleColor`  | Modal title text        | `foreground`       |
| `buttonColor` | Close/back button icons | `foreground`       |

### Card Tokens

Controls cards, selectors, and detail sections.

| Token                      | Description                            | Default Base Token      |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| `backgroundColor`          | Card background                        | `card`                  |
| `titleColor`               | Card titles, token names               | `foreground`            |
| `subtitleColor`            | Card subtitles, network names          | `foregroundMuted`       |
| `labelColor`               | Section labels                         | `foregroundMuted`       |
| `headerColor`              | Card header text                       | `foregroundMuted`       |
| `labelRightColor`          | Right-side labels                      | `foregroundMuted`       |
| `labelHighlightRightColor` | Highlighted labels (e.g., min deposit) | `warning`               |
| `textRightColor`           | Right-side text values                 | `foreground`            |
| `subtextRightColor`        | Right-side secondary text              | `foregroundMuted`       |
| `rowLeftLabel`             | Detail row labels                      | `foregroundMuted`       |
| `rowRightLabel`            | Detail row values                      | `foreground`            |
| `iconColor`                | Icon colors in cards                   | `primary`               |
| `iconBackgroundColor`      | Icon background circles                | `primary` (26% opacity) |
| `actionColor`              | Action icons (chevrons, copy)          | `foregroundMuted`       |
| `actionIcon`               | External link icons                    | `foregroundMuted`       |
| `descriptionColor`         | Description text                       | `foregroundMuted`       |

### Input Tokens

Controls text inputs and search fields.

| Token              | Description      | Default Base Token |
| ------------------ | ---------------- | ------------------ |
| `backgroundColor`  | Input background | `card`             |
| `textColor`        | Input text       | `foreground`       |
| `placeholderColor` | Placeholder text | `foregroundMuted`  |
| `borderColor`      | Input border     | `border`           |

### Button Tokens

Controls primary and secondary buttons.

| Token                 | Description                 | Default Base Token  |
| --------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------- |
| `primaryBackground`   | Primary button background   | `primary`           |
| `primaryText`         | Primary button text         | `primaryForeground` |
| `secondaryBackground` | Secondary button background | `card`              |
| `secondaryText`       | Secondary button text       | `foreground`        |

### Container Tokens

Controls status displays and deposit completion screens.

| Token                 | Description                   | Default Base Token  |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------- |
| `titleColor`          | Status titles                 | `foreground`        |
| `subtitleColor`       | Status subtitles              | `foregroundMuted`   |
| `actionColor`         | Toggle chevrons               | `foregroundMuted`   |
| `actionTitle`         | Toggle text ("See more/less") | `foregroundMuted`   |
| `buttonColor`         | Primary button background     | `primary`           |
| `buttonTitleColor`    | Primary button text           | `primaryForeground` |
| `iconBackgroundColor` | Status badge background       | `success`           |
| `iconColor`           | Status badge icon (checkmark) | `foreground`        |

### Search Tokens

Controls the token search input.

| Token              | Description             | Default Base Token |
| ------------------ | ----------------------- | ------------------ |
| `backgroundColor`  | Search input background | `card`             |
| `inputColor`       | Search text             | `foreground`       |
| `placeholderColor` | Search placeholder      | `foregroundMuted`  |

### List Tokens

Controls list section headers.

| Token               | Description                            | Default Base Token |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| `titleSectionColor` | Section headers ("Quick select", etc.) | `foregroundMuted`  |

## Complete Example

Here's a comprehensive example combining all customization options:

```tsx theme={null}
import { UnifoldProvider } from "@unifold/connect-react-native";

function App() {
  return (
    <UnifoldProvider
      publishableKey="pk_test_..."
      config={{
        // General
        appearance: "auto", // Follow system preference
        modalTitle: "Add Funds",
        hideDepositTracker: false,
        transferInputVariant: "single_input",
        
        // Fonts
        fonts: {
          regular: "SF-Pro-Regular",
          medium: "SF-Pro-Medium",
          semibold: "SF-Pro-Semibold",
          bold: "SF-Pro-Bold"
        },
        
        // Base theme colors (per mode)
        theme: {
          light: {
            primary: "#7C3AED",
            background: "#FFFFFF",
            card: "#F5F5F5",
          },
          dark: {
            primary: "#8B5CF6",
            background: "#0F0F10",
            card: "#1A1A1D",
          }
        },
        
        // Granular component overrides
        components: {
          // Flat overrides (apply to both modes)
          container: {
            iconBackgroundColor: "#22C55E"
          },
          
          // Light mode specific
          light: {
            header: {
              titleColor: "#1A1A1A"
            },
            card: {
              backgroundColor: "#F5F5F5",
              titleColor: "#1A1A1A",
              iconColor: "#7C3AED",
              iconBackgroundColor: "rgba(124, 58, 237, 0.1)"
            }
          },
          
          // Dark mode specific
          dark: {
            header: {
              titleColor: "#FFFFFF"
            },
            card: {
              backgroundColor: "#1A1A1D",
              titleColor: "#FFFFFF",
              iconColor: "#8B5CF6",
              iconBackgroundColor: "rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.15)"
            }
          }
        }
      }}
    >
      <YourApp />
    </UnifoldProvider>
  );
}
```

# UnifoldProvider

> The root provider component for Unifold SDK

The `UnifoldProvider` component initializes the Unifold SDK and must wrap your application (or the part of your app that uses Unifold).

## Import

```tsx theme={null}
import { UnifoldProvider } from '@unifold/connect-react-native';
```

## Usage

```tsx theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey="pk_live_your_key"
  config={{
    appearance: 'dark',
    modalTitle: 'Deposit Funds',
    hideDepositTracker: false,
  }}
>
  <App />
</UnifoldProvider>
```

## Props

<ParamField path="publishableKey" type="string" required>
  Your Unifold publishable key. Get this from your [Unifold Dashboard](https://unifold.io/dashboard).

  * Use `pk_test_...` for development/testing
  * Use `pk_live_...` for production
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="config" type="object">
  Optional configuration object.

  <Expandable title="config properties">
    <ParamField path="config.appearance" type="'light' | 'dark' | 'auto'" default="'dark'">
      Theme mode for the deposit modal.

      * `'light'`: Light theme
      * `'dark'`: Dark theme
      * `'auto'`: Follow system preference
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.modalTitle" type="string">
      Custom title for the deposit modal header.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.hideDepositTracker" type="boolean" default="false">
      Hide the deposit tracker button that shows recent deposits.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.transferInputVariant" type="'single_input' | 'double_input' | 'compact'" default="'double_input'">
      Layout variant for the Transfer Crypto token selector.

      * `'single_input'`: Single combined selector
      * `'double_input'`: Separate token and chain selectors (default)
      * `'compact'`: Minimal, QR-focused layout. Token and chain are picked from a single combined selector, the QR code shows the token icon with the chain as a badge, and price impact, slippage, and minimum deposit details open in an info sheet
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.depositMenuDisplay" type="'stacked' | 'tabs'" default="'stacked'">
      Layout for the deposit menu.

      * `'stacked'`: All deposit options in a single list (default)
      * `'tabs'`: A segmented tab bar splits options into **Use Crypto** and **Use Cash** tabs

      See [Deposit Menu Display](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/deposit-menu-display).
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.accentColor" type="string">
      Primary brand color override (e.g. `'#8B5CF6'`). Applied to both light and dark modes. For full color customization, use `config.theme`. See [Theming](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/ui-customization/theming).
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.theme" type="ThemeConfig">
      Full color customization per mode. See [Theming](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/ui-customization/theming).
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.fontFamily" type="string">
      Single font family for all text. Your app must load the font before rendering the SDK. See [Font Customization](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/ui-customization/fonts).
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.fonts" type="FontConfig">
      Granular font configuration for different weights (`regular`, `medium`, `semibold`, `bold`). See [Font Customization](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/ui-customization/fonts).
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.components" type="ComponentConfig">
      Component-specific token overrides (header, card, button, input, etc.). See [Theming](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/ui-customization/theming).
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.sheetBorderRadius" type="SheetBorderRadius">
      Border radius configuration for all bottom sheets. See [Border Radius](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/ui-customization/border-radius).
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.enableStripeLink" type="boolean" default="false">
      When `true`, shows **Pay with Link** (Stripe) on the deposit menu opened via `beginDeposit`. Requires **`@stripe/stripe-react-native`** in your app and **native Onramp** enabled (Expo `includeOnramp: true` or bare equivalent — see [Stripe Onramp overview](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/stripe-onramp/overview)). Stripe onramp is bundled with the main package; **no** separate `import '@unifold/connect-react-native/stripe'` is required.

      Email/phone prefill for that flow is set on each **`beginDeposit({ user: { email, phone } })`** call, not here.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.stripeLink" type="object">
      Stripe Link Pay tuning options (only applies when `enableStripeLink` is `true`):

      * **`paymentSelectorPosition`** (`'header' | 'inline'`, default `'header'`) — where to render the payment method selector: above the amount (`'header'`) or below it (`'inline'`).
      * **`skipSuccessConfirmation`** (`boolean`, default `false`) — skip the success confirmation screen and fire completion immediately.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.enableCoinbaseApplePay" type="boolean" default="dashboard, else false">
      Shows **Pay with Apple Pay** (a headless Coinbase onramp) on the deposit menu opened via `beginDeposit`. Overrides the dashboard toggle — resolves as `flag ?? dashboard ?? false` (opt-in, like Cash App / Connect Wallet). **iOS only**, and still gated by a live regional provider availability check, so the row may not appear even when set to `true`. See [Pay with Apple Pay](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/coinbase-apple-pay).

      A host-trusted email that skips the email steps is set on each **`beginDeposit({ user: { email } })`** call, not here.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.enableTransferCrypto" type="boolean" default="dashboard, else true">
      Shows the **Transfer Crypto** option on the deposit menu. Overrides the dashboard toggle (`flag ?? dashboard ?? true`).
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.enableCashApp" type="boolean" default="dashboard, else false">
      Shows the **Pay with Cash App** option on the deposit menu. Overrides the dashboard toggle (`flag ?? dashboard ?? false`).
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.enableConnectWallet" type="boolean" default="dashboard, else false">
      Shows the **Connect Wallet** option on the deposit menu. Overrides the dashboard toggle (`flag ?? dashboard ?? false`).
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.enableFiatOnramp" type="boolean" default="dashboard, else true">
      Shows the **Deposit with Card** (fiat on-ramp) option on the deposit menu. Overrides the dashboard toggle (`flag ?? dashboard ?? true`).
    </ParamField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>

<Note>
  There is **no** `config.stripeMerchantIdentifier`. The Apple Pay merchant identifier is read automatically from your **Unifold dashboard** (via the Stripe config endpoint) at runtime — you never pass it to the SDK. The `merchantIdentifier` in your `app.json` Stripe plugin is still required for the native entitlement; keep the two in sync. See the [Integration checklist](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/integration-checklist#apple-pay-merchantidentifier).
</Note>

## Example with All Options

```tsx theme={null}
import { UnifoldProvider } from '@unifold/connect-react-native';

export default function App() {
  return (
    <UnifoldProvider
      publishableKey="pk_live_abc123"
      config={{
        appearance: 'auto',
        modalTitle: 'Add Funds',
        hideDepositTracker: false,
      }}
    >
      <Navigation />
    </UnifoldProvider>
  );
}
```

## Placement

<Warning>
  `UnifoldProvider` should be placed at the root of your app, above any navigation or screens that will use the `useUnifold` hook.
</Warning>

### Expo Router

```tsx app/_layout.tsx theme={null}
import { Stack } from 'expo-router';
import { UnifoldProvider } from '@unifold/connect-react-native';

export default function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <UnifoldProvider publishableKey="pk_live_your_key">
      <Stack />
    </UnifoldProvider>
  );
}
```

For **Pay with Link** in the deposit menu, set `config.enableStripeLink: true` and complete Stripe native setup. See [Stripe Onramp overview](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/stripe-onramp/overview) and [Integration checklist](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/integration-checklist).

### React Navigation

```tsx App.tsx theme={null}
import { NavigationContainer } from '@react-navigation/native';
import { UnifoldProvider } from '@unifold/connect-react-native';

export default function App() {
  return (
    <UnifoldProvider publishableKey="pk_live_your_key">
      <NavigationContainer>
        <RootNavigator />
      </NavigationContainer>
    </UnifoldProvider>
  );
}
```

## TypeScript

```tsx theme={null}
import { UnifoldProvider, UnifoldProviderProps } from '@unifold/connect-react-native';

const config: UnifoldProviderProps['config'] = {
  appearance: 'dark',
  modalTitle: 'Deposit',
};
```

# useUnifold

> Hook to access Unifold deposit functionality

The `useUnifold` hook provides access to the deposit functionality. It must be used within a component wrapped by `UnifoldProvider`.

## Import

```tsx theme={null}
import { useUnifold } from '@unifold/connect-react-native';
```

## Usage

```tsx theme={null}
function DepositButton() {
  const { beginDeposit, closeDeposit, publishableKey } = useUnifold();

  const handleDeposit = async () => {
    const result = await beginDeposit({
      externalUserId: 'user_123',
    });
  };

  return <Button onPress={handleDeposit} title="Deposit" />;
}
```

## Return Value

<ResponseField name="beginDeposit" type="(config: DepositConfig) => Promise<DepositResult>">
  Opens the deposit modal and returns a promise that resolves when the deposit completes or rejects if cancelled.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="closeDeposit" type="() => void">
  Programmatically closes the deposit modal. Useful for closing the modal from outside the flow.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="publishableKey" type="string">
  The publishable key configured in `UnifoldProvider`.
</ResponseField>

## beginDeposit

Opens the deposit modal with the specified configuration.

### Parameters

<ParamField path="config" type="DepositConfig" required>
  Configuration for the deposit flow.
</ParamField>

### DepositConfig

<ParamField path="externalUserId" type="string" required>
  Your unique identifier for the user. This links deposits to your user in the Unifold dashboard.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="destinationChainType" type="'ethereum' | 'solana' | 'bitcoin'">
  The blockchain type for the destination. If not specified, the user can select from available options.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="destinationChainId" type="string">
  The chain ID for the destination chain (e.g. `'137'` for Polygon, `'mainnet'` for Solana). See [Supported Chains](/get-started/supported-chains) for the full list.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="destinationTokenAddress" type="string">
  The token contract address on the destination chain. Use the native token address for the chain's native currency.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="destinationTokenSymbol" type="string">
  The token symbol (e.g., `'USDC'`, `'ETH'`, `'POL'`). Used for display purposes.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="recipientAddress" type="string">
  The wallet address that will receive the funds. If not specified, Unifold will create a temporary deposit address.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="showBalance" type="boolean">
  When `true` (and destination fields are set), shows the user’s destination token balance in the deposit header once project config has loaded.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="depositConfirmationMode" type="'auto_ui' | 'auto_silent' | 'manual'" default="'auto_ui'">
  Controls waiting UI and polling after a transfer-style deposit. See SDK README or product docs for behavior of each mode.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="initialScreen" type="'main' | 'transfer' | 'card' | 'tracker' | 'cashapp' | 'wallet' | 'apple_pay' | 'stripe_link'" default="'main'">
  Which screen to open first. Defaults to `'main'` (the deposit menu). Pass another value to skip the menu and land directly on that screen (`'apple_pay'` opens [Pay with Apple Pay](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/coinbase-apple-pay); `'stripe_link'` opens [Pay with Link](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/stripe-onramp/overview)). Closing a non-menu entry screen dismisses the entire deposit flow. If the requested screen isn't available (e.g. `'apple_pay'` on Android or gated off, `'stripe_link'` while `enableStripeLink` is off, or `'tracker'` while `hideDepositTracker` is `true`), it falls back to `'main'`. See [Initial Screen](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/initial-screen).
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="defaultChainType" type="'ethereum' | 'solana' | 'bitcoin'">
  Pre-selects the source network in Transfer Crypto when combined with `defaultChainId`.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="defaultChainId" type="string">
  Pre-selects the source chain ID for Transfer Crypto.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="defaultTokenAddress" type="string">
  Pre-selects the source token on the chosen default network.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="user" type="UnifoldUser">
  Host-app-supplied user identity used to pre-fill supported deposit flows.

  * **`user.email`** — for **Pay with Apple Pay** (Coinbase), a valid trusted email **skips** the email-entry and email-OTP steps (phone verification still runs). For **Pay with Link** (Stripe), it pre-fills the email step.
  * **`user.phone`** — optional phone; use E.164 (e.g. `+12125551234`). Used by **Pay with Link**; with `user.email`, Stripe may skip the email/phone steps.

  It's an object so more fields can be added later without new top-level params. See [Pay with Apple Pay](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/coinbase-apple-pay) and [Stripe Onramp overview](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/features/stripe-onramp/overview).
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onSuccess" type="(data: DepositResult) => void">
  Callback fired when the deposit succeeds. Called immediately when success is detected.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onError" type="(error: DepositError) => void">
  Callback fired when an error occurs during the deposit flow.
</ParamField>

### Returns

Returns a `Promise<DepositResult>` that:

* **Resolves** with `DepositResult` when the deposit completes successfully
* **Rejects** with `DepositError` when the user closes the modal or an error occurs

### DepositResult

```tsx theme={null}
interface DepositResult {
  message: string;        // Human-readable success message
  transaction?: unknown;  // Transaction details (if available)
  executionId?: string;   // Unifold execution ID for tracking
}
```

### DepositError

```tsx theme={null}
interface DepositError {
  message: string;      // Human-readable error message
  error?: unknown;      // Original error object (if available)
  code?: string;        // Error code (e.g., 'DEPOSIT_CANCELLED')
}
```

## Examples

### Basic Usage

```tsx theme={null}
const { beginDeposit } = useUnifold();

await beginDeposit({
  externalUserId: 'user_123',
});
```

### With Pre-configured Destination

```tsx theme={null}
const { beginDeposit } = useUnifold();

await beginDeposit({
  externalUserId: 'user_123',
  destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
  destinationChainId: '137',
  destinationTokenAddress: '0x3c499c542cef5e3811e1192ce70d8cc03d5c3359',
  destinationTokenSymbol: 'USDC',
  recipientAddress: '0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc9e7595f0bEb2',
});
```

### With Callbacks

```tsx theme={null}
const { beginDeposit } = useUnifold();

await beginDeposit({
  externalUserId: 'user_123',
  onSuccess: (data) => {
    console.log('Deposit succeeded:', data.executionId);
    // Update UI, fetch balance, etc.
  },
  onError: (error) => {
    console.error('Deposit failed:', error.message);
    // Show error toast, log to analytics, etc.
  },
});
```

### Handling the Promise

```tsx theme={null}
const { beginDeposit } = useUnifold();

try {
  const result = await beginDeposit({
    externalUserId: 'user_123',
  });
  
  // Deposit completed successfully
  console.log('Success:', result.message);
  Alert.alert('Success', 'Your deposit has been received!');
  
} catch (error) {
  if (error.code === 'DEPOSIT_CANCELLED') {
    // User closed the modal - this is normal
    console.log('User cancelled');
  } else {
    // Actual error occurred
    console.error('Error:', error.message);
    Alert.alert('Error', error.message);
  }
}
```

### Programmatic Close

```tsx theme={null}
const { beginDeposit, closeDeposit } = useUnifold();

// Close after timeout (example)
useEffect(() => {
  const timer = setTimeout(() => {
    closeDeposit();
  }, 60000); // Close after 1 minute
  
  return () => clearTimeout(timer);
}, []);
```

## Error Handling

<Info>
  When the user closes the deposit modal without completing, the promise rejects with `code: 'DEPOSIT_CANCELLED'`. This is expected behavior and should be handled gracefully.
</Info>

```tsx theme={null}
try {
  await beginDeposit({ externalUserId: 'user_123' });
} catch (error) {
  if (error.code === 'DEPOSIT_CANCELLED') {
    // Not an error - user just closed the modal
    return;
  }
  // Handle actual errors
  showErrorToast(error.message);
}
```

# Overview

The Withdraw flow enables users to send crypto from your platform back to an external wallet address. Users enter an amount and recipient address, confirm in a modal, and Unifold handles routing, tracking, and confirmation callbacks.

## How it works

1. Your app calls `beginWithdraw()` with the source token, the user's sender address, and a `withdraw` callback
2. Unifold opens a modal where the user selects a destination token, enters an amount, and provides a recipient address (optionally pre-filled with your defaults)
3. When the user confirms, Unifold calls your `withdraw` callback with the full transaction details (`WithdrawTransactionInfo`)
4. Your app signs and broadcasts the transaction using your own wallet infrastructure
5. Unifold tracks the withdrawal and fires `onSuccess` or `onError` when it resolves

<Note>
  The React Native SDK is **wallet-agnostic**. `senderAddress` is a plain string used only to fetch the user's balance — the SDK has no knowledge of or dependency on any wallet library. You own the signing and broadcasting logic entirely inside the `withdraw` callback.
</Note>

## Prerequisites

<CodeGroup>
  ```bash npm theme={null}
  npm install @unifold/connect-react-native
  ```

  ```bash pnpm theme={null}
  pnpm add @unifold/connect-react-native
  ```

  ```bash yarn theme={null}
  yarn add @unifold/connect-react-native
  ```

  ```bash expo theme={null}
  npx expo install @unifold/connect-react-native
  ```
</CodeGroup>

## Quick start

### 1. Set up the provider

Wrap your app with `UnifoldProvider`:

```tsx theme={null}
import { UnifoldProvider } from '@unifold/connect-react-native';

export default function App() {
  return (
    <UnifoldProvider publishableKey="pk_live_your_key">
      <YourApp />
    </UnifoldProvider>
  );
}
```

### 2. Call beginWithdraw

Use the `useUnifold()` hook to launch the withdrawal modal. Pass the source token and chain up front — the user picks the destination token and amount inside the modal.

```tsx theme={null}
import { useUnifold } from '@unifold/connect-react-native';

function WithdrawButton({ userAddress }: { userAddress: string }) {
  const { beginWithdraw } = useUnifold();

  const handleWithdraw = async () => {
    await beginWithdraw({
      externalUserId: 'user_123',
      senderAddress: userAddress,

      // Source token — what the user is sending from
      sourceChainType: 'ethereum',
      sourceChainId: '8453',        // Base
      sourceTokenAddress: '0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913',
      sourceTokenSymbol: 'USDC',

      // Optional: pre-select destination (user can still change)
      defaultDestinationChainType: 'ethereum',
      defaultDestinationChainId: '1',         // Ethereum mainnet
      defaultDestinationTokenAddress: '0xa0b86991c6218b36c1d19d4a2e9eb0ce3606eb48', // USDC

      // Your platform signs and broadcasts the transaction
      withdraw: async (txInfo) => {
        // See Withdraw Functions for ready-to-use implementations
      },

      onSuccess: (data) => console.log('Withdrawal complete:', data.message),
      onError: (err) => console.error('Withdrawal failed:', err.message),
    });
  };

  return <Button onPress={handleWithdraw} title="Withdraw" />;
}
```

The `withdraw` callback receives a `WithdrawTransactionInfo` object with everything needed to construct the on-chain transaction. See [Withdraw Functions](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/withdraw/withdraw-functions) for ready-to-use implementations.

<Tip>
  The `defaultDestination*` props follow the same pattern as the deposit flow's `defaultChainType`, `defaultChainId`, and `defaultTokenAddress`. Pass all three for an exact token match, or just `defaultDestinationChainType` + `defaultDestinationChainId` to pre-select a network and let the SDK pick the first available token on that chain.
</Tip>

***

## WithdrawConfig

<ParamField path="externalUserId" type="string" required>
  Your platform's unique user identifier.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="senderAddress" type="string" required>
  The user's wallet address. Used only to fetch balance for display — wallet-agnostic, pass any address string.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="sourceChainType" type="'ethereum' | 'solana' | 'bitcoin'" required>
  Source token chain type.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="sourceChainId" type="string" required>
  Source token chain ID (e.g. `'8453'` for Base, `'1'` for Ethereum mainnet). See [Supported Chains](/get-started/supported-chains).
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="sourceTokenAddress" type="string" required>
  Contract address of the token the user is sending.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="sourceTokenSymbol" type="string">
  Token symbol for display (e.g. `'USDC'`).
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="recipientAddress" type="string">
  Pre-fills the recipient address field in the modal.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="defaultDestinationChainType" type="string">
  Pre-select the destination network type (e.g. `'ethereum'`, `'solana'`). Used with `defaultDestinationChainId` to open the modal with a destination network already selected. The user can still change it.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="defaultDestinationChainId" type="string">
  Pre-select the destination chain ID (e.g. `'1'` for Ethereum, `'137'` for Polygon). Used with `defaultDestinationChainType`.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="defaultDestinationTokenAddress" type="string">
  Pre-select the destination token by contract address on the specified chain (e.g. `'0xa0b86991c6218b36c1d19d4a2e9eb0ce3606eb48'` for USDC on Ethereum). Requires `defaultDestinationChainType` and `defaultDestinationChainId`. If only the chain fields are provided without a token address, the first available token on that chain is selected.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="withdraw" type="(txInfo: WithdrawTransactionInfo) => void | Promise<void>" required>
  Called when the user confirms the withdrawal. Your app must sign and broadcast the transaction — Unifold never holds a private key. See [Withdraw Functions](/get-started/sdk-reference/react-native/withdraw/withdraw-functions) for implementations.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onSuccess" type="(data: WithdrawResult) => void">
  Fired when the withdrawal execution reaches a succeeded state.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onError" type="(error: WithdrawError) => void">
  Fired when an error occurs during the withdrawal.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onClose" type="() => void">
  Fired when the user dismisses the withdraw modal.
</ParamField>

***

## WithdrawTransactionInfo

The object passed to your `withdraw` callback.

```typescript theme={null}
interface WithdrawTransactionInfo {
  sourceChainType: string;
  sourceChainId: string;
  sourceTokenAddress: string;
  sourceTokenSymbol: string;
  destinationChainType: string;
  destinationChainId: string;
  destinationTokenAddress: string;
  destinationTokenSymbol: string;
  amount: string;           // human-readable, e.g. "1.50"
  amountBaseUnit: string;   // exact, e.g. "1500000" for 1.5 USDC (6 decimals)
  withdrawIntentAddress: string;
  recipientAddress: string;
}
```

| Field                   | Description                                                                                                           |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `withdrawIntentAddress` | **The address your app must transfer funds to.** This is Unifold's intent address — not the user's final destination. |
| `amountBaseUnit`        | Use this for the transaction — it is exact. `amount` is for display only.                                             |
| `recipientAddress`      | The user's final destination. For display/logging only — do not send funds here directly.                             |

***

```typescript theme={null}
interface WithdrawResult {
  message: string;
  transaction?: unknown;
}

interface WithdrawError {
  message: string;
  error?: unknown;
  code?: string;
}
```
