# Withdraw Functions

Ready-to-use withdraw callback implementations for Privy and viem in React Native

The `withdraw` callback in `beginWithdraw()` is where your app signs and broadcasts the actual on-chain transaction. Below are complete implementations for the most common React Native wallet setups.

<Note>
  The React Native SDK is **wallet-agnostic** — it does not import or depend on any wallet library. The `withdraw` callback is fully owned by your app. Use whichever signing approach fits your stack.
</Note>

## EVM

### Privy (embedded MPC wallet)

Privy's React Native embedded wallet uses MPC signing. Unlike the web SDK, it does **not** expose `useSendTransaction` — instead you sign with `eth_signTransaction` (sign-only, no broadcast) and then broadcast via a viem `publicClient`.

**Key differences from the web Privy flow:**

* Must call `wallet_switchEthereumChain` before signing
* Must manually estimate gas and nonce — Privy RN ignores the `gas` field so `gasLimit` must also be set
* Must use `type: 2` (numeric) for EIP-1559 transactions
* Sign with `eth_signTransaction`, then broadcast via `publicClient.sendRawTransaction`

<Note>
  **Gas sponsorship is not currently supported on React Native.** The web Privy flow supports `{ sponsor: true }` via `useSendTransaction`, but this is not available in Privy's React Native SDK. The manual sign-and-broadcast approach below bypasses this limitation. Privy is actively working on sponsorship support for mobile — this page will be updated when it becomes available.
</Note>

```tsx theme={null}
import { usePrivy, useEmbeddedWallet } from '@privy-io/expo';
import {
  createPublicClient,
  encodeFunctionData,
  erc20Abi,
  http,
} from 'viem';
import { base } from 'viem/chains';
import { useUnifold } from '@unifold/connect-react-native';

// Map chain IDs to viem chain objects
const EVM_CHAINS: Record<number, typeof base> = {
  8453: base,
  // add other chains as needed
};

function WithdrawButton({ userAddress }: { userAddress: string }) {
  const { beginWithdraw } = useUnifold();
  const { user } = usePrivy();
  const wallet = useEmbeddedWallet();

  const handleWithdraw = async () => {
    await beginWithdraw({
      externalUserId: user!.id,
      senderAddress: wallet.account!.address,
      sourceChainType: 'ethereum',
      sourceChainId: '8453',
      sourceTokenAddress: '0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913',
      sourceTokenSymbol: 'USDC',
      sourceChainName: 'Base',

      withdraw: async (txInfo) => {
        const provider = await wallet.getProvider!();
        const fromAddress = wallet.account!.address as `0x${string}`;
        const chainIdNum = parseInt(txInfo.sourceChainId, 10);
        const viemChain = EVM_CHAINS[chainIdNum];
        if (!viemChain) throw new Error(`Chain ${txInfo.sourceChainId} not supported`);

        // Switch to the correct chain
        await provider.request({
          method: 'wallet_switchEthereumChain',
          params: [{ chainId: `0x${chainIdNum.toString(16)}` }],
        });

        const isNative = txInfo.sourceTokenAddress === 'native';
        const to = (isNative
          ? txInfo.withdrawIntentAddress
          : txInfo.sourceTokenAddress) as `0x${string}`;

        const data = isNative
          ? undefined
          : encodeFunctionData({
              abi: erc20Abi,
              functionName: 'transfer',
              args: [
                txInfo.withdrawIntentAddress as `0x${string}`,
                BigInt(txInfo.amountBaseUnit),
              ],
            });

        const value = isNative ? BigInt(txInfo.amountBaseUnit) : undefined;

        // Estimate gas and fees — Privy RN requires explicit values
        const publicClient = createPublicClient({ chain: viemChain, transport: http() });
        const [gas, { maxFeePerGas, maxPriorityFeePerGas }, nonce] = await Promise.all([
          publicClient.estimateGas({ account: fromAddress, to, data, value }),
          publicClient.estimateFeesPerGas(),
          publicClient.getTransactionCount({ address: fromAddress }),
        ]);

        const gasHex = `0x${gas.toString(16)}`;
        const txParams: Record<string, string | number> = {
          from: fromAddress,
          to,
          gas: gasHex,
          gasLimit: gasHex, // Privy RN reads gasLimit, not gas
          nonce: `0x${nonce.toString(16)}`,
          maxFeePerGas: `0x${maxFeePerGas!.toString(16)}`,
          maxPriorityFeePerGas: `0x${maxPriorityFeePerGas!.toString(16)}`,
          chainId: `0x${chainIdNum.toString(16)}`,
          type: 2, // numeric, not hex
        };
        if (data) txParams.data = data;
        if (value !== undefined) txParams.value = `0x${value.toString(16)}`;

        // Sign only — Privy RN does not broadcast
        const signedTx = await provider.request({
          method: 'eth_signTransaction',
          params: [txParams],
        }) as `0x${string}`;

        // Broadcast via viem
        await publicClient.sendRawTransaction({ serializedTransaction: signedTx });
      },

      onSuccess: (data) => console.log('Withdrawal complete:', data.message),
      onError: (err) => console.error('Withdrawal failed:', err.message),
    });
  };

  return <Button onPress={handleWithdraw} title="Withdraw" />;
}
```

***

### viem (private key / custom signer)

If your app manages keys directly (or uses any signer that can create a viem `WalletClient`), this is the simplest approach. viem handles gas estimation, nonce, and broadcasting automatically.

```tsx theme={null}
import {
  createWalletClient,
  erc20Abi,
  http,
} from 'viem';
import { privateKeyToAccount } from 'viem/accounts';
import { base } from 'viem/chains';
import { useUnifold } from '@unifold/connect-react-native';

// Map chain IDs to viem chain objects
const EVM_CHAINS: Record<number, typeof base> = {
  8453: base,
  // add other chains as needed
};

function WithdrawButton({ privateKey }: { privateKey: `0x${string}` }) {
  const { beginWithdraw } = useUnifold();

  const handleWithdraw = async () => {
    const account = privateKeyToAccount(privateKey);

    await beginWithdraw({
      externalUserId: account.address,
      senderAddress: account.address,
      sourceChainType: 'ethereum',
      sourceChainId: '8453',
      sourceTokenAddress: '0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913',
      sourceTokenSymbol: 'USDC',
      sourceChainName: 'Base',

      withdraw: async (txInfo) => {
        const chainIdNum = parseInt(txInfo.sourceChainId, 10);
        const viemChain = EVM_CHAINS[chainIdNum];
        if (!viemChain) throw new Error(`Chain ${txInfo.sourceChainId} not supported`);

        const walletClient = createWalletClient({
          account,
          chain: viemChain,
          transport: http(),
        });

        if (txInfo.sourceTokenAddress === 'native') {
          await walletClient.sendTransaction({
            to: txInfo.withdrawIntentAddress as `0x${string}`,
            value: BigInt(txInfo.amountBaseUnit),
          });
        } else {
          await walletClient.writeContract({
            address: txInfo.sourceTokenAddress as `0x${string}`,
            abi: erc20Abi,
            functionName: 'transfer',
            args: [
              txInfo.withdrawIntentAddress as `0x${string}`,
              BigInt(txInfo.amountBaseUnit),
            ],
          });
        }
      },

      onSuccess: (data) => console.log('Withdrawal complete:', data.message),
      onError: (err) => console.error('Withdrawal failed:', err.message),
    });
  };

  return <Button onPress={handleWithdraw} title="Withdraw" />;
}
```

<Warning>
  Never hardcode a private key with real funds in your app. Use a secure key management solution appropriate for your platform — hardware-backed storage, an MPC provider, or a secure enclave.
</Warning>

***

## What goes where

| Field                          | How to use it                                                                            |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `txInfo.withdrawIntentAddress` | **Send funds here** — this is Unifold's intent address, not the user's final destination |
| `txInfo.amountBaseUnit`        | Use this for the transaction amount — it is exact (e.g. `"1500000"` for 1.5 USDC)        |
| `txInfo.sourceTokenAddress`    | Token contract to call `transfer` on. `"native"` means send ETH/native currency directly |
| `txInfo.recipientAddress`      | The user's final destination — for display/logging only, do not send funds here          |

# Checkout

> React integration for the Checkout flow using @unifold/connect-react.

Accept fixed-amount crypto payments in your React app using `beginCheckout()` from the `useUnifold()` hook. For a platform-agnostic overview of how Checkout works, see the [Checkout Overview](/developer/checkout/overview).

## Usage

Access `beginCheckout` and `closeCheckout` from the `useUnifold()` hook:

```tsx theme={null}
import { useUnifold } from '@unifold/connect-react';

function CheckoutButton({ clientSecret }: { clientSecret: string }) {
  const { beginCheckout } = useUnifold();

  const handleCheckout = async () => {
    try {
      const result = await beginCheckout({
        clientSecret,
        onSuccess: (data) => console.log('Paid:', data.paymentIntentId),
        onError: (error) => console.error('Error:', error.message),
        onClose: () => console.log('User closed checkout'),
      });

      console.log('Payment complete:', result.paymentIntentId, result.status);
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('Checkout failed:', error);
    }
  };

  return <button onClick={handleCheckout}>Pay with Crypto</button>;
}
```

For the full `CheckoutConfig`, `CheckoutResult`, and `CheckoutError` type definitions, see [Checkout Functions](/developer/checkout/functions).

***

## Full example

```tsx theme={null}
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { UnifoldProvider, useUnifold } from '@unifold/connect-react';
import '@unifold/connect-react/styles.css';

function CheckoutButton({ clientSecret }: { clientSecret: string }) {
  const { beginCheckout } = useUnifold();
  const [status, setStatus] = useState<'idle' | 'pending' | 'success' | 'error'>('idle');

  const handleCheckout = async () => {
    if (!clientSecret) return;
    setStatus('pending');

    try {
      const result = await beginCheckout({
        clientSecret,
        onSuccess: (data) => {
          console.log('Payment succeeded:', data.paymentIntentId);
        },
        onError: (error) => {
          console.error('Payment error:', error.message);
        },
        onClose: () => {
          console.log('Checkout dismissed');
        },
      });

      setStatus('success');
    } catch (error: any) {
      if (error.code === 'CHECKOUT_CANCELLED') {
        setStatus('idle');
        return;
      }
      setStatus('error');
    }
  };

  return (
    <button onClick={handleCheckout} disabled={status === 'pending'}>
      {status === 'pending' ? 'Processing...' : 'Pay with Crypto'}
    </button>
  );
}

export default function CheckoutPage() {
  const clientSecret = 'pi_..._secret_...'; // from your server

  return (
    <UnifoldProvider publishableKey="pk_live_...">
      <CheckoutButton clientSecret={clientSecret} />
    </UnifoldProvider>
  );
}
```

***

## Importing types

All checkout types are exported from the package:

```tsx theme={null}
import {
  useUnifold,

  type CheckoutConfig,
  type CheckoutResult,
  type CheckoutError,

  type PaymentIntent,
  type PaymentIntentDepositAddress,
} from '@unifold/connect-react';
```

# Build the deposit UI

> Render each stage of a deposit with your own components, driven by the status from useDeposit.

A headless deposit is a small state machine. [`useDeposit`](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/headless/use-deposit) advances the state and hands you the data for each stage; you decide what to render. This guide maps every state to a piece of UI and shows a complete screen.

## Deposit states

The `status` returned by `useDeposit` moves through these states:

```mermaid theme={null}
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> idle
    idle --> creating_addresses: start
    creating_addresses --> ready: addresses ready
    creating_addresses --> error: creation fails
    ready --> processing: deposit detected
    processing --> ready: all in-flight executions settled
    error --> creating_addresses: retry
```

| State                        | What to render                                                            |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `idle`, `creating_addresses` | A loading state while the address is prepared.                            |
| `ready`                      | The deposit address, a QR code, and a copy button.                        |
| `processing`                 | A progress indicator while one or more observed executions are in flight. |
| `error`                      | An error state with a retry action (calls `start()` again).               |

## How a deposit flows

With the defaults, everything after render happens on its own: the hook creates the address, watches for the incoming transfer, and reports settlement.

```mermaid theme={null}
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant UI as Your UI
    participant Hook as useDeposit
    participant Unifold
    UI->>Hook: render (autoStart)
    Hook->>Unifold: create deposit address
    Unifold-->>Hook: address
    Hook-->>UI: status ready
    User->>Unifold: send funds on-chain
    loop until detected
        Hook->>Unifold: check for the deposit
    end
    Unifold-->>Hook: deposit detected
    Hook-->>UI: status processing
    Unifold-->>Hook: settled
    Hook-->>UI: status ready, execution status succeeded, onSuccess fires
```

## Render each state

Branch on `status` and render a component per stage. This keeps each state's UI isolated and easy to style.

```tsx theme={null}
import { useDeposit } from '@unifold/connect-react/headless';

function DepositScreen({ userId }: { userId: string }) {
  const deposit = useDeposit({
    externalUserId: userId,
    destination: {
      chainType: 'ethereum',
      chainId: '8453',       // Base
      tokenAddress: USDC_BASE,
      recipientAddress: treasuryAddress,
    },
    onSuccess: (execution) => analytics.track('deposit_succeeded', execution),
  });

  switch (deposit.status) {
    case 'idle':
    case 'creating_addresses':
      return <Loading label="Preparing your deposit address…" />;

    case 'error':
      return (
        <ErrorState
          message={deposit.error?.message ?? 'Something went wrong'}
          onRetry={deposit.start}
        />
      );

    default:
      // ready | processing
      return <AwaitingFunds deposit={deposit} />;
  }
}
```

<Note>
  This screen needs no `AbortController` or cleanup. `useDeposit` ties the session to the component and tears it down on unmount, so watching stops on its own. The `AbortController` shown on [Deposit sessions](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/headless/deposit-session#promise-helpers) is only for the imperative `waitForSuccess()` pattern, where you await the result yourself and cancel the wait manually.
</Note>

### The waiting screen

`ready` and `processing` share the same address and QR code, with an inline status message layered on top. Grouping them keeps the address visible so the user can send (or resend) at any point.

```tsx theme={null}
import type { UseDepositResult } from '@unifold/connect-react/headless';

function AwaitingFunds({ deposit }: { deposit: UseDepositResult }) {
  const address = deposit.getAddress({ chainType: 'ethereum' });
  if (!address) return null;
  const latest = deposit.latestExecution;
  const didFail = latest?.status === 'failed' || latest?.status === 'refunded';
  const didSucceed = latest?.status === 'succeeded';

  return (
    <div>
      <h2>Send USDC on Base</h2>
      <QrCode value={address.address} />
      <button onClick={() => navigator.clipboard.writeText(address.address)}>
        Copy address
      </button>

      {deposit.status === 'ready' && <p>Waiting for your transfer…</p>}
      {deposit.status === 'processing' && <p>Deposit received, settling now…</p>}
      {didFail && (
        <p>That transfer didn't complete. You can send again to the same address.</p>
      )}
      {didSucceed && <p>Deposit complete.</p>}
    </div>
  );
}
```

### The success screen

On success, `latestExecution` carries the settled amount and a link to the transaction.

```tsx theme={null}
import type { DirectExecution } from '@unifold/connect-react/headless';

function DepositSuccess({ execution }: { execution: DirectExecution }) {
  return (
    <div>
      <h2>Deposit complete</h2>
      <p>Received ${execution.destinationAmountUsd}</p>
      {execution.explorerUrl && (
        <a href={execution.explorerUrl} target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">
          View transaction
        </a>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Auto vs manual confirmation

The SDK watches for the deposit automatically in both modes. `confirmationMode` decides when it asks the backend to actively scan for the transfer, and whether your UI includes an "I've sent it" button.

|                           | Automatic (default)                                           | Manual                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `confirmationMode`        | `'auto'`                                                      | `'manual'`                                                                                                        |
| Backend scan is triggered | Shortly after the deposit screen loads                        | When the user taps your confirm button                                                                            |
| Confirm button in your UI | Not needed                                                    | Render one that calls `confirmFundsSent()`                                                                        |
| Best for                  | Most deposit screens, where the deposit just works on its own | Flows where the user explicitly signals they've sent funds, or where you want to hold off scanning until they act |

Automatic mode suits a screen where the user copies the address, sends funds, and watches the status update on its own. Choose manual mode when your UI has a distinct "I've sent it" step: render a button wired to `confirmFundsSent()`, and use `isCheckingDeposit` to reflect that active checking has begun.

```tsx theme={null}
const deposit = useDeposit({ externalUserId, destination, confirmationMode: 'manual' });

<button onClick={deposit.confirmFundsSent} disabled={deposit.isCheckingDeposit}>
  I've sent the transfer
</button>;
```

# Deposit sessions

> Await deposit results imperatively, and drive deposits outside React.

A `DepositSession` is the controller behind [`useDeposit`](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/headless/use-deposit): it creates the deposit addresses, watches for the incoming deposit, tracks status, and emits [events](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/headless/events).

In React, `useDeposit` creates and manages the session for you. With the default `autoStart: true`, it also calls `start()` automatically once inputs are ready. If you pass `autoStart: false`, your UI should call `deposit.start()` when the user enters the deposit step.

You reach the session when you want to **await a result imperatively** rather than render from `status`, or attach extra event subscriptions. You can also create and drive a session yourself in plain JavaScript.

## From useDeposit

`useDeposit` exposes its session on the `session` field. Use it inside effects or event handlers, for example to run logic once the deposit settles without threading state through your component:

```tsx theme={null}
const deposit = useDeposit({ externalUserId, destination });

useEffect(() => {
  if (!deposit.session) return;
  const controller = new AbortController();

  deposit.session
    .waitForSuccess({ signal: controller.signal })
    .then((execution) => grantAccess(execution))
    .catch(() => {}); // aborted on unmount, or the deposit failed

  return () => controller.abort();
}, [deposit.session]);
```

The `AbortController` is optional but recommended for this pattern: it cancels the wait if the component unmounts before the deposit settles, so the `.then` never runs against a gone component. It does not stop the deposit itself. When you render from `status` instead of awaiting a result, you don't need it at all.

## Promise helpers

These let you await a deposit instead of subscribing to it. They only observe the deposit; they never start or stop it.

```ts theme={null}
// Resolve when the deposit reaches a status:
await session.waitForStatus('processing');            // detected
await session.waitForStatus('ready');                 // addresses ready / all in-flight settled

// Resolve on the first successful deposit, reject on failure:
try {
  const execution = await session.waitForSuccess();
  creditUser(execution.destinationAmountUsd);
} catch (error) {
  // error is a DepositSessionWaitError
}
```

Both accept an `AbortSignal` to cancel the wait. Cancelling the wait does **not** stop the deposit; once funds are sent they still arrive. For a deadline, pass a timeout signal and treat expiry as "not settled yet", not a failure:

```ts theme={null}
await session.waitForSuccess({ signal: AbortSignal.timeout(60_000) });
```

`waitForSuccess` resolves for the **first** successful deposit only; the session keeps watching afterward. To react to every settlement (a user might send more than once), handle the [`direct_execution.succeeded`](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/headless/events) event or read `executions` from the snapshot instead.

### DepositSessionWaitError

Both helpers reject with a `DepositSessionWaitError` carrying a `code`:

| Code             | Meaning                                                                     |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DEPOSIT_FAILED` | The deposit failed. `cause` holds the failed `DirectExecution`.             |
| `SESSION_ERROR`  | A blocking session error occurred. `cause` holds the `DepositSessionError`. |
| `ABORTED`        | The provided `AbortSignal` fired.                                           |
| `DESTROYED`      | The session was torn down (for example, the component unmounted).           |

## Without React

Outside React, create a session from a client and drive it yourself. This is the framework-agnostic core, useful for Node, a service worker, or another framework.

```ts theme={null}
import { createUnifoldClient } from '@unifold/core';

const unifold = createUnifoldClient({ publishableKey: 'pk_live_...' });
const session = unifold.createDepositSession({ externalUserId, destination });

await session.start();
showQr(session.getSnapshot().addresses);

const execution = await session.waitForSuccess();
showSuccess(execution);
session.destroy();
```

### Session methods

<ResponseField name="start" type="() => Promise<void>">
  Creates the deposit addresses and begins watching for the deposit. Safe to call repeatedly while running; can be called again after `stop()` or an error to begin a fresh attempt.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="confirmFundsSent" type="() => void">
  In `'manual'` confirmation mode, prompts the backend to scan for the deposit.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="stop" type="() => void">
  Stops watching for the deposit. `start()` can be called again afterward with a fresh detection window.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="destroy" type="() => void">
  Stops the session and releases all subscriptions. The session cannot be restarted.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="getSnapshot" type="() => DepositSessionSnapshot">
  Returns the current state synchronously.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="subscribe" type="(listener: () => void) => () => void">
  Subscribes to state changes. Returns an unsubscribe function.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="on" type="(type, handler) => () => void">
  Subscribes to a specific [event](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/headless/events), or `'*'` for all events. Returns an unsubscribe function.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="waitForStatus" type="(status, options?) => Promise<DepositSessionSnapshot>">
  Resolves when the session reaches one of the given statuses. See [Promise helpers](#promise-helpers).
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="waitForSuccess" type="(options?) => Promise<DirectExecution>">
  Resolves with the first successful deposit, or rejects on failure. See [Promise helpers](#promise-helpers).
</ResponseField>

### Snapshot

`getSnapshot()` and the `subscribe` callback expose the same shape `useDeposit` returns:

```ts theme={null}
interface DepositSessionSnapshot {
  status: DepositSessionStatus;
  addresses: DepositAddress[];
  executions: DirectExecution[];   // newest first
  latestExecution: DirectExecution | null;
  isCheckingDeposit: boolean;
  error: DepositSessionError | null;
}
```

### Client methods

`createUnifoldClient` also exposes one-shot data methods, the non-React equivalent of the [resource hooks](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/headless/resource-hooks):

<ResponseField name="createDepositSession" type="(params) => DepositSession">
  Creates a deposit session. Parameters: `externalUserId`, `destination`, and optionally `confirmationMode` and `method`, the same as [`useDeposit`](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/headless/use-deposit#options).
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="getDepositAddresses" type="(params) => Promise<DepositAddress[]>">
  Creates (idempotently) and returns the user's deposit addresses for a destination.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="listExecutions" type="(params) => Promise<DirectExecution[]>">
  Returns the user's deposits.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="getSupportedDepositTokens" type="(params?) => Promise<SupportedToken[]>">
  Returns the source tokens and chains a user can deposit from.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="verifyAddress" type="(params) => Promise<AddressVerification>">
  Validates that a recipient address can receive funds for a destination.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="getProjectConfig" type="(options?) => Promise<ProjectConfigResponse>">
  Returns project configuration such as blocked regions.
</ResponseField>

# Events

> The typed event stream emitted during a deposit, and the objects it carries.

Every state change during a deposit is emitted as a typed event. Events use the same envelope as Unifold's [webhooks](/developer/webhooks/events): a top-level `id`, `type`, and `created`, an optional `method`, and the resource under `data.object`.

```ts theme={null}
type DepositSessionEvent = {
  id: string;             // "sevt_..."
  type: string;           // "resource.action", e.g. "direct_execution.succeeded"
  created: number;        // Unix timestamp (seconds)
  method?: DepositMethod; // funding method, from the session's `method` option
  data: { object: { /* typed per event type */ } };
};
```

## Subscribing

Subscribe on a [`DepositSession`](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/headless/deposit-session) with `on(type, handler)`, or `on('*', handler)` for all events. Each returns an unsubscribe function. The [`useDeposit`](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/headless/use-deposit) callbacks (`onSuccess`, `onError`, and so on) are subscriptions to these events.

```ts theme={null}
import { DepositSessionEventType } from '@unifold/connect-react/headless';

const off = session.on(DepositSessionEventType.EXECUTION_SUCCEEDED, ({ data }) => {
  creditUser(data.object);
});

// later
off();
```

Events are edge-triggered: each fires once when the change occurs and is not repeated while the state holds.

## Event types

| Enum (`DepositSessionEventType`) | `type`                                 | `data.object`                          | Fires when                                                           |
| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SESSION_STARTED`                | `deposit_session.started`              | `{ sessionId }`                        | A deposit attempt begins.                                            |
| `ADDRESSES_CREATED`              | `deposit_session.addresses_created`    | `{ sessionId, addresses }`             | Deposit addresses are ready.                                         |
| `CONFIRMATION_STARTED`           | `deposit_session.confirmation_started` | `{ sessionId, trigger }`               | The backend is prompted to scan (`trigger`: `'auto'` or `'manual'`). |
| `SESSION_STOPPED`                | `deposit_session.stopped`              | `{ sessionId }`                        | The deposit stops being watched.                                     |
| `SESSION_ERRORED`                | `deposit_session.errored`              | `{ sessionId, code, message, fatal }`  | A session error occurs.                                              |
| `EXECUTION_DETECTED`             | `direct_execution.detected`            | `DirectExecution`                      | A deposit is seen for the first time.                                |
| `EXECUTION_UPDATED`              | `direct_execution.updated`             | `DirectExecution & { previousStatus }` | A tracked deposit changes status.                                    |
| `EXECUTION_SUCCEEDED`            | `direct_execution.succeeded`           | `DirectExecution`                      | A deposit settles successfully.                                      |
| `EXECUTION_FAILED`               | `direct_execution.failed`              | `DirectExecution`                      | A deposit fails or is refunded.                                      |

<Note>
  `direct_execution.succeeded` matches the event of the same name in the [modal SDK](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/hooks#event-types) and [webhooks](/developer/webhooks/events). When you run both the modal and headless surfaces, deduplicate on `data.object.id`, since the envelope `id` is generated per emitter.
</Note>

## DirectExecution

Delivered with execution events and to `onSuccess`.

```ts theme={null}
interface DirectExecution {
  id: string;
  transactionHash: string;
  recipientAddress: string;
  depositAddress?: string;
  sourceChainType: string;
  sourceChainId: string;
  sourceTokenAddress: string;
  destinationChainType: string;
  destinationChainId: string;
  destinationTokenAddress: string;
  sourceAmountBaseUnit: string;
  sourceAmountUsd?: string;
  destinationAmountBaseUnit: string;
  destinationAmountUsd?: string;
  destinationTransactionHashes: string[];
  status: ExecutionStatus;
  failureReason: string | null;

  // Presentation fields for rendering a timeline:
  createdAt?: string;
  updatedAt?: string;
  explorerUrl?: string;
  destinationExplorerUrl?: string | null;
  sourceTokenMetadata?: { iconUrl?: string; decimals?: number };
  destinationTokenMetadata?: { iconUrl?: string; decimals?: number };
}
```

## DepositSessionError

Delivered to `onError`, and available as `error` on the session snapshot.

```ts theme={null}
interface DepositSessionError {
  code: 'ADDRESS_CREATION_FAILED' | 'POLLING_ERROR' | 'DEPOSIT_FAILED' | 'INVALID_RECIPIENT';
  message: string;
  fatal: boolean; // fatal errors end the deposit (status 'error'); non-fatal errors do not stop watching
  cause?: unknown;
}
```

| Code                      | Fatal | Meaning                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------- | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ADDRESS_CREATION_FAILED` | Yes   | Deposit addresses could not be created.                                                                                         |
| `INVALID_RECIPIENT`       | Yes   | The recipient address cannot receive funds for this destination.                                                                |
| `DEPOSIT_FAILED`          | No    | A detected deposit failed or was refunded.                                                                                      |
| `POLLING_ERROR`           | No    | A temporary network error while checking status. Only the first error in a streak is reported; it clears once polling recovers. |

## DepositMethod

Labels which funding method produced an event, carried on `event.method`.

```ts theme={null}
type DepositMethod =
  | 'transfer'
  | 'card'
  | 'cashapp'
  | 'apple_pay'
  | 'pay_with_exchange'
  | 'exchange_connect'
  | 'wallet_connect';
```

# Overview

> Build your own deposit UI on top of Unifold's deposit engine, with full control over the experience.

The headless SDK lets you build a fully custom deposit experience. You call the [`useDeposit`](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/headless/use-deposit) hook, render the deposit address and progress with your own components, and let the SDK handle address creation, detection, and settlement in the background.

It runs on the same deposit engine as the [modal SDK](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/introduction), with the same endpoints and events, and gives you full control of the interface.

**Reach for headless when you want to:**

* Embed the deposit flow directly in a page.
* Match the deposit UI exactly to your design system.
* Fold deposits into a larger multi-step flow (checkout, onboarding, funding).
* Drive the flow programmatically, for example from a wallet you already have connected.

If you'd rather ship a deposit flow without building the UI, use the [modal SDK](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/introduction). The two work well together: use the modal for card deposits and a headless screen for on-chain transfers.

## Installation

The headless hooks ship with the Connect React SDK. If your app already uses `@unifold/connect-react` for the modal, import the hooks from the `/headless` subpath. There's nothing new to install.

```tsx theme={null}
import { useDeposit } from '@unifold/connect-react/headless';
```

The subpath brings in just the hooks, so it keeps your bundle lean.

## Deposit lifecycle

The `status` you render from moves through these values:

```
idle → creating_addresses → ready ⇄ processing
                          ↘ error
```

| Status               | What to show                                                                       |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `idle`               | Nothing yet; the hook is waiting for the user and key.                             |
| `creating_addresses` | A loading state while addresses are prepared.                                      |
| `ready`              | The address and QR code, waiting for the user's transfer.                          |
| `processing`         | A progress indicator; at least one observed execution is in flight.                |
| `error`              | A blocking error, for example address creation failed or the recipient is invalid. |

## Setup

Headless hooks read your publishable key from `UnifoldProvider`. If you already use the modal SDK, reuse the same provider; there's no separate setup.

```tsx theme={null}
import { UnifoldProvider } from '@unifold/connect-react';

function App() {
  return (
    <UnifoldProvider publishableKey="pk_live_...">
      <YourApp />
    </UnifoldProvider>
  );
}
```

Combining the modal and headless surfaces? Keep a single provider so both share one `QueryClient` and cache. See the [Provider reference](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/provider) for all options.

## Build a deposit screen

`useDeposit` manages one deposit for one user and destination. Pass the user and where funds should land, then render your UI from the `status` and `addresses` it returns.

```tsx theme={null}
import { useDeposit } from '@unifold/connect-react/headless';

function DepositScreen({ userId }: { userId: string }) {
  const { status, getAddress, latestExecution, error } = useDeposit({
    externalUserId: userId,
    destination: {
      chainType: 'ethereum',
      chainId: '8453',       // Base
      tokenAddress: USDC_BASE,
      recipientAddress: treasuryAddress,
    },
    onSuccess: (execution) =>
      toast.success(`Received $${execution.destinationAmountUsd}`),
  });

  const address = getAddress({ chainType: 'ethereum' });

  if (status === 'creating_addresses' || !address) return <Spinner />;
  if (status === 'error') return <ErrorState message={error?.message} />;

  return (
    <div>
      <h2>Send USDC on Base to complete your deposit</h2>
      <QrCode value={address.address} />
      <CopyField value={address.address} />

      {status === 'ready' && <p>Waiting for your transfer…</p>}
      {status === 'processing' && <Progress execution={latestExecution!} />}
      {latestExecution?.status === 'succeeded' && (
        <SuccessState execution={latestExecution} />
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
```

That's a complete integration. By default (`autoStart: true`), the hook starts as soon as it has the user and key, creates addresses, and watches for deposits without requiring a button click.

If your flow needs explicit user intent (for example, "Open deposit screen" or "Continue"), set `autoStart: false` and call `start()` yourself at that moment.

```tsx theme={null}
const deposit = useDeposit({
  externalUserId: userId,
  destination,
  autoStart: false,
});

<button onClick={deposit.start}>Start deposit</button>;
```

From here you can:

* **React to failures and connection issues** with the `onError` callback (see [`useDeposit`](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/headless/use-deposit)).
* **Add an "I've sent it" button** by switching to [manual confirmation](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/headless/use-deposit#manual-confirmation).
* **Await the result imperatively** instead of rendering from status (see [Deposit sessions](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/headless/deposit-session#promise-helpers)).
* **Show deposit history** with [`useExecutions`](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/headless/resource-hooks#useexecutions).

# Resource hooks

> Data hooks for deposit addresses, supported tokens, history, region checks, and address validation.

These hooks fetch the data behind a custom deposit UI: token pickers, history screens, region gates, and inline validation. Each is built on [TanStack Query](https://tanstack.com/query) and shares its cache with the modal SDK, so combining surfaces never double-fetches. All require a surrounding [`UnifoldProvider`](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/provider).

## useDepositAddresses

Fetches (creating if needed) the user's deposit addresses for a destination, with caching. Use it to render a receive screen without a live [deposit session](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/headless/use-deposit).

```tsx theme={null}
import { useDepositAddresses } from '@unifold/connect-react/headless';

const { data: addresses = [], isLoading } = useDepositAddresses({
  externalUserId,
  destination: { chainType, chainId, tokenAddress, recipientAddress },
});
```

<ParamField path="externalUserId" type="string" required>
  Your platform's stable identifier for the user.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="destination" type="object">
  `{ chainType, chainId, tokenAddress, recipientAddress, contractCalls? }`.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="enabled" type="boolean" default="true">
  Whether the query runs.
</ParamField>

Returns a TanStack Query result whose `data` is `DepositAddress[]`.

## useSupportedDepositTokens

Returns the source tokens and chains a user can deposit from, for building custom pickers.

```tsx theme={null}
import { useSupportedDepositTokens } from '@unifold/connect-react/headless';

const { data: tokens = [] } = useSupportedDepositTokens({
  destination: { chainType, chainId, tokenAddress },
});
```

<ParamField path="destination" type="object">
  Optional filter `{ chainType, chainId, tokenAddress }`; all three are required together.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="productType" type="ProductType">
  Optional product filter.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="enabled" type="boolean" default="true">
  Whether the query runs.
</ParamField>

Returns a TanStack Query result whose `data` is `SupportedToken[]`.

## useExecutions

Returns the user's deposit history, for tracker and history screens.

```tsx theme={null}
import { useExecutions } from '@unifold/connect-react/headless';

const { data: executions = [], isLoading } = useExecutions({ externalUserId });
```

<ParamField path="externalUserId" type="string" required>
  Your platform's stable identifier for the user.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="refetchInterval" type="number | false" default="false">
  Polling interval in milliseconds. For live deposit detection use [`useDeposit`](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/headless/use-deposit) instead.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="actionType" type="ActionType" default="Deposit">
  Filter by action type.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="enabled" type="boolean" default="true">
  Whether the query runs.
</ParamField>

Returns a TanStack Query result whose `data` is [`DirectExecution[]`](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/headless/events#directexecution).

## useAllowedCountry

Reports whether the user's region is permitted by your project's blocked-region configuration.

Use `useAllowedCountry` to apply your project's region rules in your own UI, gating the deposit screen on `isAllowed`. With the headless flow, region enforcement is yours to place wherever it fits, so you decide when and how to run it.

```tsx theme={null}
import { useAllowedCountry } from '@unifold/connect-react/headless';

function DepositGate({ children }) {
  const { isAllowed, isLoading } = useAllowedCountry();
  if (isLoading) return <Spinner />;
  if (!isAllowed) return <p>Deposits are not available in your region.</p>;
  return children;
}
```

### Returns

<ResponseField name="isAllowed" type="boolean | null">
  `true` if allowed, `false` if blocked, `null` while loading.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="alpha2" type="string | null">
  ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (for example `"US"`).
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="country" type="string | null">
  Full country name.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="subdivisionCode" type="string | null">
  ISO 3166-2 subdivision code (for example `"NY"`), when available.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="isLoading" type="boolean">
  Whether the check is in progress.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="error" type="Error | null">
  The error, if the check failed.
</ResponseField>

## useAddressValidation

Validates that a recipient address can receive funds for a destination, primarily for Algorand asset opt-in. `useDeposit` already validates the recipient when it starts; use this hook for inline form validation beforehand.

```tsx theme={null}
import { useAddressValidation } from '@unifold/connect-react/headless';

const { isValid, failureCode, isLoading } = useAddressValidation({
  recipientAddress,
  destination: { chainType, chainId, tokenAddress },
});
```

<ParamField path="recipientAddress" type="string">
  Address to validate.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="destination" type="object">
  `{ chainType, chainId, tokenAddress }`.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="enabled" type="boolean" default="true">
  Whether validation runs.
</ParamField>

### Returns

<ResponseField name="isValid" type="boolean | null">
  Whether the address can receive funds. `null` while loading or when parameters are incomplete.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="failureCode" type="AddressValidationFailureCode | null">
  Standardized code for localizing an error message.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="metadata" type="object | null">
  Details for message interpolation, such as `chain_name` and `token_symbol`.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="isLoading" type="boolean">
  Whether validation is in progress.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="error" type="Error | null">
  The error, if validation failed.
</ResponseField>

## useUnifoldClient

Returns a client configured with the provider's publishable key, for imperative access to resource methods and [`createDepositSession`](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/headless/deposit-session) outside the provided hooks.

```tsx theme={null}
import { useUnifoldClient } from '@unifold/connect-react/headless';

const client = useUnifoldClient(); // UnifoldClient | null

const executions = await client?.listExecutions({ externalUserId });
```

# useDeposit

> Reference for the useDeposit hook: options, return values, and controls.

This is the reference for **`useDeposit`**, the primary headless hook. It creates a deposit session, tracks its status, exposes the deposit addresses and observed executions, and provides controls to start, confirm, stop, and restart the flow. Your components render the UI.

```tsx theme={null}
import { useDeposit } from '@unifold/connect-react/headless';

const deposit = useDeposit({ externalUserId, destination });
```

## Options

<ParamField path="externalUserId" type="string" required>
  Your platform's stable identifier for the user (sent as `external_user_id`). While `undefined`, no session is created and `status` stays `idle`.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="destination" type="object" required>
  What the deposit converts into and where it settles.

  <Expandable title="destination properties">
    <ParamField path="chainType" type="ChainType" required>
      Destination blockchain type: `'ethereum'`, `'solana'`, `'bitcoin'`, `'algorand'`, `'xrpl'`, or `'cardano'`.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="chainId" type="string" required>
      Target chain ID (for example `'8453'` for Base, `'mainnet'` for Solana). See [Supported Chains](/get-started/supported-chains).
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="tokenAddress" type="string" required>
      Token contract address on the destination chain.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="recipientAddress" type="string" required>
      Address that receives the settled funds. When using `contractCalls`, set this to the contract that receives and is called.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="contractCalls" type="EvmContractCall[]">
      EVM-only calls run as a batch after the funds land. Each entry is `{ to, data, value? }`. See the [Call Execution guide](/developer/call-execution/deposit-sweep).
    </ParamField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="autoStart" type="boolean" default="true">
  Controls who starts the session:

  * `true`: `useDeposit` starts automatically once `externalUserId` and the publishable key are available.
  * `false`: your UI starts it by calling `start()` (for example, after the user opens the deposit step).

  Use `autoStart: true` for always-on deposit screens. Use `autoStart: false` when the deposit should only begin after an explicit user action.
</ParamField>

<Note>
  If `autoStart` is `false` and you never call `start()`, no deposit addresses are created. Address creation happens during `start()` (`creating_addresses`), so the session stays `idle` with `addresses: []` until you start it.

  If you only need addresses (without running a live session), use [`useDepositAddresses`](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/headless/resource-hooks#usedepositaddresses) or [`getDepositAddresses`](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/headless/deposit-session#client-methods).
</Note>

<ParamField path="confirmationMode" type="'auto' | 'manual'" default="'auto'">
  Controls when the SDK prompts the backend to scan for the deposit:

  * `'auto'`: a few seconds after the deposit starts.
  * `'manual'`: only when you call `confirmFundsSent()`, typically from your own "I've sent it" button.

  Incoming-deposit detection runs from the start in both modes.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="method" type="DepositMethod" default="'transfer'">
  Labels emitted events with the funding method. Set this when the deposit is funded by a specific rail you control, such as `'wallet_connect'`. See [`DepositMethod`](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/headless/events#depositmethod).
</ParamField>

### Callbacks

Each callback subscribes to the matching [event](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/headless/events).

<ParamField path="onSuccess" type="(execution: DirectExecution) => void">
  A deposit settled successfully.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onError" type="(error: DepositSessionError) => void">
  A deposit failed, or a session error occurred. Inspect `error.code` and `error.fatal`.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onEvent" type="(event: DepositSessionEvent) => void">
  Every lifecycle event, useful for analytics.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onAddressesReady" type="(addresses: DepositAddress[]) => void">
  Deposit addresses were created.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onExecutionDetected" type="(execution: DirectExecution) => void">
  A deposit was detected for the first time.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onExecutionUpdated" type="(execution: DirectExecution & { previousStatus: ExecutionStatus | null }) => void">
  A tracked deposit changed status.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onStatusChange" type="(status: DepositSessionStatus) => void">
  The session `status` changed.
</ParamField>

## Returns

<ResponseField name="status" type="DepositSessionStatus">
  Current lifecycle status (`idle`, `creating_addresses`, `ready`, `processing`, `error`). Session status is lifecycle-only; execution outcomes are read from `latestExecution` / `executions` / execution events. See [Deposit lifecycle](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/headless/overview#deposit-lifecycle).
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="addresses" type="DepositAddress[]">
  Deposit addresses, one per chain type. Empty until created.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="getAddress" type="(query: { chainType: ChainType }) => DepositAddress | undefined">
  Returns the address matching the query. The object shape keeps the API forward-compatible with additional selectors.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="executions" type="DirectExecution[]">
  All deposits observed during this session, newest first.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="latestExecution" type="DirectExecution | null">
  The most recently observed deposit.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="isCheckingDeposit" type="boolean">
  `true` while active backend checking is armed and running.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="error" type="DepositSessionError | null">
  The latest error, if any. A transient polling error clears automatically once polling recovers.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="start" type="() => Promise<void>">
  Starts a deposit attempt: creates addresses (if needed) and begins watching. Primary use is `autoStart: false`; it is also safe to call for retry after `stop()` or `error`.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="confirmFundsSent" type="() => void">
  In `'manual'` mode, prompts the backend to scan for the deposit.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="stop" type="() => void">
  Stops watching for the deposit.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="restart" type="() => Promise<void>">
  Stops and restarts the deposit with a fresh detection window.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="session" type="DepositSession | null">
  The underlying [`DepositSession`](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/headless/deposit-session). Use it for additional event subscriptions or the promise helpers.
</ResponseField>

<Note>
  Changing `externalUserId` or any `destination` field replaces the current deposit session with a new one. The hook is safe for server rendering: the session is created in an effect, so server renders show `status: 'idle'` with empty arrays.
</Note>

## Manual start (`autoStart: false`)

Use manual start when your product wants an explicit "begin deposit" step.

```tsx theme={null}
const deposit = useDeposit({
  externalUserId,
  destination,
  autoStart: false,
});

<Button onClick={deposit.start} disabled={deposit.status === 'creating_addresses'}>
  Start deposit
</Button>;
```

## Manual confirmation

With `confirmationMode: 'manual'`, the SDK prompts the backend to scan for the deposit only when you call `confirmFundsSent()`. Wire it to your own confirmation button.

```tsx theme={null}
const deposit = useDeposit({
  externalUserId,
  destination,
  confirmationMode: 'manual',
  onExecutionUpdated: (execution) => setTimeline((t) => [...t, execution]),
  onError: (error) => {
    if (error.code === 'POLLING_ERROR') showBanner('Connection issue, still watching');
    else showFailure(error);
  },
});

<Button onClick={deposit.confirmFundsSent} disabled={deposit.isCheckingDeposit}>
  I've sent the transfer
</Button>;
```

## Deposit detection window

The session uses a fixed 60-second lookback to catch deposits sent moments before `start()`. Only deposits still in progress within this window are picked up and tracked to completion.

A deposit that had already settled before the session started is treated as history and does not re-trigger `onSuccess` or `onError`, so reopening a deposit screen shortly after a success cannot double-count it. Render past deposits with [`useExecutions`](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/headless/resource-hooks#useexecutions).

A single session can observe more than one deposit. For example, if the user sends twice, or on two chains, to the same addresses, each settlement reports its own success. To credit every deposit, handle the [`direct_execution.succeeded`](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/headless/events) event (deduplicating on `execution.id`) or read `executions`.

# Hooks

> React hooks for accessing deposit, checkout, and withdraw functionality.

## useUnifold()

React hook that provides access to deposit, checkout, and withdraw functionality.

### Returns

<ResponseField name="publishableKey" type="string">
  The current publishable key.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="beginDeposit" type="(config: DepositConfig) => Promise<DepositResult>">
  Function to launch the deposit modal. Returns a Promise that resolves when the deposit completes.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="closeDeposit" type="() => void">
  Function to programmatically close the deposit modal. Calling this will reject the promise with code `'DEPOSIT_CANCELLED'`.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="beginCheckout" type="(config: CheckoutConfig) => Promise<CheckoutResult>">
  Function to launch the checkout modal for fixed-amount payments. Pass a `clientSecret` from a server-created Payment Intent. Returns a Promise that resolves when the payment succeeds. See [Checkout Overview](/developer/checkout/overview) for details.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="closeCheckout" type="() => void">
  Function to programmatically close the checkout modal. Calling this will reject the promise with code `'CHECKOUT_CANCELLED'`.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="beginWithdraw" type="(config: WithdrawConfig) => Promise<WithdrawResult>">
  Function to launch the withdraw modal. Returns a Promise that resolves when the withdrawal completes. Supports optional `defaultDestination*` props to pre-select the receive token (same matching logic as deposit `defaultSource*`). See [Withdraw Overview](/developer/withdraw/overview) for details.
</ResponseField>

### Example

```tsx theme={null}
const { beginDeposit, closeDeposit, beginCheckout, closeCheckout, beginWithdraw, publishableKey } = useUnifold();
```

## beginDeposit(config)

Launches the deposit modal with the specified configuration.

### Parameters

<ParamField path="externalUserId" type="string" required>
  Your user's unique identifier. Used for wallet creation and deposit tracking.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="destinationChainType" type="string" required>
  The blockchain type. Supported values:

  * `'ethereum'` — EVM-compatible chains
  * `'solana'` — Solana
  * `'bitcoin'` — Bitcoin
  * `'algorand'` — Algorand
  * `'xrpl'` — XRPL (Ripple)
  * `'cardano'` — Cardano
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="destinationChainId" type="string" required>
  Target chain ID (e.g. `'137'` for Polygon, `'mainnet'` for Solana). See [Supported Chains](/get-started/supported-chains) for the full list.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="destinationTokenAddress" type="string" required>
  Token contract address on the destination chain.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="destinationTokenSymbol" type="string" required>
  Token symbol displayed in the UI (e.g., `'USDC'`).
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="recipientAddress" type="string" required>
  Wallet address that will receive the deposited tokens. When using `contractCalls`, set this to the contract that will receive the funds and be called.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="contractCalls" type="EvmContractCall[]">
  Arbitrary contract calls after the swap lands in the destination chain. `contractCalls` are run in a batch transaction so the order matters. Each entry is `{ to, data, value? }` — `value` is optional and defaults to `"0"`. (only support `ethereum`, `arbitrum`, `base`, `megaeth`) See the [Call Execution guide](/developer/call-execution/deposit-sweep).

  ```typescript theme={null}
  interface EvmContractCall {
    to: `0x${string}`;
    data: `0x${string}`;
    value?: string;
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onSuccess" type="(data: DepositResult) => void">
  Callback fired immediately when deposit completes. Useful for analytics or toasts.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onError" type="(error: DepositError) => void">
  Callback fired immediately when an error occurs.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onClose" type="() => void">
  Callback fired when the user dismisses the deposit dialog (X button, Escape key, or programmatic `closeDeposit()`). Useful for re-enabling UI, resetting state, or tracking abandonment.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onEvent" type="(event: DepositEvent) => void">
  Callback fired when deposit lifecycle events occur. Use this to react to intermediate steps in the deposit flow — for example, tracking when an onramp session is created before the user leaves your site. Each event follows a consistent envelope shape with `id`, `type`, `created`, and `data.object`. See [Event Types](#event-types) below for the full list.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="defaultSourceChainType" type="string">
  Pre-select the source network type in the Transfer Crypto screen. Supported values:

  * `'ethereum'` — EVM-compatible chains
  * `'solana'` — Solana
  * `'bitcoin'` — Bitcoin
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="defaultSourceChainId" type="string">
  Pre-select the source chain ID (e.g. `'1'` for Ethereum, `'137'` for Polygon, `'mainnet'` for Solana). Used together with `defaultSourceChainType`.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="defaultSourceTokenAddress" type="string">
  Pre-select a specific source token by its contract address. When provided alongside `defaultSourceChainType` and `defaultSourceChainId`, the Transfer Crypto screen opens with both the network and token pre-selected.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="defaultSourceSymbol" type="string">
  Pre-select a source token by symbol (e.g. `'USDC'`, `'ETH'`). Can be used as an alternative to `defaultSourceTokenAddress` when the contract address is not known.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="prefilledAmountUsd" type="string">
  Optional USD amount used to prefill **every fiat amount input** across the deposit flow (Connect Wallet, Deposit with Card, Bank Transfer, Cash App). The value is applied as initial typed input, so the user can still edit it before continuing.

  When a step collects a **non-USD fiat currency** (for example a bank transfer denominated in EUR or GBP), the USD amount is automatically converted into that currency using the live exchange rate — so the field is prefilled with the equivalent value in the local currency the user actually enters. Pass the amount as a plain decimal string (e.g. `'25.00'`), without a currency symbol.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="initialScreen" type="'main' | 'transfer' | 'card' | 'tracker'">
  First screen when the modal opens. Defaults to `main` (deposit menu). Use `transfer`, `card`, or `tracker` for [standalone entry](/developer/deposit/entry-screens) without showing the menu first.
</ParamField>

### Returns

Returns a `Promise<DepositResult>` that:

* **Resolves** when the deposit completes successfully
* **Rejects** when an error occurs or the user cancels

### DepositResult

```typescript theme={null}
interface DepositResult {
  message: string;
  executionId?: string;
  /**
   * Fully-typed `direct_execution.succeeded` event envelope.
   * Same shape as the `onEvent` payload — use this in new code.
   */
  execution?: DirectExecutionSucceededEvent;
  /** Funding method that produced this success (transfer, card, wallet_connect, ...). */
  method?: DepositMethod;
  /**
   * @deprecated Use `execution` (or `onEvent`) instead. `transaction` is the
   * raw execution row in legacy snake_case API shape and will be removed in a
   * future minor release.
   */
  transaction?: unknown;
}
```

<Warning>
  `DepositResult.transaction` is **deprecated** and will be removed in a future release. It currently holds the raw `DirectExecutionResponse` (legacy `AutoSwapResponse`) row in snake\_case API shape. Use `result.execution.data.object` (camelCase, typed via `DirectExecution`) or listen for `direct_execution.succeeded` on `onEvent` instead.
</Warning>

### DepositMethod

Identifies which funding method produced a deposit success/error event. Available on `DepositResult.method` and `DepositError.method`, and on `event.method` for any `DepositEvent`.

```typescript theme={null}
type DepositMethod =
  | 'transfer'
  | 'card'
  | 'cashapp'
  | 'pay_with_exchange'
  | 'exchange_connect'
  | 'wallet_connect';
```

### DepositError

```typescript theme={null}
interface DepositError {
  message: string;
  error?: unknown;
  code?: string;
  /** Funding method that produced this error, when known. */
  method?: DepositMethod;
}
```

#### Error Codes

| Code                 | Description                                 |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `DEPOSIT_CANCELLED`  | User intentionally closed the modal         |
| `POLLING_ERROR`      | Network error while checking deposit status |
| `DEPOSIT_SUPERSEDED` | Another deposit was started                 |

#### Handling Errors

```tsx theme={null}
import { type DepositError } from '@unifold/connect-react';

function handleError(error: DepositError) {
  switch (error.code) {
    case 'DEPOSIT_CANCELLED':
      // User intentionally closed the modal
      return;
    
    case 'POLLING_ERROR':
      // Network error checking deposit status
      showRetryButton();
      break;
    
    case 'DEPOSIT_SUPERSEDED':
      // Another deposit was started
      break;
    
    default:
      // Unknown error
      showErrorMessage(error.message);
  }
}
```

### Event Types

The `onEvent` callback receives a `DepositEvent` — conceptually similar to [webhook events](/developer/webhooks/events), but emitted client-side. Each event has `id`, `type`, `created`, and the payload nested under `data.object`.

```typescript theme={null}
type DepositEvent = {
  id: string;          // Client-generated ID (sevt_ prefix)
  type: string;        // Event type in resource.action format
  created: number;     // Unix timestamp (seconds)
  method?: DepositMethod; // Funding method that triggered this event
  data: {
    object: { ... };   // Typed per event — see below
  };
};
```

<Tip>
  Prefer `onEvent` over `onSuccess` for anything beyond "did the deposit complete?". `onEvent` exposes the full lifecycle (onramp redirects, direct execution success, …) under one consistent envelope shape — the same one used by [webhooks](/developer/webhooks/events) — and is the recommended integration point unless you only need the final result.
</Tip>

Available events:

| SDK Enum                                      | `event.type` string            | Description                                                                                                        |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `DepositEventType.ONRAMP_SESSION_CREATED`     | `"onramp_session.created"`     | An onramp session is created, just before the user is redirected to the provider                                   |
| `DepositEventType.DIRECT_EXECUTION_SUCCEEDED` | `"direct_execution.succeeded"` | A direct execution (transfer / card / wallet / exchange deposit) reached `SUCCEEDED`. Fires alongside `onSuccess`. |

#### `onramp_session.created`

When `event.type` is `"onramp_session.created"`, the full event looks like:

```typescript theme={null}
{
  id: string;       // e.g. "sevt_2NxK..."
  type: "onramp_session.created";
  created: number;  // Unix timestamp (seconds)
  data: {
    object: OnrampSessionCreatedData;
  };
}

interface OnrampSessionCreatedData {
  externalId: string;
}
```

<ResponseField name="event.data.object.externalId" type="string">
  Unique identifier for the onramp session (prefixed `orsext_`). Use this to correlate the client-side event with server-side [webhook events](/developer/webhooks/events) for the same session.
</ResponseField>

#### `direct_execution.succeeded`

Fires when a direct execution (the on-chain transfer that lands funds in the recipient address) reaches `SUCCEEDED`. Emitted from the same poller that drives `onDepositSuccess` — so if you've already wired `onEvent`, you no longer need to listen to `onSuccess` for the result.

```typescript theme={null}
{
  id: string;       // e.g. "sevt_2NxK..."
  type: "direct_execution.succeeded";
  created: number;  // Unix timestamp (seconds)
  method?: DepositMethod; // e.g. "transfer", "card", "wallet_connect"
  data: {
    object: DirectExecution;
  };
}

interface DirectExecution {
  id: string;
  transactionHash: string;
  recipientAddress: string;
  depositAddress?: string;
  sourceChainType: string;
  sourceChainId: string;
  sourceTokenAddress: string;
  destinationChainType: string;
  destinationChainId: string;
  destinationTokenAddress: string;
  sourceAmountBaseUnit: string;
  sourceAmountUsd?: string;
  destinationAmountBaseUnit: string;
  destinationAmountUsd?: string;
  destinationTransactionHashes: string[];
  status: ExecutionStatus;
  failureReason: string | null;
}
```

<Note>
  The `DirectExecution` object exposed to callbacks is **camelCase** and intentionally minimal — it's not the same as the legacy `DirectExecutionResponse` (formerly `AutoSwapResponse`) API row. The same object is delivered via `result.execution.data.object` on `onDepositSuccess` for convenience.
</Note>

#### Example: Listening to events

```tsx theme={null}
import {
  useUnifold,
  type DepositEvent,
  DepositEventType,
} from '@unifold/connect-react';

function DepositButton() {
  const { beginDeposit } = useUnifold();

  const handleDeposit = () => {
    beginDeposit({
      externalUserId: 'user_123',
      destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
      destinationChainId: '137',
      destinationTokenAddress: '0x2791bca1f2de4661ed88a30c99a7a9449aa84174',
      destinationTokenSymbol: 'USDC',
      recipientAddress: '0x606C49ca2Fa4982F07016265040F777eD3DA3160',

      onEvent: (event) => {
        switch (event.type) {
          case DepositEventType.ONRAMP_SESSION_CREATED:
            analytics.track('onramp_session_created', {
              externalId: event.data.object.externalId,
            });
            break;

          case DepositEventType.DIRECT_EXECUTION_SUCCEEDED:
            // Same envelope shape as the webhook event of the same name.
            analytics.track('direct_execution_succeeded', {
              method: event.method,           // 'transfer' | 'card' | ...
              executionId: event.data.object.id,
              transactionHash: event.data.object.transactionHash,
              status: event.data.object.status,
            });
            break;
        }
      },

      // Optional once you're on `onEvent` — kept for "did it succeed?" style code.
      onSuccess: (data) => console.log('Deposit completed:', data.executionId),
      onError: (error) => console.error('Deposit failed:', error),
    });
  };

  return <button onClick={handleDeposit}>Deposit</button>;
}
```

<Tip>
  `onEvent` is the recommended integration point — use it unless you only care about the terminal success/failure. It fires for every lifecycle event (onramp redirects, direct execution success, …) and gives you the same envelope shape as [webhooks](/developer/webhooks/events). `onSuccess` / `onError` / `onClose` still fire for terminal outcomes and dialog dismissal; use them alongside `onEvent` if you want both.
</Tip>

### Example

```tsx theme={null}
// Promise pattern
try {
  const result = await beginDeposit({
    externalUserId: 'user_123',
    destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
    destinationChainId: '137',
    destinationTokenAddress: '0x2791bca1f2de4661ed88a30c99a7a9449aa84174',
    destinationTokenSymbol: 'USDC',
    recipientAddress: '0x606C49ca2Fa4982F07016265040F777eD3DA3160',
  });
  
  console.log('Success:', result);
} catch (error) {
  console.error('Error:', error);
}

// Callback pattern (with onClose)
beginDeposit({
  externalUserId: 'user_123',
  destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
  destinationChainId: '137',
  destinationTokenAddress: '0x2791bca1f2de4661ed88a30c99a7a9449aa84174',
  destinationTokenSymbol: 'USDC',
  recipientAddress: '0x606C49ca2Fa4982F07016265040F777eD3DA3160',
  onSuccess: (data) => console.log('Deposit completed:', data),
  onError: (error) => console.error('Deposit failed:', error),
  onClose: () => console.log('User dismissed the dialog'),
});

// Pre-select source token (Transfer Crypto defaults to USDC on Solana)
beginDeposit({
  externalUserId: 'user_123',
  destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
  destinationChainId: '137',
  destinationTokenAddress: '0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359',
  destinationTokenSymbol: 'USDC',
  recipientAddress: '0x606C49ca2Fa4982F07016265040F777eD3DA3160',
  defaultSourceChainType: 'solana',
  defaultSourceChainId: 'mainnet',
  defaultSourceTokenAddress: 'EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v',
  defaultSourceSymbol: 'USDC',
});

// Prefill an editable USD amount into every fiat input.
// Non-USD fiat steps (e.g. a EUR/GBP bank transfer) are auto-converted
// from this USD value using the live exchange rate.
beginDeposit({
  externalUserId: 'user_123',
  destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
  destinationChainId: '137',
  destinationTokenAddress: '0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359',
  destinationTokenSymbol: 'USDC',
  recipientAddress: '0x606C49ca2Fa4982F07016265040F777eD3DA3160',
  prefilledAmountUsd: '25.00',
});
```

***

## useAllowedCountry()

Checks whether the current user is in an allowed country based on their IP address and your project's blocked countries configuration. Automatically uses the `publishableKey` from `UnifoldProvider`.

### Returns

<ResponseField name="isAllowed" type="boolean | null">
  `true` if allowed, `false` if blocked, `null` while loading or on error.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="isLoading" type="boolean">
  Whether the geo check is in progress.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="alpha2" type="string | null">
  ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g. `"us"`, `"gb"`).
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="country" type="string | null">
  Full country name (e.g. `"United States"`).
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="error" type="Error | null">
  Error if the API call failed.
</ResponseField>

### Example

```tsx theme={null}
import { useAllowedCountry } from '@unifold/connect-react';

function DepositGate({ children }) {
  const { isAllowed, isLoading } = useAllowedCountry();

  if (isLoading) return <Spinner />;
  if (!isAllowed) return <p>Deposits are not available in your region.</p>;

  return children;
}
```

# Installation

> Install the Unifold React SDK and peer dependencies.

## Prerequisites

Before installing, ensure you have:

* React >= 18.0.0
* Node.js >= 18.0.0
* A Unifold publishable key from the [Unifold Dashboard](https://dashboard.unifold.io)

## Install the package

<CodeGroup>
  ```bash npm theme={null}
  npm install @unifold/connect-react
  ```

  ```bash pnpm theme={null}
  pnpm add @unifold/connect-react
  ```

  ```bash bun theme={null}
  bun add @unifold/connect-react
  ```

  ```bash yarn theme={null}
  yarn add @unifold/connect-react
  ```
</CodeGroup>

## Solana dependencies

`@unifold/connect-react` requires `@solana/web3.js` as a peer dependency for cross-chain deposits from Solana. You must install it separately:

<CodeGroup>
  ```bash npm theme={null}
  npm install @solana/web3.js
  ```

  ```bash pnpm theme={null}
  pnpm add @solana/web3.js
  ```

  ```bash bun theme={null}
  bun add @solana/web3.js
  ```

  ```bash yarn theme={null}
  yarn add @solana/web3.js
  ```
</CodeGroup>

<Warning>
  `@solana/web3.js` v2 is not supported. Make sure you are using a v1.x release (`< 2.0.0`).
</Warning>

## Setup

### 1. Import the styles

Add the SDK styles to your app's root layout or entry file:

```tsx theme={null}
import '@unifold/connect-react/styles.css';
```

### 2. Wrap your app with UnifoldProvider

```tsx theme={null}
import { UnifoldProvider } from '@unifold/connect-react';
import '@unifold/connect-react/styles.css';

function App() {
  return (
    <UnifoldProvider 
      publishableKey="pk_test_your_key"
      config={{
        modalTitle: 'Deposit Crypto',
      }}
    >
      <YourApp />
    </UnifoldProvider>
  );
}
```

### 3. Launch the deposit modal

Call `beginDeposit()` from anywhere in your app:

```tsx theme={null}
import { useUnifold } from '@unifold/connect-react';

function DepositButton() {
  const { beginDeposit } = useUnifold();

  const handleDeposit = async () => {
    try {
      const result = await beginDeposit({
        externalUserId: 'user_123',
        destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
        destinationChainId: '137',
        destinationTokenAddress: '0x2791bca1f2de4661ed88a30c99a7a9449aa84174',
        destinationTokenSymbol: 'USDC',
        recipientAddress: '0x606C49ca2Fa4982F07016265040F777eD3DA3160',
      });
      
      console.log('Deposit completed!', result);
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('Deposit failed:', error);
    }
  };

  return <button onClick={handleDeposit}>Deposit</button>;
}
```

## Verify installation

If the app renders without errors and the deposit modal opens when you call `beginDeposit()`, the installation is complete.

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Module not found errors">
    Clear your build cache and reinstall dependencies:

    ```bash theme={null}
    rm -rf node_modules .next
    npm install
    ```
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Styles not loading">
    Make sure you import the CSS file at the top of your app's entry file:

    ```tsx theme={null}
    import '@unifold/connect-react/styles.css';
    ```

    If using Next.js App Router, add the import in `app/layout.tsx`. For Pages Router, add it in `pages/_app.tsx`.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="@solana/web3.js peer dependency warning">
    Install the Solana dependency separately and ensure you are on a v1.x release:

    ```bash theme={null}
    npm install @solana/web3.js@^1
    ```
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Next.js or Vite build errors">
    If you encounter build errors related to Solana dependencies with webpack-based setups, ensure they are configured as externals. Vite users should check for alias override workarounds if optional peer dependency errors appear.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

# Overview

> Integrate crypto deposits, checkout, and fiat onramp into your React web app.

The `@unifold/connect-react` SDK provides a seamless way to integrate crypto deposits, checkout, and fiat onramp into your React web application.

## Features

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Crypto Deposits" icon="wallet">
    Accept crypto deposits from any wallet via QR code or address copy
  </Card>

  <Card title="Fiat Onramp" icon="credit-card">
    Buy with card via integrated onramp providers
  </Card>

  <Card title="Checkout" icon="cart-shopping">
    Accept fixed-amount crypto payments with a single function call
  </Card>

  <Card title="Multi-Chain Support" icon="link">
    Support for Ethereum, Polygon, Solana, Bitcoin, and more
  </Card>

  <Card title="Customizable UI" icon="palette">
    Light and dark mode with full theme customization
  </Card>

  <Card title="Browser Wallet" icon="plug">
    Optional browser wallet connection for direct deposits
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

## How It Works

1. **Install the SDK** and its peer dependency
2. **Import the styles** into your app's entry file
3. **Wrap your app** with `UnifoldProvider` using your publishable key
4. **Call `beginDeposit()`** to open the deposit modal

```tsx theme={null}
import { UnifoldProvider, useUnifold } from '@unifold/connect-react';
import '@unifold/connect-react/styles.css';

// 1. Wrap your app
<UnifoldProvider publishableKey="pk_live_...">
  <App />
</UnifoldProvider>

// 2. Launch deposit flow
const { beginDeposit } = useUnifold();
await beginDeposit({ externalUserId: 'user_123' });
```

## Requirements

* React 18 or higher
* A Unifold publishable key from the [Unifold Dashboard](https://dashboard.unifold.io)
