# Provider

> The UnifoldProvider component that wraps your app and provides the Unifold context.

## UnifoldProvider

Wraps your application and provides the Unifold context.

### Props

<ParamField path="publishableKey" type="string" required>
  Your Unifold API publishable key. Obtain this from the [Unifold Dashboard](https://dashboard.unifold.io).
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="queryClient" type="QueryClient">
  Bring your own [TanStack Query](https://tanstack.com/query) `QueryClient` (v5+). When provided, `UnifoldProvider` uses this client for all internal queries and **does not** add its own `QueryClientProvider` — it assumes one already exists higher in the tree.

  This avoids shadowing the host app's `QueryClient`, so Unifold hooks share the same cache, devtools, and default options as the rest of your app.

  When omitted, an internal `QueryClient` is created automatically (backward-compatible default).

  ```tsx theme={null}
  import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';

  const queryClient = new QueryClient();

  function App() {
    return (
      <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
        <UnifoldProvider publishableKey="pk_test_..." queryClient={queryClient}>
          {/* Your app — one shared QueryClient */}
        </UnifoldProvider>
      </QueryClientProvider>
    );
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="config" type="object">
  Optional configuration object.

  <Note>
    The **deposit menu title** and **Deposit with Card onramp** options (`transferCryptoTitle`, `depositTrackerSubTitle`, `hideDepositFlowInfo`, `hideDisplayDescription`, etc.) use the same `config` shape for **React** (`@unifold/connect-react`) and **Svelte** (`@unifold/connect-svelte`): the Svelte provider passes `config` into `@unifold/ui-web`, which runs the same widget. You can also set them as props on `DepositModal` from `@unifold/ui-react` if you embed that component directly. **Mobile native SDKs** (React Native, iOS, Android) do not use this `config` object.
  </Note>

  <Expandable title="config properties" defaultOpen>
    <ParamField path="config.displayMode" type="'stacked' | 'tabs'" default="'stacked'">
      Layout for the deposit modal main menu.

      * `'stacked'`: All deposit methods in a single vertical list (default)
      * `'tabs'`: Methods grouped into **Use Crypto** and **Use Cash** tabs

      See [Tab Layout](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/tab-layout) for details on grouping, auto-hiding, and `initialScreen` behavior.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.modalTitle" type="string">
      Custom title displayed in the deposit modal header.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.hideDepositTracker" type="boolean" default="false">
      Hide the deposit tracker button from the main modal view.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.transferCryptoTitle" type="string">
      Overrides the **Transfer Crypto** row title on the main deposit menu (and the Transfer Crypto flow header). Omit to use the default locale string (e.g. `"Transfer Crypto"` in English).
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.depositWithCardTitle" type="string">
      Overrides the **Deposit with Card** row title (and the card flow header when not on the quotes step). Default locale string is `"Deposit with Card"` in English.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.payWithExchangeTitle" type="string">
      Overrides the **Pay with Exchange** row title (and the exchange flow header). Default locale string is `"Pay with Exchange"` in English.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.depositTrackerTitle" type="string">
      Overrides the **Deposit Tracker** row title on the main menu and the tracker list header. Default locale string is `"Deposit Tracker"` in English.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.depositTrackerSubTitle" type="string">
      Overrides the subtitle (description line) under **Deposit Tracker** on the main menu. Default locale string is `"Track your deposit progress"` in English.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.hideDepositFlowInfo" type="boolean" default="false">
      On **Deposit with Card**, after the user picks a provider (“Complete transaction with …”), hides the summary card that shows **You use → You buy → You receive**.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.hideDisplayDescription" type="boolean" default="false">
      On the same onramp step, hides the informational note that the wallet address shown in the payment provider is a temporary deposit address.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.appearance" type="'light' | 'dark' | 'auto'" default="'dark'">
      Theme appearance for the modal.

      * `'light'`: Force light mode
      * `'dark'`: Force dark mode (default)
      * `'auto'`: Use system preference and respond to changes
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.showBalanceHeader" type="boolean" default="true">
      Show the destination wallet balance in the deposit modal header.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.transferInputVariant" type="'single_input' | 'double_input'" default="'double_input'">
      Layout variant for the Transfer Crypto token selector.

      * `'single_input'`: Single combined selector
      * `'double_input'`: Separate token and chain selectors (default)
    </ParamField>

    <Note>
      **Deposit method toggles** — the `enableXXX` options below control which payment methods appear on the deposit menu. Each one overrides the matching toggle in your dashboard: when the flag is set it wins, otherwise the method follows your **Dashboard → Project Settings → SDK Configuration** setting (and is shown by default if neither is set). Use these to show or hide methods for a specific integration without changing your dashboard defaults.
    </Note>

    <ParamField path="config.enableTransferCrypto" type="boolean">
      Show the **Transfer Crypto** option, letting users deposit by sending crypto from another wallet or exchange. Overrides the dashboard setting.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.enableConnectWallet" type="boolean">
      Show the browser wallet connection option, allowing users to connect and deposit directly from a browser wallet. Overrides the dashboard setting.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.enablePayWithExchange" type="boolean">
      Show the **Pay with Exchange** option, letting users pay from a connected exchange account. Overrides the dashboard setting.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.enableFiatOnramp" type="boolean">
      Show the fiat on-ramp option (shown as **Deposit with Card**), letting users buy crypto with a card or other fiat method. Overrides the dashboard setting.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.enableConnectExchange" type="boolean">
      Show the **Connect Exchange** option for a direct Coinbase Connect integration. Overrides the dashboard setting.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.enableCashApp" type="boolean">
      Show the **Pay with Cash App** option. Overrides the dashboard setting.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.enablePayWithStripeLink" type="boolean">
      Show the **Pay with Link** option — Stripe's headless crypto onramp that runs inline in the deposit modal (card, Apple Pay / Google Pay, Stripe Link, and KYC). Requires the `@stripe/crypto` peer dependency. Overrides the dashboard setting. See the [Stripe integration guide (React / web)](/developer/integrations/stripe#react-web).

      <Note>
        **Pay with Link is in Private Preview.** Your Stripe account must have Crypto Onramp enabled — Unifold's Stripe partnership can fast-track approval and unlock discounted fees. See the [Stripe integration guide](/developer/integrations/stripe#prerequisites).
      </Note>
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.browserWalletAmountQuickSelect" type="'percentage' | 'usd'" default="'percentage'">
      Controls the quick-select amount pills shown on the Connect Wallet "Enter amount" step.

      * `'percentage'`: Shows percentage-of-balance chips — **10 %**, **25 %**, **50 %**, **75 %**, **MAX** (default)
      * `'usd'`: Shows fixed USD amount chips — **$25**, **$50**, **$100**, **$250**, **\$500**
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.defaultInitialScreen" type="'main' | 'transfer' | 'card' | 'cashapp' | 'tracker' | 'pay_with_exchange' | 'exchange_connect' | 'wallet_connect'">
      Default first screen for `beginDeposit()` when the call omits `initialScreen`. See [Standalone entry screens](/developer/deposit/entry-screens) and [Tab Layout](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/tab-layout).
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.withdrawModalTitle" type="string">
      Custom title displayed in the withdraw modal header. Defaults to `"Withdraw"`.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="config.accentColor" type="string">
      Simple accent/primary color override applied to both light and dark modes (e.g. `'#8B5CF6'`). For full color customization, use `config.theme` instead. See [Customize Appearance](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/ui-customization/overview).
    </ParamField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>

### Example

```tsx theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider 
  publishableKey="pk_test_..."
  config={{
    modalTitle: 'Deposit Crypto',
    withdrawModalTitle: 'Withdraw Crypto',
    hideDepositTracker: false,
    appearance: 'dark',
    // Optional: show/hide deposit methods (otherwise follow Dashboard → Project Settings → SDK Configuration)
    // enableCashApp: false,
    // enableConnectWallet: true,
    // enablePayWithStripeLink: true, // Stripe "Pay with Link" — requires the @stripe/crypto peer dependency
    // Optional: main menu row titles (same config for @unifold/connect-svelte via ui-web)
    // transferCryptoTitle: 'Send crypto',
    // depositTrackerSubTitle: 'View status',
    // Optional: simplify the card onramp confirmation step
    // hideDepositFlowInfo: true,
    // hideDisplayDescription: true,
  }}
>
  {children}
</UnifoldProvider>
```

If you use `DepositModal` from `@unifold/ui-react` directly, the same options are available as component props (`transferCryptoTitle`, `hideDepositFlowInfo`, etc.).

# Component Styles

> Granular control over individual component properties for precise customization

Component styles provide fine-grained control over specific UI elements. Use them when you need precise customization beyond what semantic colors offer.

## Configuration Structure

Component styles can be configured in three ways:

1. **Flat (Universal)** - Applies to both light and dark modes
2. **Light Mode Specific** - Overrides flat styles in light mode
3. **Dark Mode Specific** - Overrides flat styles in dark mode

```tsx theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey="pk_test_..."
  config={{
    components: {
      // Flat - applies to BOTH modes (lowest priority)
      card: {
        backgroundColor: "#F5F5F5",
        titleColor: "#000000",
        borderRadius: 16,
      },
      
      // Mode-specific overrides (higher priority)
      light: {
        card: {
          backgroundColor: "#FFFFFF",
          titleColor: "#0F172A",
        }
      },
      dark: {
        card: {
          backgroundColor: "#292929",
          titleColor: "#F8FAFC",
        }
      }
    }
  }}
/>
```

## Priority System

When resolving component token values, the SDK follows this priority order:

1. **Mode-specific token** (`components.light.card.titleColor`)
2. **Flat token** (`components.card.titleColor`)
3. **Semantic theme color** (`theme.light.foreground`)
4. **Built-in default**

<Tip>
  Use **flat styles** for properties that should be the same in both modes (like border radius), and **mode-specific styles** only when you need different values for light vs dark.
</Tip>

## Header Styles

Controls navigation and header elements.

<ParamField path="header.titleColor" type="string">
  Color for header title text.

  **Falls back to:** `theme.*.foreground`

  ```tsx theme={null}
  components: {
    header: { titleColor: "#0F172A" }
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="header.buttonColor" type="string">
  Color for header action buttons and icons.

  **Falls back to:** `theme.*.foreground`

  ```tsx theme={null}
  components: {
    header: { buttonColor: "#64748B" }
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

### Example

```tsx theme={null}
components: {
  // Flat (both modes)
  header: {
    titleColor: "#000000",
    buttonColor: "#666666",
  },
  
  // Light mode specific
  light: {
    header: {
      titleColor: "#0F172A",
      buttonColor: "#64748B",
    }
  },
  
  // Dark mode specific
  dark: {
    header: {
      titleColor: "#F8FAFC",
      buttonColor: "#94A3B8",
    }
  }
}
```

```tsx theme={null}
      button: { borderRadius: 8 },

          titleColor: "#0F172A",
          subtitleColor: "#64748B",
          labelColor: "#94A3B8",
          headerColor: "#64748B",

          backgroundColor: "#FFFFFF",

        card: {
          backgroundColor: "#292929",
          titleColor: "#F8FAFC",
```

## TypeScript Support

```tsx theme={null}
import type { ComponentConfig, CardTokens, ButtonTokens } from '@unifold/connect-react';

const myComponents: ComponentConfig = {
  card: {
    backgroundColor: "#FFFFFF",
    titleColor: "#0F172A",
    borderRadius: 16,
  },
  button: {
    primaryBackground: "#667eea",
    borderRadius: 8,
  },
};
```

## Style usage by screen

The following mapping shows which component styles apply to each part of the deposit UI. Use it to target specific screens or elements when customizing.

### Headers (all modals and sheets)

* **Title text** → `header.titleColor`
* **Back / Close buttons** → `header.buttonColor`

Used on: Deposit modal, Transfer Crypto, Deposit with Card, Select Token, Select Provider, Currency modal, Deposit Tracker, Deposit Details, Glossary, Complete transaction (onramp).

### Transfer Crypto (single & double input)

* **Label** (“Select token to deposit”) → `card.labelColor`
* **Token selector card** background → `card.backgroundColor` (with `card.borderRadius`, `card.borderColor`)
* **Token symbol** (e.g. USDC.e) → `card.titleColor`
* **Network name** (e.g. Polygon) → `card.subtitleColor`
* **“\$X min”** on the right → `card.labelHighlightRightColor`
* **Chevron (›)** → `card.actionColor`
* **Intent address** label and **copy icon** → `card.labelColor`, `card.actionColor` (success when copied)
* **Footer “Terms” link** → semantic `primary`

### Select Token / Select Network (sheets & dropdowns)

* **Search** background, input text, placeholder → `search.backgroundColor`, `search.inputColor`, `search.placeholderColor`
* **Section headers** (“Quick select”, “All supported tokens”) → `list.titleSectionColor`
* **List row** background → `card.backgroundColor`
* **Token/network name** → `card.titleColor`
* **Secondary text** (network, “Minimum:”) → `card.subtitleColor`, `card.textRightColor`
* **Minimum amount** (e.g. \$10) → `card.labelHighlightRightColor`
* **Selection checkmark** → semantic `primary`
* **Dropdown items** (shared Select): item text → `card.titleColor`; checkmark → `primary`; content background → `card.backgroundColor`

### Deposit with Card

* **Currency pill** text and chevron → `card.titleColor`, `card.actionColor`
* **Amount** → `container.titleColor`
* **Conversion subtitle** (e.g. ≈ 481.40 USDC) → `container.subtitleColor`
* **Quick amount buttons** background → `card.backgroundColor`; selected border → `primary`
* **“Provider” label** → `card.labelColor`; **“Refreshing in 60s”** → `card.labelRightColor`
* **Provider card** “Auto-picked for you” → `card.headerColor`
* **Provider name** and **highlight label** (green) → `card.titleColor`, semantic `success`
* **Chevron** → `card.actionColor`
* **Continue button** → `container.buttonColor`, `container.buttonTitleColor`

### Select Provider (quotes list)

* **Provider card** background, border → `card.backgroundColor`, `card.borderColor`
* **Provider name** → `card.titleColor`
* **Provider highlight** badge → semantic `success`
* **Amount** (right) → `card.textRightColor`; **Fee / fiat** → `card.subtextRightColor`
* **Selected card border** → `primary`
* **Chevron** → `card.actionColor`

### Complete transaction (onramp / Banxa)

* **Title** (“Complete transaction with Banxa”) → `container.titleColor`
* **Subtitle** (“You can close this modal.”) → `container.subtitleColor`
* **Flow card** background → `card.backgroundColor`
* **Step titles** (USD, USDC) → `card.titleColor`
* **Step labels** (You use, You buy, You receive) → `card.subtitleColor`
* **Arrow icons** between steps → `card.iconColor`
* **Info block** background and **description text** → `card.backgroundColor`, `card.descriptionColor`

### Currency modal

* **Search** → `search.backgroundColor`, `search.inputColor`, `search.placeholderColor`
* **Section headers** (“Popular currencies”, “All currencies”) → `list.titleSectionColor`
* **Row** background → `card.backgroundColor`
* **Currency name** → `card.titleColor`; **code** (USD, EUR) → `card.subtitleColor`
* **Selection checkmark** → `primary`

### Deposit Tracker (list)

* **Row** background → `card.backgroundColor`
* **“Deposit completed” / “Deposit processing”** → `card.titleColor`
* **Date/time** → `card.subtitleColor`
* **Amount** (right) → `card.textRightColor`
* **Chevron** → `card.actionColor`

### Deposit Details (after tapping a row)

* **Status** (“Completed” / “Processing”) and **timestamp** → `container.titleColor`, `container.subtitleColor`
* **Detail card** background → `card.backgroundColor`
* **Row labels** (Amount Sent, Amount Received, etc.) → `card.rowLeftLabel`
* **Row values** → `card.rowRightLabel`
* **“See more details”** text and chevron → `container.actionTitle`, `container.actionColor`
* **External link icon** next to tx hashes → `card.actionIcon`

### Glossary (Price Impact & Slippage)

* **Modal** background → optional; defaults to semantic `background`
* **Header** title and close → `header.titleColor`, `header.buttonColor`
* **Card** sections → `card.backgroundColor`, `card.titleColor`, `card.descriptionColor`

### Deposit method cards (main modal)

* **Card** background, border → `card.backgroundColor`, `card.borderRadius`, `card.borderColor`
* **Title and subtitle** → `card.titleColor`, `card.subtitleColor`
* **Icon** (Transfer Crypto, Deposit with Card, etc.) → `card.iconColor`

***

## Best Practices

<Tip>
  **Use semantic colors first**, then layer component styles only where you need specific overrides. This keeps your configuration manageable.
</Tip>

<Tip>
  **Put shape properties (borderRadius, borderWidth) in flat styles** since they typically stay the same across light and dark modes. Put color properties in mode-specific styles.
</Tip>

<Warning>
  **Don't override every token**. Only specify the properties you actually want to customize. Unspecified properties will use semantic theme colors or sensible defaults.
</Warning>

<Info>
  **Test in both modes** when using mode-specific styles. Switch between light and dark appearance to ensure proper contrast and readability.
</Info>

# Examples

> Complete real-world examples of SDK theming configurations

Explore complete theming configurations for common use cases. Copy and adapt these examples to match your brand.

## Basic Examples

### Minimal Configuration

The simplest way to theme the SDK - just set accent color:

```tsx theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey="pk_test_..."
  config={{
    accentColor: "#667eea"
  }}
>
  {/* Your app */}
</UnifoldProvider>
```

### Light & Dark Modes

Basic semantic color configuration for both modes:

```tsx theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey="pk_test_..."
  config={{
    appearance: "auto",
    theme: {
      light: {
        background: "#FFFFFF",
        foreground: "#0F172A",
        primary: "#667eea",
      },
      dark: {
        background: "#191919",
        foreground: "#F8FAFC",
        primary: "#667eea",
      }
    }
  }}
>
  {/* Your app */}
</UnifoldProvider>
```

```tsx theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
```

### Next.js with Per-Weight Fonts

```tsx theme={null}
import { Inter, Space_Grotesk } from 'next/font/google';

const inter = Inter({ subsets: ['latin'], variable: '--font-inter' });
const spaceGrotesk = Space_Grotesk({ subsets: ['latin'], variable: '--font-space' });

export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
  return (
    <html className={`${inter.variable} ${spaceGrotesk.variable}`}>
      <body>
        <UnifoldProvider
          publishableKey="pk_test_..."
          config={{
            fonts: {
              regular: "var(--font-inter), sans-serif",
              medium: "var(--font-inter), sans-serif",
              semibold: "var(--font-space), sans-serif",
              bold: "var(--font-space), sans-serif",
            }
          }}
        >
          {children}
        </UnifoldProvider>
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

### Preview in Multiple Modes

```tsx theme={null}
function ThemeDemo() {
  const [mode, setMode] = useState<'light' | 'dark' | 'auto'>('auto');
  
  return (
    <>
      <button onClick={() => setMode('light')}>Light</button>
      <button onClick={() => setMode('dark')}>Dark</button>
      <button onClick={() => setMode('auto')}>Auto</button>
      
      <UnifoldProvider
        publishableKey="pk_test_..."
        config={{
          appearance: mode,
          theme: { /* your theme */ }
        }}
      >
        {/* Your components */}
      </UnifoldProvider>
    </>
  );
}
```

# Custom Fonts

> Configure custom typography and font families for your SDK components

The Unifold React SDK allows you to customize typography by configuring custom font families. Apply your brand's typeface to create a cohesive user experience.

## Basic Configuration

Set a custom font family through the `fontFamily` property:

```tsx theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey="pk_test_..."
  config={{
    fontFamily: "Inter, -apple-system, sans-serif"
  }}
>
  {/* Your app */}
</UnifoldProvider>
```

<Info>
  The SDK will apply your `fontFamily` to all text elements within its components, including buttons, inputs, cards, and headers.
</Info>

## Per-Weight Font Configuration

For more precise control, use the `fonts` property to specify different font families for each weight:

```tsx theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey="pk_test_..."
  config={{
    fonts: {
      regular: "Inter Regular, sans-serif",
      medium: "Inter Medium, sans-serif",
      semibold: "Inter SemiBold, sans-serif",
      bold: "Inter Bold, sans-serif",
    }
  }}
>
  {/* Your app */}
</UnifoldProvider>
```

### FontConfig Properties

<ParamField path="fonts.regular" type="string">
  Font family for regular weight (400) text — body copy, labels, and default text.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="fonts.medium" type="string">
  Font family for medium weight (500) text — subtitles and emphasized content.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="fonts.semibold" type="string">
  Font family for semi-bold weight (600) text — section headers and strong emphasis.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="fonts.bold" type="string">
  Font family for bold weight (700) text — headings and primary actions.
</ParamField>

<Tip>
  All properties in `fonts` are optional. Unspecified weights fall back to the SDK's built-in font. Use `fontFamily` for a single font across all weights, or `fonts` when you need per-weight control.
</Tip>

<Warning>
  If both `fontFamily` and `fonts` are provided, `fonts` takes precedence for each weight it defines.
</Warning>

### When to Use Per-Weight Fonts

Per-weight font configuration is useful when:

* Your brand uses different typefaces for headings vs body text
* You're using non-variable fonts that require separate files per weight
* You want a display font for bold/semibold and a body font for regular/medium

```tsx theme={null}
config={{
  fonts: {
    regular: "Inter, sans-serif",
    medium: "Inter, sans-serif",
    semibold: "Space Grotesk, sans-serif",
    bold: "Space Grotesk, sans-serif",
  }
}}
```

### San Francisco (Apple)

```tsx theme={null}
config={{

}}
```

### Segoe UI (Windows)

```tsx theme={null}

```

## Using Google Fonts

### Step 1: Import the Font

Add the Google Fonts link to your HTML `<head>`:

```html theme={null}
<head>
  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
  <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;500;600;700&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
</head>
```

Or import in your CSS:

```css theme={null}
@import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;500;600;700&display=swap');
```

### Step 2: Configure the SDK

```tsx theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey="pk_test_..."
  config={{
    fontFamily: "Inter, sans-serif"
  }}
>
  {/* Your app */}
</UnifoldProvider>
```

## Using Custom/Self-Hosted Fonts

### Step 1: Define Font Face

Add `@font-face` rules to your CSS:

```css theme={null}
@font-face {
  font-family: 'MyCustomFont';
  src: url('/fonts/MyCustomFont-Regular.woff2') format('woff2'),
       url('/fonts/MyCustomFont-Regular.woff') format('woff');
  font-weight: 400;
  font-style: normal;
  font-display: swap;
}

@font-face {
  font-family: 'MyCustomFont';
  src: url('/fonts/MyCustomFont-Bold.woff2') format('woff2'),
       url('/fonts/MyCustomFont-Bold.woff') format('woff');
  font-weight: 700;
  font-style: normal;
  font-display: swap;
}
```

### Step 2: Configure the SDK

```tsx theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey="pk_test_..."
  config={{
    fontFamily: "MyCustomFont, sans-serif"
  }}
>
  {/* Your app */}
</UnifoldProvider>
```

## Font Stack Best Practices

Always provide fallback fonts to ensure text displays properly while custom fonts load:

```tsx theme={null}
config={{
  fontFamily: "Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif"
}}
```

<Tip>
  **Include system fonts as fallbacks** to ensure your UI remains readable even if the custom font fails to load.
</Tip>

## Advanced Font Configuration

### Using Next.js Font Optimization

If you're using Next.js, leverage the built-in font optimization:

```tsx theme={null}
// app/layout.tsx
import { Inter } from 'next/font/google';

const inter = Inter({
  subsets: ['latin'],
  weight: ['400', '500', '600', '700'],
  variable: '--font-inter',
});

export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en" className={inter.variable}>
      <body>
        <UnifoldProvider
          publishableKey="pk_test_..."
          config={{
            fontFamily: "var(--font-inter), sans-serif"
          }}
        >
          {children}
        </UnifoldProvider>
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

### Using Variable Fonts

Variable fonts provide multiple font weights in a single file:

```css theme={null}
@import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@100..900&display=swap');
```

```tsx theme={null}
config={{
  fontFamily: "Inter, sans-serif"
}}
```

## Font Loading Strategies

### Preload Critical Fonts

Add `<link rel="preload">` for faster font loading:

```html theme={null}
<link rel="preload" href="/fonts/Inter-Regular.woff2" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>
```

### Font Display Strategy

Use `font-display: swap` to show fallback text immediately:

```css theme={null}
@font-face {
  font-family: 'Inter';
  src: url('/fonts/Inter-Regular.woff2') format('woff2');
  font-display: swap;
}
```

## TypeScript Support

Both font configuration options are fully typed:

```tsx theme={null}
import type { FontConfig } from '@unifold/connect-react';

// Single font family
const config = {
  fontFamily: "Inter, sans-serif",
};

// Per-weight configuration
const fonts: FontConfig = {
  regular: "Inter, sans-serif",
  medium: "Inter Medium, sans-serif",
  semibold: "Inter SemiBold, sans-serif",
  bold: "Inter Bold, sans-serif",
};
```

## Testing Your Fonts

### Visual Testing

1. Open the SDK components in your browser
2. Open DevTools (F12)
3. Check the computed font-family in the Elements tab
4. Verify the correct font is loading in the Network tab

### Font Loading Verification

```javascript theme={null}
document.fonts.ready.then(() => {
  console.log('All fonts loaded');
  console.log(document.fonts.check('1em Inter')); // true if loaded
});
```

## Common Issues

<Warning>
  **Font not displaying?** Ensure:

  1. Font files are accessible (check Network tab)
  2. CORS headers allow font loading
  3. Font name matches exactly in `fontFamily` or `fonts` config
  4. Font weights used in SDK (400, 500, 600, 700) are included in your font import
</Warning>

<Tip>
  **Performance tip:** Only load the font weights you actually use (400, 500, 600, 700). Avoid loading the full 100-900 range unless necessary.
</Tip>

## Quick Start

### 1. Minimal Configuration

Just set an accent color:

```tsx theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey="pk_test_..."
  config={{
    accentColor: "#667eea"
  }}
>
  {children}
</UnifoldProvider>
```

### 2. Basic Theme

Add semantic colors for light and dark modes:

```tsx theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey="pk_test_..."
  config={{
    appearance: "auto",
    theme: {
      light: {
        background: "#FFFFFF",
        foreground: "#0F172A",
        primary: "#667eea",
      },
      dark: {
        background: "#191919",
        foreground: "#F8FAFC",
        primary: "#667eea",
      }
    }
  }}
>
  {children}
</UnifoldProvider>
```

### 3. Granular Control

Add component styles for fine-tuned customization:

```tsx theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey="pk_test_..."
  config={{
    appearance: "auto",
    theme: { /* semantic colors */ },
    components: {
      // Shape properties shared across modes
      card: { borderRadius: 16, borderWidth: 1 },
      button: { borderRadius: 8 },
      
      // Color overrides per mode
      light: {
        card: {
          backgroundColor: "#F8FAFC",
          titleColor: "#0F172A",
          borderColor: "#E2E8F0",
        }
      },
      dark: {
        card: {
          backgroundColor: "#292929",
          titleColor: "#F8FAFC",
          borderColor: "#38383A",
        }
      }
    }
  }}
>
  {children}
</UnifoldProvider>
```

## What Can You Customize?

### Semantic Theme (17 styles)

Global colors affecting all components:

* **Base**: background, card, cardHover
* **Text**: foreground, foregroundMuted, foregroundSubtle
* **Borders**: border, borderSecondary
* **Brand**: primary, primaryForeground
* **Status**: success, successBackground, warning, warningBackground, error, errorBackground
* **Overlay**: overlay

### Component Styles (48 properties)

Fine-grained control over 7 component categories:

* **Header** (2): titleColor, buttonColor
* **Card** (19): backgroundColor, titleColor, subtitleColor, labelColor, headerColor, labelRightColor, labelHighlightRightColor, textRightColor, subtextRightColor, rowLeftLabel, rowRightLabel, iconColor, iconBackgroundColor, actionColor, actionIcon, descriptionColor, borderRadius, borderWidth, borderColor
* **Button** (7): primaryBackground, primaryText, secondaryBackground, secondaryText, borderRadius, borderWidth, borderColor
* **Input** (6): backgroundColor, textColor, placeholderColor, borderColor, borderRadius, borderWidth
* **Container** (9): titleColor, subtitleColor, actionColor, actionTitle, buttonColor, buttonTitleColor, iconBackgroundColor, iconColor, borderRadius
* **Search** (3): backgroundColor, inputColor, placeholderColor
* **List** (2): titleSectionColor, rowBorderRadius

### Typography

* **Single font** (`fontFamily`): One font family for all text weights
* **Per-weight fonts** (`fonts`): Different font families for regular, medium, semibold, and bold weights
* Google Fonts, self-hosted fonts, system fonts, Next.js font optimization

# Overview

> Customize the look and feel of Unifold React SDK components.

The Unifold React SDK provides a comprehensive theming system that allows you to customize every aspect of your UI components. Whether you need simple brand color updates or complete design control, our theming system has you covered.

## Two Levels of Customization

The SDK offers two complementary approaches to theming:

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Semantic Theme" icon="palette" href="./semantic-colors">
    Global color system affecting all components. Perfect for brand consistency and quick styling.
  </Card>

  <Card title="Component Styles" icon="sliders" href="./component-styles">
    Granular control over individual component properties. Ideal for fine-tuned customization.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

## Quick Start

```tsx theme={null}
import { UnifoldProvider } from '@unifold/connect-react';

function App() {
  return (
    <UnifoldProvider
      publishableKey="pk_test_..."
      config={{
        // Light/Dark mode
        appearance: "dark", // "light" | "dark" | "auto"
        
        // Quick brand color
        accentColor: "#667eea",
        
        // Semantic colors
        theme: {
          light: {
            background: "#FFFFFF",
            foreground: "#0F172A",
            primary: "#667eea",
          },
          dark: {
            background: "#191919",
            foreground: "#F8FAFC",
            primary: "#667eea",
          }
        },
        
        // Component styles
        components: {
          card: {
            backgroundColor: "#F8FAFC",
            titleColor: "#0F172A",
            borderRadius: 16,
          },
          button: {
            borderRadius: 8,
          },
        },
        
        // Custom fonts
        fontFamily: "Inter, sans-serif",
      }}
    >
      {/* Your app */}
    </UnifoldProvider>
  );
}
```

## Key Concepts

### Appearance Modes

The SDK supports three appearance modes:

* **`light`** - Force light mode
* **`dark`** - Force dark mode
* **`auto`** - Automatically matches system preference

### Theme Priority System

When resolving colors, the SDK follows this priority order (highest to lowest):

1. **Mode-specific component token** (e.g., `components.light.card.titleColor`)
2. **Flat component token** (e.g., `components.card.titleColor`)
3. **Semantic theme color** (e.g., `theme.light.foreground`)
4. **Built-in default**

This priority system gives you maximum flexibility while maintaining sensible defaults.

### Color Format Support

All color properties accept standard CSS color formats:

* **Hex**: `"#667eea"`, `"#667eea80"` (with alpha)
* **RGB**: `"rgb(102, 126, 234)"`
* **RGBA**: `"rgba(102, 126, 234, 0.5)"`
* **HSL**: `"hsl(235, 75%, 66%)"`

## What Can You Customize?

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Semantic Theme Colors (17 styles)">
    Global colors that affect all components:

    * Background, foreground, card colors
    * Primary brand color
    * Border colors
    * Success, warning, error states (with backgrounds)
    * Overlay
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Component Styles (48 properties)">
    Fine-grained control over 7 component categories:

    * **Header** (2): title, buttons
    * **Card** (19): background, title, subtitle, labels, icons, actions, borders, radius
    * **Button** (7): primary/secondary backgrounds and text, borders, radius
    * **Input** (6): background, text, placeholder, borders, radius
    * **Container** (9): titles, subtitles, actions, buttons, icons, radius
    * **Search** (3): background, input, placeholder
    * **List** (2): section titles, row radius

    See **Style usage by screen** in [Component Styles](./component-styles#style-usage-by-screen) for a mapping of which styles apply to each screen (Transfer Crypto, Select Token, Deposit with Card, Deposit Tracker, etc.).
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Typography">
    * Single font family for all text (`fontFamily`)
    * Per-weight font families for granular control (`fonts`)
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Interactive Playground

To try out theming in real-time with our UI Playground, contact us.

The UI playground allows you to:

* Toggle between light and dark modes
* Adjust semantic colors with color pickers
* Customize individual component styles
* Adjust border radius and border width
* See changes applied instantly
* Copy generated configuration code

# Quick Reference

> Fast lookup guide for all theming configuration options

A comprehensive cheat sheet for all available theming options in the Unifold React SDK.

The same `config` object shape is used by **Svelte** (`@unifold/connect-svelte`): it is typed as `UnifoldConfig` from `@unifold/ui-web` and forwarded into the same web widget.

## Configuration Structure

```tsx theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey="pk_test_..."
  config={{
    appearance: "light" | "dark" | "auto",
    accentColor: string,
    fontFamily: string,
    fonts: {
      regular: string,
      medium: string,
      semibold: string,
      bold: string,
    },
    theme: {
      light: { /* ThemeColors */ },
      dark: { /* ThemeColors */ }
    },
    components: {
      /* Flat styles */
      header: { /* HeaderStyles */ },
      card: { /* CardStyles */ },
      button: { /* ButtonStyles */ },
      input: { /* InputStyles */ },
      container: { /* ContainerStyles */ },
      search: { /* SearchStyles */ },
      list: { /* ListStyles */ },
      
      /* Mode-specific styles */
      light: {
        header: { /* HeaderStyles */ },
        card: { /* CardStyles */ },
        button: { /* ButtonStyles */ },
        input: { /* InputStyles */ },
        container: { /* ContainerStyles */ },
        search: { /* SearchStyles */ },
        list: { /* ListStyles */ },
      },
      dark: {
        header: { /* HeaderStyles */ },
        card: { /* CardStyles */ },
        button: { /* ButtonStyles */ },
        input: { /* InputStyles */ },
        container: { /* ContainerStyles */ },
        search: { /* SearchStyles */ },
        list: { /* ListStyles */ },
      }
    }
  }}
/>
```

## Component Styles (48 properties)

### Header Styles (2 properties)

```tsx theme={null}
header: {
  titleColor: string,   // Header title          → foreground
  buttonColor: string,  // Header buttons        → foreground
}
```

### Card Styles (19 properties)

```tsx theme={null}
card: {
  // Color properties
  backgroundColor: string,         // Card background           → card
  titleColor: string,              // Card title                → foreground
  subtitleColor: string,           // Card subtitle             → foregroundMuted
  labelColor: string,              // Card labels               → foregroundMuted
  headerColor: string,             // Card header text          → foregroundMuted
  labelRightColor: string,         // Right-aligned labels      → foregroundMuted
  labelHighlightRightColor: string,// Highlighted right labels  → warning
  textRightColor: string,          // Right-aligned text        → foreground
  subtextRightColor: string,       // Right-aligned subtext     → foregroundMuted
  rowLeftLabel: string,            // Left column labels        → foregroundMuted
  rowRightLabel: string,           // Right column labels       → foreground
  iconColor: string,               // Card icons                → primary
  iconBackgroundColor: string,     // Icon bg                   → primary + 15% opacity
  actionColor: string,             // Action indicators         → foregroundMuted
  actionIcon: string,              // Action icons              → foregroundMuted
  descriptionColor: string,        // Description text          → foregroundMuted
  // Shape properties
  borderRadius: number,            // Corner radius (px)        → 12
  borderWidth: number,             // Border width (px)         → 0
  borderColor: string,             // Border color              → border
}
```

### Button Styles (7 properties)

```tsx theme={null}
button: {
  primaryBackground: string,   // Primary button bg         → primary
  primaryText: string,         // Primary button text       → primaryForeground
  secondaryBackground: string, // Secondary button bg       → card
  secondaryText: string,       // Secondary button text     → foreground
  borderRadius: number,        // Corner radius (px)        → 12
  borderWidth: number,         // Border width (px)         → 0
  borderColor: string,         // Border color              → border
}
```

### Input Styles (6 properties)

```tsx theme={null}
input: {
  backgroundColor: string, // Input background           → card
  textColor: string,       // Input text                 → foreground
  placeholderColor: string, // Placeholder text           → foregroundMuted
  borderColor: string,     // Border color               → border
  borderRadius: number,    // Corner radius (px)         → 8
  borderWidth: number,     // Border width (px)          → 1
}
```

### Container Styles (9 properties)

```tsx theme={null}
container: {
  titleColor: string,          // Container title           → foreground
  subtitleColor: string,       // Container subtitle        → foregroundMuted
  actionColor: string,         // Action elements           → foregroundMuted
  actionTitle: string,         // Action title text         → foregroundMuted
  buttonColor: string,         // Button background         → primary
  buttonTitleColor: string,    // Button text               → primaryForeground
  iconBackgroundColor: string, // Status icon bg            → success
  iconColor: string,           // Status icon               → foreground
  borderRadius: number,        // Modal corner radius (px)  → 24
}
```

### Search Styles (3 properties)

```tsx theme={null}
search: {
  backgroundColor: string, // Search background          → card
  inputColor: string,      // Search text                → foreground
  placeholderColor: string, // Search placeholder         → foregroundMuted
}
```

### List Styles (2 properties)

```tsx theme={null}
list: {
  titleSectionColor: string, // List section headers      → foregroundMuted
  rowBorderRadius: number,   // Row corner radius (px)    → 12
}
```

***

## Priority System

Colors are resolved in this order (highest to lowest):

<Steps>
  <Step title="Mode-Specific Component Style">
    `components.light.card.titleColor` or `components.dark.card.titleColor`
  </Step>

  <Step title="Flat Component Style">
    `components.card.titleColor`
  </Step>

  <Step title="Semantic Theme Color">
    `theme.light.foreground` or `theme.dark.foreground`
  </Step>

  <Step title="Built-in Default">
    SDK's default color values
  </Step>
</Steps>

***

## Common Patterns

### Minimal Setup

```tsx theme={null}
config={{
  accentColor: "#667eea"
}}
```

### Basic Theme

```tsx theme={null}
config={{
  theme: {
    light: {
      background: "#FFFFFF",
      foreground: "#0F172A",
      primary: "#667eea",
    }
  }
}}
```

### With Component Styles

```tsx theme={null}
config={{
  theme: {
    light: { primary: "#667eea" }
  },
  components: {
    card: { borderRadius: 16 },
    light: {
      card: { titleColor: "#0F172A" }
    }
  }
}}
```

### Full Configuration

```tsx theme={null}
config={{
  appearance: "auto",
  accentColor: "#667eea",
  fontFamily: "Inter, sans-serif",
  theme: {
    light: { /* all 17 styles */ },
    dark: { /* all 17 styles */ }
  },
  components: {
    // Flat styles (shapes)
    card: { borderRadius: 16, borderWidth: 1 },
    button: { borderRadius: 8 },
    input: { borderRadius: 8 },
    container: { borderRadius: 20 },
    list: { rowBorderRadius: 8 },
    
    // Mode-specific (colors)
    light: {
      card: { /* properties */ },
      button: { /* properties */ },
    },
    dark: {
      card: { /* properties */ },
      button: { /* properties */ },
    }
  }
}}
```

***

## Color Format Support

All color properties accept:

<CodeGroup>
  ```tsx Hex theme={null}
  "#667eea"
  "#667eea80" // with alpha
  ```

  ```tsx RGB theme={null}
  "rgb(102, 126, 234)"
  ```

  ```tsx RGBA theme={null}
  "rgba(102, 126, 234, 0.5)"
  ```

  ```tsx HSL theme={null}
  "hsl(235, 75%, 66%)"
  ```

  ```tsx CSS Variables theme={null}
  "var(--my-color)"
  ```

  ```tsx Gradients (buttons) theme={null}
  "linear-gradient(135deg, #667eea 0%, #764ba2 100%)"
  ```
</CodeGroup>

## Checklist

Use this checklist when configuring your theme:

<Steps>
  <Step title="Set Appearance Mode">
    Choose `light`, `dark`, or `auto`
  </Step>

  <Step title="Configure Accent Color">
    Set your primary brand color
  </Step>

  <Step title="Add Semantic Colors (Optional)">
    Customize global color styles
  </Step>

  <Step title="Add Component Styles (Optional)">
    Fine-tune specific components
  </Step>

  <Step title="Adjust Borders & Shapes (Optional)">
    Set borderRadius and borderWidth on cards, buttons, inputs
  </Step>

  <Step title="Set Custom Font (Optional)">
    Configure single font or per-weight fonts
  </Step>

  <Step title="Test in Both Modes">
    Verify light and dark appearance
  </Step>

  <Step title="Check Contrast">
    Ensure readability (4.5:1 ratio)
  </Step>
</Steps>

***

## Common Mistakes

<Warning>
  **Using `components.card` and `components.light.card` together**

  Mode-specific styles override flat styles. Be intentional about which you use. Put shared shape properties (like `borderRadius`) in flat styles, and mode-specific colors in `light`/`dark`.
</Warning>

<Warning>
  **Forgetting dark mode**

  Always test with `appearance: "dark"` to ensure proper contrast.
</Warning>

<Warning>
  **Inconsistent font loading**

  Ensure custom fonts are loaded before the SDK initializes.
</Warning>

<Warning>
  **Not providing fallbacks**

  Always include fallback fonts in `fontFamily` or `fonts` configuration.
</Warning>

# Semantic Colors

> Global color tokens that provide consistent theming across all components

Semantic colors are global color tokens that affect all components in the SDK. They provide a consistent foundation for your UI theme and are the easiest way to apply your brand colors across the entire SDK.

## Configuration

Configure semantic colors through the `theme` property in your `UnifoldProvider` config:

```tsx theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey="pk_test_..."
  config={{
    theme: {
      light: {
        // Your light mode colors
      },
      dark: {
        // Your dark mode colors
      }
    }
  }}
>
  {/* Your app */}
</UnifoldProvider>
```

## Complete Token Reference

### Base Colors

<ParamField path="background" type="string">
  Primary background color for the entire interface.

  **Default (Light):** `#FFFFFF`\
  **Default (Dark):** `#191919`

  ```tsx theme={null}
  theme: {
    light: { background: "#FFFFFF" },
    dark: { background: "#191919" }
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="card" type="string">
  Background color for card components and elevated surfaces.

  **Default (Light):** `#F8FAFC`\
  **Default (Dark):** `#292929`

  ```tsx theme={null}
  theme: {
    light: { card: "#F8FAFC" },
    dark: { card: "#292929" }
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="cardHover" type="string">
  Background color for cards in hover state.

  **Default (Light):** `#F1F5F9`\
  **Default (Dark):** `#48474A`

  ```tsx theme={null}
  theme: {
    light: { cardHover: "#E2E8F0" },
    dark: { cardHover: "#3F3F45" }
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

### Text Colors

<ParamField path="foreground" type="string">
  Primary text color for headings and important content.

  **Default (Light):** `#0F172A`\
  **Default (Dark):** `#F8FAFC`

  ```tsx theme={null}
  theme: {
    light: { foreground: "#1F2937" },
    dark: { foreground: "#F9FAFB" }
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="foregroundMuted" type="string">
  Secondary text color for less prominent content.

  **Default (Light):** `#64748B`\
  **Default (Dark):** `#94A3B8`

  ```tsx theme={null}
  theme: {
    light: { foregroundMuted: "#6B7280" },
    dark: { foregroundMuted: "#9CA3AF" }
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="foregroundSubtle" type="string">
  Tertiary text color for subtle content and hints.

  **Default (Light):** `#94A3B8`\
  **Default (Dark):** `#64748B`

  ```tsx theme={null}
  theme: {
    light: { foregroundSubtle: "#9CA3AF" },
    dark: { foregroundSubtle: "#6B7280" }
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

### Border Colors

<ParamField path="border" type="string">
  Primary border color for input fields and dividers.

  **Default (Light):** `#E2E8F0`\
  **Default (Dark):** `#38383A`

  ```tsx theme={null}
  theme: {
    light: { border: "#D1D5DB" },
    dark: { border: "#38383A" }
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="borderSecondary" type="string">
  Secondary border color for subtle separators.

  **Default (Light):** `#CBD5E1`\
  **Default (Dark):** `#48484A`

  ```tsx theme={null}
  theme: {
    light: { borderSecondary: "#E5E7EB" },
    dark: { borderSecondary: "#48484A" }
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

### Brand Colors

<ParamField path="primary" type="string">
  Primary brand color for buttons, links, and key actions.

  **Default:** `#3B82F6`

  ```tsx theme={null}
  theme: {
    light: { primary: "#667eea" },
    dark: { primary: "#667eea" }
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="primaryForeground" type="string">
  Text color on primary colored backgrounds.

  **Default:** `#FFFFFF`

  ```tsx theme={null}
  theme: {
    light: { primaryForeground: "#FFFFFF" },
    dark: { primaryForeground: "#FFFFFF" }
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

### Status Colors

<ParamField path="success" type="string">
  Color for success states and positive actions.

  **Default:** `#22C55E`

  ```tsx theme={null}
  theme: {
    light: { success: "#22C55E" },
    dark: { success: "#22C55E" }
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="successBackground" type="string">
  Background color for success messages and alerts.

  **Default (Light):** `#DCFCE7`\
  **Default (Dark):** `rgba(34, 197, 94, 0.1)`

  ```tsx theme={null}
  theme: {
    light: { successBackground: "#DCFCE7" },
    dark: { successBackground: "rgba(34, 197, 94, 0.1)" }
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="warning" type="string">
  Color for warning states and caution indicators.

  **Default:** `#F59E0B`

  ```tsx theme={null}
  theme: {
    light: { warning: "#F59E0B" },
    dark: { warning: "#F59E0B" }
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="warningBackground" type="string">
  Background color for warning messages and alerts.

  **Default (Light):** `#FEF3C7`\
  **Default (Dark):** `rgba(245, 158, 11, 0.1)`

  ```tsx theme={null}
  theme: {
    light: { warningBackground: "#FEF3C7" },
    dark: { warningBackground: "rgba(245, 158, 11, 0.1)" }
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="error" type="string">
  Color for error states and destructive actions.

  **Default:** `#EF4444`

  ```tsx theme={null}
  theme: {
    light: { error: "#EF4444" },
    dark: { error: "#EF4444" }
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="errorBackground" type="string">
  Background color for error messages and alerts.

  **Default (Light):** `#FEE2E2`\
  **Default (Dark):** `rgba(239, 68, 68, 0.1)`

  ```tsx theme={null}
  theme: {
    light: { errorBackground: "#FEE2E2" },
    dark: { errorBackground: "rgba(239, 68, 68, 0.1)" }
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

### Overlay

<ParamField path="overlay" type="string">
  Background color for the modal overlay/backdrop.

  **Default (Light):** `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)`\
  **Default (Dark):** `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.7)`

  ```tsx theme={null}
  theme: {
    light: { overlay: "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)" },
    dark: { overlay: "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.7)" }
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

All semantic color tokens are fully typed:

```tsx theme={null}
import type { ThemeColors } from '@unifold/connect-react';

const myTheme: Partial<ThemeColors> = {
```

## Best Practices

<Tip>
  **Start with semantic colors** before diving into component styles. They provide the foundation for your entire theme and will handle 80% of your styling needs.
</Tip>

<Warning>
  **Maintain sufficient contrast** between `foreground` and `background` colors to ensure readability. Aim for a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 for normal text.
</Warning>

<Info>
  **Use the same `primary` color** in both light and dark modes for brand consistency, but adjust surrounding colors for proper contrast.
</Info>

# Troubleshooting

> Solutions to common theming issues and configuration problems.

Solutions to common theming issues and configuration problems.

## Theme Not Applying

### Issue: Custom colors not showing up

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Check configuration is passed correctly">
    Ensure your `config` object is properly passed to `UnifoldProvider`:

    ```tsx theme={null}
    // ❌ Wrong - missing config prop
    <UnifoldProvider publishableKey="pk_test_...">
      {children}
    </UnifoldProvider>

    // ✅ Correct
    <UnifoldProvider
      publishableKey="pk_test_..."
      config={{
        theme: { /* your theme */ }
      }}
    >
      {children}
    </UnifoldProvider>
    ```
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Verify you're using the correct property names">
    Property names are case-sensitive:

    ```tsx theme={null}
    // ❌ Wrong - incorrect capitalization
    config={{
      theme: {
        light: {
          Background: "#FFFFFF", // Should be lowercase
          Primary: "#667eea"      // Should be lowercase
        }
      }
    }}

    // ✅ Correct
    config={{
      theme: {
        light: {
          background: "#FFFFFF",
          primary: "#667eea"
        }
      }
    }}
    ```
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Check if components are inside UnifoldProvider">
    Components must be rendered within the `UnifoldProvider` tree:

    ```tsx theme={null}
    // ❌ Wrong - component outside provider
    <div>
      <UnifoldProvider config={...} />
      <DepositModal /> {/* Won't receive theme */}
    </div>

    // ✅ Correct
    <UnifoldProvider config={...}>
      <DepositModal /> {/* Will receive theme */}
    </UnifoldProvider>
    ```
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

### Issue: Theme not updating when config changes

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Force remount by changing key prop">
    React may not detect config changes. Use a key to force remount:

    ```tsx theme={null}
    const [theme, setTheme] = useState(initialTheme);
    const themeKey = useMemo(() => JSON.stringify(theme), [theme]);

    return (
      <UnifoldProvider
        key={themeKey} // Forces remount on change
        publishableKey="pk_test_..."
        config={{ theme }}
      >
        {children}
      </UnifoldProvider>
    );
    ```
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Ensure config object is memoized">
    Create config outside render or use `useMemo`:

    ```tsx theme={null}
    // ❌ Wrong - new object every render
    function App() {
      return (
        <UnifoldProvider
          config={{
            theme: { light: { primary: "#667eea" } }
          }}
        />
      );
    }

    // ✅ Better - memoized config
    function App() {
      const config = useMemo(() => ({
        theme: { light: { primary: "#667eea" } }
      }), []);

      return <UnifoldProvider config={config} />;
    }
    ```
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

***

## Mode-Specific Issues

### Issue: Dark mode colors not working

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Check appearance setting">
    Ensure `appearance` is set correctly:

    ```tsx theme={null}
    // If you want dark mode
    config={{
      appearance: "dark", // not "darkMode" or "night"
      theme: {
        dark: { /* your dark colors */ }
      }
    }}
    ```
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Verify dark theme is defined">
    Make sure you've defined colors in `theme.dark`:

    ```tsx theme={null}
    // ❌ Wrong - only light theme defined
    config={{
      appearance: "dark",
      theme: {
        light: { primary: "#667eea" }
        // Missing dark!
      }
    }}

    // ✅ Correct
    config={{
      appearance: "dark",
      theme: {
        light: { primary: "#667eea" },
        dark: { primary: "#667eea" }
      }
    }}
    ```
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Test with forced mode instead of auto">
    If using `auto`, temporarily switch to `dark` to isolate the issue:

    ```tsx theme={null}
    // For testing
    config={{
      appearance: "dark", // Force dark mode
      theme: {
        dark: { /* colors */ }
      }
    }}
    ```
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

### Issue: Component tokens not overriding semantic colors

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Check component token structure">
    Ensure you're using the correct nesting for mode-specific tokens:

    ```tsx theme={null}
    // ❌ Wrong - incorrect structure
    config={{
      components: {
        card: {
          light: { titleColor: "#000" }, // Wrong nesting
          dark: { titleColor: "#FFF" }
        }
      }
    }}

    // ✅ Correct
    config={{
      components: {
        light: {
          card: { titleColor: "#000" }
        },
        dark: {
          card: { titleColor: "#FFF" }
        }
      }
    }}
    ```
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Understand the priority system">
    Mode-specific component tokens have highest priority:

    ```tsx theme={null}
    config={{
      theme: {
        light: { foreground: "#000" } // Priority: 3
      },
      components: {
        card: { titleColor: "#333" }, // Priority: 2
        light: {
          card: { titleColor: "#111" } // Priority: 1 (wins!)
        }
      }
    }}
    ```
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

***

## Font Issues

### Issue: Custom font not loading

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Verify font is actually loaded">
    Check browser DevTools Network tab:

    1. Open DevTools (F12)
    2. Go to Network tab
    3. Filter by "Font"
    4. Refresh page
    5. Verify font files load with 200 status

    If fonts aren't loading, check the file path and CORS headers.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Check font-family name matches @font-face">
    Font name in config must match `@font-face` declaration:

    ```css theme={null}
    @font-face {
      font-family: 'MyFont'; /* Must match exactly */
      src: url('/fonts/MyFont.woff2');
    }
    ```

    ```tsx theme={null}
    config={{
      fontFamily: "MyFont, sans-serif" // Exact match
    }}
    ```
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Add fallback fonts">
    Always include system font fallbacks:

    ```tsx theme={null}
    // ❌ No fallback
    fontFamily: "CustomFont"

    // ✅ With fallbacks
    fontFamily: "CustomFont, -apple-system, sans-serif"
    ```
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Use font-display: swap">
    Ensure text is visible while font loads:

    ```css theme={null}
    @font-face {
      font-family: 'Inter';
      src: url('/fonts/Inter.woff2');
      font-display: swap; /* Important! */
    }
    ```
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

### Issue: Google Font not working

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Import font before SDK loads">
    Add Google Fonts link in HTML `<head>`:

    ```html theme={null}
    <head>
      <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
      <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
      <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;600&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
    </head>
    ```
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Use correct font name">
    Check Google Fonts page for the exact family name:

    ```tsx theme={null}
    // ❌ Wrong - incorrect name
    fontFamily: "Inter-Regular, sans-serif"

    // ✅ Correct - just family name
    fontFamily: "Inter, sans-serif"
    ```
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

***

## Color Issues

### Issue: Colors not matching design

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Verify hex color format">
    Ensure colors are valid CSS values:

    ```tsx theme={null}
    // ✅ Valid formats
    primary: "#667eea"
    primary: "#667eeaff" // with alpha
    primary: "rgb(102, 126, 234)"
    primary: "rgba(102, 126, 234, 0.8)"
    primary: "hsl(235, 75%, 66%)"

    // ❌ Invalid
    primary: "667eea" // missing #
    primary: "#ZZZ" // invalid hex
    ```
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Check for typos in property names">
    Property names must be exact:

    ```tsx theme={null}
    // ❌ Wrong - typos
    config={{
      theme: {
        light: {
          primaryColor: "#667eea", // Should be 'primary'
          backgroundColor: "#FFF"   // Should be 'background'
        }
      }
    }}

    // ✅ Correct
    config={{
      theme: {
        light: {
          primary: "#667eea",
          background: "#FFFFFF"
        }
      }
    }}
    ```
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Test with high contrast colors">
    Use very obvious colors to verify theming works:

    ```tsx theme={null}
    // For debugging
    theme: {
      light: {
        background: "#FF0000", // Bright red
        foreground: "#00FF00", // Bright green
        primary: "#0000FF"     // Bright blue
      }
    }
    ```

    If these don't show up, there's a configuration issue.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

### Issue: Insufficient contrast / readability problems

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Check contrast ratios">
    Use a contrast checker tool:

    * [WebAIM Contrast Checker](https://webaim.org/resources/contrastchecker/)
    * Target: 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text

    ```tsx theme={null}
    // ❌ Poor contrast
    background: "#666666"
    foreground: "#777777" // Only 1.3:1 contrast

    // ✅ Good contrast
    background: "#FFFFFF"
    foreground: "#0F172A" // 16.2:1 contrast
    ```
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Test in both modes">
    Colors with good contrast in light mode may fail in dark:

    ```tsx theme={null}
    // Always test both!
    theme: {
      light: {
        background: "#FFFFFF",
        foreground: "#0F172A" // Good contrast
      },
      dark: {
        background: "#0F172A",
        foreground: "#FFFFFF" // Good contrast
      }
    }
    ```
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

***

## TypeScript Issues

### Issue: Type errors with config

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Import types explicitly">
    ```tsx theme={null}
    import type { UnifoldConfig } from '@unifold/connect-react';

    const config: UnifoldConfig = {
      theme: {
        light: {
          primary: "#667eea"
        }
      }
    };
    ```
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Check for typos in property names">
    TypeScript will catch invalid properties:

    ```tsx theme={null}
    const config: UnifoldConfig = {
      theme: {
        light: {
          primaryColor: "#667eea" // ❌ Type error!
          // Property 'primaryColor' does not exist
        }
      }
    };

    // Use correct property name
    const config: UnifoldConfig = {
      theme: {
        light: {
          primary: "#667eea" // ✅ Correct
        }
      }
    };
    ```
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Performance Issues

### Issue: Slow initial render

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Preload custom fonts">
    Use `<link rel="preload">`:

    ```html theme={null}
    <link
      rel="preload"
      href="/fonts/Inter-Regular.woff2"
      as="font"
      type="font/woff2"
      crossorigin
    >
    ```
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Optimize font loading">
    Only load weights you use:

    ```html theme={null}
    <!-- ❌ All weights (slow) -->
    <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@100..900&display=swap">

    <!-- ✅ Only needed weights -->
    <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;600;700&display=swap">
    ```
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Common Error Messages

### "Cannot read property 'background' of undefined"

**Cause:** Theme object structure is incorrect

**Solution:**

```tsx theme={null}
// ❌ Wrong
config={{
  theme: {
    background: "#FFFFFF" // Missing light/dark
  }
}}

// ✅ Correct
config={{
  theme: {
    light: {
      background: "#FFFFFF"
    }
  }
}}
```

### "Invalid color value"

**Cause:** Color format is not valid CSS

**Solution:**

```tsx theme={null}
// ❌ Wrong
primary: "667eea" // Missing #

// ✅ Correct
primary: "#667eea"
```

# Withdraw

> React integration for the Withdraw flow using @unifold/connect-react.

Let users send crypto from your platform to any external wallet using `beginWithdraw()` from the `useUnifold()` hook. Unifold opens a modal for amount and recipient entry; your app signs and broadcasts the resulting transaction with its own wallet infrastructure. For a platform-agnostic overview see [Withdraw Overview](/developer/withdraw/overview).

## Usage

Access `beginWithdraw` from the `useUnifold()` hook. Pass the source token up front — the user picks the destination token and amount inside the modal.

```tsx theme={null}
import { useUnifold, WithdrawEventType } from '@unifold/connect-react';

function WithdrawButton({ userAddress }: { userAddress: string }) {
  const { beginWithdraw } = useUnifold();

  const handleWithdraw = async () => {
    await beginWithdraw({
      externalUserId: 'user_123',
      senderAddress: userAddress,

      // Source token — what the user is sending from
      sourceChainType: 'ethereum',
      sourceChainId: '8453',         // Base
      sourceTokenAddress: '0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913',
      sourceTokenSymbol: 'USDC',

      // Optional: pre-select destination (user can still change)
      defaultDestinationChainType: 'ethereum',
      defaultDestinationChainId: '137',  // Polygon
      defaultDestinationSymbol: 'USDC',

      // Your app signs and broadcasts the transaction
      withdraw: async (txInfo) => {
        // See Withdraw Functions for ready-to-use implementations
      },

      // Recommended: handle lifecycle events the same way you handle webhooks.
      onEvent: (event) => {
        if (event.type === WithdrawEventType.DIRECT_EXECUTION_SUCCEEDED) {
          console.log('Withdraw landed:', event.data.object.transactionHash);
        }
      },

      // Optional — use only if you just need "did it complete?".
      onSuccess: (data) => console.log('Withdrawal complete:', data.executionId),
      onError: (err) => console.error('Withdrawal failed:', err.message),
      onClose: () => console.log('Modal closed'),
    });
  };

  return <button onClick={handleWithdraw}>Withdraw</button>;
}
```

<Tip>
  Prefer `onEvent` unless you only care about the terminal result. It exposes the full lifecycle (including `direct_execution.succeeded`) in the same envelope shape as deposit events and [webhooks](/developer/webhooks/events).
</Tip>

The `withdraw` callback receives a `WithdrawTransactionInfo` with everything needed to construct the on-chain transaction. See [Withdraw Functions](/developer/withdraw/functions) for ready-to-use implementations across Privy, viem/wagmi, and Solana.

For the full `WithdrawConfig`, `WithdrawTransactionInfo`, `WithdrawResult`, and `WithdrawError` type definitions, see the [Withdraw Hook](/developer/withdraw/hook) reference.

<Warning>
  You **must** provide a `withdraw` callback unless your app is purely wallet-connect based. If neither a `withdraw` callback nor a matching connected browser wallet is available, the modal shows an error.
</Warning>

***

# Configuration

Vite configuration, styles, and build setup for Solid JS.

## Styles

The SDK ships two CSS entry points. Pick **one** strategy based on whether your host app uses Tailwind.

| File                                     | When to use                          | Includes                                                            |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@unifold/connect-solid/styles-base.css` | **Plain Vite + Solid** (no Tailwind) | Tailwind Preflight resets, widget utilities, theme variables, fonts |
| `@unifold/connect-solid/styles.css`      | **Solid + Tailwind** host app        | Widget utilities and theme variables only (no Preflight)            |

### Plain Vite + Solid (recommended default)

Import `styles-base.css` once in your entry file:

```tsx theme={null}
// src/index.tsx
import "@unifold/connect-solid/styles-base.css";
import "./app.css";
```

This is the **single import** you need. It includes:

* Button and form resets (transparent backgrounds, normalised inputs)
* Scoped Tailwind variable initialisation inside `[class*="uf-"]` nodes
* All utility classes the deposit widget uses (`uf-flex`, `uf-w-5`, etc.)
* Theme CSS variables and the Sons font family

<Warning>
  Import SDK styles **before** your app CSS. Global `button { … }` rules in your stylesheet can override widget styling if they load later.
</Warning>

The deposit modal renders into `document.body` via a portal. Host CSS cannot target widget internals easily, but global element rules (especially on `button`, `svg`, and `input`) still affect it — another reason to load SDK CSS first and keep host resets minimal.

### Solid + Tailwind host app

If your app already includes Tailwind Preflight (or an equivalent global reset), import **only** `styles.css`:

```tsx theme={null}
// src/index.tsx
import "@unifold/connect-solid/styles.css";
import "./app.css";
```

Do **not** import `styles-base.css` in this setup — Preflight would be applied twice and can conflict with your host Tailwind configuration.

### Styles still look wrong?

Some older `@unifold/connect-solid` releases shipped a `styles-base.css` that included Preflight but not the scoped Tailwind variable initialisation from `styles.css`. In a **plain Vite + Solid app with no Tailwind**, that could cause white button backgrounds, wrong SVG sizing, or missing transforms inside the widget.

**Workaround — import both, in this order:**

```tsx theme={null}
// src/index.tsx
import "@unifold/connect-solid/styles-base.css";
import "@unifold/connect-solid/styles.css";
import "./app.css";
```

* `styles-base.css` → Preflight resets (buttons, inputs, box-sizing)
* `styles.css` → scoped `--tw-*` variable init for widget nodes

Use this dual import **only** in non-Tailwind apps. Do not combine both when your host app already ships Tailwind Preflight.

<Tip>
  Upgrade to the latest `@unifold/connect-solid` to pick up an updated `styles-base.css` that includes both layers. After upgrading, drop the `styles.css` import and keep only `styles-base.css`.
</Tip>

### Troubleshooting styling

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="White button backgrounds or wrong icon sizes">
    Usually means Preflight resets or scoped utility variables are missing. First confirm you import `styles-base.css` (not `styles.css` alone). If problems persist, try the [dual-import workaround](./configuration#styles-still-look-wrong) above.

    Symptom checklist:

    * Close button appears as a white square → missing button reset
    * SVG icons render at wrong size → missing `display: block` / utility variable init
    * Layout looks unstyled → stylesheet not imported or not processed by Vite
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Double resets or broken host layout">
    If your app uses Tailwind and you also import `styles-base.css`, remove the base import and keep only `styles.css`.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Fonts not loading">
    `@unifold/connect-solid` ships font files under `dist/assets/fonts/` alongside the compiled CSS. If you use workspace-linked packages in a monorepo, widen Vite's filesystem allowlist (see below).
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Full Vite config

```ts theme={null}
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import solid from "vite-plugin-solid";
import { fileURLToPath } from "url";

// optional
const solanaStub = fileURLToPath(
  new URL("./src/stubs/solana.js", import.meta.url)
);

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [solid()],
  optimizeDeps: {
    include: ["@unifold/ui-web", "@unifold/connect-solid"],
  },

  resolve: {
      // optional — only if you don't use Solana browser wallets
      alias: {
        "@solana/web3.js": solanaStub,
        "@solana/spl-token": solanaStub,
      },
    },

  server: {
    fs: {
      allow: ["../.."],
    },
  },
});
```

## Solana stubs (optional)

The widget optionally uses `@solana/web3.js` and `@solana/spl-token` for the browser-wallet Solana flow. If your app doesn't use Solana browser wallets, stub these out to avoid installing them:

Create `src/stubs/solana.js`:

```js theme={null}
export default {};
```

Then alias them in Vite (see full config above).

<Info>
  If your app *does* support Solana wallet deposits, install the real packages instead and remove the aliases.
</Info>

## Filesystem access

When using workspace-linked packages (e.g. in a monorepo), Vite's dev server restricts file access to the project root by default. Widen the scope so assets like fonts can be served:

```ts theme={null}
server: {
  fs: {
    allow: ["../.."],
  },
},
```

## SolidStart / SSR

`UnifoldProvider` only loads the widget inside `onMount` (browser-only). During SSR it renders children without initialising the widget.

Wrap your root layout the same way as a plain Vite entry file — provider plus style imports at the top of the layout module (exact file name depends on your SolidStart version, e.g. `src/app.tsx` or a root route layout):

```tsx theme={null}
import { UnifoldProvider } from "@unifold/connect-solid";
import "@unifold/connect-solid/styles-base.css";
import type { ParentProps } from "solid-js";

const publishableKey = import.meta.env.VITE_UNIFOLD_PUBLISHABLE_KEY ?? "";

export default function RootLayout(props: ParentProps) {
  return (
    <UnifoldProvider publishableKey={publishableKey} config={{ appearance: "dark" }}>
      {props.children}
    </UnifoldProvider>
  );
}
```

If you hit bundler errors during SSR, the provider already defers `@unifold/ui-web` to `onMount` — ensure you are not importing the web runtime in server-only code paths.

## Environment variables

| Variable                       | Description                  | Example          |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `VITE_UNIFOLD_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | Your Unifold publishable key | `pk_test_abc123` |

Create a `.env.example` for your team:

```bash theme={null}
VITE_UNIFOLD_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=pk_test_your_key_here
```

# Overview

> Integrate crypto deposits and fiat on-ramp into your Solid JS web app.

The `@unifold/connect-solid` package is a native Solid SDK for the Unifold deposit widget. Wrap your app with `<UnifoldProvider>`, call `useUnifold().beginDeposit()`, and the full deposit UI opens as a modal.

## Features

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Crypto deposits" icon="wallet">
    Transfer crypto via QR code or address copy
  </Card>

  <Card title="Fiat on-ramp" icon="credit-card">
    Deposit with card via integrated on-ramp providers
  </Card>

  <Card title="Multi-chain support" icon="link">
    Ethereum, Polygon, Solana, Bitcoin, and more
  </Card>

  <Card title="Customizable UI" icon="palette">
    Light and dark mode with shared theme `config` options
  </Card>

  <Card title="Browser wallet" icon="plug">
    Optional browser wallet connection for direct deposits
  </Card>

  <Card title="Solid-native API" icon="braces">
    Context provider and `useUnifold()` hook — no React in your app code
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

## How it works

1. **Install** `@unifold/connect-solid` and set up a Vite + Solid app
2. **Import styles** once in your entry file (`styles-base.css` for plain Vite, or `styles.css` if your app already uses Tailwind Preflight)
3. **Wrap your app** with `<UnifoldProvider>` and your publishable key
4. **Call `beginDeposit()`** from any child component via `useUnifold()`

The widget runtime loads in the browser inside `onMount` and renders into `document.body`. Your Solid tree only holds the provider shell until a deposit is opened.
