# Quickstart

Add the Unifold deposit widget to a Solid JS app in under 5 minutes.

The `@unifold/connect-solid` package is a native Solid SDK for the Unifold deposit widget. It provides idiomatic Solid APIs — a context-based provider and the `useUnifold()` hook — so the widget feels like a first-class part of your app.

## Prerequisites

Before you begin, create a Unifold project and copy your publishable key from the [Unifold Dashboard](https://dashboard.unifold.io).

* **Solid JS** 1.6+ with **Vite** (or SolidStart)
* **Publishable key** starting with `pk_test_` or `pk_live_`

## Installation

Install the SDK and the packages needed for a Vite + Solid app:

<CodeGroup>
  ```bash npm theme={null}
  npm install @unifold/connect-solid solid-js
  npm install -D vite vite-plugin-solid typescript
  ```

  ```bash pnpm theme={null}
  pnpm add @unifold/connect-solid solid-js
  pnpm add -D vite vite-plugin-solid typescript
  ```

  ```bash yarn theme={null}
  yarn add @unifold/connect-solid solid-js
  yarn add -D vite vite-plugin-solid typescript
  ```
</CodeGroup>

<Info>
  `@unifold/connect-solid` lists `solid-js` as a peer dependency. `vite-plugin-solid` is required to compile JSX in your app (the SDK ships pre-built JS for its own components).
</Info>

## 1. Configure environment variables

Create a `.env` file in your project root:

```bash theme={null}
VITE_UNIFOLD_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=pk_test_your_key_here
```

| Variable                       | Description                                                                |
| ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `VITE_UNIFOLD_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | Your Unifold publishable key, exposed to the client via `import.meta.env`. |

<Warning>
  Get your key from the [Unifold Dashboard](https://dashboard.unifold.io). Use `pk_test_...` for development.
</Warning>

## 2. Import styles

Import the SDK stylesheet **once** in your entry file, before your app CSS.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Plain Vite + Solid (no Tailwind)">
    Use a single import of `styles-base.css`. It includes Tailwind Preflight resets and all widget utilities:

    ```tsx theme={null}
    // src/index.tsx
    import "@unifold/connect-solid/styles-base.css";
    import "./app.css";
    ```

    <Warning>
      On current SDK versions, `styles-base.css` alone is enough. If styling looks off on an older release, see [Styles still look wrong?](./configuration#styles-still-look-wrong).
    </Warning>
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Solid + Tailwind host app">
    If your app already ships Tailwind Preflight (or your own global reset), import **only** `styles.css`:

    ```tsx theme={null}
    // src/index.tsx
    import "@unifold/connect-solid/styles.css";
    import "./app.css";
    ```

    <Warning>
      Do **not** import `styles-base.css` when your host app already applies Preflight — duplicate resets can cause layout conflicts.
    </Warning>
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

See the [Styles](./configuration#styles) section for a full comparison and troubleshooting tips.

## 3. Add the provider

Wrap your app with `<UnifoldProvider>` in your entry file. This initialises the SDK once and makes it available to child components via Solid context.

```tsx theme={null}
// src/index.tsx
import { render } from "solid-js/web";
import { UnifoldProvider } from "@unifold/connect-solid";
import "@unifold/connect-solid/styles-base.css";
import "./app.css";
import { App } from "./App";

const publishableKey =
  import.meta.env.VITE_UNIFOLD_PUBLISHABLE_KEY ?? "pk_test_your_key_here";

render(
  () => (
    <UnifoldProvider publishableKey={publishableKey} config={{ appearance: "dark" }}>
      <App />
    </UnifoldProvider>
  ),
  document.getElementById("root")!
);
```

## 4. Open a deposit

Use `useUnifold()` in any child component to access the deposit API:

```tsx theme={null}
// src/App.tsx
import { createSignal, Show } from "solid-js";
import { useUnifold } from "@unifold/connect-solid";
import type { DepositResult, DepositError } from "@unifold/connect-solid";

export function App() {
  const unifold = useUnifold();

  const [status, setStatus] = createSignal<"idle" | "loading" | "success" | "error">("idle");
  const [result, setResult] = createSignal<DepositResult | null>(null);
  const [error, setError] = createSignal<DepositError | null>(null);

  async function openDeposit() {
    setStatus("loading");
    setResult(null);
    setError(null);

    try {
      const depositResult = await unifold.beginDeposit({
        externalUserId: "user_123",
        destinationChainType: "ethereum",
        destinationChainId: "42161",
        destinationTokenAddress: "0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831",
        destinationTokenSymbol: "USDC",
        recipientAddress: "0x309a4154a2CD4153Da886E780890C9cb5161553C",
      });

      setResult(depositResult);
      setStatus("success");
    } catch (err) {
      const depositError = err as DepositError;
      setError(depositError);
      setStatus(depositError?.code === "DEPOSIT_CANCELLED" ? "idle" : "error");
    }
  }

  return (
    <main>
      <button onClick={openDeposit} disabled={status() === "loading"}>
        {status() === "loading" ? "Opening..." : "Deposit Funds"}
      </button>

      <Show when={status() === "success" && result()}>
        <pre>{JSON.stringify(result(), null, 2)}</pre>
      </Show>
      <Show when={status() === "error" && error()}>
        <pre>{JSON.stringify(error(), null, 2)}</pre>
      </Show>
    </main>
  );
}
```

That's it — clicking the button opens the Unifold deposit modal. The promise resolves when the deposit completes, or rejects if the user cancels or an error occurs.

<Tip>
  See the [Configuration](./configuration) page for optional Vite settings (Solana stubs, monorepo filesystem access).
</Tip>

# Reference

Provider props, hooks, and types for `@unifold/connect-solid`.

Everything exported from `@unifold/connect-solid`.

## UnifoldProvider

A Solid component that initialises the deposit widget and provides it to child components via Solid context.

```tsx theme={null}
import { UnifoldProvider } from "@unifold/connect-solid";

<UnifoldProvider publishableKey="pk_test_..." config={{ appearance: "dark" }}>
  <App />
</UnifoldProvider>
```

### Props

<ParamField path="publishableKey" type="string" required>
  Your Unifold publishable key. Starts with `pk_test_` (sandbox) or `pk_live_` (production).
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="config" type="UnifoldConfig">
  Optional configuration object controlling appearance and behaviour. The Solid provider forwards this to `@unifold/ui-web`, which uses the same options as `@unifold/connect-react` (see [React Provider](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/provider) for the full list).

  <Expandable title="UnifoldConfig properties">
    <ParamField path="appearance" type="'light' | 'dark' | 'auto'" default="'dark'">
      Theme appearance mode. `'auto'` follows system preference.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="modalTitle" type="string">
      Custom title shown in the deposit modal header.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="hideDepositTracker" type="boolean">
      Hide the deposit tracker UI.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="transferCryptoTitle" type="string">
      Overrides the **Transfer Crypto** row title on the main deposit menu.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="depositWithCardTitle" type="string">
      Overrides the **Deposit with Card** row title.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="payWithExchangeTitle" type="string">
      Overrides the **Pay with Exchange** row title.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="depositTrackerTitle" type="string">
      Overrides the **Deposit Tracker** row title.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="depositTrackerSubTitle" type="string">
      Overrides the subtitle under **Deposit Tracker** on the main menu.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="hideDepositFlowInfo" type="boolean" default="false">
      On **Deposit with Card**, hides the You use / You buy / You receive summary card.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="hideDisplayDescription" type="boolean" default="false">
      On the onramp step, hides the temporary deposit address disclaimer.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="showBalanceHeader" type="boolean" default="true">
      Show the balance in the deposit modal header.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="transferInputVariant" type="'single_input' | 'double_input'" default="'double_input'">
      Layout variant for the transfer amount input.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="enableConnectWallet" type="boolean" default="false">
      Enable the browser wallet connection option.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="enableFiatOnramp" type="boolean">
      Enable **Deposit with Card**. Defaults to your dashboard setting.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="enablePayWithExchange" type="boolean">
      Enable **Pay with Exchange**. Defaults to your dashboard setting.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="enableConnectExchange" type="boolean" default="false">
      Enable direct Coinbase Connect integration.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="enableCashApp" type="boolean" default="false">
      Enable **Pay with Cash App**.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="browserWalletAmountQuickSelect" type="'percentage' | 'usd'" default="'percentage'">
      Quick-select chips on the Connect Wallet amount step.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="accentColor" type="string">
      Simple accent colour override for both light and dark modes.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="theme" type="ThemeConfig">
      Full theme colour customisation per mode. See [Svelte Semantic Colors](/get-started/sdk-reference/svelte/ui-customization/semantic-colors).
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="fontFamily" type="string">
      Single font family for all widget text. Your app must load the font.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="fonts" type="FontConfig">
      Granular font family configuration for different weights.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="components" type="ComponentConfig">
      Component-specific token overrides.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="defaultInitialScreen" type="'main' | 'transfer' | 'card' | 'tracker'">
      Default first screen for `beginDeposit()` when the call omits `initialScreen`. See [Standalone entry screens](/developer/deposit/entry-screens).
    </ParamField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="children" type="JSX.Element">
  Child components that can call `useUnifold()`.
</ParamField>

### Lifecycle

1. During SSR (SolidStart), `UnifoldProvider` renders its children immediately — no widget is loaded server-side.
2. On mount (browser only), it dynamically imports `@unifold/ui-web` and initialises the widget.
3. Any `beginDeposit()` calls made before initialisation completes await the ready promise automatically.
4. On cleanup, open deposits are closed, the widget is destroyed, and resources are freed.

***

## useUnifold

Returns the Unifold context from the nearest `<UnifoldProvider>`. Must be called inside a component that is a descendant of `<UnifoldProvider>`.

```tsx theme={null}
import { useUnifold } from "@unifold/connect-solid";

function DepositButton() {
  const unifold = useUnifold();
  // ...
}
```

<Warning>
  Calling `useUnifold()` outside of a `<UnifoldProvider>` tree throws:
  `"useUnifold() must be called inside a component wrapped by <UnifoldProvider>"`
</Warning>

***

## UnifoldContextValue

The object returned by `useUnifold()`.

### beginDeposit

Opens the deposit modal and returns a promise that resolves when the deposit completes.

```ts theme={null}
beginDeposit(config: DepositConfig): Promise<DepositResult>
```

The promise rejects with a `DepositError` if the user cancels or an error occurs.

```tsx theme={null}
const unifold = useUnifold();

async function deposit() {
  try {
    const result = await unifold.beginDeposit({
      externalUserId: "user_123",
      destinationChainType: "ethereum",
      destinationChainId: "42161",
      destinationTokenAddress: "0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831",
      destinationTokenSymbol: "USDC",
      recipientAddress: "0x309a4154a2CD4153Da886E780890C9cb5161553C",
    });
    console.log("Success:", result.message);
  } catch (err) {
    const error = err as DepositError;
    if (error.code === "DEPOSIT_CANCELLED") {
      console.log("User cancelled");
    } else {
      console.error("Deposit failed:", error.message);
    }
  }
}
```

### closeDeposit

Programmatically closes the deposit modal if it is open. No-ops silently if the modal is not open or the provider has unmounted.

```ts theme={null}
closeDeposit(): void
```

***

## Styles exports

Import one strategy from [Configuration — Styles](./configuration#styles):

```tsx theme={null}
// Plain Vite + Solid (no Tailwind) — current SDK
import "@unifold/connect-solid/styles-base.css";

// Solid + Tailwind host app
import "@unifold/connect-solid/styles.css";
```

If styling is broken on an older release in a non-Tailwind app, import **both** (base first, then styles). See [Styles still look wrong?](./configuration#styles-still-look-wrong).

***

## Types

All types are re-exported from `@unifold/connect-solid` for convenience.

### DepositConfig

Configuration passed to `beginDeposit()`.

<ParamField path="externalUserId" type="string" required>
  Your app's user identifier.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="destinationChainType" type="ChainType" required>
  Target blockchain type.

  ```ts theme={null}
  type ChainType = "ethereum" | "solana" | "bitcoin" | "algorand" | "xrpl" | "cardano"
  ```
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="destinationChainId" type="string" required>
  Target chain ID. For example, `"42161"` for Arbitrum, `"1"` for Ethereum mainnet.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="destinationTokenAddress" type="string" required>
  Contract address of the destination token.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="destinationTokenSymbol" type="string" required>
  Symbol of the destination token (e.g. `"USDC"`, `"ETH"`).
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="recipientAddress" type="string" required>
  Wallet address that receives the deposited tokens.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="depositConfirmationMode" type="DepositConfirmationMode" default="'auto_ui'">
  How the deposit is confirmed after the on-chain transaction.

  ```ts theme={null}
  type DepositConfirmationMode = "auto_ui" | "auto_silent" | "manual"
  ```
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onSuccess" type="(data: DepositResult) => void">
  Optional callback fired when the deposit succeeds, before the promise resolves.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onError" type="(error: DepositError) => void">
  Optional callback fired when the deposit fails, before the promise rejects.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onClose" type="() => void">
  Optional callback when the user dismisses the dialog.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="initialScreen" type="'main' | 'transfer' | 'card' | 'tracker'">
  First screen when the modal opens. See [Standalone entry screens](/developer/deposit/entry-screens).
</ParamField>

### DepositResult

```ts theme={null}
interface DepositResult {
  message: string;
  transaction?: unknown;
  executionId?: string;
}
```

### DepositError

```ts theme={null}
interface DepositError {
  message: string;
  error?: unknown;
  code?: string;
}
```

| `code`                | Meaning                                             |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `"DEPOSIT_CANCELLED"` | User closed the modal without completing a deposit. |

# Configuration

Vite configuration, SSR handling, and build setup for SvelteKit.

Because SvelteKit uses Vite and supports SSR, a few build-time settings are required so the Unifold SDK bundles and renders correctly.

## Full Vite config

```ts theme={null}
// vite.config.ts
import { sveltekit } from "@sveltejs/kit/vite";
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import { fileURLToPath } from "url";

// optional
const solanaStub = fileURLToPath(
  new URL("./src/stubs/solana.js", import.meta.url)
);

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [sveltekit()],

  resolve: {
    // optional
    alias: {
      "@solana/web3.js": solanaStub,
      "@solana/spl-token": solanaStub,
    },
    dedupe: ["react", "react-dom", "react/jsx-runtime"],
  },

  server: {
    fs: {
      allow: ["../.."],
    },
  },

  ssr: {
    noExternal: ["@unifold/connect-svelte"],
    external: ["@unifold/ui-web"],
  },
});
```

Each section is explained below.

## Internal dependency deduplication

`@unifold/ui-web` bundles its own internal rendering engine. In some monorepo setups, Vite may resolve duplicate copies of internal libraries, causing runtime errors. Adding a `dedupe` rule prevents this:

```ts theme={null}
resolve: {
  dedupe: ["react", "react-dom", "react/jsx-runtime"],
},
```

<Info>
  You don't need to install these packages yourself — they're bundled inside `@unifold/ui-web`. This setting only affects how Vite resolves them at dev time.
</Info>

## SSR settings

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="noExternal: @unifold/connect-svelte">
    Svelte packages contain `.svelte` files that must be compiled by Vite. Marking the package as `noExternal` ensures the SSR build processes it through the Svelte compiler instead of treating it as a pre-built Node module.

    ```ts theme={null}
    ssr: {
      noExternal: ["@unifold/connect-svelte"],
    }
    ```
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="external: @unifold/ui-web">
    `@unifold/ui-web` is browser-only — it requires a DOM to render the deposit widget. The Svelte SDK only imports it inside `onMount` (which never fires during SSR), but Vite's SSR bundler still tries to resolve it statically. Marking it as `external` tells Vite to skip it during SSR.

    ```ts theme={null}
    ssr: {
      external: ["@unifold/ui-web"],
    }
    ```
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Solana stubs (optional)

The widget optionally uses `@solana/web3.js` and `@solana/spl-token` for the browser-wallet Solana flow. If your app doesn't use Solana browser wallets, you can stub these out to avoid installing them:

Create `src/stubs/solana.js`:

```js theme={null}
export default {};
```

Then alias them in Vite:

```ts theme={null}
resolve: {
  alias: {
    "@solana/web3.js": solanaStub,
    "@solana/spl-token": solanaStub,
  },
},
```

<Info>
  If your app *does* support Solana wallet deposits, install the real packages instead and remove the aliases.
</Info>

## Filesystem access

When using workspace-linked packages (e.g. in a monorepo), Vite's dev server restricts file access to the project root by default. Widen the scope so assets like fonts can be served:

```ts theme={null}
server: {
  fs: {
    allow: ["../.."],
  },
},
```

## Styles

Import `styles-base.css` once in your root layout. This stylesheet includes baseline resets that the widget's components depend on:

```svelte theme={null}
<script>
  import "@unifold/connect-svelte/styles-base.css";
</script>
```

<Warning>
  Use `styles-base.css`, not `styles.css`. The base variant includes box-sizing and form-element resets needed for Svelte apps. `styles.css` is intended for apps that already include their own CSS reset.
</Warning>

## Environment variables

| Variable             | Description                  | Example          |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `PUBLIC_UNIFOLD_KEY` | Your Unifold publishable key | `pk_test_abc123` |

Create a `.env.example` for your team:

```bash theme={null}
PUBLIC_UNIFOLD_KEY=pk_test_your_key_here
```

### Deposit Implementation

Shows a complete deposit flow with state management:

```svelte title="src/routes/+page.svelte" theme={null}
<script lang="ts">
  import { useUnifold } from '@unifold/connect-svelte';
  
  const { beginDeposit } = useUnifold();
  let status = 'idle';
  let message = '';

  async function handleDeposit() {
    status = 'loading';
    
    try {
      const result = await beginDeposit({
        userId: 'user_123',
        destinationChainId: '137',
        destinationTokenAddress: '0x2791bca1f2de4661ed88a30c99a7a9449aa84174',
        destinationTokenSymbol: 'USDC',
        recipientAddress: '0x606C49ca2Fa4982F07016265040F777eD3DA3160',
      });
      
      status = 'success';
      message = result.message;
    } catch (error) {
      status = 'error';
      message = error.message;
    }
  }
</script>

<button on:click={handleDeposit} disabled={status === 'loading'}>
  {status === 'loading' ? 'Processing...' : 'Deposit'}
</button>

{#if status === 'success'}
  <div class="success">✅ {message}</div>
{/if}

{#if status === 'error'}
  <div class="error">❌ {message}</div>
{/if}
```

## Troubleshooting

### Environment Variable Not Loading

Make sure your `.env` file is in the project root and the variable starts with `PUBLIC_`:

```bash theme={null}
# ✅ Correct
PUBLIC_UNIFOLD_KEY=pk_test_...

# ❌ Wrong (won't be exposed to browser)
UNIFOLD_KEY=pk_test_...
```

### Module Not Found

If you see import errors, ensure dependencies are installed:

```bash theme={null}
rm -rf node_modules package-lock.json
npm install
```

### Port Already in Use

Change the port in `vite.config.ts`:

```typescript theme={null}
export default defineConfig({
  server: {
    port: 3000
  }
});
```

# Quickstart

Add the Unifold deposit widget to a SvelteKit app in under 5 minutes.

The `@unifold/connect-svelte` package is a native Svelte SDK for the Unifold deposit widget. It provides idiomatic Svelte APIs — context-based provider, reactive state — so the widget feels like a first-class part of your app.

## Prerequisites

* SvelteKit 2+ with Svelte 4 or 5
* A Unifold publishable key (starts with `pk_test_` or `pk_live_`)

## Installation

```bash theme={null}
npm install @unifold/connect-svelte
```

<CodeGroup>
  ```bash npm theme={null}
  npm install @unifold/connect-svelte
  ```

  ```bash pnpm theme={null}
  pnpm add @unifold/connect-svelte
  ```

  ```bash yarn theme={null}
  yarn add @unifold/connect-svelte
  ```
</CodeGroup>

## 1. Configure environment variables

Create a `.env` file in your SvelteKit project root:

```bash theme={null}
PUBLIC_UNIFOLD_KEY=pk_test_your_key_here
```

<Info>
  SvelteKit exposes env vars prefixed with `PUBLIC_` to the client via `$env/static/public`.
</Info>

## 2. Add the provider

Wrap your app with `<UnifoldProvider>` in your root layout. This initialises the SDK once and makes it available to all child components via Svelte context.

```svelte theme={null}
<!-- src/routes/+layout.svelte -->
<script lang="ts">
  import { UnifoldProvider } from "@unifold/connect-svelte";
  import { PUBLIC_UNIFOLD_KEY } from "$env/static/public";
  import "@unifold/connect-svelte/styles-base.css";

  const publishableKey = PUBLIC_UNIFOLD_KEY;
</script>

<UnifoldProvider
  {publishableKey}
  config={{
    appearance: "dark",
  }}
>
  <slot />
</UnifoldProvider>
```

<Warning>
  The `styles-base.css` import is required. It includes baseline resets (box-sizing, button/input normalisation) that the widget depends on.
</Warning>

## 3. Open a deposit

Use `getUnifold()` in any child component to access the deposit API:

```svelte theme={null}
<!-- src/routes/+page.svelte -->
<script lang="ts">
  import { getUnifold } from "@unifold/connect-svelte";
  import type { DepositResult, DepositError } from "@unifold/connect-svelte";

  const unifold = getUnifold();

  let status: "idle" | "loading" | "success" | "error" = "idle";
  let result: DepositResult | null = null;
  let error: DepositError | null = null;

  async function openDeposit() {
    status = "loading";
    result = null;
    error = null;

    try {
      const depositResult = await unifold.beginDeposit({
        externalUserId: "user_123",
        destinationChainType: "ethereum",
        destinationChainId: "42161",
        destinationTokenAddress: "0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831",
        destinationTokenSymbol: "USDC",
        recipientAddress: "0x309a4154a2CD4153Da886E780890C9cb5161553C",
      });

      result = depositResult;
      status = "success";
    } catch (err) {
      error = err as DepositError;
      status =
        (err as DepositError)?.code === "DEPOSIT_CANCELLED" ? "idle" : "error";
    }
  }
</script>

<button on:click={openDeposit} disabled={status === "loading"}>
  {status === "loading" ? "Opening..." : "Deposit Funds"}
</button>

{#if status === "success" && result}
  <p>Deposit complete: {result.message}</p>
{/if}

{#if status === "error" && error}
  <p>Error: {error.message}</p>
{/if}
```

That's it — clicking the button opens the Unifold deposit modal. The promise resolves when the deposit completes, or rejects if the user cancels or an error occurs.

## 4. Configure Vite

SvelteKit uses Vite under the hood. A few settings are needed so the SDK bundles correctly:

```ts theme={null}
// vite.config.ts
import { sveltekit } from "@sveltejs/kit/vite";
import { defineConfig } from "vite";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [sveltekit()],
  ssr: {
    noExternal: ["@unifold/connect-svelte"],
    external: ["@unifold/ui-web"],
  },
});
```

<Tip>
  See the [Configuration](./configuration) page for a full explanation of each Vite option and optional Solana stub setup.
</Tip>

# Reference

Provider props, context methods, and types for @unifold/connect-svelte

Everything exported from `@unifold/connect-svelte`.

## UnifoldProvider

A Svelte component that initialises the deposit widget and provides it to child components via Svelte context.

```svelte theme={null}
<script>
  import { UnifoldProvider } from "@unifold/connect-svelte";
</script>

<UnifoldProvider publishableKey="pk_test_..." config={{ appearance: "dark" }}>
  <slot />
</UnifoldProvider>
```

### Props

<ParamField path="publishableKey" type="string" required>
  Your Unifold publishable key. Starts with `pk_test_` (sandbox) or `pk_live_` (production).
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="config" type="UnifoldConfig">
  Optional configuration object controlling appearance and behaviour. The Svelte provider forwards this to `@unifold/ui-web`, which uses the same options as `@unifold/connect-react` (see [React Provider](/get-started/sdk-reference/react/provider) for the full list).

  <Expandable title="UnifoldConfig properties">
    <ParamField path="appearance" type="'light' | 'dark' | 'auto'" default="'dark'">
      Theme appearance mode. `'auto'` follows system preference.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="modalTitle" type="string">
      Custom title shown in the deposit modal header.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="hideDepositTracker" type="boolean">
      Hide the deposit tracker UI.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="transferCryptoTitle" type="string">
      Overrides the **Transfer Crypto** row title on the main deposit menu (and the Transfer Crypto flow header). Omit for the default locale string (e.g. `"Transfer Crypto"` in English).
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="depositWithCardTitle" type="string">
      Overrides the **Deposit with Card** row title (and the card flow header when not on the quotes step). Default locale string is `"Deposit with Card"` in English.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="payWithExchangeTitle" type="string">
      Overrides the **Pay with Exchange** row title (and the exchange flow header). Default locale string is `"Pay with Exchange"` in English.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="depositTrackerTitle" type="string">
      Overrides the **Deposit Tracker** row title on the main menu and the tracker list header. Default locale string is `"Deposit Tracker"` in English.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="depositTrackerSubTitle" type="string">
      Overrides the subtitle (description line) under **Deposit Tracker** on the main menu. Default locale string is `"Track your deposit progress"` in English.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="hideDepositFlowInfo" type="boolean" default="false">
      On **Deposit with Card**, after the user picks a provider (“Complete transaction with …”), hides the summary card that shows **You use → You buy → You receive**.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="hideDisplayDescription" type="boolean" default="false">
      On the same onramp step, hides the informational note that the wallet address shown in the payment provider is a temporary deposit address.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="showBalanceHeader" type="boolean" default="true">
      Show the balance in the deposit modal header.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="transferInputVariant" type="'single_input' | 'double_input'" default="'double_input'">
      Layout variant for the transfer amount input.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="enableConnectWallet" type="boolean" default="false">
      Enable the browser wallet connection option.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="browserWalletAmountQuickSelect" type="'percentage' | 'usd'" default="'percentage'">
      Controls the quick-select amount pills on the Connect Wallet "Enter amount" step.

      * `'percentage'`: Percentage-of-balance chips — 10 %, 25 %, 50 %, 75 %, MAX (default)
      * `'usd'`: Fixed USD amount chips — $25, $50, $100, $250, \$500
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="enablePayWithExchange" type="boolean">
      Enable the "Pay with Exchange" option. Defaults to your dashboard setting.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="accentColor" type="string">
      Simple accent/primary colour override applied to both light and dark modes. Accepts any CSS colour value.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="theme" type="ThemeConfig">
      Full theme colour customisation per mode. See [Semantic Colors](./ui-customization/semantic-colors).
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="fontFamily" type="string">
      Single font family for all text. The host app must load the font.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="fonts" type="FontConfig">
      Granular font family configuration for different weights.
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="components" type="ComponentConfig">
      Component-specific token overrides. See [Component Tokens](./ui-customization/component-tokens).
    </ParamField>

    <ParamField path="defaultInitialScreen" type="'main' | 'transfer' | 'card' | 'tracker'">
      Default first screen for `beginDeposit()` when the call omits `initialScreen`. See [Standalone entry screens](/developer/deposit/entry-screens).
    </ParamField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>

### Lifecycle

1. During SSR, `UnifoldProvider` renders its `<slot />` immediately — no widget is loaded server-side.
2. On mount (browser only), it dynamically imports the widget runtime and initialises it.
3. Any `beginDeposit()` calls made before initialisation completes will await the ready promise automatically.
4. On destroy, the widget is torn down and all resources are cleaned up.

***

## getUnifold

Returns the `UnifoldContext` from the nearest `<UnifoldProvider>`. Must be called during component initialisation (top-level `<script>`) inside a descendant of `<UnifoldProvider>`.

```svelte theme={null}
<script>
  import { getUnifold } from "@unifold/connect-svelte";

  const unifold = getUnifold();
</script>
```

<Warning>
  Calling `getUnifold()` outside of a `<UnifoldProvider>` tree throws:
  `"getUnifold() must be called inside a component wrapped by <UnifoldProvider>"`
</Warning>

***

## UnifoldContext

The object returned by `getUnifold()`.

### beginDeposit

Opens the deposit modal and returns a promise that resolves when the deposit completes.

```ts theme={null}
beginDeposit(config: DepositConfig): Promise<DepositResult>
```

The promise rejects with a `DepositError` if the user cancels or an error occurs.

```svelte theme={null}
<script>
  const unifold = getUnifold();

  async function deposit() {
    try {
      const result = await unifold.beginDeposit({
        externalUserId: "user_123",
        destinationChainType: "ethereum",
        destinationChainId: "42161",
        destinationTokenAddress: "0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831",
        destinationTokenSymbol: "USDC",
        recipientAddress: "0x309a4154a2CD4153Da886E780890C9cb5161553C",
      });
      console.log("Success:", result.message);
    } catch (err) {
      if (err.code === "DEPOSIT_CANCELLED") {
        console.log("User cancelled");
      } else {
        console.error("Deposit failed:", err.message);
      }
    }
  }
</script>
```

### closeDeposit

Programmatically closes the deposit modal if it is open. No-ops silently if the modal is not open or the instance has been destroyed.

```ts theme={null}
closeDeposit(): void
```

***

## Types

All types are re-exported from `@unifold/connect-svelte` for convenience.

### DepositConfig

Configuration passed to `beginDeposit()`.

<ParamField path="externalUserId" type="string" required>
  Your app's user identifier.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="destinationChainType" type="ChainType" required>
  Target blockchain type.

  ```ts theme={null}
  type ChainType = "ethereum" | "solana" | "bitcoin" | "algorand" | "xrpl" | "cardano"
  ```
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="destinationChainId" type="string" required>
  Target chain ID. For example, `"42161"` for Arbitrum, `"1"` for Ethereum mainnet.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="destinationTokenAddress" type="string" required>
  Contract address of the destination token.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="destinationTokenSymbol" type="string" required>
  Symbol of the destination token (e.g. `"USDC"`, `"ETH"`).
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="recipientAddress" type="string" required>
  Wallet address that receives the deposited tokens.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="depositConfirmationMode" type="DepositConfirmationMode" default="'auto_ui'">
  How the deposit is confirmed after the on-chain transaction.

  ```ts theme={null}
  type DepositConfirmationMode = "auto_ui" | "auto_silent" | "manual"
  ```

  | Mode          | Behaviour                                       |
  | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
  | `auto_ui`     | Automatically confirms and shows a success UI.  |
  | `auto_silent` | Automatically confirms without UI feedback.     |
  | `manual`      | Waits for your app to confirm programmatically. |
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onSuccess" type="(data: DepositResult) => void">
  Optional callback fired immediately when the deposit succeeds, before the promise resolves.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onError" type="(error: DepositError) => void">
  Optional callback fired immediately when the deposit fails, before the promise rejects.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="onClose" type="() => void">
  Optional callback when the user dismisses the dialog (close button, Escape, or `closeDeposit()`).
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="initialScreen" type="'main' | 'transfer' | 'card' | 'tracker'">
  First screen when the modal opens. Defaults to `main` (deposit menu). See [Standalone entry screens](/developer/deposit/entry-screens).
</ParamField>

### DepositResult

Returned when a deposit completes successfully.

```ts theme={null}
interface DepositResult {
  message: string;
  transaction?: unknown;
  executionId?: string;
}
```

| Field         | Description                                    |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `message`     | Human-readable success message.                |
| `transaction` | Raw transaction data (shape depends on chain). |
| `executionId` | Unique identifier for the deposit execution.   |

### DepositError

Returned when a deposit fails or is cancelled.

```ts theme={null}
interface DepositError {
  message: string;
  error?: unknown;
  code?: string;
}
```

| Field     | Description                                                                     |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `message` | Human-readable error message.                                                   |
| `error`   | Underlying error object, if available.                                          |
| `code`    | Machine-readable error code. `"DEPOSIT_CANCELLED"` indicates user cancellation. |

***

# Component Tokens

> Granular control over individual component properties for precise customization

Component tokens provide fine-grained control over specific UI elements. Use them when you need precise customization beyond what semantic colors offer.

## Configuration Structure

Component tokens can be configured in three ways:

1. **Flat (Universal)** — Applies to both light and dark modes
2. **Light Mode Specific** — Overrides flat tokens in light mode
3. **Dark Mode Specific** — Overrides flat tokens in dark mode

```svelte theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey={PUBLIC_UNIFOLD_KEY}
  config={{
    components: {
      // Flat — applies to BOTH modes (lowest priority)
      card: {
        backgroundColor: "#F5F5F5",
        titleColor: "#000000",
        borderRadius: 16,
      },

      // Mode-specific overrides (higher priority)
      light: {
        card: {
          backgroundColor: "#FFFFFF",
          titleColor: "#0F172A",
        }
      },
      dark: {
        card: {
          backgroundColor: "#292929",
          titleColor: "#F8FAFC",
        }
      }
    }
  }}
>
  <slot />
</UnifoldProvider>
```

## Priority System

When resolving component token values, the SDK follows this priority order:

1. **Mode-specific token** (`components.light.card.titleColor`)
2. **Flat token** (`components.card.titleColor`)
3. **Semantic theme color** (`theme.light.foreground`)
4. **Built-in default**

<Tip>
  Use **flat tokens** for properties that should be the same in both modes (like border radius), and **mode-specific tokens** only when you need different values for light vs dark.
</Tip>

## Available Component Categories

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Header" icon="heading" href="#header-tokens">
    Navigation and header elements (2 properties)
  </Card>

  <Card title="Card" icon="square" href="#card-tokens">

## Header Tokens

Controls navigation and header elements.

<ParamField path="header.titleColor" type="string">
  Color for header title text.

  **Falls back to:** `theme.*.foreground`
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="header.buttonColor" type="string">

  **Falls back to:** `theme.*.foreground`
</ParamField>

```ts theme={null}
  }
}
```

## Complete Example

Here's a full example combining all component tokens in a SvelteKit layout:

```svelte theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey={PUBLIC_UNIFOLD_KEY}
  config={{
    components: {
      // Flat tokens (apply to both modes) — great for shape properties
      card: { borderRadius: 16, borderWidth: 1 },
      button: { borderRadius: 8 },
      input: { borderRadius: 8, borderWidth: 1 },
      container: { borderRadius: 20 },
      list: { rowBorderRadius: 8 },

      // Light mode specific
      light: {
        header: {
          titleColor: "#0F172A",
          buttonColor: "#64748B",
        },
        card: {
          backgroundColor: "#FFFFFF",
          titleColor: "#0F172A",
          subtitleColor: "#64748B",
          iconColor: "#3B82F6",
          iconBackgroundColor: "rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.15)",
          borderColor: "#E2E8F0",
        },
        button: {
          primaryBackground: "#667eea",
          primaryText: "#FFFFFF",
          secondaryBackground: "#F3F4F6",
          secondaryText: "#1F2937",
          borderColor: "#E2E8F0",
        },
        input: {
          backgroundColor: "#FFFFFF",
          textColor: "#0F172A",
          placeholderColor: "#94A3B8",
          borderColor: "#E2E8F0",
        },
        container: {
          titleColor: "#0F172A",
          subtitleColor: "#64748B",
          buttonColor: "#667eea",
          buttonTitleColor: "#FFFFFF",
        },
        search: {
          backgroundColor: "#F3F4F6",
          inputColor: "#0F172A",
          placeholderColor: "#94A3B8",
        },
        list: {
          titleSectionColor: "#64748B",
        }
      },

      // Dark mode specific
      dark: {
        header: {
          titleColor: "#F8FAFC",
          buttonColor: "#94A3B8",
        },
        card: {
          backgroundColor: "#292929",
          titleColor: "#F8FAFC",
          subtitleColor: "#94A3B8",
          iconColor: "#3B82F6",
          iconBackgroundColor: "rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.15)",
          borderColor: "#38383A",
        },
        button: {
          primaryBackground: "#667eea",
          primaryText: "#FFFFFF",
          secondaryBackground: "#38383A",
          secondaryText: "#F8FAFC",
          borderColor: "#38383A",
        },
        input: {
          backgroundColor: "#292929",
          textColor: "#F8FAFC",
          placeholderColor: "#64748B",
          borderColor: "#38383A",
        },
        container: {
          titleColor: "#F8FAFC",
          subtitleColor: "#94A3B8",
          buttonColor: "#667eea",
          buttonTitleColor: "#FFFFFF",
        },
        search: {
          backgroundColor: "#292929",
          inputColor: "#F8FAFC",
          placeholderColor: "#64748B",
        },
        list: {
          titleSectionColor: "#94A3B8",
        }
      }
    }
  }}
>
  <slot />
</UnifoldProvider>
```

## Best Practices

<Tip>
  **Use semantic colors first**, then layer component tokens only where you need specific overrides. This keeps your configuration manageable.
</Tip>

<Tip>
  **Put shape properties (borderRadius, borderWidth) in flat tokens** since they typically stay the same across light and dark modes. Put color properties in mode-specific tokens.
</Tip>

<Warning>
  **Don't override every token**. Only specify the properties you actually want to customize. Unspecified properties will use semantic theme colors or sensible defaults.
</Warning>

<Info>
  **Test in both modes** when using mode-specific tokens. Switch between light and dark appearance to ensure proper contrast and readability.
</Info>

# Examples

> Complete real-world examples of Svelte SDK theming configurations

Explore complete theming configurations for common use cases. Copy and adapt these examples to match your brand.

All examples show the `config` prop passed to `<UnifoldProvider>` in your SvelteKit layout.

## Basic Examples

### Minimal Configuration

The simplest way to theme the SDK — just set an accent color:

```svelte theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey={PUBLIC_UNIFOLD_KEY}
  config={{
    accentColor: "#667eea"
  }}
>
  <slot />
</UnifoldProvider>
```

### Light & Dark Modes

Basic semantic color configuration for both modes:

```svelte theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey={PUBLIC_UNIFOLD_KEY}
  config={{
    appearance: "auto",
    theme: {
      light: {
        background: "#FFFFFF",
        foreground: "#0F172A",
        primary: "#667eea",
      },
      dark: {
        background: "#191919",
        foreground: "#F8FAFC",
        primary: "#667eea",
      }
    }
  }}
>
  <slot />
</UnifoldProvider>
```

# Custom Fonts

> Configure custom typography and font families for your Svelte SDK components

The Unifold Svelte SDK allows you to customize typography by configuring custom font families. Apply your brand's typeface to create a cohesive user experience.

## Basic Configuration

Set a custom font family through the `fontFamily` property:

```svelte theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey={PUBLIC_UNIFOLD_KEY}
  config={{
    fontFamily: "Inter, -apple-system, sans-serif"
  }}
>
  <slot />
</UnifoldProvider>
```

<Info>
  The SDK will apply your `fontFamily` to all text elements within its components, including buttons, inputs, cards, and headers.
</Info>

## Per-Weight Font Configuration

For more precise control, use the `fonts` property to specify different font families for each weight:

```svelte theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey={PUBLIC_UNIFOLD_KEY}
  config={{
    fonts: {
      regular: "Inter Regular, sans-serif",
      medium: "Inter Medium, sans-serif",
      semibold: "Inter SemiBold, sans-serif",
      bold: "Inter Bold, sans-serif",
    }
  }}
>
  <slot />
</UnifoldProvider>
```

### FontConfig Properties

<ParamField path="fonts.regular" type="string">
  Font family for regular weight (400) text — body copy, labels, and default text.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="fonts.medium" type="string">
  Font family for medium weight (500) text — subtitles and emphasized content.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="fonts.semibold" type="string">
  Font family for semi-bold weight (600) text — section headers and strong emphasis.
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="fonts.bold" type="string">
  Font family for bold weight (700) text — headings and primary actions.
</ParamField>

<Tip>
  All properties in `fonts` are optional. Unspecified weights fall back to the SDK's built-in font. Use `fontFamily` for a single font across all weights, or `fonts` when you need per-weight control.
</Tip>

<Warning>
  If both `fontFamily` and `fonts` are provided, `fonts` takes precedence for each weight it defines.
</Warning>

### When to Use Per-Weight Fonts

Per-weight font configuration is useful when:

* Your brand uses different typefaces for headings vs body text
* You're using non-variable fonts that require separate files per weight
* You want a display font for bold/semibold and a body font for regular/medium

```ts theme={null}
fonts: {
  regular: "Inter, sans-serif",
  medium: "Inter, sans-serif",
  semibold: "Space Grotesk, sans-serif",
  bold: "Space Grotesk, sans-serif",
}
```

## Using System Fonts

### San Francisco (Apple)

```ts theme={null}
fontFamily: "-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, sans-serif"
```

### Segoe UI (Windows)

```ts theme={null}
fontFamily: "Segoe UI, Tahoma, sans-serif"
```

### Roboto (Android)

```ts theme={null}
fontFamily: "Roboto, sans-serif"
```

## Using Google Fonts in SvelteKit

### Step 1: Import the Font

In SvelteKit, add the Google Fonts link using `<svelte:head>` in your layout:

```svelte theme={null}
<!-- src/routes/+layout.svelte -->
<svelte:head>
  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com" />
  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin="anonymous" />
  <link
    href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;500;600;700&display=swap"
    rel="stylesheet"
  />
</svelte:head>
```

Alternatively, import in your global CSS file (`src/app.css`):

```css theme={null}
@import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;500;600;700&display=swap');
```

### Step 2: Configure the SDK

```svelte theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey={PUBLIC_UNIFOLD_KEY}
  config={{
    fontFamily: "Inter, sans-serif"
  }}
>
  <slot />
</UnifoldProvider>
```

### Complete Layout Example

```svelte theme={null}
<!-- src/routes/+layout.svelte -->
<script lang="ts">
  import { UnifoldProvider } from "@unifold/connect-svelte";
  import { PUBLIC_UNIFOLD_KEY } from "$env/static/public";
  import "@unifold/connect-svelte/styles-base.css";
</script>

<svelte:head>
  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com" />
  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin="anonymous" />
  <link
    href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;500;600;700&display=swap"
    rel="stylesheet"
  />
</svelte:head>

<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey={PUBLIC_UNIFOLD_KEY}
  config={{
    fontFamily: "Inter, sans-serif",
    appearance: "auto",
  }}
>
  <slot />
</UnifoldProvider>
```

## Using Custom/Self-Hosted Fonts

### Step 1: Define Font Face

Add `@font-face` rules to your `src/app.css`:

```css theme={null}
@font-face {
  font-family: 'MyCustomFont';
  src: url('/fonts/MyCustomFont-Regular.woff2') format('woff2'),
       url('/fonts/MyCustomFont-Regular.woff') format('woff');
  font-weight: 400;
  font-style: normal;
  font-display: swap;
}

@font-face {
  font-family: 'MyCustomFont';
  src: url('/fonts/MyCustomFont-Bold.woff2') format('woff2'),
       url('/fonts/MyCustomFont-Bold.woff') format('woff');
  font-weight: 700;
  font-style: normal;
  font-display: swap;
}
```

Place font files in the `static/fonts/` directory of your SvelteKit project.

### Step 2: Configure the SDK

```svelte theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey={PUBLIC_UNIFOLD_KEY}
  config={{
    fontFamily: "MyCustomFont, sans-serif"
  }}
>
  <slot />
</UnifoldProvider>
```

## Font Stack Best Practices

Always provide fallback fonts to ensure text displays properly while custom fonts load:

```ts theme={null}
fontFamily: "Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif"
```

<Tip>
  **Include system fonts as fallbacks** to ensure your UI remains readable even if the custom font fails to load.
</Tip>

## Font Loading Strategies

### Preload Critical Fonts

Add `<link rel="preload">` in `<svelte:head>` for faster font loading:

```svelte theme={null}
<svelte:head>
  <link rel="preload" href="/fonts/Inter-Regular.woff2" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin="anonymous" />
</svelte:head>
```

### Font Display Strategy

Use `font-display: swap` to show fallback text immediately:

```css theme={null}
@font-face {
  font-family: 'Inter';
  src: url('/fonts/Inter-Regular.woff2') format('woff2');
  font-display: swap;
}
```

## Common Issues

<Warning>
  **Font not displaying?** Ensure:

  1. Font files are accessible (check Network tab)
  2. CORS headers allow font loading
  3. Font name matches exactly in `fontFamily` or `fonts` config
  4. Font weights used in SDK (400, 500, 600, 700) are included in your font import
</Warning>

<Tip>
  **Performance tip:** Only load the font weights you actually use (400, 500, 600, 700). Avoid loading the full 100-900 range unless necessary.
</Tip>

<Info>
  **SvelteKit static assets:** Place font files in the `static/` directory. They'll be served from the root path (e.g., `/fonts/MyFont.woff2` for `static/fonts/MyFont.woff2`).
</Info>


### Elegant & Minimal

```ts theme={null}

```

# Overview

> Customize the look and feel of Unifold Svelte SDK components.

The Unifold Svelte SDK provides a comprehensive theming system that allows you to customize every aspect of your UI components. Whether you need simple brand color updates or complete design control, our theming system has you covered.

Since `@unifold/connect-svelte` wraps the same rendering engine as the React SDK, you get the **exact same customization capabilities** — all configured through the `config` prop on `<UnifoldProvider>`.

## Two Levels of Customization

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Semantic Theme" icon="palette" href="./semantic-colors">
    Global color system affecting all components. Perfect for brand consistency and quick styling.
  </Card>

  <Card title="Component Tokens" icon="sliders" href="./component-tokens">
    Granular control over individual component properties. Ideal for fine-tuned customization.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

## Quick Start

```svelte theme={null}
<!-- src/routes/+layout.svelte -->
<script lang="ts">
  import { UnifoldProvider } from "@unifold/connect-svelte";
  import { PUBLIC_UNIFOLD_KEY } from "$env/static/public";
  import "@unifold/connect-svelte/styles-base.css";
</script>

<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey={PUBLIC_UNIFOLD_KEY}
  config={{
    // Light/Dark mode
    appearance: "dark",

    // Quick brand color
    accentColor: "#667eea",

    // Semantic colors
    theme: {
      light: {
        background: "#FFFFFF",
        foreground: "#0F172A",
        primary: "#667eea",
      },
      dark: {
        background: "#191919",
        foreground: "#F8FAFC",
        primary: "#667eea",
      }
    },

    // Component tokens
    components: {
      card: {
        backgroundColor: "#F8FAFC",
        titleColor: "#0F172A",
        borderRadius: 16,
      },
      button: {
        borderRadius: 8,
      },
    },

    // Custom fonts
    fontFamily: "Inter, sans-serif",
  }}
>
  <slot />
</UnifoldProvider>
```

## Key Concepts

### Appearance Modes

The SDK supports three appearance modes:

* **`light`** — Force light mode
* **`dark`** — Force dark mode
* **`auto`** — Automatically matches system preference

### Theme Priority System

When resolving colors, the SDK follows this priority order (highest to lowest):

1. **Mode-specific component token** (e.g., `components.light.card.titleColor`)
2. **Flat component token** (e.g., `components.card.titleColor`)
3. **Semantic theme color** (e.g., `theme.light.foreground`)
4. **Built-in default**

This priority system gives you maximum flexibility while maintaining sensible defaults.

### Color Format Support

All color properties accept standard CSS color formats:

* **Hex**: `"#667eea"`, `"#667eea80"` (with alpha)
* **RGB**: `"rgb(102, 126, 234)"`
* **RGBA**: `"rgba(102, 126, 234, 0.5)"`
* **HSL**: `"hsl(235, 75%, 66%)"`

## What Can You Customize?

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Semantic Theme Colors (17 tokens)">
    Global colors that affect all components:

    * Background, foreground, card colors
    * Primary brand color
    * Border colors
    * Success, warning, error states (with backgrounds)
    * Overlay
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Component Tokens (48 properties)">
    Fine-grained control over 7 component categories:

    * **Header** (2): title, buttons
    * **Card** (19): background, title, subtitle, labels, icons, actions, borders, radius
    * **Button** (7): primary/secondary backgrounds and text, borders, radius
    * **Input** (6): background, text, placeholder, borders, radius
    * **Container** (9): titles, subtitles, actions, buttons, icons, radius
    * **Search** (3): background, input, placeholder
    * **List** (2): section titles, row radius
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Typography">
    * Single font family for all text (`fontFamily`)
    * Per-weight font families for granular control (`fonts`)
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

# Quick Reference

> Fast lookup guide for all Svelte SDK theming configuration options

A comprehensive cheat sheet for all available theming options in the Unifold Svelte SDK.

## Configuration Structure

```svelte theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey={PUBLIC_UNIFOLD_KEY}
  config={{
    appearance: "light" | "dark" | "auto",
    accentColor: string,
    fontFamily: string,
    fonts: {
      regular: string,
      medium: string,
      semibold: string,
      bold: string,
    },
    theme: {
      light: { /* ThemeColors */ },
      dark: { /* ThemeColors */ }
    },
    components: {
      /* Flat styles */
      header: { /* HeaderStyles */ },
      card: { /* CardStyles */ },
      button: { /* ButtonStyles */ },
      input: { /* InputStyles */ },
      container: { /* ContainerStyles */ },
      search: { /* SearchStyles */ },
      list: { /* ListStyles */ },

      /* Mode-specific styles */
      light: {
        header: { /* HeaderStyles */ },
        card: { /* CardStyles */ },
        button: { /* ButtonStyles */ },
        input: { /* InputStyles */ },
        container: { /* ContainerStyles */ },
        search: { /* SearchStyles */ },
        list: { /* ListStyles */ },
      },
      dark: {
        header: { /* HeaderStyles */ },
        card: { /* CardStyles */ },
        button: { /* ButtonStyles */ },
        input: { /* InputStyles */ },
        container: { /* ContainerStyles */ },
        search: { /* SearchStyles */ },
        list: { /* ListStyles */ },
      }
    }
  }}
>
  <slot />
</UnifoldProvider>
```

***

## Provider Config Options

| Option                           | Type                                          | Default          | Description                                                          |
| -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `appearance`                     | `'light' \| 'dark' \| 'auto'`                 | `'dark'`         | Theme appearance mode                                                |
| `modalTitle`                     | `string`                                      | —                | Custom modal header title                                            |
| `hideDepositTracker`             | `boolean`                                     | `false`          | Hide the deposit tracker UI                                          |
| `transferCryptoTitle`            | `string`                                      | i18n default     | Main menu: Transfer Crypto row title                                 |
| `depositWithCardTitle`           | `string`                                      | i18n default     | Main menu: Deposit with Card row title                               |
| `payWithExchangeTitle`           | `string`                                      | i18n default     | Main menu: Pay with Exchange row title                               |
| `depositTrackerTitle`            | `string`                                      | i18n default     | Main menu: Deposit Tracker row title                                 |
| `depositTrackerSubTitle`         | `string`                                      | i18n default     | Main menu: Deposit Tracker subtitle                                  |
| `hideDepositFlowInfo`            | `boolean`                                     | `false`          | Hide You use / You buy / You receive on card onramp                  |
| `hideDisplayDescription`         | `boolean`                                     | `false`          | Hide temporary-address disclaimer on card onramp                     |
| `showBalanceHeader`              | `boolean`                                     | `true`           | Show balance in modal header                                         |
| `transferInputVariant`           | `'single_input' \| 'double_input'`            | `'double_input'` | Transfer amount input layout                                         |
| `enableConnectWallet`            | `boolean`                                     | `false`          | Enable browser wallet option                                         |
| `browserWalletAmountQuickSelect` | `'percentage' \| 'usd'`                       | `'percentage'`   | Connect Wallet amount pill style: percentage-of-balance or fixed USD |
| `enablePayWithExchange`          | `boolean`                                     | dashboard value  | Enable "Pay with Exchange"                                           |
| `accentColor`                    | `string`                                      | —                | Quick primary color override                                         |
| `fontFamily`                     | `string`                                      | —                | Single font for all weights                                          |
| `fonts`                          | `FontConfig`                                  | —                | Per-weight font families                                             |
| `theme`                          | `ThemeConfig`                                 | —                | Semantic color overrides                                             |
| `components`                     | `ComponentConfig`                             | —                | Component style overrides                                            |
| `defaultInitialScreen`           | `'main' \| 'transfer' \| 'card' \| 'tracker'` | `main`           | Default first screen when `beginDeposit()` omits `initialScreen`     |

## Component Styles (48 properties)

### Header Styles (2 properties)

```ts theme={null}
header: {
  titleColor: string,   // Header title          → foreground
  buttonColor: string,  // Header buttons        → foreground
}
```

### Card Styles (19 properties)

```ts theme={null}
card: {
  backgroundColor: string,         // Card background           → card
  titleColor: string,              // Card title                → foreground
  subtitleColor: string,           // Card subtitle             → foregroundMuted
  labelColor: string,              // Card labels               → foregroundMuted
  headerColor: string,             // Card header text          → foregroundMuted
  labelRightColor: string,         // Right-aligned labels      → foregroundMuted
  labelHighlightRightColor: string,// Highlighted right labels  → warning
  textRightColor: string,          // Right-aligned text        → foreground
  subtextRightColor: string,       // Right-aligned subtext     → foregroundMuted
  rowLeftLabel: string,            // Left column labels        → foregroundMuted
  rowRightLabel: string,           // Right column labels       → foreground
  iconColor: string,               // Card icons                → primary
  iconBackgroundColor: string,     // Icon bg                   → primary + 15% opacity
  actionColor: string,             // Action indicators         → foregroundMuted
  actionIcon: string,              // Action icons              → foregroundMuted
  descriptionColor: string,        // Description text          → foregroundMuted
  borderRadius: number,            // Corner radius (px)        → 12
  borderWidth: number,             // Border width (px)         → 0
  borderColor: string,             // Border color              → border
}
```

### Button Styles (7 properties)

```ts theme={null}
button: {
  primaryBackground: string,   // Primary button bg         → primary
  primaryText: string,         // Primary button text       → primaryForeground
  secondaryBackground: string, // Secondary button bg       → card
  secondaryText: string,       // Secondary button text     → foreground
  borderRadius: number,        // Corner radius (px)        → 12
  borderWidth: number,         // Border width (px)         → 0
  borderColor: string,         // Border color              → border
}
```

### Input Styles (6 properties)

```ts theme={null}
input: {
  backgroundColor: string, // Input background           → card
  textColor: string,       // Input text                 → foreground
  placeholderColor: string, // Placeholder text           → foregroundMuted
  borderColor: string,     // Border color               → border
  borderRadius: number,    // Corner radius (px)         → 8
  borderWidth: number,     // Border width (px)          → 1
}
```

### Container Styles (9 properties)

```ts theme={null}
container: {
  titleColor: string,          // Container title           → foreground
  subtitleColor: string,       // Container subtitle        → foregroundMuted
  actionColor: string,         // Action elements           → foregroundMuted
  actionTitle: string,         // Action title text         → foregroundMuted
  buttonColor: string,         // Button background         → primary
  buttonTitleColor: string,    // Button text               → primaryForeground
  iconBackgroundColor: string, // Status icon bg            → success
  iconColor: string,           // Status icon               → foreground
  borderRadius: number,        // Modal corner radius (px)  → 24
}
```

### Search Styles (3 properties)

```ts theme={null}
search: {
  backgroundColor: string, // Search background          → card
  inputColor: string,      // Search text                → foreground
  placeholderColor: string, // Search placeholder         → foregroundMuted
}
```

### List Styles (2 properties)

```ts theme={null}
list: {
  titleSectionColor: string, // List section headers      → foregroundMuted
  rowBorderRadius: number,   // Row corner radius (px)    → 12
}
```

## Priority System

Colors are resolved in this order (highest to lowest):

<Steps>
  <Step title="Mode-Specific Component Style">
    `components.light.card.titleColor` or `components.dark.card.titleColor`
  </Step>

  <Step title="Flat Component Style">
    `components.card.titleColor`
  </Step>

  <Step title="Semantic Theme Color">
    `theme.light.foreground` or `theme.dark.foreground`
  </Step>

  <Step title="Built-in Default">
    SDK's default color values
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Checklist

Use this checklist when configuring your theme:

<Steps>
  <Step title="Set Appearance Mode">
    Choose `light`, `dark`, or `auto`
  </Step>

  <Step title="Configure Accent Color">
    Set your primary brand color
  </Step>

  <Step title="Add Semantic Colors (Optional)">
    Customize global color styles
  </Step>

  <Step title="Add Component Styles (Optional)">
    Fine-tune specific components
  </Step>

  <Step title="Adjust Borders & Shapes (Optional)">
    Set borderRadius and borderWidth on cards, buttons, inputs
  </Step>

  <Step title="Set Custom Font (Optional)">
    Configure single font or per-weight fonts
  </Step>

  <Step title="Load Fonts via svelte:head">
    Add Google Font links or @font-face in your layout
  </Step>

  <Step title="Test in Both Modes">
    Verify light and dark appearance
  </Step>

  <Step title="Check Contrast">
    Ensure readability (4.5:1 ratio)
  </Step>
</Steps>

***

## Common Mistakes

<Warning>
  **Using `components.card` and `components.light.card` together**

  Mode-specific styles override flat styles. Be intentional about which you use. Put shared shape properties (like `borderRadius`) in flat styles, and mode-specific colors in `light`/`dark`.
</Warning>

<Warning>
  **Forgetting dark mode**

  Always test with `appearance: "dark"` to ensure proper contrast.
</Warning>

<Warning>
  **Inconsistent font loading**

  Ensure custom fonts are loaded via `<svelte:head>` or `src/app.css` before the SDK initializes.
</Warning>

<Warning>
  **Not providing fallbacks**

  Always include fallback fonts in `fontFamily` or `fonts` configuration.
</Warning>

# Semantic Colors

> Global color tokens that provide consistent theming across all Svelte SDK components

Semantic colors are global color tokens that affect all components in the SDK. They provide a consistent foundation for your UI theme and are the easiest way to apply your brand colors across the entire SDK.

## Configuration

Configure semantic colors through the `theme` property in your `<UnifoldProvider>` config:

```svelte theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey={PUBLIC_UNIFOLD_KEY}
  config={{
    theme: {
      light: {
        // Your light mode colors
      },
      dark: {
        // Your dark mode colors
      }
    }
  }}
>
  <slot />
</UnifoldProvider>
```

## Complete Token Reference

### Base Colors

<ParamField path="background" type="string">
  Primary background color for the entire interface.

  **Default (Light):** `#FFFFFF`\
  **Default (Dark):** `#191919`

  ```ts theme={null}
  theme: {
    light: { background: "#FFFFFF" },
    dark: { background: "#191919" }
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="card" type="string">
  Background color for card components and elevated surfaces.

  **Default (Light):** `#F8FAFC`\
  **Default (Dark):** `#292929`

  ```ts theme={null}
  theme: {
    light: { card: "#F8FAFC" },
    dark: { card: "#292929" }
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="cardHover" type="string">
  Background color for cards in hover state.

  **Default (Light):** `#F1F5F9`\
  **Default (Dark):** `#48474A`

  ```ts theme={null}
  theme: {
    light: { cardHover: "#E2E8F0" },
    dark: { cardHover: "#3F3F45" }
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

### Text Colors

<ParamField path="foreground" type="string">
  Primary text color for headings and important content.

  **Default (Light):** `#0F172A`\
  **Default (Dark):** `#F8FAFC`

  ```ts theme={null}
  theme: {
    light: { foreground: "#1F2937" },
    dark: { foreground: "#F9FAFB" }
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="foregroundMuted" type="string">
  Secondary text color for less prominent content.

  **Default (Light):** `#64748B`\
  **Default (Dark):** `#94A3B8`

  ```ts theme={null}
  theme: {
    light: { foregroundMuted: "#6B7280" },
    dark: { foregroundMuted: "#9CA3AF" }
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="foregroundSubtle" type="string">
  Tertiary text color for subtle content and hints.

  **Default (Light):** `#94A3B8`\
  **Default (Dark):** `#64748B`

  ```ts theme={null}
  theme: {
    light: { foregroundSubtle: "#9CA3AF" },
    dark: { foregroundSubtle: "#6B7280" }
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

### Border Colors

<ParamField path="border" type="string">
  Primary border color for input fields and dividers.

  **Default (Light):** `#E2E8F0`\
  **Default (Dark):** `#38383A`

  ```ts theme={null}
  theme: {
    light: { border: "#D1D5DB" },
    dark: { border: "#38383A" }
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="borderSecondary" type="string">
  Secondary border color for subtle separators.

  **Default (Light):** `#CBD5E1`\
  **Default (Dark):** `#48484A`

  ```ts theme={null}
  theme: {
    light: { borderSecondary: "#E5E7EB" },
    dark: { borderSecondary: "#48484A" }
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

### Brand Colors

<ParamField path="primary" type="string">
  Primary brand color for buttons, links, and key actions.

  **Default:** `#3B82F6`

  ```ts theme={null}
  theme: {
    light: { primary: "#667eea" },
    dark: { primary: "#667eea" }
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="primaryForeground" type="string">
  Text color on primary colored backgrounds.

  **Default:** `#FFFFFF`

  ```ts theme={null}
  theme: {
    light: { primaryForeground: "#FFFFFF" },
    dark: { primaryForeground: "#FFFFFF" }
  }
  ```
</ParamField>

### Status Colors

<ParamField path="success" type="string">
  Color for success states and positive actions.

  **Default:** `#22C55E`
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="successBackground" type="string">
  Background color for success messages and alerts.

  **Default (Light):** `#DCFCE7`\
  **Default (Dark):** `rgba(34, 197, 94, 0.1)`
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="warning" type="string">
  Color for warning states and caution indicators.

  **Default:** `#F59E0B`
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="warningBackground" type="string">
  Background color for warning messages and alerts.

  **Default (Light):** `#FEF3C7`\
  **Default (Dark):** `rgba(245, 158, 11, 0.1)`
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="error" type="string">
  Color for error states and destructive actions.

  **Default:** `#EF4444`
</ParamField>

<ParamField path="errorBackground" type="string">
  Background color for error messages and alerts.

  **Default (Light):** `#FEE2E2`\
  **Default (Dark):** `rgba(239, 68, 68, 0.1)`
</ParamField>

### Overlay

<ParamField path="overlay" type="string">
  Background color for the modal overlay/backdrop.

  **Default (Light):** `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)`\
  **Default (Dark):** `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.7)`
</ParamField>

## Complete Example

```svelte theme={null}
<UnifoldProvider
  publishableKey={PUBLIC_UNIFOLD_KEY}
  config={{
    theme: {
      light: {
        background: "#FFFFFF",
        card: "#F8FAFC",
        cardHover: "#F1F5F9",
        foreground: "#0F172A",
        foregroundMuted: "#64748B",
        foregroundSubtle: "#94A3B8",
        border: "#E2E8F0",
        borderSecondary: "#CBD5E1",
        primary: "#667eea",
        primaryForeground: "#FFFFFF",
        success: "#22C55E",
        successBackground: "#DCFCE7",
        warning: "#F59E0B",
        warningBackground: "#FEF3C7",
        error: "#EF4444",
        errorBackground: "#FEE2E2",
        overlay: "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)",
      },
      dark: {
        background: "#191919",
        card: "#292929",
        cardHover: "#48474A",
        foreground: "#F8FAFC",
        foregroundMuted: "#94A3B8",
        foregroundSubtle: "#64748B",

        borderSecondary: "#48484A",
```

## Best Practices

<Tip>
  **Start with semantic colors** before diving into component tokens. They provide the foundation for your entire theme and will handle 80% of your styling needs.
</Tip>

<Warning>
  **Maintain sufficient contrast** between `foreground` and `background` colors to ensure readability. Aim for a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 for normal text.
</Warning>

<Info>
  **Use the same `primary` color** in both light and dark modes for brand consistency, but adjust surrounding colors for proper contrast.
</Info>

# Supported Chains

> Blockchain networks supported by Unifold

Unifold supports a wide range of blockchain networks. When calling `beginDeposit()`, you specify both `destinationChainType` and `destinationChainId` to indicate where the funds should be received.

<Note>
  **Destination vs Source Chains**: The destination chain is where your user's funds will ultimately arrive. Unifold handles cross-chain routing automatically—users can deposit from any supported source chain, and funds will be converted and delivered to your specified destination chain and token.
</Note>

## Supported Chains

The following chains are supported for both:

* **Incoming deposits** — chains your users can deposit from
* **Destination** — chains where converted funds are delivered

When calling `beginDeposit()`, specify the destination using `destinationChainType` and `destinationChainId`.

## Example Usage

```tsx theme={null}
// Deposit to Polygon (EVM)
await beginDeposit({
  externalUserId: 'user_123',
  destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
  destinationChainId: '137',
  destinationTokenAddress: '0x2791bca1f2de4661ed88a30c99a7a9449aa84174',
  destinationTokenSymbol: 'USDC',
  recipientAddress: '0x...',
});

// Deposit to Solana
await beginDeposit({
  externalUserId: 'user_123',
  destinationChainType: 'solana',
  destinationChainId: 'mainnet',
  destinationTokenAddress: 'EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v',
  destinationTokenSymbol: 'USDC',
  recipientAddress: '...',
});

// Deposit to Ethereum ETH
await beginDeposit({
  externalUserId: 'user_123',
  destinationChainType: 'ethereum',
  destinationChainId: '1',
  destinationTokenAddress: 'native', // use 'native' as native token's address
  destinationTokenSymbol: 'ETH',
  recipientAddress: '...',
});
```

        ```tsx theme={null}
              <DepositButton />
            </UnifoldProvider>

        function DepositButton() {
          const { beginDeposit } = useUnifold();

          return (
        ```

        ```tsx theme={null}
        function DepositButton() {
          const { beginDeposit } = useUnifold();

          return (
            <Button
              title="Deposit"

              })}
            />
          );

        export default function App() {
        ```

        ```kotlin theme={null}
        import io.unifold.android.*
        import io.unifold.android.ui.views.DepositBottomSheet

        @Composable
        fun DepositScreen() {
            var showDeposit by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }

            val config = DepositConfiguration(
                externalUserId = "user_123",
                publishableKey = "pk_live_...",
                destinationTokenSymbol = "USDC",
                destinationChainType = ChainType.ETHEREUM,
                destinationChainId = "137",
                recipientAddress = "0x606C...3160",
            )

            Button(onClick = { showDeposit = true }) {
                Text("Deposit")
            }

            DepositBottomSheet(
                isVisible = showDeposit,
                configuration = config,
                onDismiss = { showDeposit = false }
            )
        }
        ```
